allCourses.title: Conduct of Research
allCourses.description: Introduces new graduate students to ethical conduct of scientific research, mentoring, and current research in the Department of chemistry.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms I
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of basic mechanistic principles of modern organic chemistry. Topics include molecular orbital theory, orbital symmetry control of organic reactions, aromaticity, carbonium ion chemistry, free radical chemistry, the chemistry of carbenes and carbanions, photochemistry, electrophilic substitutions, aromatic chemistry.

allCourses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms II
allCourses.description: Topics include more in-depth treatment of mechanistic concepts, kinetics, conformational analysis, computational methods, stereoelectronics, and both solution and enzymatic catalysis.

allCourses.title: Organic Spectroscopy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Modern methods used in structure determination of organic molecules. Topics include mass spectrometry; ultraviolet, chiroptical, infrared, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C) or (CHEM H52A and CHEM H52B and CHEM H52C)

allCourses.title: Organic Synthesis I
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry is developed. Major emphasis is on carbon-carbon bond forming methodology. Topics include carbonyl annelations, cycloadditions, sigmatropic rearrangements, and organometallic methods.

allCourses.title: Organic Synthesis II
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry will be developed. Major emphasis this quarter is on natural product total synthesis and retrosynthetic (antithetic) analysis.

allCourses.title: Advanced Data Acquisition and Analysis
allCourses.description: Introduces students to a variety of practical laboratory techniques, including lock-in, boxcar, coincidence counting, noise filtering, PID control, properties of common transducers, computer interfacing to instruments, vacuum technology, laboratory safety, basic mechanical design, and shop skills. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Applied Physical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts in molecular structure and reactivity: theory of bonding, valence and molecular orbitals; structure and reactivity in inorganic chemistry; elements in molecular group theory; nomenclature in organic chemistry; and survey of macromolecules.

allCourses.title: Math Methods
allCourses.description: Applications of mathematics to physical and chemical problems. Calculus of special functions, complex variables and vectors; linear vector spaces and eigenvalue problems. Differential equations.

allCourses.title: Chemical Kinetics
allCourses.description: Surveys gas phase and organic reaction mechanisms and their relationship to kinetic rate laws; treats the basic theory of elementary reaction rates.  A brief presentation of modern cross-sectional kinetics is included.

allCourses.title: Inorganic Chemistry I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of modern inorganic chemistry with applications to chemical systems of current interest. Inorganic phenomena are organized into general patterns which rationalize observed structures, stabilities, and physical properties.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 107 and CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

allCourses.title: Organometallic Chemistry
allCourses.description: Synthesis and reactivity of organometallic complexes with an emphasis on mechanisms. Topics include bonding and fluxional properties; metal-carbon single and multiple bonds; metal š-complexes. Applications to homogenous catalysis and organic synthesis are incorporated throughout the course.

allCourses.title: Physical Inorganic Chemistry
allCourses.description: General principles of the spectroscopy and magnetism of inorganic compounds. Characterization of inorganic complexes by infrared, near-infrared, visible, ultraviolet, NMR, EPR, EXAFS, and Mossbauer spectroscopies. Some necessary group theory developed.

allCourses.title: Metallobiochemistry
allCourses.description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.

allCourses.title: Chemical and Structural Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey of the organic chemistry underlying biological function. Introduction to chemical genetics, receptor-ligand interactions, small molecule agonists and antagonists, combinatorial synthesis, high throughput assays, molecular evolution, protein and small molecule design.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Molecular Biophysics
allCourses.description: An overview of the principles and concepts in molecular biophysics.  Topics covered include energy and entropy in biology, non-equilibrium reaction kinetics, random walks and molecular diffusion, molecular forces in biology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate courses in physical chemistry and biochemistry.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Biological Macromolecules
allCourses.description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Biophotonics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the application of photonic technologies to biomolecular and cellular systems. Sample technologies Optical Tweezers, Linear and Nonlinear Optical Microscopy and Fluorescence Lifetime and Correlation Methods, and their use to investigate emergent problems in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology.

allCourses.title: Polymer Chemistry:  Synthesis and Characterization of Polymers
allCourses.description: Structure of synthetic and natural polymers.  Survey of modern polymer synthetic methods.  Molecular weight and molecular weight distribution.  Chain conformation and stereochemistry. Introduction to polymer characterization, chain models, and solution behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate courses in organic and physical chemistry.

allCourses.title: Electromagnetism
allCourses.description: Maxwell’s equations, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves and radiation, wave propagation in media, interference and quantum optics, coherent and incoherent radiation, with practical applications in interferometry, lasers, waveguides, and optical instrumentation.

allCourses.title: Computational Methods
allCourses.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

allCourses.title: Classical Mechanics and Electromagnetic Theory
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of classical mechanics and electromagnetic theory are developed with specific application to molecular systems. Newtonian, Lagrangian, and Hamiltonian mechanics are developed. Boundary value problems in electrostatics are investigated. Multipole expansion and macroscopic media are discussed from a molecular viewpoint.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: The postulates of quantum mechanics are discussed and applied to a variety of model problems.

allCourses.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: Approximate methods for solving atomic and molecular structure problems are developed, and the application of quantum mechanics to spectroscopy is introduced.

allCourses.title: Molecular Spectroscopy
allCourses.description: Theory and techniques of spectroscopy as used for the study of molecular and condensed phase properties. Coherent time domain spectroscopies are covered.

allCourses.title: Thermodynamics and Introduction to Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.description: A detailed discussion from an advanced point of view of the principles of classical thermodynamics. The fundamentals of statistical mechanics. Topics include an introduction to ensemble theory, Boltzmann statistics, classical statistical mechanics, and the statistical mechanics of ideal gas systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 131A AND CHEM 131B AND CHEM 131C AND ( NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER )

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.description: Continued discussion of the principles of statistical mechanics. Applications to topics of chemical interest including imperfect gases, liquids, solutions, and crystals. Modern techniques such as the use of autocorrelation function methods.

allCourses.title: Non-Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.description: Phenomenology of material processes, including: kinetic theories of transport and continuum, linear response theory, critical phenomena of phase transition, self-assembly, and nucleation.

allCourses.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Methods in Chemistry
allCourses.description: Survey of essential math methods in chemistry. Topics may include series and limits, complex analysis, Fourier and Laplace transforms, linear algebra and operators (theory and algorithms), differential equations, and probability concepts for stochastic processes.

allCourses.title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.

allCourses.title: Advanced Instrumental Analysis
allCourses.description: Theory and applications of modern advanced instrumental methods of analysis. Includes data acquisition, storage, retrieval, and analysis; Fourier transform methods; vacuum technologies; magnetic sector; quadrupole and ion trap mass spectrometry; surface science spectroscopic methods; lasers and optics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 152 and CHEM 132C. CHEM 152 with a grade of B or better. CHEM 132C with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Detection and Measurement of Radiation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of detection and measurement of ionizing radiation; both theory and practical aspects of measurement techniques for alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation, properties of different detector materials, electronics and data treatments, and analysis.

allCourses.title: Gas-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.description: Sources, chemistry, sinks, and measurements of key atmospheric gaseous species. Chemistry of photochemical oxidant formation, transformation of key inorganic and organic trace gases, and stratospheric ozone cycling. Applications of atmospheric chemistry models to control strategies.

allCourses.title: Multi-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.description: Chemical and physical processes leading to the production, aging, and removal of atmospheric particles. Multi-phase processes involving gases, particles, water droplets, and environmental surfaces. Approaches for modeling these processes with applications to control strategies.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Separations and Chromatography
allCourses.description: Introduction to modern separation techniques such as gas chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography, supercritical fluid chromatography, capillary electrophoresis, and field flow fractionation. Applications of these separation strategies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Current Problems in Analytical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Surveys current research challenges in analytical chemistry. Topics include electrochemistry, chromatography, spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry.

allCourses.title: Electrochemistry
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of electrochemistry including thermodynamics and the electrochemical potential, charge transfer kinetics, and mass transfer. Methods based on controlled potential and controlled current are described; the effects of slow heterogeneous kinetics and the perturbation caused by homogeneous chemistry are discussed.

allCourses.title: Analytical Spectroscopy
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of spectroscopic techniques and instrumentation. Atomic and molecular absorption, emission, and scattering processes and their application to quantitative chemical analysis are outlined. Puts different spectroscopic techniques in perspective and demonstrates most appropriate applications to analytical problems.

allCourses.title: Computational Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic concepts, methods, and techniques in computational chemistry: density functional and wavefunction theory, molecular property calculations, analysis tools, potential energy surfaces, vibrational effects, molecular dynamics simulations.

allCourses.title: Computational Chemistry Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the practice of modern computational chemistry through a series of advanced computational experiments.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in organic chemistry.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Physical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in physical chemistry. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Computational and Theoretical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Subjects covered vary from year to year.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Materials Chemistry
allCourses.description: An introduction to crystalline solids, descriptive crystal chemistry, solid-state synthesis and characterization techniques, x-ray and electron diffraction, phase diagrams, electronic band structure of extended solids, semi conductors, and nanoscale inorganic materials.

allCourses.title: Analytical Methods for Organic Nanomaterials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of analytical techniques related to measuring the structure and dynamics of organic nanomaterials. Topics include transmission electron microscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, liquid phase electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, light scattering, small angle X-ray, and neutron scattering.

allCourses.title: Current Topics in Chemical, Applied, and Materials Physics
allCourses.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year.  Connection between fundamental principles and implementations in practice in science, industry, and technology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Photochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Photochemical and photovoltaic processes in molecules and semiconductors; quantum mechanics; statistical thermodynamics; kinetics; and experimental techniques relevant to photon absorption and emission; photochemical charge separation, recombination, and transport of electrons and ions; and interfacial redox chemistry.

allCourses.title: NMR Spectroscopy
allCourses.description: Students learn the theoretical basis of solid-state or solution NMR (alternate times), including the basics of pulse sequence design. Extensive literature reading is required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Technical Communication Skills

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Early Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from its origins in the Bronze Age to the mid-Archaic period. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, religion, and archaeological remains.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society:  Late Archaic and Classical Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the Late Archaic period to the Classical period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Fourth-Century and Hellenistic Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the fourth century BCE through to the Hellenistic period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Origins to Roman Republic
allCourses.description: A survey of the development of Roman civilization from its eighth century BCE beginnings to the civil wars of the first century BCE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Roman Empire
allCourses.description: A survey of Roman civilization from Augustus’s consolidation of power following the civil wars of the first century BCE to the crisis of the third century CE. Includes social history, literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: The Fall of Rome
allCourses.description: A survey of Roman civilization from the crisis of the third century CE to the so-called “fall of Rome” in 476 CE.  Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: Classical Mythology: The Heroes
allCourses.description: An overview of the main myths of the heroes of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

allCourses.title: Classical Mythology: Ancient and Modern Perspectives of Classical Mythology
allCourses.description: Detailed examination of key Greek and Roman myths, their interpretations, and the influence they have exerted on literature, art, and popular culture in subsequent periods.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to canonical texts in psychoanalysis coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken before CLT&THY 200A.

allCourses.description: Introduces doctoral students to an interdisciplinary conversation about black queer sexuality and black heteropatriarchy. Uses disciplinary formations as a tool for understanding knowledge formations about the shifting relations that constitute sexuality, gender, and racial blackness.

allCourses.title: Afro-Pessimism and the Status of the Subject

allCourses.description: Afro-Pessimism theorizes the Black as a being against which all other beings become legible as human subjects. Focuses on either the subject of psychoanalysis or the subject of capital accumulation in their explorations of the antagonism between Blackness.

allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Teaches programming tools, skills, and conventions for collaborative work in computational cognitive science. Topics covered include program structure, version control, random number generation, plotting, basic model fitting, and numerical optimization methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYC 14M or PSYC 114M or COGS 14P or ICS 31) and (PSYC 10C or STAT 7 or STAT 110)

allCourses.title: Cognitive Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Cognitive process models analyzed using computational Bayesian methods. Formal statistical specification of models, parameter estimation, model evaluation, and research applications. Covers multinomial process trees, signal detection theory, Thurstone ranking models, item-response theory, decision models, and reaction time models.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYC 14M or PSYC 114M or COGS 14P or ICS 31 or MATH 9) and (PSYC 10C or STAT 7 or STAT 110) and (MATH 2B or MATH 5B or MATH 7B)

allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 2B OR MATH 5B OR MATH 7B ) AND ( STATS 7 OR PSYCH 10C OR STATS 110 OR AP STATISTICS ) AND ( MATH 0 OR COGS 14P OR PSYCH 14M OR I&C SCI 31 OR PSYCH 114M )

allCourses.description: Learn multiple ways of visualizing data, of transforming data, looking for consistencies and patterns in data, and interpreting these patterns to reach conclusions. Serves as first introduction to computer programming using the R language.

allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Hearing and Speech Sciences Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on thorough understanding of the probabilistic and logical basis of formal statistical inference, and the concept of statistical evidence. Applications in R.

allCourses.description: Students learn about standard procedures in statistics for the social sciences, with a focus on linear models for discovering the underlying structure in data. Applications in R.

allCourses.title: Judgment and Decision Making
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The psychology of human decision making. Theories, models, experiments, and data that inform how people make choices, judgments, and other decisions. Topics include optimality and bias, mental simulation, learning and feedback, expertise, emotional effects, and group decision making.

allCourses.title: Principles of Learning Theory
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Investigation of the learning and memory processes of human and animals.  Basic experimental approaches to learning and memory, empirical results, and theoretical interpretations of the evidence are discussed.

allCourses.title: Human Memory
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Developments in the area of memory; history of memory research; theories of the nature of memory. Visual memory, recognition memory, high-speed scanning, free recall, short-term memory, mnemonics, retrieval, relationship of memory to thinking. Selected theoretical formulations for memory.

allCourses.title: MATLAB Programming
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: MATLAB is a mathematical software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology. Topics include rudiments of programming, statistical analysis of data, matrix algebra, signal processing, graphic visualization, and simulated models of cognitive and perceptual processes.

allCourses.title: Scientific Python for Research
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces Python for data analysis and modeling encountered in cognitive science and neuroscience. Topics include data structures, execution control, graphic visualization, and interaction with sound and display interfaces. Application in statistical analysis, model simulation, and stimulus presentation and experimental control.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the neural basis of human perceptual, motor, and cognitive abilities. Topics include sensory perception, motor control, memory, language, attention, emotion, frontal lobe function, functional brain imaging, and neuropsychological disorders.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYC 7A or PSCI 9) or ((PSYC 9A or PSCI 11A) and (PSYC 9B or PSCI 11B))

allCourses.title: Brain Disorders and Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYC 7A or PSCI 9) or ((PSYC 9A or PSCI 11A) and (PSYC 9B or PSCI 11B)) or BIOL 35 or BIOL N110 or BIOL N115A

allCourses.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Sciences Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.

allCourses.title: Proseminar in the Cognitive Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the conceptual foundations and basic research results in the cognitive sciences for first-year graduate students.

allCourses.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Logic and set theory are covered during the first three weeks, using an interactive computer system. The remaining seven weeks are devoted to probability theory and cover elementary concepts from samples spaces to Chebychev's Inequality and the moment generating function.

allCourses.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to statistical estimation and statistical inference. Topics include sufficiency and the Rao-Blackwell Theorem, completeness and the Lehmann-Scheffe Theorem. The method of maximum likelihood is explored in some detail. Inference in linear models covers regression and analysis of variance.

allCourses.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of the fundamentals of statistical inference and computational implementations of common statistical models.

allCourses.title: Applied Mathematics for Cognitive Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Covers the basics of linear systems analysis, focusing on linear algebra, Fourier analysis, differential equations, and elementary signal processing. Applications in Cognitive Science and Cognitive Neuroscience research are developed.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Professional Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on grant writing and submission process, responsible conduct of research, and ethics training.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Professional Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Development of professional skills. Focus on scientific presentations and preparation.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Professional Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on career opportunities, interests and information, and community outreach.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces rudiments of programming, statistical analysis and probability theory, graphic visualization, GUI design, spectral analysis, and simulation models using MATLAB, a software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology.

allCourses.title: Computational Lab Skills for Cognitive Scientists I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an in-depth introduction to writing MATLAB programs to run auditory and visual experiments. Topics covered include program structure, stimulus generation, presentation, and data collection.

allCourses.title: Computational Lab Skills for Cognitive Scientists II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to a number of computational statistics approaches including exploratory data analysis and modeling using a probabilistic framework with Bayesian graphical models. Emphasis on in-class programming using MATLAB.

allCourses.title: Neural Networks and Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction and review of the current state of the art in neural networks and machine learning with specific emphasis of applications to behavioral and neuroscience data analysis and modeling.

allCourses.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences I: Topics in Perception
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on visual, auditory, and somatic perception and bottom-up mechanisms of attention.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences II: Topics in Cognition
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on emotion, top-down attention, goal-directed behavior, categorization, judgment, and decision-making.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences III: Topics in Learning and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses experimental data, formal models of learning, and evidence linking learning and development to its neural substrates. Topics include Pavlovian and instrumental conditioning, language acquisition, causal reasoning, perceptual learning, category formation, and structure learning.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: The Mind/Body Problem
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary, drawing on information from the fields of quantum physics, computer vision, artificial intelligence, cognition, neurophysiology, philosophy, and psychophysics.

allCourses.title: Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Considers a range of statistical methods of data analysis and simple cognitive models using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.

allCourses.title: Hearing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines auditory sensation and perception using psychophysical and neuroscientific perspectives. Covers physical aspects of sound; subcortical auditory processing; aspects of sensation and perception such as sensitivity, sound localization, and complex-sound recognition; neuroscientific studies of cortical function; and abnormal auditory processing.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Human Cognition
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in brain/ behavior relationships, human memory, and learning theory is presented.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Analysis of Neural Time Series
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Hands-on introduction to techniques for the analysis of neural time series data, with a primary focus on the electroencephalogram (EEG). Topics may include the physiological basis of EEG, time-frequency analysis, spatial filtering, and methods of assessing connectivity.

allCourses.title: Advanced Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Considers a range of advanced cognitive process models including models of signal detection, memory retention, category learning, stimulus representation, and reasoning using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Methodology and Models
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in cognitive sciences methodologies, concepts, and models is presented.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Human Performance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in the human issues involved with sensation, perception, and cognition.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cortical Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Physiology of the cerebral cortex, theoretical neuroscience, and the neural basis of perception.

allCourses.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: It is impossible to truly understand human behavior without some understanding of the physical structure that enables behavior. Examines recent findings in functional neuroantomy through lectures and papers discussing links between particular behaviors and specific brain structures.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Functional MRI
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Describes the fundamentals of imaging the human brain function using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI). Topics include basic fMRI physics, experimental design, and data acquisition and analysis.

allCourses.title: Computational Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computational neuroscience. Mathematical models of single neurons, neural circuits, thalamocortical systems, and cortical mass action can stimulate single-unit, local field potential, and EEG dynamics. These models are used to investigate mechanisms of sensation, motor control, attention, and consciousness.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Robotics
allCourses.description: Introduces concepts for studying cognitive function by embedding brain models on robotic platforms. Topics include robot construction, computer programming, and the notion of embodiment. Students construct simple robots and program these robots to perform different behaviors.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in cognitive neuroscience.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Sensation and Perception
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in the reception and processing of visual and auditory stimuli presented.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Cognitive Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Cognitive Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences I
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Honors students only. Psychology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.

allCourses.title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences II
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Honors students only. Psychology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.

allCourses.title: Honors Seminar in Psychology and Cognitive Sciences III
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Honors students only. Psychology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.

allCourses.title: Topics in World Literature
allCourses.description: Introduction to texts from across the globe and from different historical periods.  Readings in English and English translation.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Nations, Regions, and Beyond
allCourses.description: Intensive study of national and regional cultural and literary traditions from across the globe, among them the literary and cultural production of the Middle East, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Asia.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: An Introduction to Translation Studies
allCourses.description: Focuses on theories of translation and on how these theories help students understand the role of translation in the world. Students develop a critical vocabulary for discussing translation in multiple linguistic traditions and complete a final translation project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Working knowledge of at least one foreign language.

allCourses.title: Comparative Studies in Literature and Theory
allCourses.description: In-depth discussion of special topics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Comparative Multiculturalism
allCourses.description: Treats the literatures and cultures of one or more minority groups in California and the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicano/Latinos, and Native Americans, and their relations to other national literatures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Colonialisms and Postcolonialisms
allCourses.description: Explores topics such as colonialism and race, decolonization, pre- and postcoloniality, globalization, and the cultural dynamics of colonization and subjectivity.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Diasporic Literatures and Cultures
allCourses.description: Literatures, cultures, and histories of diasporic groups, e.g., literature of the Persian diaspora; cinema of the African diaspora.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Narrative, Pattern, and Text
allCourses.description: Explores textual patterns, structures, and effects.  May include topics such as novel, hypertext, genre, reader responses, intertextuality.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Literatures in Dialogue
allCourses.description: Studies how texts interact across time and space in a global context. Uses concepts of influence, imitation, and parody, to ask, for example, how the Homeric epics can help us understand Caribbean novels and U.S. movies such as Troy.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Gender, Sexuality, Race, Class
allCourses.description: Discusses the roles of differences such as race, class, gender, and sexuality in society, culture, and literature across the globe, covering topics such as theoretical and literary representations of queer sexuality, gender performance, critical race theory.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Psychoanalysis and Culture
allCourses.description: Discusses major psychoanalytic writings of Freud and others in connection with questions of culture.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Discourse, Ideologies, and Politics
allCourses.description: Compares ideologies and systems, e.g., nationalism and fundamentalism, as they affect literature and culture in a global context.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Critical Cultural Studies
allCourses.description: Introduces a variety of ways of understanding cultural phenomena in relation to different power structures.  These cultural phenomena may include comics, film, literature, sports, music, festivals, telling stories, or eating out.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: The Metropolis and Other Cultural Geographies
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between space and culture; cultural production in the city, suburb, and/or countryside; spaces in texts and artifacts (film, literature, comics, photographs) in a global context.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Literature, Arts, and Media
allCourses.description: Explores literature and other arts and media in a global context. May include film and electronic media, fine arts, oral cultures, architecture, in an international framework.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Literature, History, and Society
allCourses.description: Explores the relationship between literary texts and their historical and social contexts in an international framework. Courses may address, for example, literary and cultural expressions in social revolutions or the way literary texts talk back to medicine, religion, and anthropology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Literature in Translation
allCourses.description: The study of literary works in one or more genres in English translation.  May be a comparative study of works from several different original languages or a concentration on works from a single cultural/linguistic tradition.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: World Cinema
allCourses.description: Comparative analysis of contemporary film in languages other than English.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Advanced Seminar in Comparative Literature and Theory
allCourses.restriction: School of Humanities students only.
allCourses.description: Capstone seminar for the Comparative Literature major. Deepens understanding of the field through investigation of a special topic and a substantial research and writing project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Comparative Literature
allCourses.description: To be taken only when the materials to be studied lie outside the normal run of departmental offerings.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: History of Comparative Literature and Introduction to Methods and Theories of CL
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar designed to introduce graduate students in Comparative Literature to the discipline of Comparative Literature. Issues and theories of comparative literary and cultural study are covered. Strongly recommended for first and second year students before the M.A. exam and review.

allCourses.title: Theories of Translation
allCourses.description: The reproduction, translation, and transfer of literary and cultural, ideological and political, and symbolic codes and texts have long been the object of study in Comparative Literature. Addresses the diverse ways in which expressive systems interact and intersect.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Theories of Globalization, Inter-Nationalism, and Postcolonialism
allCourses.description: Addresses both theories and the complex history of literary and cultural expression in a national, trans-, inter-, and post-national, global frame. Topics may include: globalism and nationhood, theories of citizenship and political subjecthood, postcolonial literature and theory.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Comparative Studies
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Comparative Literature. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Translation Workshop
allCourses.description: Trains students in the methodologies and practice of translation.  Students focus on the translating process in a series of case studies and individual projects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Professionalization Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The first of two required professionalization seminars in Comparative Literature. Intended for second and third year students and covers preparation for the M.A. and Ph.D. exams, conference presentations, teaching and classroom management, and publishing journals.

allCourses.title: Professionalization Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The second of two required professionalization seminars in Comparative Literature. Intended for fourth and fifth year students and covers course design, applying for grants, dissertation prospectus and support, and the job application process.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COM LIT 280A. COM LIT 280A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Reading and Conference
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Guided Reading Course
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Teaching Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Graduate students develop their pedagogical practices by accompanying a professor teaching a UCI undergraduate class. Meets individually with the professor to discuss relevant pedagogical practices, syllabus design, lecturing, assessment, classroom management, etc. Actively participates in one teaching component.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A units-only course for students in the dissertation phase.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Just Reading: Developing the Reading Experience
allCourses.description: Develops the reading experience apart from writing. Develops tools for sustained attention in reading practice across a wide range of genres and media from across the globe. Students learn to appreciate elements of reading experience such as attention and perplexity.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: World Literature
allCourses.description: An introduction to the comparative study of literatures and cultures in a global context. Studies literary texts and other media across the borders of various cultures, historical periods, and traditions. All texts are read in English translation.

allCourses.title: Reading with Theory
allCourses.description: Introduction to theory and methods of literary and cultural criticism in a global context. Students read theoretical approaches to literature, culture, and ideas. Marx and Freud, e.g., may be studied alongside readings in narrative poetry, film, song lyrics, novel.

allCourses.title: Cultural Studies
allCourses.description: Introduces students to a variety of cultural practices (literature, blogs, films, radio, comics) from across the globe. Focuses on the ways that context, genre, and medium (e.g., written, visual, oral) affect how these practices are produced, circulated, and received.

allCourses.title: Travels in Comparative Literature
allCourses.description: Readings in English and in English translation on such topics as love, war, cities, travel writing, politics, fantasy and science fiction, violence.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Multiculturalism
allCourses.description: Various themes and forms of literary and cultural production within a multicultural framework, including African American, Asian American, Chicano/Latino, and Native American literatures and cultures.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Programming and Problem Solving with C++
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Advanced programming language concepts for more complex, higher performance software design. Builds depth of programming skills in C++ as a foundation for upper-division courses and projects. Focuses on strengthening programming, debugging, and problem solving skills.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Digital Image Processing
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts of digital signal and image processing as applicable in areas such as multimedia, graphics, AI, data mining, databases, vision, or video games. Topics include image representation, space- and frequency-domain transformations, filters, segmentation, and compression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46) and I&C SCI 6D and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N). I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. CSE 46 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 6D with a grade of C or better. MATH 3A with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 6N with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Graphics
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of 3D computer graphics including polygonal modeling, geometric transformations, visibility algorithms, illumination models, texturing, and rasterization. Use of an independently-learned 3D graphics API to implement these techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 46 and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N). I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. MATH 3A with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 6N with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Game Development
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the principles of interactive 2D and 3D computer game development. Concepts in computer graphics, algorithms, software engineering, art and graphics, music and sound, story analysis, and artificial intelligence are presented and are the basis for student work.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 112 or COMPSCI 171 or IN4MATX 121 or ART 106B or I&C SCI 163 or I&C SCI 166

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Projects in Advanced 3D Computer Graphics
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Projects in advanced 3D graphics such as illumination, geometric modeling, visualization, and animation. Topics include physically based and global illumination, solid modeling, curved surfaces, multiresolution modeling, image-based rendering, basic concepts of animation, and scientific visualization.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CSE 161 AND COMPSCI 112 AND COMPSCI 161 AND COMPSCI 164 AND COMPSCI 165 AND ( CSE 45C OR I&C SCI 45C )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Simulation
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discrete event-driven simulation; continuous system simulation; basic probability as pertaining to input distributions and output analysis; stochastic and deterministic simulation; static and dynamic system simulation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 AND I&C SCI 6B AND IN4MATX 43 AND ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N ) AND ( STATS 67 OR ( STATS 120A AND ( STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS ) ) ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Photography and Vision
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the problems of computer vision through the application of computational photography. Specific topics include photo-editing (image warping, compositing, hole filling), panoramic image stitching, and face detection for digital photographs.

Topics include computer graphics pipeline, human visual system and perception, head mounted displays, image formation, sensors and tracking, and 3D sound. Students use a popular cross-platform game engine to create VR environments.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Retrieval
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to information retrieval including indexing, retrieval, classifying, and clustering text and multimedia documents.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( I&C SCI 45C OR I&C SCI 45J ) AND ( STATS 7 OR STATS 67 OR AP STATISTICS )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Data Management
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for applications. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational design theory, and Structured Query Language (SQL) programming.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 33 or EECS 114. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Databases and Web Applications
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to advanced database technologies and web applications. Topics include database connectivity (ODBC/JDBC), extending databases using stored procedures, database administration, web servers, web programming languages (Java servlets, XML, Ajax, and mobile platforms).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (COMPSCI 122A or EECS 116) and (I&C SCI 45J or AP Computer Science A). AP Computer Science A with a minimum score of 4

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Data Management
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying data management systems. Content includes key techniques including storage management, buffer management, record-oriented file system, access methods, query optimization, and query processing.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Beyond SQL Data Management
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science and Engineering and all School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Survey of modern data management and analysis technologies beyond relational (SQL) database management. Topics include semistructured data, NoSQL databases, big data analysis, and text search/query engines. Additional topics vary and may include data frames, streaming data, and/or time-series data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 46 and I&C SCI 51 and (COMPSCI 122A or EECS 116)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Next Generation Search Systems
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discusses concepts and techniques related to all aspects of search systems. After considering basic search technology and the state-of-art systems, rapidly developing techniques for multimedia search, local search, event-search, and video-on-demand are explored.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"OR":["CSE 41","I&C SCI 31","I&C SCI 32A","AP COMP SCI A","AP COMP SCI AB"]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( CSE 41 OR I&C SCI 31 OR I&C SCI 32A OR AP COMP SCI A OR AP COMP SCI AB ) AND UPPER DIVISION STANDING ONLY

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Parallel and Distributed Computing
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Parallel and distributed computer systems. Parallel programming models. Common parallel and distributed programming issues. Specific topics include parallel programming, performance models, coordination and synchronization, consistency and replication, transactions, fault tolerance.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 53 and I&C SCI 53L) or COMPSCI 143A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Networks
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Computer network architectures, protocols, and applications.  Internet congestion control, addressing, and routing. Local area networks. Multimedia networking.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Computer Networks
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles in computer networks are applied to obtain practical experience and skills necessary for designing and implementing computer networks, protocols, and network applications. Various network design techniques, simulation techniques, and UNIX network programming are covered.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Network Security
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of modern computer and networks security, attacks, and countermeasures. Authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Also covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 6D and (I&C SCI 33 or CSE 43) and (COMPSCI 122A or EECS 116 or COMPSCI 132 or COMPSCI 143A)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Internet Applications Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concepts in Internet applications engineering with emphasis on the Web. Peer-to-Peer and Interoperability. Topics include HTTP and REST, Remote Procedure/Method Calls, Web Services, data representations, content distribution networks, identity management, relevant W3C/IETF standards, and relevant new large-scale computing styles.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Concepts in Programming Languages I
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: In-depth study of several contemporary programming languages stressing variety in data structures, operations, notation, and control. Examination of different programming paradigms, such as logic programming, functional programming and object-oriented programming; implementation strategies, programming environments, and programming style.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 51 or CSE 31 or EECS 31) and (I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46). I&C SCI 51 with a grade of C or better. CSE 31 with a grade of C or better. EECS 31 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. CSE 46 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Compilers and Interpreters
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory of programming language processors covering lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, code generation, optimization, interpretation, and run-time support.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Language Processor Construction
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Project course which provides working laboratory experience in construction and behavior of compilers and interpreters. Students build actual language processors and perform experiments which reveal their behaviors.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Operating Systems
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles and concepts of process and resource management, especially as seen in operating systems. Processes, memory management, protection, scheduling, file systems, and I/O systems are covered. Concepts illustrated in the context of several well-known systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46) and (I&C SCI 51 or EECS 31 or CSE 31)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Operating System Organization
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Detailed specification and design of critical components of an actual operating system including a memory manager, a process server, and a file/IO subsystem. Hardware/software tradeoffs. Emphasis on logical organization of system and communication.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Embedded Software
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of embedded computing systems: embedded systems architecture, hardware/software components, system software and interfacing, real-time operating systems, hardware/software co-development, and communication issues. Examples of embedded computing in real-world application domains. Simple programming using an embedded systems development environment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CSE 46 or I&C SCI 46) and (I&C SCI 51 or EECS 31 or CSE 31)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Embedded Software Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory section to accompany COMPSCI 145.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Programming in Multitasking Operating Systems
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: User- and systems-level programming of modern Internet-connected, multi-user, multitasking operating systems. Shells, scripting, filters, pipelines, programmability, extensibility, concurrency, inter-process communication. Concrete examples of a modern operating system (such as, but not necessarily, Unix programmed in C) are used.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 AND COMPSCI 143A AND ( CSE 46 OR I&C SCI 46 )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Internet of Things (IoT) Software and Systems
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the Internet of Things (IoT) from a systems and software perspective. IoT ecosystem including sensors, embedded CPUs, networking protocols, software, cloud services, and security and privacy requirements. IoT use cases, system design, and programming project.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Digital Logic Design
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Boolean algebra. Design/analysis of combinational and sequential systems using SSI/MSI/LSI modules. Number systems. Error detecting and correction codes. Arithmetic algorithms. Hardware/ firmware implementation of algorithms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 33 or CSE 43) and I&C SCI 51 and I&C SCI 6B and I&C SCI 6D. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better. CSE 43 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 51 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Systems Architecture
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design of computer elements; ALU, control unit, and arithmetic circuits. Memory hierarchy and organization. Caches. Function unit sharing and pipelining. I/O and interrupt processing. RTL and behavioral modeling using hardware description languages. Microprocessor organization and implementation techniques.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Logic Design Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to standard integrated circuits. Construction and debugging techniques. Design of digital systems using LSI and MSI components. Practical use of circuits in a laboratory environment, including implementation of small digital systems such as arithmetic modules, displays, and timers.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Design Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Underlying primitives of computer instruction sets. Principles of microprogramming. Microprogramming. Microprograms written for one or more systems. Typical microprogramming applications discussed and implemented or simulated.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Software Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Data Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Management, Computer Game Science, and Informatics majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Techniques for efficient algorithm design, including divide-and-conquer and dynamic programming, and time/space analysis. Fast algorithms for problems applicable to networks, computer games, and scientific computing, such as sorting, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, network flow, and pattern matching.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 6B AND I&C SCI 6D AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( CSE 46 OR I&C SCI 46 ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Formal Languages and Automata
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Language Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Formal aspects of describing and recognizing languages by grammars and automata.  Parsing regular and context-free languages. Ambiguity, nondeterminism. Elements of computability; Turning machines, random access machines, undecidable problems, NP-completeness.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 6B AND I&C SCI 6D AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( CSE 46 OR I&C SCI 46 )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Graph  Algorithms
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Algorithms for solving fundamental problems in graph theory. Graph representations, graph traversal, network flow, connectivity, graph layout, matching problems.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Geometry and Geometric Modeling
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Algorithms and data structures for computational geometry and geometric modeling, with applications to game and graphics programming. Topics: convex hulls, Voronoi diagrams, algorithms for triangulation, motion planning, and data structures for geometric searching and modeling of 2D and 3D objects.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46. I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. CSE 46 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Algorithms and Data Structures
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science and Engineering majors and all School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Design, implementation, execution, and analysis of algorithms for problems such as sorting, searching, data compression, and data encryption. Time-space-structure trade-offs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CSE 45C AND I&C SCI 45C AND ( CSE 161 OR COMPSCI 161 )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Quantum Computation and Information
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic models for quantum computation and their foundations in quantum mechanics. Quantum complexity classes and quantum algorithms, including algorithms for factoring and quantum simulation. Introduction to quantum information theory and quantum entanglement.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A) and (COMPSCI 161 or PHYSICS 113A). I&C SCI 6N with a grade of C+ or better. MATH 3A with a grade of C+ or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Applied Cryptography
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the essential aspects of applied cryptography, as it is used in practice. Topics include classical cryptography, block ciphers, stream ciphers, public-key cryptography, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, basic cryptographic protocols, and digital certificates and credentials.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Optimization
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A broad introduction to optimization. Unconstrained and constrained optimization. Equality and inequality constraints. Linear and integer programming. Stochastic dynamic programming.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N ) AND ( STATS 67 OR ( STATS 120A AND ( STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS ) ) ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Different means of representing knowledge and uses of representations in heuristic problem solving. Representations considered include predicate logic, semantic nets, procedural representations, natural language grammars, and search trees.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( CSE 46 OR I&C SCI 46 ) AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( STATS 67 OR ( STATS 120A AND ( STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS ) ) ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
