allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Neural network and deep learning from multiple perspectives. Theory of parallel distributed processing systems, algorithmic approaches for learning from data in various manners, applications to difficult problems in AI from computer vision, to natural language understanding, to bioinformatics and chemoinformatics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (STATS 120A and STATS 120B) or MATH 121A or COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Artificial Intelligence Frontiers: Technical, Ethical, and Societal
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the frontiers of artificial intelligence and related technologies with a focus on the underlying ethical, legal, and societal challenges and opportunities they create. Encourages critical thinking about these issues.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Artificial Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Construction of a working artificial intelligence system. Evaluation of capabilities of the system including impact of knowledge representation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applications of Probability in Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of probability to real-world problems in computer science. Typical topics include analysis of algorithms and graphs, probabilistic language models, network traffic modeling, data compression, and reliability modeling.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: STATS 67 AND I&C SCI 6B AND I&C SCI 6D AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Machine Learning and Data-Mining
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and data-mining applied to real-world datasets. Typical applications include spam filtering, object recognition, and credit scoring.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND":["I&C SCI 6B","I&C SCI 6D",{"OR":["MATH 3A","I&C SCI 6N"]},{"OR":["MATH 2B","AP CALCULUS BC"]},{"OR":["STATS 67",{"AND":["STATS 120A",{"OR":["STATS 7","AP STATISTICS"]}]}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 6B AND I&C SCI 6D AND ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N ) AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( STATS 67 OR ( STATS 120A AND ( STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS ) ) ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Algorithms for Probabilistic and Deterministic Graphical Models
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Graphical model techniques dealing with probabilistic and deterministic knowledge representations. Focuses on graphical models such as constraint networks, Bayesian networks, and Markov networks that have become a central paradigm for knowledge representation and reasoning in AI and general computer science.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students to solve a substantial real-world problem with knowledge gained from many areas in computer science. Project has a focus on computer science but can overlap with neighbor disciplines.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students to solve a substantial real-world problem with knowledge gained from many areas in computer science. Project has a focus on computer science but can overlap with neighbor disciplines.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
allCourses.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computational methods in molecular biology, aimed at those interested in learning about this interdisciplinary area. Covers computational approaches to understanding and predicting the structure, function, interactions, and evolution of DNA, RNA, proteins, and related molecules and processes.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Systems Biology
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Computational inference and modeling of gene regulation networks, signal transduction pathways, and the effects of regulatory networks in cellular processes, development, and disease. Introduction of required mathematical, computational, and data handling tools.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Information and Computer Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 AND ( EECS 116 OR COMPSCI 122A ) AND ( CSE 46 OR I&C SCI 46 )
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation with Computer Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Computer Science Research
allCourses.description: Graduate colloquium series. Includes weekly talks by notable computer scientists.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Foundations of Cryptographic Protocols
allCourses.description: Explores fundamental cryptographic tools, including encryption, signatures, and identification schemes. Students are introduced to the provable security paradigm of modern cryptography, focusing on understanding of security properties provided by cryptographic tools, and on proving security (or insecurity) of cryptographic constructions.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Security
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computer security, including systems, technology, and management. Topics include authorization, authentication, data integrity, malware, operating systems security, network security, web security, and basic cryptography.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Knowledge of Python or C++ programming is required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Cryptography
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of algorithms for applied cryptography. Topics include symmetric and asymmetric key encryption, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, digital certificates and credentials, and techniques for authorization, non-repudiation, authentication, identification, data integrity, proofs of knowledge, and access control.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Cryptography
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of algorithms for applied cryptography. Topics include symmetric and asymmetric key encryption, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, digital certificates and credentials, and techniques for authorization, non-repudiation, authentication, identification, data integrity, proofs of knowledge, and access control.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
allCourses.description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network Security
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to network security, including network threats and attacks, as well as defenses against such attacks. Topics include network infrastructure security, mobile and Wi-Fi security, spam, phishing, firewalls, anonymity, secure email, secure and private cloud computing, and web security.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Systems Security
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lecture and discuss latest security research in software, OS, protocols, mobile devices, machine learning, sensors, and emerging IoT/CPS systems such as smart home and smart transportation. Students perform research projects and gain hands-on experience evaluating and designing secure systems.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Scientific Computing
allCourses.description: Overview of widely used principles and methods of numerical and scientific computing, including basic concepts and computational methods in linear algebra, optimization, and probability.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic courses in multivariate calculus, linear algebra, and probability.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Scientific Computing
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of widely used principles and methods of numerical and scientific computing, including basic concepts and computational methods in floating-point, linear algebra, optimization, simulation, modeling, and probability/statistics as it relates to model evaluation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic knowledge of multivariate calculus, linear algebra, and familiarity with MATLAB.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Graphics and Visualization
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Interactive 3D graphics rendering pipeline, illumination and shading, ray tracing, texture-, bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing, multiresolution representations, volume rendering techniques, iso-surface extraction.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Familiarity with linear algebra is required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Visual Computing
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of image processing (convolution, linear filters, spectral analysis), vision geometry (projective geometry, camera models and calibration, stereo reconstruction), radiometry (color, shading, illumination, BRDF), and visual content synthesis (graphics pipeline, texture- bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing).

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Graphics and Visualization
allCourses.description: Interactive 3D graphics rendering pipeline,  illumination and shading, ray tracing,  texture-, bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing,  multiresolution representations, volume rendering techniques, iso-surface extraction.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Realistic Image Synthesis
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an in-depth overview on a core sub-field of computer graphics. Graduate  students who take this course are better prepared for conducting research on the related topics in computer graphics, vision, and scientific computing.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multimedia Systems and Applications
allCourses.description: Organization and structure of modern multimedia systems; audio and video encoding/compression; quality of service concepts; scheduling algorithms for multimedia; resource management in distributed and multimedia systems; multimedia protocols over high-speed networks; synchronization schemes; multimedia applications; and teleservices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 131 AND COMPSCI 132 AND COMPSCI 133 AND COMPSCI 161 AND COMPSCI 143A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Visual Perception
allCourses.description: Introduction to the process of human visual perception. Offers the physiological and psychophysical approach to understand vision, introducing concepts of perception of color, depth, movement. Examples of quantification and application of these models in computer vision, computer graphics, multimedia, HCI.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Image Understanding
allCourses.description: The goal of image understanding is to extract useful semantic information from image data. Course covers low-level image and video processing techniques, feature descriptors, segmentation, objection recognition, and tracking.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B AND I&C SCI 6D AND ( CSE 46 OR I&C SCI 46 ) AND ( MATH 3A OR MATH 6G OR I&C SCI 6N )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Light and Geometry in Computer Vision
allCourses.description: Examines the issues of light transport and multiview geometry in computer vision. Applications include camera calibration, 3D understanding, stereo reconstruction, and illumination estimation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 46 AND I&C SCI 6D AND COMPSCI 211A AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( MATH 3A OR MATH 6G OR I&C SCI 6N )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Graphics and Visualization
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research and research trends in computer graphics, visualization, virtual/augmented reality, and other visual computing topics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Databases and Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for managing and utilizing data. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational schema design, and use of SQL (Structured Query Language).

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Retrieval, Filtering, and Classification
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Algorithms for the storage, retrieval, filtering, and classification of textual and multimedia data. The vector space model, Boolean and probabilistic queries, and relevance feedback. Latent semantic indexing; collaborative filtering; and relationship to machine learning methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 161 and COMPSCI 171 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Data Management
allCourses.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying data management systems. Content includes key techniques including storage management, buffer management, record-oriented file system, access methods, query optimization, and query processing.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying data management systems. Understanding and implementation of key techniques including storage management, buffer management, record-oriented file system, access methods, query optimization, and query processing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: C++ programming skills, understanding of data structures and algorithms.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Transaction Processing and Distributed Data Management
allCourses.description: Covers fundamental principles underlying transaction processing including database consistency, concurrency control, database recovery, and fault-tolerance. Includes transaction processing in centralized, distributed, parallel, and client-server environments.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Transaction Processing and Distributed Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamental principles underlying transaction processing systems including database consistency, atomicity, concurrency control, database recovery, replication, commit protocols, and fault-tolerance. Includes transaction processing in centralized, distributed, parallel, and client-server environments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 222P or COMPSCI 222. COMPSCI 222P with a grade of B or better. COMPSCI 222 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Big Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on Big Data management frameworks such as Hadoop and Spark. Also covers relational and non-relational database technologies, including document (“NoSQL”) databases as well as emerging cloud data management solutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 220P or COMPSCI 122A. COMPSCI 220P with a grade of B or better. COMPSCI 122A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Next Generation Search Systems
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses concepts and techniques related to all aspects of search systems. After considering basic search technology and the state-of-art systems, rapidly developing techniques for multimedia search, local search, event-search, and video-on-demand are explored.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 21 or CSE 21 or IN4MATX 41 or I&C SCI 31 or CSE 41

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Distributed Computer Systems
allCourses.description: Principles of distributed computing systems. Topics covered include message-passing, remote procedure calls, distributed shared memory synchronization, resource and process/thread management, distributed file systems, naming and security.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Distributed Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of distributed computing systems. Topics covered include message-passing, remote procedure calls, distributed shared memory synchronization, resource and process/thread management, distributed file systems, naming and security.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Parallel and Distributed Computing for Professionals
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers a wide variety of concepts related to the design and application of high-performance concurrent computing systems, including architectural features, communications networks and models, parallel program development for numerical and non-numerical applications, programming models, and more.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Communication Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Communication Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Internet architecture, protocols, and services. Advanced concepts of IP and TCP, including addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, and implementations of flow and congestion control. Internet services such as Network Address Translation and Domain Name Servers. Overview of Local Area Networks.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Networking Laboratory
allCourses.description: A laboratory-based introduction to basic networking concepts such as addressing, sub-netting, bridging, ARP, and routing. Network simulation and design. Structured around weekly readings and laboratory assignments.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Networks
allCourses.description: Design principles of networked systems, advanced routing and congestion control algorithms, network algorithms, network measurement, management, security, Internet economics, and emerging networks.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NET SYS 201 or COMPSCI 232 or EECS 248A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Wireless and Mobile Networking
allCourses.description: Introduction to wireless networking. The focus is on layers 2 and 3 of the OSI reference model, design, performance analysis, and protocols. Topics covered include: an introduction to wireless networking, digital cellular, next generation cellular, wireless LANs, and mobile IP.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Middleware for Networked and Distributed Systems
allCourses.description: Discusses concepts, techniques, and issues in developing distributed systems middleware that provides high performance and Quality of Service for emerging applications. Also covers existing standards (e.g., CORBA, DCOM, Jini, Espeak) and their relative advantages and shortcomings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: An undergraduate-level course in operating systems and networks.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Operating Systems
allCourses.description: Focuses on advanced and graduate-level topics in operating systems. Presents important recent developments in operating systems, topics not covered in undergraduate operating systems courses. This includes novel operating system designs and techniques to improve existing ones.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Operating Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In-depth organization of the core operating system abstraction and its implementation (virtual memory, kernel and user mode, system calls, threads, context switches, interrupts, inter-process communication, hardware interface, etc.) and a range of recent developments in de-facto industry standard operating systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Working knowledge of C and the Linux environment.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Compiler Construction
allCourses.description: Advanced study of programming language implementation techniques: optimizations such as common sub-expression elimination, register allocation, and instruction scheduling. Implementation of language features such as type-directed dispatch, garbage collection, dynamic linking, and just-in-time code generation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Parallel Computing
allCourses.description: Definition of parallel processing systems. Theory and application of arrays, trees, and hypercubes. Computational models, applications: sorting, integer arithmetic, matrix operations, Fast Fourier Transform, and others. Interconnection networks: a framework for the description, analysis, and construction of hypercube-derived networks.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Compilers and Interpreters
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides in-depth study of compilers and interpreters which are the primary forms of programming language processing in computing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Knowledge of C++ programming is required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: High-Performance Architectures and Their Compilers
allCourses.description: Emphasis on the development of automatic tools (i.e., compilers/environments) for the efficient exploitation of parallel machines, and the trade-offs between hardware and software in the design of supercomputing and high-performance machines.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Embedded and Ubiquitous Systems
allCourses.description: Embedded and ubiquitous system technologies including processors, DSP, memory, and software. System interfacing basics; communication strategies; sensors and actuators, mobile and wireless technology. Using pre-designed hardware and software components. Design case studies in wireless, multimedia, and/or networking domains.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 and COMPSCI 152 and COMPSCI 161 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G or I&C SCI 6D). B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Internet of Things
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develops a comprehensive understanding of the hardware and software technology, the communication protocols, and the security and privacy requirements underlying the Internet of Things ecosystem, particularly those using computing elements (processors, DSPs/ ASIPs), sensors, and accessing cloud services.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level familiarity with fundamentals of integrated circuit blocks, processors, optimization/algorithm design, and some programming experience.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software for Embedded Systems
allCourses.description: Embedded computing elements, device interfaces, time-critical IO handling. Embedded software design under size, performance, and reliability constraints. Software timing and functional validation. Programming methods and compilation for embeddable software. Embedded runtime systems. Case studies of real-time software systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 and COMPSCI 152 and COMPSCI 161 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G or I&C SCI 6D). B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Complex Software Systems: Project Course
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Building complex systems software systems, such as Database Management Systems, Operating Systems, and Optimizing Compilers. Such systems often involve low-level programming and intricate performance optimizations. Students learn how to build such a system.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Ubiquitous Computing
allCourses.description: The "disappearing computer" paradigm. Differences to the desktop computing model: applications, interaction in augmented environments, security, alternate media, small operating systems, sensors, and embedded systems design. Evaluation by project work and class participation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Ubiquitous Computing and Interaction
allCourses.description: Principles and design techniques for ubiquitous computing applications. Conceptual basis for tangible and embodied interaction. Interaction in virtual and augmented environments. Design methods and techniques. Design case studies. Examination by project work.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Systems Architecture
allCourses.description: Study of architectural issues and their relation to technology and software: design of processor, interconnections, and memory hierarchies.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Modern Computer Systems
allCourses.description: Fundamental concepts and recent advances in computer systems architecture necessary to achieve high performance and efficiency on systems available today. Topics span modern processor features, accelerators, storage and network architectures, as well as architecture-optimized software.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Systems Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of architectural issues and their relation to technology and software: design of processor, interconnections, and memory hierarchies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level familiarity with fundamentals of integrated circuit blocks, processors, and optimization/algorithm design, and some programming experience.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computer Design
allCourses.description: The methodology and use of CAD tools for computer design, accomplished by a lab in which students practice design using commercially available silicon compilers and other tools.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Analysis of Programming Languages
allCourses.description: Concepts in modern programming languages, their interaction, and the relationship between programming languages and methods for large-scale, extensible software development. Empirical analysis of programming language usage.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Programming and Problem Solving
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides in-depth preparation for industry interviews requiring demonstration of problem solving and programming skills. Emphasis is on understanding problem statements, considering edge cases, developing effective test cases, designing correct solutions, explaining these clearly, and implementing a solution correctly.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Systems and Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Course is divided into two parts. The first half covers recent research in systems for machine learning (ML) that enabled rapid progress in ML/AI. The second half revolves around application of machine learning in systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: An undergraduate machine-learning course and an undergraduate course in one of the following areas: networking, distributed systems, or operating systems.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Design Science
allCourses.description: Current research and research trends in design science. Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 18 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of the Design and Analysis of Algorithms
allCourses.description: Covers fundamental concepts in the design and analysis of algorithms and is geared toward non-specialists in theoretical computer science. Topics include: deterministic and randomized graph algorithms, fundamental algorithmic techniques like divide-and-conquer strategies and dynamic programming, and NP-completeness.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Algorithms with Applications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers fundamental concepts in the design and analysis of algorithms and is geared toward practical application and implementation. Topics include greedy algorithms, deterministic and randomized graph algorithms, models of network flow, fundamental algorithmic techniques, and NP-completeness.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Data Structures
allCourses.description: An in-depth treatment of data structures and their associated management algorithms including resource complexity analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Data Structures with Applications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Data structures and their associated management algorithms, including their applications and analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Complexity
allCourses.description: Advanced course in computational models and complexity classes. Covers the fundamentals of Turing Machines, Decidability, and NP-completeness. Includes discussion of more advanced topics including polynomial hierarchy, randomized complexity classes, #P-completeness and hardness of approximation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Text Processing and Pattern Matching
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Techniques for pattern matching and parsing character strings. Topics include substring searching, finite state machines, regular expressions, and context-free grammars, as well as applications in lexical analyzers, compilers, word processors, malware detectors, and search engines.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Analysis of Algorithms
allCourses.description: Analysis of correctness and complexity of various efficient algorithms; discussion of problems for which no efficient solutions are known.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Quantum Computation and Information
allCourses.description: Basic models for quantum computation and their foundations in quantum mechanics. Quantum complexity classes and quantum algorithms, including algorithms for factoring and quantum simulation. Introduction to quantum information theory and quantum entanglement.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic courses in linear algebra and algorithms.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Graph Algorithms
allCourses.description: Graph definitions, representation methods, graph problems, algorithms, approximation methods, and applications.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Geometry
allCourses.description: An overview of some of the basic problems in computational geometry and of some algorithmic and data-structuring techniques appropriate to their solution.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Data Compression
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the theory and practice of modern data compression techniques. Topics include codes, coding, modeling, text compression, lossless and lossy image compression standards and systems, audio compression.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Optimization
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A broad introduction to optimization. Unconstrained and constrained optimization. Equality and inequality constraints. Linear and integer programming. Stochastic dynamic programming.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N ) AND ( STATS 67 OR ( STATS 120A AND ( STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS ) ) )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Optimization Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A broad introduction to optimization methods and their applications. Unconstrained and constrained optimization. Direct, first, and second order methods. Use of optimization software libraries. Equality and inequality constraints, optimal conditions, and methods. Applications to modeling in computer science, engineering.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in the Theory of Algorithms and Data Structures
allCourses.description: Current research and research trends in the Theory of algorithms and data structures.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 18 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
allCourses.description: The study of theories and computational models for systems which behave and act in an intelligent manner. Fundamental subdisciplines of artificial intelligence including knowledge representation, search, deduction, planning, probabilistic reasoning, natural language parsing and comprehension, knowledge-based systems, and learning.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Artificial Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The study of theories and computational models for systems which behave and act in an intelligent manner. Fundamental sub-disciplines of artificial intelligence, including knowledge representation, search, deduction, planning, probabilistic reasoning, natural language parsing and comprehension, knowledge-based systems, and learning.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Statistical Natural Language Processing
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistical models, machine learning algorithms, and computational tasks involved in natural language processing. Focuses on approaches that learn these models from data, and covers applications such as information extraction, dialog systems, machine translation, and question answering.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Machine Learning
allCourses.description: Computational approaches to learning algorithms for classifications, regression, and clustering. Emphasis is on discriminative classification methods such as decision trees, rules, nearest neighbor, linear models, and naive Bayes.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and data-mining. Learning algorithms for classifications, regression, and clustering. Emphasis is on discriminative classification methods such as decision trees, rules, nearest neighbor, linear models, and naive Bayes.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Probablistic Learning: Theory and Algorithms
allCourses.description: An introduction to probabilistic and statistical techniques for learning from data, including parameter estimation, density estimation, regression, classification, and mixture modeling.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Learning in Graphical Models
allCourses.description: Models for data analysis are presented in the unifying framework of graphical models. The emphasis is on learning from data but inference is also covered. Real world examples are used to illustrate the material.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
allCourses.description: Neural network and deep learning from multiple perspectives. Theory of parallel distributed processing systems, algorithmic approaches for learning from data in various manners, applications to difficult problems in AI from computer vision, to natural language understanding, to bioinformatics and chemoinformatics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (STATS 120A and STATS 120B) or MATH 121A or COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A
allCourses.overlap: COMPSCI 274A, COMPSCI 277, COMPSCI 276, COMPSCI 278, COMPSCI 274B, COMPSCI 273A.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Artificial Intelligence Frontiers: Technical, Ethical, and Societal
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the frontiers of artificial intelligence and related technologies with a focus on the underlying ethical, legal, and societal challenges and opportunities they create.  Encourages critical thinking about these issues.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Deep Generative Models
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses probabilistic approaches to deep learning such as generative models and their applications in computer vision, NLP, the natural sciences, and other fields. Coursework may include both homework and project components.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A or STATS 120B. Recommended: Advanced machine learning or graphical models courses such as COMPSCI 274A or COMPSCI 274B or CS 273C or COMPSCI 276.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and neural networks. Architecture design. Feedforward and recurrent networks. Learning models and algorithms.  Applications to data analysis and prediction problems in areas such as machine vision, natural language processing, biomed, and finance.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 271P. COMPSCI 271P with a grade of B or better. Required: Knowledge of Python programming.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network-Based Reasoning/Constraint Networks
allCourses.description: Study of the theory and techniques of constraint network model. Covers techniques for solving constraint satisfaction problems: backtracking techniques, consistency algorithms, and structure-based techniques. Tractable subclasses. Extensions into applications such as temporal reasoning, diagnosis, and scheduling.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic course in algorithm design and analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Graphical Models and Statistical Learning
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of statistical machine learning with probabilistic graphical models. Studies efficient inference algorithms based on optimization-based variational methods, and simulation-based Monte Carlo methods. Several approaches to learning from data are covered.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Reasoning in Probabilistic Graphical Models
allCourses.description: Focuses on algorithms for probabilistic reasoning using graphical models such as Bayesian Networks and Markov Networks that encode knowledge as local probabilistic relations. Tasks include finding most likely scenarios over a subset of variables, or updating posterior probability, given observations.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Control and Reinforcement Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to learning agents that make sequences of decisions to interact with a system and control it. The main focus is reinforcement learning from a reward signal, with emphasis on algorithms that can learn differentiable policy parametrizations (Deep Reinforcement Learning).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 178 or COMPSCI 273A. Recommended: COMPSCI 274A and CS 275B and CS 275C and COMPSCI 276.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Probability Models
allCourses.description: Advanced probability, discrete time Markov chains, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains. Queuing or simulation as time permits.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine
allCourses.description: Introduction to computational methods in molecular biology, aimed at those interested in learning about this interdisciplinary area. Covers computational approaches to understanding and predicting the structure, function, interactions, and evolution of DNA, RNA, proteins, and related molecules and processes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: A Basic course in algorithms or a basic course in molecular biology.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Systems Biology
allCourses.description: Computational inference and modeling of gene regulation networks, signal transduction pathways, and the effects of regulatory networks in cellular processes, development, and disease. Introduction of required mathematical, computational, and data handling tools.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Mathematical and Computational Biology
allCourses.description: Analytical and numerical methods for dynamical systems, temporal-spatial dynamics, steady state, stability, stochasticity. Application to life sciences: genetics, tissue growth and patterning, cancers, ion channels gating, signaling networks, morphogen gradients. Probabilistic methods.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Algorithms for Matching Markets
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses algorithms underlying matching markets, drawing ideas from CS theory, economics, and game-theory. Topics include Gale-Shapley stable-matching algorithm, its incentive compatibility and LP formulation; online bipartite matching and Adwords market; one-sided matching markets; and market equilibria.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: COMPSCI 263 and COMPSCI 295 (when the topic title is Game Theory), or a course on linear programming, or working knowledge of LP-duality theory.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Keystone Professional Writing and Communication for Computer Science Careers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Well-developed written and oral communication skills relevant to computer science professionals including oral presentations, short descriptive writing assignments, and one longer writing assignment related to a research replication project.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Information and Computer Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Keystone Project for Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and development of a software system or a hardware component of a system based on knowledge of advanced computer science principles. Students implement at least a working prototype and test this using relevant input data.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Elements of Scientific Writing
allCourses.description: Introduces the concepts and principles of good scientific writing, demonstrates them by examples drawn from the literature, and uses a hands-on approach to apply them to documents being written by the participants.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Professional Writing and Communication for Computer Science Careers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Written and oral communication for computer science and IT careers. Production of the detailed design and development document for the concurrent capstone design class and refinement of written documents and oral communications skills needed for a successful job search.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Design Project for Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and development of app, software system, or hardware component of system based on students' prior knowledge of advanced computer science principles. Implement at least a working prototype and test this using relevant use cases and/or input data.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Thesis Supervision
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. School of Information and Computer Science majors only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Science Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Internship in which students work individually at an outside organization to gain experience with the challenges involved in technology-related work.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. School of Information and Computer Science majors only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation with Computer Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Supervised individual study in computer science.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Research
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only. Bren School of ICS Honors students only. Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Directed independent research in computer science for honors students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Political Economy: Methods and Critique
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to canonical texts in Marxism coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken after CLT&THY 200B.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Criminology, Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces three interdisciplinary literatures: criminology, socio-legal studies, and justice studies. Focuses on theoretical and empirical work addressing law making, law breaking, and legal systems.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Criminology, Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: American Law
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to substantive and procedural law governing private dispute resolution, including common law (tort, property, contracts), lawsuits (civil procedure), and alternative dispute resolution; emphasis on the socio-legal ramifications of private disputes, particularly the modern tort system and tort reform movement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Comparative Study of Legal Cultures
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Traces the anthropological and comparative cultural study of law from the nineteenth century to the present; briefly surveys the diversity of recorded legal cultures and critically examines key concepts which have been used to describe and classify them.

allCourses.title: US Legal Thought
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Evolution of legal thought in socio-historical context from 19th century to present; emphasizes the rise and fall of legal classicism and modern socio-legal critiques, including the law and society movement, critical legal studies, feminist legal theory, and critical race studies.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Law
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines law creation and law enforcement in their social and political context. Discusses the major theories of law and the modern state, and presents case studies in order to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of these theoretical perspectives.

allCourses.title: Psychology and the Law
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Psychological assumptions of the American legal system and mental health aspects of provision of criminal justice services. Civil commitment, insanity defense, competence to stand trial, jury selection, eyewitness identification. Use of police, courts, correctional institutions in prevention of behavior disorder.

allCourses.title: Crime and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores nature and dimensions of crime in America and uses and limits of various strategies to control it. Topics include growth of imprisonment, the problem of domestic violence, the death penalty, gun control, and the potential of crime prevention programs.

allCourses.title: Deviance
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.

allCourses.title: Criminological Theory
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the question of crime causation from a number of theoretical perspectives in the social sciences. Schools of thought examined include utilitarianism, positivism, human ecology, social structural approaches, social process (learning) theories, labeling, and radical-critical (political) perspectives.

allCourses.title: Juvenile Delinquency
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Patterns of delinquent behavior, theories that explain behavior, current research aimed at enhancing exploratory power. Attempts to prevent and control delinquency are put in historical perspective. Development of the current juvenile justice system and evolution of modern juvenile law.

allCourses.title: Community Context of Crime
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the social context of high-crime communities, with special emphasis on the problems of poverty, joblessness, economic inequality, and racial discrimination. Assesses debates on the causes of these problems, and on the most effective policies to combat them.

allCourses.title: Theories of Punishment
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Survey of the various schools of thought regarding formal punishment theory. The purposes of legal sanctions are examined, including those of deterrence, rehabilitation, retribution, and incapacitation. Considers problems in realizing formal goals of punishment in practice.

allCourses.title: Legal Sanctions and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of criminal sanctions as mechanisms of social control. Includes the nature, function, and organization of courts as sanction generating institutions, and problems associated with punishing white-collar and corporate illegalities.

allCourses.title: Gender and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the legal system's use of sex as an organizing characteristic, focusing particularly on sameness and difference feminism, and tracing the evolution of equal treatment of men and women in the areas of constitutional rights, employment, education, and military service.

allCourses.title: Miscarriages of Justice
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Systematically describes, explains, and analyzes the causes and consequences of the wrongful accusation, prosecution, incarceration, and sometimes even execution, of the innocent in the American criminal justice system.

allCourses.title: Prisons, Punishment, and Corrections
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A review of how the U.S. punishes and rehabilitates convicted law violators. The conflicts among the major purposes of sentencing—rehabilitation, deterrence, incapacitation—are discussed, as well as the effects of different sanctions on public safety, offender rehabilitation, and justice system costs.

allCourses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and sociological survey of racial and ethnic group relations in contexts of crime control, emphasizing the roles of racial ideology, structural racism, and social movements in shaping these dynamic relations, and their significance to American liberal democracy.

allCourses.title: Imprisonment and Reentry
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of imprisonment and reentry in the contemporary United States. Examines the development of the prison in the United States and explores changes in its composition, structure, and purpose over time.

allCourses.title: Domestic Violence
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: General perspectives about domestic violence and theoretical accounts about what causes such behavior.

allCourses.title: Violence in Intimate Relationships
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Responses to various forms of domestic violence, such as intimate partner violence and child abuse. Covers barriers to reporting to the police, and prosecutors and courts. Human services, such as safety planning for victims, treatment programs, and restorative justice approaches.

allCourses.title: Law and Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Various aspects of the law as related to three specific areas of inequality: immigration and immigrants, race, and gender. The role of law as a tool of social reform and limitations of the legal system historically in resolving inequality issues.

allCourses.title: Constitutional Law
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the evolution of civil liberties and individual rights in the United States, focusing on how Constitutional Amendments and U.S. Supreme Court decision-making have shaped the ongoing political and legal struggles over issues such as privacy, abortion, and free speech.

allCourses.title: Family Law
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines legal issues surrounding marriage, cohabitation, divorce, child custody and support, adoption, and the rights of parents and children in the family context. The findings of social science research are used to illuminate the legal issues.

allCourses.title: Mental Health and the Justice System
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the history of criminalization of persons with mental illness; challenges and needs; civil and outpatient commitment; law enforcement responses; mentally ill in jails and prisons; community supervision strategies; and reentry strategies for offenders with mental illness.

allCourses.title: Drugs, Crime, and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Implementation of drug crime policy in the U.S.; historical views of U.S. social control and crime policies. Students critically examine drugs and crime research and policy, with attention to causal rigor and how policies interact with and affect socioeconomic conditions.

allCourses.title: Hate Crimes
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the causes, manifestations, and consequences of hate crimes and the larger social context within which they occur. The politics and dynamics of intergroup violence born of bigotry and manifested as discrimination; social policy designed to control bias-motivated violence.

allCourses.title: Environmental Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors only. Urban Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Environmental law as a combination of traditional legal principles and newly created statutes, rules, and decisions applied to environmental protection. Investigates roles of courts, legislature, executive branch and administrative agencies, and private citizens attempting to regulate environmental quality.

allCourses.title: Seminar on Gangs
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of gangs, including the nature and definition of gangs; types of gangs; diversity of membership; theoretical explanations; criminal behavior; drug use and sales; law enforcement responses; gangs in correctional institutions; intervention and prevention strategies; and public policy issues.

allCourses.title: Organized Crime and American Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of the phenomenon of American organized crime from a sociological perspective. Explanation of methods by which organized crime is tolerated at various levels of society. Emphasis on ways in which "underworld" interests interact with legitimate economic and political institutions.

allCourses.title: Forensic Science, Law, and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines use of "forensic science" to resolve issues arising in criminal cases including crime scene analysis, DNA testing, fingerprints, trace evidence comparisons, profiling, lie detectors, other forensic techniques; evaluation, statistical characterization, and legal admissibility of evidence; regulation of forensic laboratories.

allCourses.title: Homicide and Suicide
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines similarities and differences among homicide and suicide, two major causes of death.

allCourses.title: Victimless Crimes
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines major theoretical, empirical, and policy-oriented research related to the design, implementation, and analysis of government intervention, through the criminal sanction, in the spheres of vice and morality.

allCourses.title: Mass Incarceration and Social Inequality in America
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the origins and consequences of mass incarceration; extraordinarily high incarceration rates within particular demographic groups above and beyond historical levels in the U.S. Theoretical explanations for, and current policy debates around, mass incarceration are covered.

allCourses.title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C) and PSCI 102C and (PSCI 178S or CRM/LAW C149)

allCourses.title: Media Effects on Law and Justice
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines theoretical and methodological frameworks necessary for understanding mass media effects. Trains students to analyze and create media content that cover a wide array of law and justice topics, such as criminal trial procedures, coerced confessions, and mass incarceration.

allCourses.title: Police and Change
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Organizational efforts to modify police conduct are addressed by focusing on the history of policing in the United States including training, education, and the contributions of women.

allCourses.title: Surveillance and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores the development and deployment of surveillance technologies in contemporary society. The social and legal impact of surveillance technologies, in such areas as crime control, privacy, trust, community, democracy, and the war on terror.

allCourses.title: Anthropology of Law
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the anthropological study of law through a focus on the foundations of this subfield, its primary methodologies, and several important topics of inquiry, including policing, immigration, and structural inequalities. Provides an international perspective on law and society.

allCourses.title: White-Collar Crime
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines criminal activity in business and corporate enterprise, organizations, and the professions. Theories regarding the causes and control of white-collar and corporate crime are covered as well as the numerous definitions of these terms.

allCourses.title: Criminal Law
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Deals specifically with the substantive nature of criminal law and its historical development. Focuses on understanding the development of fundamental doctrinal principles upon which criminal law is based, including mens rea, actus reus, homicide, causation, group criminality, and exculpation.

allCourses.title: Government Crime
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the legal, organizational, and political issues involved in the generation and control of government lawlessness. Readings present historical and theoretical perspectives in the abuse of government authority and the ability of the legal system to control such behavior.

allCourses.title: Violence in Society
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Current theory and research on aggression; anger and violence as problems in individual and social functioning.
