allCourses.title: Structure of Japanese
allCourses.description: An overview of the linguistic features of modern Japanese. Provides students with a systematic introduction to the nature and characteristics of the language.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Linguistics
allCourses.description: In-depth examination of selected topics in the linguistics of East Asian languages, including Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Korean Society and Culture
allCourses.description: Studies of the social and cultural forces that affect the lives of the Koreans, including those in the United States. Considers traditional values and contemporary issues within a historical framework.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Korean Literature and Society

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Literature in Translation
allCourses.description: East Asian literary works in translation. Taught in English.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Cultural Studies in East Asia
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary and theoretical introduction to issues in cultural studies that are pertinent to the study of East Asia. All readings in English.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in Chinese Literature
allCourses.restriction: Korean Literature and Culture Majors only. Chinese Studies Majors only. Japanese Language Literature Majors only. East Asian Cultures Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to major themes in Chinese literature and culture through the close reading, discussion, and analysis of selected texts in English translation.

allCourses.description: Introduces students to major themes in Japanese literature and culture through the close reading, discussion, and analysis of selected texts in English translation.

allCourses.restriction: Korean Literature and Culture Majors only. Chinese Studies Majors only. Japanese Language Literature Majors only. East Asian Cultures Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to major themes in Korean literature and culture through the close reading, discussion, and analysis of selected texts in English translation.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Cinema
allCourses.description: Study of East Asian cinema from historical, theoretical, and comparative perspectives. Taught in English.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Gender in East Asia
allCourses.description: Explores the construction of gender in East Asian cultures and literatures. Pays close attention to the specificity of historical, cultural, and literary contexts of East Asia as it investigates various theoretical and critical perspectives on gender and sexuality.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Junior-Senior Colloquium
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Korean Literature and Culture Majors only. Chinese Studies Majors only. Japanese Language Literature Majors only. East Asian Cultures Majors only.
allCourses.description: Specialized courses dealing with primary sources; required reports and papers. Each colloquium reflects the instructor's intellectual interest and is conducted as a discussion group. Limited to 15 students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Junior-Senior Seminar
allCourses.description: Analysis of a literary or cultural topic or problem through research and writing of two short and one long research paper for a minimum of 4,000 total words. Seminar follows EAS 190; related to the colloquium's subject.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( EAS 190 OR E ASIAN 190 ) AND LOWER DIVISION WRITING
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Investigation of special topics through directed reading in translation. Paper required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian Religions
allCourses.description: An introduction to Asian religions (Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism, Shamanism) including both elite doctrinal aspects and forms of more popular religiosity.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Religions
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the religions of East Asia, e.g., Buddhism, Daoism, Shintô, Islam, shamanism.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Cultural Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar, with topics varying from year to year. Research paper required.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Applied Linguistics
allCourses.description: In-depth examination of selected topics in applied linguistics, with a particular emphasis on language acquisition and language pedagogy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Cinema
allCourses.description: An examination of the possibilities of East Asian cinematic narrative. Possible topics: cinematic history; cinema in popular culture; comparisons with literary texts; major auteurs. Emphasis on technical as well as on thematic aspects. Includes readings in film theory.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Directed research on topic determined in consultation with faculty member. A term paper or project is required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Dissertation research for students who are advanced to doctoral candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in East Asian Popular Culture
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the popular cultural traditions of East Asia designed to introduce students both to problems in situating culture in a specific time and place and to contemporary theories of popular culture and their application to East Asian contexts.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to East Asian Cultures
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary courses organized each year around a broad theme designed to introduce students to the cultures of East Asia. Topical organization of courses addresses issues that have been of importance historically and are reshaping East Asia today.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Traveling East/West
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Traveling East/West presents a wide range of travel writings by Chinese, Indian, and Euro-American authors in which they contemplate the complexities of cross-cultural encounters and how knowledge about others and knowledge of ourselves are closely intertwined.

allCourses.title: Research in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Ecology and Evolutionary Biological faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Ecology and Evolutionary Biological faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Research in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Ecology and Evolutionary Biological faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Invited speakers, graduate students, and faculty present current research in ecology and evolutionary biology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Graduate Tutorial in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced study in areas not represented by formal courses. May involve individual or small group study through reading, discussion, and composition.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Graduate Tutorial in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced study in areas not represented by formal courses. May involve individual or small group study through reading, discussion, and composition.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Graduate Tutorial in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced study in areas not represented by formal courses. May involve individual or small group study through reading, discussion, and composition.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Writing Grant Proposals
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with hands-on experience writing proposals in the research areas of ecology, evolution, or physiology.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of special topics in Ecology.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Evolution
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Extensive introduction to the primary literature of evolutionary biology. Topics include population genetics, quantitative genetics, neutralism, molecular evolution, evolution of genetic systems, genetic architecture of fitness, speciation, and macroevolution.

allCourses.title: Quantitative Methods in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistics for ecologists and evolutionary biologists. Emphasis on specific applications and underlying assumptions rather than on methods of calculation. Topics include experimental design, parametric and nonparametric methods, analysis of variance and covariance, and multiple regression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Completion of at least one quarter of statistics including regression and analysis of variance.

allCourses.title: Ecological and Evolutionary Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A summary of information in organismal biology, comparative and ecological physiology, and the biophysical basis of organismal function. Course offered every other fall.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Physical and functional principles common to many living forms. Course forms a basis for subsequent specialization in any of the subdisciplines of physiology. Course offered in even years.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Ecology
allCourses.description: Weekly discussion of current topics in ecology at the graduate level.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Statistical Learning in Ecology and Evolution
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews basic principals of variance/bias trade-offs. Topics include models for prediction and classification, variable selection methods, cross-validation, tree based methods, unsupervised learning. Applications in ecology and evolution using R.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECO EVO 207. ECO EVO 207 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Plant Physiological Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a summary of information on plant organismal biology, comparative and ecological physiology, and functional ecology. Offered every other fall.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Microbial Ecology
allCourses.description: Weekly discussion of current topics in ecology, biogeochemistry, evolution, and physiology of microbial organisms.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Communication Skills for Environmental Scholars
allCourses.description: Students learn to communicate with non-specialist audiences about climate and environmental issues. Hands-on activities build technical, presentation, and contextual skills required for effective communication across a range of media types and careers.

allCourses.title: Experimental Evolution
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. School of Biological Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Explores experimental evolution, which is now a well-established part of evolutionary biology. With the advent of genomics, it is now one of the most powerful tools for studying the genetic foundations of biology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Human Dimensions in Conservation and Restoration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The non-human “environment” we know today is the result of past social, political, scientific, and economic forces. Examines the forces that drove environmental conservation efforts, which often sought progress at the expense of local cultures.

allCourses.title: Marine Conservation Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theory-based seminar tackles pressing issues in marine ecology, conservation, and restoration. Focuses on the science of marine ecosystems, resources and tools for their conservation, and management and the socioeconomic and policy dimensions.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Ecology and Evolution Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Weekly discussion of teaching techniques and challenges that are specific to courses in ecology and evolutionary biology.  Emphasis will be on using evidence-based pedagogy techniques.  There will be a combination of readings, group discussions and speakers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Behavioral Endocrinology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Comparative examination of the major hormone systems that regulate behavior across animals. Emphasizes the reciprocating nature of hormone-behavior interactions and seeks to understand how natural selection drives the evolution of hormone structure and function.

allCourses.title: Evolutionary and Ecological Principles in Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explore the dynamics of populations on an ecological, epidemiological, and medical level. Considers the dynamics of competition, predation, and parasitism; the spread and control of infectious diseases; and the in vivo dynamics of viral infections and the immune system.

allCourses.title: Functional and Structural Evolutionary Genomics
allCourses.description: Function and organization of genomes analyzed from an evolutionary perspective. Review of some of the most recent experimental approaches in genome analysis and comparative genomics. Relevant software to analyze DNA and expression data is used.

allCourses.title: Professional Workshop
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Identify and attend professional or technical skill workshops to gain professional knowledge and certifications related to conservation and restoration science.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Conservation Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores concepts in ecology with potential for conserving biological diversity. Identifies creative applications of ecological research that mitigate impacts of rapid human population growth and habitat destruction on biodiversity.

allCourses.title: Restoration Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of principles and practices that help recover degraded ecosystems  including restoration in different ecological systems, restoration motives and intensities, implementation and monitoring, and scope and success of case studies.

allCourses.title: Field Methods in Restoration
allCourses.description: Laboratory experience performing field methods that help recover degraded ecosystems  in different ecological systems.  Emphasis on the plant community composition, soil, irrigation, maintenance, and monitoring of a project.

allCourses.title: Science Communication
allCourses.description: Develops students' abilities to convey information related to conservation and restoration in a way that has broad appeal and/or effective messaging for non-scientific audiences by assessing the audience, developing effective storytelling, and deploying a persuasive information campaign.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Technical Writing
allCourses.description: Practice developing key documents for restoration projects including a response to a request for proposal (RFP), a restoration project plan, and a monitoring and maintenance plan.

allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.description: Discover the planning, design, implementation, and aftercare phases of managing a conservation or restoration project.  Students will project cost, manage risk, analyze sites, evaluate and review projects, and become familiar with common permitting and consultation requirements.

allCourses.title: GIS for Environmental Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of GIS. Topics include cartography, creating/editing GIS data, georeferencing, map projections, geospatial analysis, spatial statistics, and development of GIS models. Focuses on theory and practice.

allCourses.title: Marine Research and Conservation Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Field-based introduction to marine ecology and conservation management through the study of the ecology, resource management, and conservation of marine habitats and species, and the use of a variety of marine field research methods.

allCourses.title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World
allCourses.description: Investigation of plant diversity in California and throughout the world, including basic systematic concepts, introduction to major groups of flowering plants, and the effects of global biological change on plant diversity. Students carry out a phylogenetic analysis using appropriate software.

allCourses.title: Wildlife Ecology and Sampling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Field-based introduction to wildlife management through the study of the ecology, physiology, population biology management, and conservation of vertebrate wildlife species, and the use of a variety of different wildlife sampling techniques.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Informatics for Biologists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics and the unix operating system (including the shell and Sun Grid Engine) in order to assemble a eukaryotic genome.

allCourses.title: Advanced Informatics for Biologists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn advanced informatics including the analysis of: Poolseq, RNAseq, ATACseq, and ChiPseq datasets using programs such as bwa, tophat, cufflinks, DEseq, Trinity, Agustus, etc., in a unix high-performance computing environment. Statistical tests carried out and publication quality.

allCourses.title: Topics in Evolutionary Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Weekly discussion of recent research on evolutionary genetics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: MCRS Capstone
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Apply knowledge and skills in a practical professional setting, working with practitioners to identify a conservation or management problem and then to plan, implement, and evaluate a solution.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Documenting Research Through Cinematic Production
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students gain advanced media expertise by conceptualizing investigative research into publicly engaging video projects. Popularly accessible research topics will be adapted into documentary, television, or cinematic pieces that provide opportunities for developing professionally marketable skills in educationally effective media production.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Teaching Science in Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective secondary science teachers learn how to teach science in grades 7-12. Covers State science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, criteria for selecting science curricular materials, and how to plan science lessons, units, experiments, projects, and demonstrations.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Mandatory course for Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Teaching Assistants, required in each quarter in which student has a Teaching Assistant position. Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Economics
allCourses.restriction: No Economics Majors. ECON 1 may not be taken for credit if taken concurrently or after ECON 20A or ECON 20B.
allCourses.description: An analysis of the problems society faces in organizing itself to provide goods and services. How decisions of government, business, and the individual relate to current economic problems such as unemployment, inflation, poverty, and environmental pollution.

allCourses.restriction: No Quantitative Economics Majors. Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Determinants of supply and demand; operation of competitive and monopolistic markets; imperfections of the market system, explanations of unemployment, inflation, recessions; public policy for macroeconomic problems.

allCourses.description: A collection of concepts and methods for effective decision making. allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Builds off of economic theory to explore topics in health economics including health care demand, health insurance markets, the supply of health care, and examine health care policy.

allCourses.description: Examines the role of the government in the economy and its impact on individuals and firms.

allCourses.description: Theory of public goods, externalities, voting models, analysis of bureaucracy, the Tiebout model, income redistribution, intergovernmental grants.

allCourses.description: The theory of market structure. Imperfect markets, government policies, and industry performance.

allCourses.description: Uses tools of economics, game theory in particular, to develop an understanding of business decision-making. Deals with questions such as how the firm decides what kind of business to be in, how large should it be, and others.

allCourses.description: Political economy seeks explanations that combine insights from both economics and politics. Topics include the interaction of government and markets, the causes of the Great Recession, and the sources of income and wealth inequality.

allCourses.description: Arms students with tools, concepts, and evidence that can be used to analyze complex policy questions in education, enabling students to arrive at their own reasoned judgments about how to improve education.

allCourses.title: Graduate Colloquium for Economics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Economics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors. Supplemented by class discussion of these presentations and other material on current research methodology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Mathematics for Economists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Gives students the mathematical background required for graduate work in economics. Topics covered include multivariate calculus, differential equations, and linear algebra.

allCourses.title: Basic Economics I
allCourses.restriction: Economics, Quantitative Economics, Business Economics, and Business Info Management majors have first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4A may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20A.
allCourses.description: The fundamentals of microeconomics. The behavior of firms and consumers: markets, supply/demand, utility maximization, resource allocation, and efficiency.

allCourses.title: Basic Economics II
allCourses.restriction: Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4B may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20B.
allCourses.description: The fundamentals of macroeconomics. Government behavior: monetary and fiscal policy, inflation, and unemployment. Effective fall 2006, the content of Economics 20B is macroeconomics. This course cannot be taken to repeat Economics 20B taken prior to fall 2006.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( ECON 13 OR ECON 23 OR ECON 20A OR INTL ST 13 OR AP ECONOMICS:MICRO ) AND NO AP ECONOMICS:MACRO score of 4 or greater AND NO MGMT 4B AND ( BUSINESS ECONOMICS MAJORS ONLY OR ECONOMICS MAJORS ONLY OR QUANTITATIVE ECON MAJORS ONLY OR INTERNATIONL STUDIES MAJORS ONLY OR CIVIL ENGINEERING MAJORS ONLY OR ENVIRONMENTAL ENGR MAJORS ONLY OR MECHANICAL ENGR MAJORS ONLY OR AEROSPACE ENGR MAJORS ONLY OR BUSINESS INFO MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR UNDECLARED MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.title: Microeconomic Theory I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical microeconomics. Emphasis on the meaning and empirical interpretation of theoretical models. Topics include theory of the firm, theory of the market, theory of the consumer, duality theory, application to econometrics, general equilibrium and welfare economics, uncertainty, game theory.

allCourses.title: Microeconomic Theory II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical microeconomics. Emphasis on the meaning and empirical interpretation of theoretical models. Topics include theory of the firm, theory of the market, theory of the consumer, duality theory, application to econometrics, general equilibrium and welfare economics, uncertainty, game theory.

allCourses.title: Microeconomic Theory III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical microeconomics. Emphasis on the meaning and empirical interpretation of theoretical models. Topics include theory of the firm, theory of the market, theory of the consumer, duality theory, application to econometrics, general equilibrium and welfare economics, uncertainty, game theory.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomic Theory I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced macroeconomic theory including alternative macroeconomic models, microeconomic foundations of macroeconomics, investment and growth theory, inflation and unemployment, rational expectations and macroeconomic policy, wealth effects, crowding out and fiscal policy, money and interest, open economy models.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomic Theory II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced macroeconomic theory including alternative macroeconomic models, microeconomic foundations of macroeconomics, investment and growth theory, inflation and unemployment, rational expectations and macroeconomic policy, wealth effects, crowding out and fiscal policy, money and interest, open economy models.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomic Theory III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced macroeconomic theory including alternative macroeconomic models, microeconomic foundations of macroeconomics, investment and growth theory, inflation and unemployment, rational expectations and macroeconomic policy, wealth effects, crowding out and fiscal policy, money and interest, open economy models.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomics Theory II Lab
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of stochastic processes; introduction to dynamic programming; two equilibrium concepts; Ricardian equivalence; real business cycle model; complete versus incomplete markets; asset pricing and the equity premium puzzle.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Economic Theory
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Economic Theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Econometrics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Takes up where ECON 202 leaves off. Continuing in the likelihood perspective, begins with Bayesian point estimation and then covers interval estimation and hypothesis testing from both frequentist and Bayesian perspectives.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Econometrics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Begins by relaxing the ideal conditions of the standard regression model. Potential topics include kernel density estimation, instrumental variables (IV), two stage least squares (2SLS), panel data models, and simulation-based Bayesian methods, including Gibbs sampling, and the bootstrap.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Econometrics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers econometric time series, discrete choice and count models, sample selection, and duration models along with Bayesian and classical asymptotic methods.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Econometrics Laboratory I
allCourses.description: Discussion of problems in statistics and econometrics, and their relationships to statistical and econometrics theory. Instruction in the use of computers for applied econometric work.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Econometrics Laboratory II
allCourses.description: Discussion of problems in statistics and econometrics, and their relationships to statistical and econometrics theory. Instruction in the use of computers for applied econometric work.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Econometrics Laboratory III
allCourses.description: Discussion of problems in statistics and econometrics, and their relationships to statistical and econometrics theory. Instruction in the use of computers for applied econometric work.

allCourses.title: Discrete Choice Econometrics
allCourses.description: Specification, estimation, and testing of discrete choice models, with emphasis on cross-sectional and panel data models and applications. Students use computer packages to apply models and techniques to real data.

allCourses.title: Time Series Econometrics
allCourses.description: Econometric analysis of time series data. Moving average and autoregressive series, regression analysis, Box-Jenkins techniques, computational methods, and causality conditions.

allCourses.title: Experimental Econ I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to experimental social science. Students learn experimental methodology, design, and analysis, and be exposed to active research areas. Each student writes a proposal for their own experiment and presents the design in class.

allCourses.title: Experimental Econ II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on implementing experimental projects in a laboratory environment. Subjects learn about human subjects protection, program experimental software for their own projects, and conduct live experiment sessions.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Econometrics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Econometrics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Basic Economics for Engineers
allCourses.restriction: Engineering Majors only. Mechanical Engineering Majors only. Aerospace Engineering Majors only. Civil Engineering Majors only. Environmental Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: The fundamentals of microeconomics. The behavior of firms and of consumers: markets, supply/demand, utility maximization, resource allocation, and efficiency.

allCourses.title: Business Cycles in Historical Perspective
allCourses.description: Investigates business cycles in the United States and worldwide during the last two centuries. Topics include causes and consequences of business fluctuations, monetary and fiscal policy, models of fluctuations, and empirical macroeconomics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 210A and ECON 210B and ECON 210C and ECON 210D and ECON 210E and ECON 210F

allCourses.title: American Economic History
allCourses.description: Focuses on American economic history from colonization onwards. Topics include the development of legal systems, transport systems, financial markets, industrialization, migration, immigration, technological change, and the consequences of slavery.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 210A and ECON 210B and ECON 210C and ECON 210D and ECON 210E and ECON 210F

allCourses.title: Health and Development in Historical Perspective
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Investigates the evolution of population health over time and across the development process. Examines how the environment, nutrition, public health systems, and medical innovations have influenced health and demographic behavior. Also explores the interplay between health capital and economic growth.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 210A and ECON 210B and ECON 210C and ECON 220A and ECON 220B

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Financial Economics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Financial Economics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Industrial Organization I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the structure and economic performance of markets, and the impact of public policy and their efficiency and equity. Effects of information structure. Oligopoly, cartels, mergers, vertical integration, patents, innovation, antitrust, and regulation.

allCourses.title: Industrial Organization II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the structure and economic performance of markets, and the impact of public policy and their efficiency and equity. Effects of information structure. Price flexibility and dispersion, auctions, search and industrial structure, intrafirm organization.

allCourses.title: Development Economics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Uses theory and empirics to understand the economies of low- and middle-income countries. Explores the concept, determinants, and consequences of economic growth, drawing on historical and cross-country evidence. Topics include poverty, inequality, agriculture, demography, and strategies of risk management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 210A and ECON 210B and ECON 210C and ECON 220A and ECON 220B

allCourses.title: Game Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A formal introduction to non-cooperative game theory. Topics include properties of Nash Equilibrium and equilibrium refinements, games with imperfect information, and games with incomplete information.

allCourses.title: Advanced Game Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides advanced instruction in game theory. The topics covered will be (i) the theory of repeated games and (ii) evolutionary game theory. Applications include bargaining, collusion, reputation, social norms, and the evolution of preferences via natural selection and cultural transmission.

allCourses.title: Empirical Methods in Applied Microeconomics
allCourses.description: Focuses on the empirical methods used in modern applied microeconomics. Teaches methods that can be applied to produce original research in applied fields using cross-sectional and panel data. Applications will be drawn heavily from labor, public, health and development economics.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Microeconomics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Microeconomics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: The Economics of Accounting Decisions
allCourses.restriction: Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to accounting concepts and principles, including the accounting model and accounting style, transaction analysis, and preparation of financial statements. An analysis of the similarities and differences between accounting and economic concepts (e.g., value, profits).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( ECON 20A OR AP ECONOMICS:MICRO ) AND NO MGMT 30A

allCourses.title: Labor Economics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the relationships between education and the labor market (human capital theory), between resources devoted to education and the return to education (the education production function) and between education and labor market inequality (the theory of skill-biased technical change).

allCourses.title: Labor Economics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of core topics in labor economics, with an emphasis on empirical methods.  Topics may include minimum wages, discrimination, gender, aging and retirement, labor market networks, personnel economics, and employment policy.

allCourses.title: Labor Economics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of treatment effect/program evaluation in labor economics, emphasizing identification. Classical labor topics, including human capital, technology, wages, labor supply, and migration are discussed in the context of causal inference. A unified framework is used in analyzing identification strategies.

allCourses.title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of microeconomics that are required for applied policy analysis. Provides students with an intuitive understanding of the microeconomic approach, and familiarizes them with concepts used in applied public policy analysis.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Labor Economics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Labor Economics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Monetary Economics II
allCourses.description: Surveys recent issues on monetary policy in uncertain environments. Examines settings where both the policy makers and the private sector are uncertain of future outcomes or the underlying economic structure.

allCourses.title: International Trade I
allCourses.description: Covers theoretical models, empirical methods, and policy issues in international trade. Following the conventional treatment of the Richardian model, the Heckscher-Ohlin model and the specific factors model, new trade models which incorporate scale economics and imperfect competition will be discussed.

allCourses.title: Advanced Macroeconomics I
allCourses.description: Students build Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) macroeconomic models from microeconomic foundations. This approach emphasizes intertemporal optimization by firms and households and typically incorporates nominal rigidities such as sluggish price and/or wage adjustment.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Macroeconomics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Macroeconomics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Political Economy I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.

allCourses.title: Political Economy II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.

allCourses.title: Political Economy III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.

allCourses.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Considers empirical research from the economics literature on various topics related to the criminal justice system, such as policing, bail reform, incarceration, or recidivism.

allCourses.title: Public Economics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers welfare economics, the theory of optimal taxation, tax incidence, and empirical methods in tax policy. Empirical topics include tax evasion, measurement of incidence, efficiency costs, and other policy issues.

allCourses.title: Public Economics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the theory of public goods and models of decentralized provision of such goods, including voluntary provision, voting, bureaucratic provision, and preference revelation mechanisms, as well as the Tiebout model. Also covers externalities, cost-benefit analysis, and intergovernmental competition.

allCourses.title: Public Economics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the rationale for and effects of government intervention in insurance markets and for redistribution. Includes theoretical and empirical analyses of cash and in-kind assistance programs, unemployment insurance, disability insurance, Social Security, and other programs.

allCourses.title: Economics of Government
allCourses.description: Prepares students to analyze public policy questions with tools from economics. By the end, students should be able to identify important economic issues in public policy debates and consume and critique economic research on these topics.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Political Economy
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Political Economy. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Urban Economics I
allCourses.description: Economic reasons for the existence of cities, analysis of urban spatial structure, urban sprawl, Third World urbanization, hedonic price analysis, housing tenure choice.

allCourses.title: Urban Economics II
allCourses.description: Housing in the portfolio, land-use controls, rent control, homelessness, neighborhood effects, urban quality-of-life measurement, and subcenters.

allCourses.title: Transportation Economics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Applies microeconomic concepts of demand, costs, pricing, investment, and project evaluation to analyze transportation activities. Empirical studies include travel demand using discrete models, and cost functions.

allCourses.title: Transportation Economics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Economics of the airline industry. Hub-and-spoke networks, the effects of competition on airfares, price dispersion, airline alliances, airport congestion, product unbundling.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Economics faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Independent research with Economics faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Economics Honors Colloquium I
allCourses.restriction: Economics Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Colloquium required for honors students in economics, quantitative economics, and business economics. Introduces students to independent research. Helps students plan a research program. Prepares students for thesis writing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Cyber-Physical Systems Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Requirements and specification, models of computation, tools, design, merging cyber and physical, data-driven modeling for edge artificial intelligence systems, cyber-physical examples. Design process, specification, requirements, modeling, components, selection, interfaces, system structure, different levels, verification, testing.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Embedded Systems Modeling and Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Embedded systems definition, system-level specification, models and languages. Concepts, requirements, examples. Embedded system models at different levels of abstraction. Test benches, design under test, IP components. Discrete event simulation, semantics, and algorithms.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Embedded System Software
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Embedded system software requirements, concepts, and examples for applications in the cyber-physical domain. Embedded operating systems, real-time system software (RTOS), I/O software. Multithreading. System software for power and energy management, and middleware.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Sensors, Actuators, and Sensor Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles and applications of sensors, actuators. Smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices. Introduction to signal processing and sensor/actuator networks, deployment and architecture, wireless communication, multiple access control layer, data gathering, routing and querying, collaborating signal processing.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Real-Time and Distributed Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Time dependent systems, clock synchronization, real-time communication protocols, specification of requirements, task scheduling. Validation of timelines, real-time configuration management. Middleware architecture for distributed real-time and secure services.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Security and Privacy in Cyber-Physical Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Embedded and cyber-physical systems security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, confidentiality, data integrity, authorization, access control, security protocols. Privacy awareness and mitigation. Side-channel attacks and defenses. Applications of public key and symmetric cryptography, digital certificates, credentials.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Control Systems for Cyber-Physical Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Dynamic models, from first principles or via identification. Concepts in control (stability, controllability, observability). Control design (continuous times) and digital implementation. Introduction to optimization and direct discrete time control. Multi-agent systems, their control and implementation related concepts.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Cyber-Physical Systems Case Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers CPS case studies in applications such as (but not limited to): automotive and transportation, manufacturing, power distribution grid, medical and healthcare, robotics, civil infrastructure, avionics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Cyber-Physical Systems Project
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students are required to complete a project that deals with a specific emphasis of Cyber-Physical Systems, such as (but not limited to): automotive, transportation, manufacturing, power grid, medical healthcare, robotics, civil infrastructure, avionics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of machine learning and data-mining.  Learning algorithms for classifications, regression, and clustering.  Emphasis is on discriminative classification methods such as decision trees, rules, nearest neighbor, linear models, and naive Bayes.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Entrepreneurship for Scientists and Engineers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Real-world introduction to the theory and practice of entrepreneurship. Explores organizational, strategic, and financial challenges; start-up strategies; business-idea evaluation; and business-plan writing. Presentations by prestigious entrepreneurs and industry leaders.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Internet of Things Systems and Software
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Internet of Things (IoT) concept, sensors and actuators, serial protocols, network and communication protocols and programming, IoT platforms, real-time performance, middleware architecture for IoT, edge and cloud support for IoT applications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Special Topics in CPS
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of CPS. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Educational Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed to help students become intelligent consumers of research and independent researchers, and provides an introduction to the basic principles of educational research. Topics include research questions, literature reviews, and qualitative and quantitative research designs.

allCourses.title: Educational Strategies for Tutoring and Teacher Aiding
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Placement in a public elementary or secondary school to gain experience as a tutor or teacher aide. Emphasis on cognitive learning and the development of instructional strategies and resources which can be used in effective cross-age and cross-cultural experiences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Strategies for Tutoring and Teacher Aiding in a Bilingual Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Placement in a dual immersion school setting to gain experience as a bilingual (Spanish) tutor or teacher aide. Emphasis on cognitive learning and the development of instructional strategies and resources which can be used in effective cross-age and cross-cultural experiences.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Must be able to communicate in Spanish.

allCourses.title: The Arts and Human Development
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students use various arts disciplines (e.g. studio art, music, dance, drama, and media arts) to investigate how visual and performing arts support individual human development. Introduction to pedagogy for integrating the arts in K-12 settings. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Multimedia and the Arts in the Multicultural Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multiculturalism and under-represented U.S. minorities and the visual and performing arts: perspectives in artistic perception, creative expression, historical and cultural context, aesthetic valuing, and media literacy in the interpretation and production of multimedia arts products and applications for K-12 classrooms.

allCourses.title: Early Childhood Education Curriculum and Instruction
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide an introductory survey of the nature, needs, and education of young children. Explores questions such as "What should we teach young children?" and "How should we teach?".

allCourses.title: Child Development in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the pathways of normally developing children's growth and change over time. In particular, focuses on how cognitive and social development impact and are driven by educational contexts.

allCourses.title: Adolescent Development and Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social development of adolescents, with an emphasis on the practical implications of developmental theory and research findings for teachers and other professionals who work with adolescents in middle or high school contexts.

allCourses.title: Reading and Writing in Mathematics and Science
allCourses.description: Emphasis is placed on understanding the literacy processes (listening, speaking, viewing, thinking, reading, and writing) as they relate to middle and high school mathematics and science. Students integrate literacy-related strategies with curriculum-based goals supported in the California State Frameworks.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Positive Psychology in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Positive psychology is a recent focus area within the field of psychology that explores what is positive, creative, and fulfilling in human behavior. It is the scientific study of well-being and flourishing.

allCourses.title: Applied Positive Psychology in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers select positive psychology topics, theories, and interventions at an advanced level. Students focus on developing an understanding of positive psychology evidence-based practices that can be applied in classrooms and schools to promote learning in an academic environment.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Elementary Mathematics Learning I
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides understanding of fundamental mathematics necessary to teach for conceptual understanding and higher-level reasoning and problem solving. Conceptual understanding of place value, fractions, proportionality, geometry, algebra, functions, probability, statistics, and measurement. Instructional applications of these concepts in grades K-8 teaching.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Elementary Mathematics Learning II
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides understanding of fundamental mathematics necessary to teach for conceptual understanding and higher-level reasoning and problem solving. Conceptual understanding of place value, fractions, proportionality, geometry, algebra, functions, probability, statistics, and measurement. Instructional applications of these concepts in grades K-8 teaching.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Elementary Mathematics Learning III
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides understanding of fundamental mathematics necessary to teach for conceptual understanding and higher-level reasoning and problem solving. Conceptual understanding of place value, fractions, proportionality, geometry, algebra, functions, probability, statistics, and measurement. Instructional applications of these concepts in grades K-8 teaching.

allCourses.title: Multicultural Education in K-12 Schools
allCourses.description: Provides a theoretical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting low-income immigrant and U.S. born minority student populations in an increasingly diverse and changing society.

allCourses.title: Children, Schools, and Cinema
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Through popular films, analyzes aspects of school dynamics and interaction of schools with students, teachers, and public.  Melding educational studies and film studies provides deeper understanding of methods used to transmit information and attitudes about schools to the lay public.

allCourses.title: Ethics and Education
allCourses.description: Ethics in education and how ethicists frame moral problems.  Presents major ethical themes that affect education.   Analysis of models for dealing with ethical goals and developing morality for K–12 students.  Models for solving ethical dilemmas within an educational context.

allCourses.title: Moral Education for Youth Development I
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: The first of a two-course series that examines research-based theories for how school settings and adult mentors contribute to the moral development of adolescents. Students examine theory in the context of real-world application in four program observations.

allCourses.title: Moral Education for Youth Development II
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Continuation of EDUC 127A. Allows students from 127A to experience the role of adults in the moral development of youth. Students receive training to deliver curriculum and apply research-based theories and methods in real-world youth settings.

allCourses.title: Exceptional Learners
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introductory survey of the nature, needs, and education of K–12 children with exceptionalities. Covers the categories and characteristics of exceptionalities, relevant state and federal legislation, and the role of general education teachers in special education.

allCourses.title: Children's Learning and Media
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only. Informatics Majors only. Informatics Minors only.
allCourses.description: Examines how popular media may impact how young people learn, develop, and communicate by looking at research related to the impacts of a wide range of popular media including television, video games, digital environments, mobile devices, and other multimedia.

allCourses.title: Educational Technology
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents an overview of the types and uses of educational technology to support and enhance the K–12 learning experience. Familiarizes students with lesson planning, instructional design, learning theory, and integrating technology into the curriculum.

allCourses.title: Reading and Writing Enrichment for After-School Programs
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines literacy development and the implementation of research-based practices to enrich learners' reading and writing skills in after-school programs. A minimum of 20 hours of after-school program fieldwork is required in order to design and implement literacy enrichment activities.

allCourses.title: Teaching English Internationally
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers methods of teaching English as a foreign language, basic language knowledge for English teachers, the social context of English language teaching around the world, and essential information about securing international employment as an English teacher.

allCourses.title: Arts for Elementary Learners
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and practice in art education for the elementary school classroom. Includes content and pedagogy for future teachers and others interested in the relationship between child development and the production of visual art. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Children's Literature in the Elementary Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the wealth of children's literature that can be integrated into the elementary classroom. Surveys traditional literature, fiction, nonfiction, and poetry that make curriculum accessible to all students. Focuses on literary elements for both reading and creating text.

allCourses.title: Courts, Classrooms, and Controversies in Education Policy
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines policies and laws defining the K-12 U.S. education system and the politics and controversies surrounding the political decision-making process at the federal, state, and local levels. Discusses original intent versus effects on organization of schools and educational equity.

allCourses.title: American History and Education Policy: An Intimate Relationship
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the interplay between history, politics, and policy. Students examine the interactions between sociopolitical development and environmental contexts (e.g. familial, social, school, cultural) and contemplate the power of normative values in the formulation of education policy.

allCourses.title: Controversies in College
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the fascinating world of postsecondary education. Every week students dive deeper into controversies that make college more than just where students attend class, but rather, one of the most important social institutions shaping our world.

allCourses.title: Classroom Interactions I
allCourses.description: Focuses on research-based instructional strategies for enhancing the learning of secondary mathematics and science. Students learn about adolescent and second-language development to assist them in developing analyzing, teaching, and critiquing lessons for secondary classrooms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PS 105 or BIOL 101) and EDUC 55. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Classroom Interactions II
allCourses.description: Focuses on equity and multicultural education research, special education, and research-based instructional and assessment strategies to assist students in designing, teaching, and assessing lessons that meet the needs of all secondary mathematics and science students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PS 105 or BIOL 101) and EDUC 55 and EDUC 143AW and EDUC 148. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The American Charter School
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the legitimacy of the charter school as a viable educational reform movement. Critical themes include the role of choice and privatization in public education and charter schools as a vehicle for fulfilling the promise of educational equality.

allCourses.title: Theories and Pedagogies of Race in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces theoretical frameworks to examine the role of race in American education. Emphasis is placed on introducing students to different race and ethnicity paradigms.

allCourses.title: Education, Learning, and Culture
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of learning and development through a cultural lens, drawing from a range of research traditions and disciplines to broaden understandings of theories that inform teaching and learning in formal and informal settings.

allCourses.title: Poverty, Education, and Social Change
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores how institutional and demographic changes in the U.S. have shaped disparities in education, the mechanisms through which poverty and social class influence families, and students, and promising programs and interventions to address inequity. Includes community service.

allCourses.title: Complex Pedagogical Design
allCourses.description: In this Cal Teach capstone course, students design lesson plans and complex instructional units, using approaches such as mathematics and science integration, problem-based instruction, project-based learning, technology, representations, scientific and mathematical analysis/modeling, authentic assessment, contextualization, and designing equitable learning environments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PS 105 or BIOL 101) and EDUC 55 and EDUC 143AW

allCourses.title: Family, School, and Community in Early Childhood
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the many socializing aspects of young children's social worlds. Through the use of ecological perspectives, explores the role of families, schools, and communities on children's social development, especially in early childhood.

allCourses.title: Statistics for Education Research
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to the use of statistics in educational research. Focuses on testing and measurement, and provides basic tools to read, interpret, and draw conclusions from quantitative educational research.

allCourses.title: Changing the High School Experience
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of problems in high school education (e.g., student disengagement and underachievement of disadvantaged) and proposals for changing curriculum, instruction, and school organization. Students suggest own reforms and analyze effective/ineffective school practices.

allCourses.title: Language and Literacy
allCourses.restriction: Language Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Education Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses the linguistic principles and processes that underlie oral and written language proficiency. Emphasis is on how to use phonology, morphology, orthography, semantics, syntax, and pragmatics to support literacy and oral language development for K-12 students.

allCourses.title: Theory and Practice of Reading Interventions for Students At-Risk for Reading Failure
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines the research concerning reading failure in young children and interventions used to support them. Topics include reading development and reading intervention. Students critically evaluate the relation between their fieldwork experience and the research and evaluation literature.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Latino Families and Youth
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Current issues in theory, methods, and research in U.S. Latino/a youth and families are examined. An advanced level study, with a particular focus on history, theories, methods, research, and applied social issues.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Field Methods in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to methods for studying human behavior in context. It prepares students for conducting applied educational research, including designing needs assessments; conducting observations, interviews and focus groups; organizing and analyzing data; and synthesizing and presenting research findings.

allCourses.title: Educational Research and Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers qualitative and quantitative research methods relevant for the evaluation of educational programs. Students have the opportunity to plan, execute, and write-up a small evaluation project.

allCourses.title: Student Teaching Mathematics and Science in Middle/High School
allCourses.description: Student teaching includes orientation, seminars, preparation, and assumption of secondary school classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements and in conjunction with the public school calendar. Five days/week and a minimum four hours/day over two quarters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PS 105 or BIOL 101) and EDUC 55 and EDUC 143AW and EDUC 143BW and EDUC 148
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Experimental Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed to help students to develop the ability to think critically about research, and to develop an understanding of how to design and conduct experiments. The overall goal is to prepare students to independently plan and implement a research study.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Out-of-School Learning
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. May be taken a second time if student is a candidate for Certificate in After-School Education, and the first time was prior to Fall 2008.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of child and adolescent learning through participation in out-of-school activities and settings. Recognizes the importance of matching out-of-school experiences with the interests, needs, and development level of students. Observation-based fieldwork included.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Discovering Science in Out-of-School Hours
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the design principles and teaching techniques that science museums and other out-of-school science programs use to motivate children and youth to learn science through discovery. Includes field experience at a science learning center or after-school program. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Chicanx/Latinx Education
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latinx low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

allCourses.title: Cognition and Learning in Educational Settings
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Education Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Exploration of historical foundations of cognitive psychology and cognitive development, cognitive neuroscience in education, complex cognition, individual differences, and cognitive foundations of learning.

allCourses.title: Education and the American Dream: Historical Perspectives on Democracy and Education
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between public schooling and the promotion of democratic ideals in American society over the past two centuries.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Foundational questions of education are viewed from newly emerging developmental perspectives which treat cognition as embodied action and learning as cultural recapitulation. Historical, sociological, psychological, and philosophical implications of views toward aspects of teaching, learning, curriculum, and pedagogy are considered.

allCourses.title: Psychology of Learning, Abilities, and Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Education Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of classic positions on the mind, human abilities, and intelligence, especially as related to academic achievement. Contrasting views: psychometric versus information processing; experimental versus correlational research.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11A OR PSCI 11B OR PSCI 11C OR PSYCH 7A OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11A OR PSY BEH 11B OR PSY BEH 11C )

allCourses.title: Advanced Writing for Education Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Writing for multiple audiences and purposes about central concepts in education sciences, such as schools as organizations; social structures in education and stratification; individual decision making, government regulation and markets; human development and learning.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Interdisciplinary Topics in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of issues in education from interdisciplinary perspectives. Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Principles and Practices of Coaching Sports I
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on foundational theories and instructional practices in coaching sports from fourth grade to the collegiate level. Prepares students for the coach's mandatory state certification examination for high school sports in California.

allCourses.title: Social Development in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of contextual, psychosocial, and biological factors contributing to the social development of children and adolescents. Theoretical perspectives, empirical findings, and methodological issues are emphasized. Implications of the scientific evidence for practical and policy decision-making surrounding development are discussed.
