allCourses.title: Principles and Practices of K–6 After School Sports and Fitness
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on foundational theories and instructional practices in after-school sports and fitness for K–6 students. Includes a 20-hour field experience in an after-school setting.

allCourses.title: Advanced Fieldwork in After-School Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Capstone fieldwork experience for students seeking to earn the Department of Education-sponsored Certificate in After-School Education. Students are required to complete 50 or more hours of fieldwork and related assignments at an instructor-approved after-school program.

allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Early Childhood Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Advanced study of early childhood education under the direction of a faculty member, coupled with a community-based practicum.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Directed Research in Education
allCourses.restriction: Sophomores only. Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Individually or in small groups, students are exposed to or participate in work related to a faculty member's research. Students also attend a weekly seminar and complete a research paper or comparable project.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Intensified advanced study in areas in which a student has considerable background, under the direction of a faculty member who will guide and evaluate the study.

allCourses.title: Outcomes of Schooling/Student Assessment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education-MA/PhD Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on establishment of learning goals and assessment tools that are valid for all students, inform educational decisions, and promote educational success. Provides critical examination of different forms of assessment used in K–12 schools, including developmental assessments and appropriate interventions.

allCourses.title: Design of Learning Environments for Teachers in Secondary School Subjects
allCourses.description: Research on comprehension, conceptual understanding, reasoning, critical thinking, and problem solving with applications to pedagogy in secondary school subjects. Required for M.A.T. single subject students, unless substitution of Education 207 is authorized.

allCourses.title: Reading and Writing Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers major theories and evidence about mechanisms and factors that contribute to development and difficulties with reading and writing skills. These include language, cognition, biological and environmental factors, bilingual and second language acquisition, and educational implications.

allCourses.title: Writing Theory and Practice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of histories, theories, and research in the field of composition studies from 1950 to the present. Addresses the influences of theory and research on teaching practice at K–12 and college levels.

allCourses.title: Literacy and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theoretical, historical, and contemporary relationships of technology and literacy. Topics include online communication, multimodality, video games, the use of technology for literacy instruction in schools, and research approaches for investigating literacy development with technology.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Digital Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students are introduced to historical, constructionist, instructionist, and new literacies perspectives through reading major works in educational technology and discussing how they apply to both teaching and research.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Teaching, Learning, and Educational Improvement
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced seminar designed to engage students in highly interactive examination of current issues in teaching and learning. Topics and content vary by quarter, depending upon research interests of the faculty and students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 10 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Developing Adolescent Literacy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how adolescents leverage vocabulary knowledge, word-reading skills, background understanding, and knowledge of content-specific text features to master an increasing range of texts both independently and for subject-area learning.

allCourses.title: Longitudinal and Advanced Structural Equation Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers advanced and longitudinal structural equation models. Topics include measurement invariance, growth curve models, measurement models, mixture models, and missing data.

allCourses.title: Research Epistemologies and Methodologies
allCourses.restriction: Ed.D. Program students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to epistemological underpinnings of educational research and to a range of research methodologies in education. Includes examination of quantitative and qualitative studies through reading and analyzing contemporary research. Critique of selected research studies pertinent to educational practice and policy.

allCourses.title: Oral Language Acquisition and Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Learn about research on domains of development in oral language (phonology, vocabulary, grammar, and extended discourse), bilingual development, and second language acquisition with attention to cognitive, biological, and environmental factors. Focus on learning in school settings and educational implications.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Educational Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced seminar focused on innovative educational research methods and analytic techniques. Topics and content vary by quarter, depending upon the research interests of the faculty and students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Learning Analytics Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a survey of learning analytics (LA), emphasizing its application across educational contexts, rather than its underlying algorithmic details. A comprehensive overview orients students to this nascent field and prepares them for advanced research in LA.

allCourses.title: Learning Analytics Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Helps students gain hands-on experience working as educational data scientists, while simultaneously learning some of the key guiding principles behind effectively using data to make predictions and decisions. Culminates in an interdisciplinary group research project.

allCourses.title: Learning, Development, and Culture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores issues of learning and development through a cultural lens. The interplay between culture and learning and culture and development is analyzed through the discussion of relevant readings from both psychological and anthropological research traditions.

allCourses.title: University Teaching: Concepts and Practices
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Prepares doctoral students for course design and instruction at the university level. Addresses topics including the university teaching context, preparing a syllabus, and inclusive teaching and learning.

allCourses.title: Science Education for the 21st-Century Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Aims to develop foundational understanding about science education research. Contemporary research from early childhood through high school is introduced. Issues of equity, social justice, pedagogy, professional development, and innovation in and out of school settings are addressed.

allCourses.title: Theories of Human Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines developmental theory as a guide for research and practice in education. The evolution of classical development theories and the emergence of new theoretical models are considered. Theoretical perspectives include ecological systems, life course, psychobiology, attachment, and social-cognitive theories.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Human Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines seminal concepts, issues, and theories that underlie contemporary developmental science. Students develop an understanding of these concepts, and develop their skills in using theory as a guide in their own research and practice.

allCourses.title: The History and Culture of Schooling in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Considers the historical, cultural, and structural processes that contextualize American schooling. In particular, examines the roles of race, class, and gender in the context of public education in the United States.

allCourses.title: Interrogating Race and Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critically explores how race is a socially constructed concept and how it manifests itself in American society. Attention is given to African American, Asian, and Mexican communities throughout U.S. history, with particular emphasis on educational inequality.

allCourses.title: Mathematics Cognition and Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of mathematical cognition, learning, and development. Combines readings from cognitive and developmental psychology, education, and learning sciences with the purpose of identifying the most useful applications of cognitive theory and methods for educational research and practice.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Atypical Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Includes advanced examination of current issues in theories of atypical development, assessment, and intervention as applied to special needs. Understanding physical and/or cognitive mechanisms of child development and disorders. Knowledge and skills for areas of disability.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 5 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Measurement and Psychometrics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on appraisal and development of measures, measurement theory, and its application using a classical test theory approach. Topics include scaling, construction, reliability and validity assessment, and item analysis; as well as cross-cultural and cross-linguistic considerations in test development.

allCourses.title: Applied Linguistics and Literacy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines research in applied linguistics as related to teaching literacy. Overview of language knowledge required to understand development and instruction of literacy.  Topics include English language structures, psychological processing of these structures, and methodologies to study language and literacy.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Teaching and Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Situates learning in relation to teaching, content, and context. Locates the work of teaching and learning as a cultural practice and considers the limitations of existing theories for advancing learning opportunities for historically under-served and under-resourced communities.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Human Development in Context
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced seminar designed to engage students in highly interactive examination of current issues in human development. Topics and content vary by quarter, depending upon the research interests of the faculty and students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 10 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience and Human Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the latest empirical work at the intersection of neuroscience, cognitive psychology, developmental science, and educational practice; explores how educational neuroscience fits within those fields; and discusses the main conceptual and practical challenges facing the field.

allCourses.title: Children’s Sense Making in Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Investigates elementary students as individuals who construct understanding of concepts through their interactions with others and the world around them. Observations of children in informal settings to analyze learning in context.

allCourses.title: The Policy Environment of Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines research and public perceptions about school-based educational processes, the influence of institutional structures and educational policy on the lives of teachers, and the challenges of school reform at the local and classroom levels.

allCourses.title: Learning Inside and Outside of School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: A field-based course focused on observing adolescents in out-of-school contexts to examine adolescent learning and development in a range of contexts, how out-of-school contexts motivate learning and development, and consider the implications for teaching.

allCourses.title: Teaching Investigations: Identifying Dilemmas of Practice
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on identifying problems of teaching practice that arise in student teaching, examining the theoretical foundations that underlie problems of practice, and developing approaches for inquiring into strategies to systematically address instructional challenges.

allCourses.title: Teaching Investigations: Exploring Dilemmas of Practice
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on exploring problems of teaching practice that arise in student teaching, drawing on research to examine the theoretical foundations that underlie problems of practice, and to propose courses of action to address and study educational interventions.

allCourses.title: Understanding Teacher Agency
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Considers how teachers can become agents of change within their school contexts, through their participation in professional organizations and via social media. Candidates experiment with using different avenues for sharing images of practice and action research.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Education: Disciplinary Perspectives
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides insights into educational organizations and processes by developing understanding of concepts used by four different disciplines (economics, history, psychology, and sociology) to analyze key issues and phenomenon in the field of education that profoundly influence individual life course outcomes.

allCourses.title: Research Practice Partnerships
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to research-practice partnerships (RPPs). It examines the distinctive characteristics of this approach to education improvement by discussing examples of established partnerships and inviting students to become familiar with methods and tools to advance RPP work.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Educational Policy and Politics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An in-depth study of topics relevant to educational reform and policy-making. Topics include: the policy-making process, the role of values and interest groups, policy analysis, equality of educational opportunity, systemic reform, implementation, and politics at the school site.

allCourses.title: Social Organization of Schools and Classrooms
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how schools are organizations with ambiguous goals, faced with challenges around effective leadership and cooperation, part of loosely coupled systems, and subject to coercive, normative, and mimemtic pressures from organizational environments, shaping institutional practices and structures.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Educational Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews disciplinary models that economists and sociologists employ in approaching education-related policy issues, including markets as emergent systems, human capital, social and cultural capital, and rational choice and institutional models of administrators and teachers.

allCourses.title: College Access and Persistence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to how social, political, and economic forces impact college access and persistence in the U.S. higher education system. Investigates historical perspectives and theoretical underpinnings of college access and retention research and the link between K–12 schooling and postsecondary stratification.

allCourses.title: Immigration and the New Second Generation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on Asian, Latino, and Black children of immigrants. Investigates how today's second generation adapts, incorporates into the U.S. social structure, transforms the social and economic landscape. Explores assimilation, immigrant families/communities, language, racial/ethnic identities, gender, education, changing U.S. racial structure.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Educational Policy and Social Context
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced seminar designed to engage students in highly interactive examination of current issues in educational policy and social context. Topics and content will vary by quarter, depending upon the research interests of the faculty and students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 10 times.

allCourses.title: Community Research and Action
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the theoretical underpinnings and research approaches of the field of Community Psychology. Project-based course focused on research and action in communities, organizations, and other extra-individual units (e.g., schools).

allCourses.title: The Arts, Human Development, and Social Context
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the state of empirical knowledge on the impact of visual and performing arts education on the development of academic, communication, and social-emotional skills. The role of the arts in forming personal and cultural identity is discussed.

allCourses.title: Social and Cultural Foundations of Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a critical understanding of the social and cultural foundations of education through reproduction theory. Explores the unique ways in which culture and power intersect within schools and schooling systems to reproduce and resist educational inequality.

allCourses.title: Economic Foundations of Education and Social Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Beginning/intermediate microeconomics course provides students with an introduction to how economists think about household decision-making, markets, benefit-cost analysis, social policy issues in general and education policy in particular.

allCourses.title: Applied Regression Analysis for Education and Social Scientific Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a working knowledge of multiple regression and the statistical analysis of longitudinal data. Topics include a review of the OLS regression model, event-history methods, and various other techniques for analyzing longitudinal data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EDUC 288A. EDUC 288A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Design-Based Implementation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores design-based implementation research (DBIR) to organize research and improvement efforts in education. Delves deeper into different techniques of partnership development, design, implementation, and improvement science to build a repertoire of practices for students' studies.

allCourses.title: Out-of-School Learning and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theory, research, and policy concerning out-of-school time and youth development. Several out-of-school contexts are considered (e.g, unsupervised care, informal leisure activities, and organized activities). A range of developmental outcomes are considered (e.g., achievement, social-emotional competence, and physical health).

allCourses.title: Studies of Professional and Staff Development
allCourses.restriction: Doctoral students only.
allCourses.description: Research and theory of effective strategies for professional and staff development. Topics include: adult learning as related to professional growth of teachers, staff development as vehicle for systemic reform, reforms to enhance teacher professionalization and empowerment.

allCourses.title: Early Childhood Education Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers core topics in the field of early education policy. Integrates research from the various perspectives relevant to child policy in a practical way to understand the mechanisms of intervention and to develop policy solutions.

allCourses.title: Experimental Designs in Educational Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to enable students to think critically about experimental research, and to develop an understanding of how to design and conduct experiments. The overall goal is to prepare students to independently plan and implement an experimental research study.

allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Further developing qualitative inquiry skills for examining human interaction and studying lived experiences of individuals and communities. Practices and techniques for collecting, working with, and analyzing qualitative data to develop and justify claims.

allCourses.title: Research Methods: Hierarchical Linear Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Philosophy Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Research data often have a hierarchical structure, which require multi-level models. Students learn to use HLM; conduct appropriate analyses; and write the methods and results section for a peer-reviewed journal article. Previous coursework in regression is required.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to qualitative research methodologies and methods and explores strengths and challenges of this research tradition. Topics include logistical and ethical issues, reliability, validity and generalizability, and the role of reflexivity. Students will also engage in fieldwork.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides methods for conducting and analyzing qualitative research in educational settings. Topics include data collection, coding, representing qualitative data, and using software for qualitative data analysis.

allCourses.title: Theories of Learning Cognition
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of theories applicable to learning in schools and extracurricular contexts. Cognitive, psychometric, behavioral, and neuroscience perspectives are applied to such topics as memory, knowledge structures, problem solving, motivation, self-referent beliefs, expertise, assessment, and cognitive abilities, including intelligence.

allCourses.title: Quantitative Data Analysis in Education Research and Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistical aspects of survey-based evaluations and quantitative research in education. Includes sampling, coding open-ended information, data management, scale construction, statistical analysis, and presentation of findings. Students analyze data sets - a district-based evaluation and a national survey - using SPPS.

allCourses.title: Causal Inference: Methods for Program Evaluation and Policy Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a comprehensive overview of how to perform some more advanced statistical methods useful in answering policy questions using observational or experimental data.

allCourses.title: Educational, Social, and Behavioral Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed for graduate students with previous course work in statistics, including experience with statistical software such as SPSS or Stata. The emphasis is on regression analysis and the general linear model. Students learn to analyze real data using Stata.

allCourses.title: Structural Equation Modeling for Educ, Soc & Behavioral Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Rigorous introduction to structural equation modeling for students with strong prior course work in statistics. Topics include path diagrams, SEM with observed variables, factor analysis, SEM with latent variables. Maximum likelihood estimating, goodness-of-fit measures, nested models, related topics.

allCourses.title: Use of Video in Educational Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with conceptual and methodological tools for using video in educational research.  Students work with their own video data or with publicly accessible databases.

allCourses.title: Pre-Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Independent study course taken under the direction of a faculty member who guides the student's research. May include guidance on data collection, methodology, human subjects protocol, conference presentation, scholarly publication, program benchmark activities.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Professional Writing in Educational Research I
allCourses.description: First of a two-course series designed to extend students’ knowledge of conducting and publishing educational research. Topics include the logic of research and how to effectively communicate research findings, with particular emphasis on proficient scientific writing.

allCourses.title: Professional Writing in Educational Research II
allCourses.description: Second of a two-course series designed to extend students’ knowledge of conducting and publishing educational research. Topics include the logic of research and how to effectively communicate research findings, with particular emphasis on proficient scientific writing.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research on topics related to education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Reserach
allCourses.restriction: Doctoral students only.
allCourses.description: Specifically designed for students researching and writing their dissertations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: 21st Century Literacies
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of literacies required for academic and career success in the 21st century. Issues addressed include reading, writing, academic language, research skills, media and technology skills, scientific literacy, critical thinking, communication, collaboration, and creativity.

allCourses.title: Directed Elementary Field Experiences in Diverse Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Fieldwork experiences and seminars to provide introduction to the California Teaching Performance Expectations, including guidelines for professional expectations, observation and participation in classrooms, instructional planning, classroom management, and formative experiences and preparation for the state-mandated Teaching Performance Assessment.

allCourses.title: Directed Secondary Field Experiences
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Field work experiences and seminars to provide introduction to the California Teaching Performance Expectations, including guidelines for professional expectations, observation and participation in classrooms, instructional planning, classroom management, and formative experiences and preparation for the State-mandated Teaching Performance Assessment.

allCourses.title: Student Teaching in the Elementary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching seminars prepare candidates for assumption of classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements. Four full days a week of student teaching in public school elementary classrooms in winter quarter and five full days in spring quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Learning to Learn from Teaching in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Analytic tools for (1) observing and reflecting on observed instruction; (2) examining student thinking and the relationship between teaching and learning; (3) understanding particular components of the teaching/learning process; and (4) planning effective instruction including innovative teaching practices.

allCourses.title: Supervised Teaching in Bilingual Education, Elementary
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching experiences in bilingual public school classrooms to include orientation, regular seminars, and preparation for bilingual classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements and in conjunction with the public school calendar.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Student Teaching in Intermediate/Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching includes orientation, seminars, and preparation for and assumption of secondary school classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements and in conjunction with public school calendar. Five full days a week in both winter and spring quarters.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Teaching Physical and Health Education in Elementary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods of teaching physical education for the elementary classroom teacher. Through an interactive environment, students experience the California Physical Education and Health content standards with appropriate pedagogy. Concepts address motor skills, physical fitness, and personal responsibility for lifelong health.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Mathematics I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Scope, sequence, and methods of teaching mathematics at all levels of elementary school. Presented through lectures, discussions, demonstrations, and exploration of a variety of materials. Covers how to plan lessons, motivate students, diagnose difficulties, and evaluate learning in mathematics.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Mathematics II
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Part two of a course addressing pedagogical methods for elementary mathematics. Lectures, discussions, and exploration of instructional strategies and materials support preservice teacher development in the critical areas of planning, instruction, and assessment for conceptual understanding in mathematics.

allCourses.title: Curriculum Methods in Elementary Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective elementary teachers learn how to teach science in grades K-8. Covers state science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, and criteria for selecting science curriculum materials.

allCourses.title: Curriculum Methods in Elementary Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective elementary teachers learn how to teach science in grades K-8. Covers state science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, criteria for selecting science curriculum materials, and how to plan science lessons, units, experiments, projects, and demonstrations.

allCourses.title: Teaching the Visual and Performing Arts in Elementary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the issues and practices — including student diversity, academic literacy, and interdisciplinary content —  involved in integrating the California visual and performing arts curriculum framework and academic content standards with developmentally appropriate teaching strategies for the elementary classroom. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Reading
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Teaching an integrated reading/language arts program in the elementary classroom. Implementing theories, principles, and methods which are research and reality-based. Creating a child-centered, language-rich program to meet needs of children in multicultural/multilingual settings.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Languages other than English in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prepares future teachers of foreign language or primary/home language. Emphasizes hands-on, practical strategies for communication-based instruction and authentic assessment in reading, writing, listening, speaking, and culture.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Social Science in the Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theories, strategies, and methodologies related to the teaching of history and social science in the secondary school. Emphasis on the planning, delivery, and assessment of lessons reflecting an understanding of the History-Social Science Framework for California.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching English in the Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to teaching reading, writing, and speaking skills in secondary school. Emphasis upon integrative approach to teaching literature, composition, and grammar consistent with the California State Framework. Practice in the design of lesson plans that are both integrated and cumulative.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Visual Arts in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theory, curriculum, and strategies for teaching visual arts in the secondary school. Emphasis on the planning, delivery, and assessment of lessons consistent with California State Framework and content standards.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Mathematics in Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theories, strategies, and methodologies related to the teaching of mathematics in the secondary school. Emphasis on the planning, delivery, and assessment of lessons reflecting an understanding of the Mathematics Framework for California and the recommendations of professional organizations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units.

allCourses.title: Teaching Science in Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective secondary science teachers learn how to teach science in grades 7-12. Covers State science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, criteria for selecting science curricular materials, and how to plan science lessons, units, experiments, projects, and demonstrations.

allCourses.title: Applied Instructional Strategies in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. EDUC 342 and EDUC 342A may not both be taken for credit.
allCourses.description: Application of pedagogy and research to practice teaching experiences in the secondary schools. A continuation of the methodology course series with an emphasis on the needs of students with culturally diverse backgrounds. Conducted in a five-week format.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Applied Instructional Strategies in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. EDUC 342 and EDUC 342B may not both be taken for credit.
allCourses.description: Application of pedagogy and research to practice teaching experiences in the secondary schools. A continuation of the methodology course series with an emphasis on the needs of students with culturally diverse backgrounds. Conducted in a five-week format.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Reading and Writing in Middle School and High School Classrooms
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasis is placed upon understanding the literacy processes (listening, speaking, viewing, reading, and writing) as they relate to all Single Subject areas. Teachers are guided to integrate literacy-related strategies with curriculum-based goals supported in the California State Frameworks.

allCourses.title: Culture, Diversity, and Educational Equity
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of and social theories about the origins and consequences of U.S. racial, gender, and social inequality, and the effects of poverty and racism on the educational opportunities and outcomes of minority groups in the United States.

allCourses.title: Educational Equity and the Exceptional Learner
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Knowledge, skills, and strategies to teach exceptional learners in the general education classroom. Legislation pertaining to the education of exceptional learners. Role of general education teacher in the special education process. Inclusive curriculum to provide equal access to content.

allCourses.title: Educational Equity and the Exceptional Learner I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on knowledge, skills, and strategies needed to teach special populations in general education secondary classrooms. Covers categories and characteristics of disability and exceptionality, state and federal legislation, and the role of general education teachers in the special education process.

allCourses.title: Educational Equity and the Exceptional Learner II
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the use of differentiated instruction to meet special needs and the creation of a positive, inclusive learning environment that provides access to the core curriculum for special needs students.

allCourses.title: Theories and Methods of English Language Development Applied to Secondary Students
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theories and methods of English language development and instruction of English language learners, with focus on secondary students. Includes language acquisition theory, language and content, assessment strategies, and preparation of curricula and instruction for grades 7–12 English language learners.

allCourses.title: Media and Information Literacy in the Secondary Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how teachers can help their students to become critical, ethical, and effective users of technological resources in the secondary classroom. Students learn tools for evaluating, selecting, and incorporating appropriate learning technologies into the secondary classroom.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary Social Science and Information Literacy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods of instruction for Social Science at the K–6 level. Includes integration of the use of technology, development of content literacy, and use of evidence to construct arguments.

allCourses.title: The Adolescent Learner
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Issues of adolescent development and learning in family, school, and community contexts from biological, psychological, cognitive, and social perspectives. Focuses on how adolescents learn, what motivates them to learn, and how schools and teachers contribute to adolescents’ growth.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary Language Arts  and English Language Development
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods, instructional practices, and assessment strategies for teaching English-Language Arts, with a focus on instructional practices for supporting English Language Learners. Focuses on core language arts topics, including composition of persuasive, expository, and narrative texts; speaking; and listening.

allCourses.title: Instructional Design and Education Technology for the Elementary Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how teachers can effectively integrate educational technologies for teaching and learning in the elementary school classroom. Students learn tools for evaluating, selecting, and incorporating appropriate technologies into their classroom activities.

allCourses.title: Learning and Child Development
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Issues of child development and learning in family, school, and community contexts from biological, psychological, cognitive, and social perspectives. Focuses on how young children learn and develop, how schools and teachers contribute to children’s growth, and implications for instruction.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Theories of Development and Learning Applied to Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an introductory examination of central theories of human development and learning in their application to contemporary educational settings.

allCourses.title: Origins, Purposes, and Central Issues in K-12 Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the role of education in U.S. society and to central issues in K–12 education. Education is studied from four different perspectives: social, historical, philosophical, and political.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of current issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. Topics include dimensions of bilingualism, the effects of bilingualism on children's linguistic and cognitive development, bilingual education programs, literacy, special needs, and assessment.

allCourses.title: Knowing and Learning in Mathematics and Science
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary study of knowing and learning in secondary school mathematics and science. Topics include standards for knowing, scientific epistemologies, mental representations, problem solving, expert-novice studies, assessment, and domain-specific thinking, learning, and teaching. Applied analysis of learning through clinical interviews.

allCourses.title: Interdisciplinary Topics in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of issues in education from interdisciplinary perspectives. Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the fields of Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering, including possible careers in both traditional and new emerging areas. Background on both the Electrical Engineering and the Computer Engineering majors, curriculum requirements, specializations, and faculty research interests.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computational Methods in Electrical and Computer Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to computers and structured programming. Binary Data Representation. Hands-on experience with a high-level structured programming language. Introduction to algorithm efficiency. Applications of structured programming in solving engineering problems. Programming laboratory.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"OR":["MATH 2A","AP CALCULUS AB","AP CALCULUS BC","AP CALCULUS AB SUB"]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 2A OR AP CALCULUS AB OR AP CALCULUS BC OR AP CALCULUS AB SUB )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Vision
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The use of digital computers for the analysis of visual scenes; image formation and sensing, color, segmentation, shape estimation, motion, stereo, pattern classification, computer architectures, applications. Computer experiments are used to illustrate fundamental principles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: System Software
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multiprogramming, interrupt, processes, kernel, parallelism, critical sections, deadlocks, communication, multiprocessing, multilevel memory management, binding, name management, file systems, protection, resource allocation, scheduling. Experience with concurrent programming, synchronization mechanisms, interprocess communication.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 112 AND ( EECS 114 OR I&C SCI 46 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Organization of Digital Computers
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Building blocks and organization of digital computers, the arithmetic, control, and memory units, and input/out devices and interfaces. Microprogramming and microprocessors.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Organization of Digital Computers Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Specification and implementation of a processor-based system using a hardware description language such as VHDL. Hands-on experience with design tools including simulation, synthesis, and evaluation using testbenches.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Processor Hardware/Software Interfaces
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science and Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Hardware/software interfacing, including memory and bus interfaces, devices, I/O, and compiler code generation/instruction scheduling. Experience microcontroller programming and interfacing. Specific compiler code generation techniques including local variable and register allocations, instruction dependence and scheduling, and code optimization.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Data Structures and Algorithms
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces abstract behavior of classes data structures, alternative implementations, informal analysis of time and space efficiency. Also introduces classic algorithms and efficient algorithm design techniques (recursion, divide-and-conquer, branch-and-bound, dynamic programming).

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Data Management
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for applications. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational design theory, and Structured Query Language (SQL) programming.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Parallel Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: General introduction to parallel computing focusing on parallel algorithms and architectures. Parallel models: Flynn's taxonomy, dataflow models. Parallel architectures: systolic arrays, hypercube architecture, shared memory machines, dataflow machines, reconfigurable architectures. Parallel algorithms appropriate to each machine type area also discussed.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction of basic concepts in artificial intelligence. Knowledge representation and reasoning, search, planning, declarative programing, problem solving, and data science.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: VLSI
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design techniques for Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) systems and chips. Review CMOS and related process technologies; primitives such as logic gates and larger design blocks; layout; floor planning; design hierarchy, component interfaces; use of associated CAD tools for design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to computers and programming. Python programming syntax/style, types. Numbers and sequences. Control flow. I/O and errors/exceptions. Function calling, parameter passing, formal arguments, return values. Variable scoping. Programming laboratory.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"OR":["MATH 2A","AP CALCULUS AB","AP CALCULUS BC","AP CALCULUS AB SUB"]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 2A OR AP CALCULUS AB OR AP CALCULUS BC OR AP CALCULUS AB SUB )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Parallel Computing
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of parallel computing, focusing on parallel algorithms and architectures. Topics include design of parallel and I/O efficient algorithms, basics of parallel machine architectures, and current/emerging programming models (shared memory, distributed memory, and accelerators).

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: System Security
allCourses.description: Fundamentals and practices of system security. Topics include cryptographic (encryption, decryption, and message authentication), software vulnerabilities (buffer overflow), network security (layer 2-7 attacks and defenses and PKI), web security (XSS and XSRF), and privacy.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Communication Systems I
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to analog communication systems including effects of noise. Modulation-demodulation for AM, DSB-SC, SSB, VSB, QAM, FM, PM, and PCM with application to radio, television, and telephony. Signal processing as applied to communication systems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Communication Systems II
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Signal space analysis. Optimum receivers for digital communication. Maximum a posteriori and maximum likelihood detection. Matched filter and correlation receiver.  PAM, QAM, PSK, FSK, and MSK and their performance. Introduction to equalization, synchronization, information theory, and error control codes.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Antenna Design for Wireless Communication Links
allCourses.description: Analysis and synthesis of antennas and antenna arrays.  Adaptive arrays and digital beam forming for advanced wireless links.  Friis transmission formula.  Wireless communication equations for cell-site and mobile antennas, interference, slow and fast fading in mobile communication.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Electrical Engineering Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Vector calculus, complex functions, and linear algebra with applications to electrical engineering problems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computer Networks
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Computer network architectures, protocols, and applications.  Internet congestion control, addressing, and routing. Local area networks. Multimedia networking.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Continuous-Time Signals and Systems
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Characteristics and properties of continuous-time (analog) signals and systems. Analysis of linear time-invariant continuous-time systems using differential equation convolutional models. Analysis of these systems using Laplace transforms, Fourier series, and Fourier transforms. Examples from applications to telecommunications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Digital Signal Processing
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Nature of sampled data, sampling theorem, difference equations, data holds, z-transform, w-transform, digital filters, Butterworth and Chebychev filters, quantization effects.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Digital Signal Processing Design and Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design and implementation of algorithms on a DSP processor and using computer simulation. Applications in signal and image processing, communications, radar, etc.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Senior Design Project I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Science Engineering Majors only. Electrical Engineering Majors only. Computer Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Teaches problem definition, detailed design, integration, and testability with teams of students specifying, designing, building, and testing complex systems. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of engineering decisions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Senior Design Project II
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors only. Electrical Engineering Majors only. Computer Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Teaches problem definition, detailed design, integration, and testability with teams of students specifying, designing, building, and testing complex systems. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of engineering decisions. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (CMOSFET), device scaling, device modeling and fabrication, equivalent circuits, and their applications for digital, analog, RF.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Metal-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MESFET), heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT), microwave semiconductor devices, equivalent circuits, device modeling and fabrication, microwave amplifiers, transmitters, and receivers.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nanotechnology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fabrication and characterization techniques of electrical circuit elements at the nanometer scale. Quantized conductance, semiconductor quantum dots, single electron transistors, molecular wires, carbon nanotubes, self-assembly of nano-circuit elements, quantum methods of information processing.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro-System Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale.  Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Two- and three-dimensional boundary value problems, dielectric waveguides and other special waveguides, microwave networks and antenna arrays, electromagnetic properties of materials, and electromagnetic optics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering electromagnetics (e.g. EECS 180A).

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Analysis and Design II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design of microwave amplifiers using computer-aided design tools. Covers low-noise amplifiers, multiple stage amplifiers, broadband amplifiers, and power amplifiers. Hybrid circuit design techniques including filters and baluns. Theory and design rules for microwave oscillator design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: RF Antenna Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced transmission line design, radiation of electromagnetic waves, dipole antennas, antenna arrays, advanced antenna designs, and practical design considerations in communications systems. Course is supplemented by RF design tools and modeling.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Optical Communications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Lasers and Photonics
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of lasers and applications, including Gaussian beam propagation, interaction of optical radiation with matters, and concepts of optical gain and feedback. Applications are drawn from diverse fields of optical communication, signal processing, and material diagnosis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate course work in electromagnetic theory and atomic physics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nano Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theory and practice of modern nanoscale imaging techniques and applications. Traces the development of microscopy from ancient times to modern day techniques used for visualizing the nano-world from atoms to molecules including hands-on experience in the laboratory.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Optical Communications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level Engineering Electromagnetics I (e.g. EECS E80A).

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fabrication of Biomedical and Wearable Microdevices
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers preliminary details on prototyping and fabrication techniques for biomedical and wearable microdevices. Fabrication and behavior of modern biomed device materials such as hydrogel, PDMS, biopolymer, smart materials, and their uses are introduced.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Knowledge of undergraduate-level basic physics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro/Nano Biotechnology and Biosensing: Fundamentals, Designs, and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides insight into the current topics in Micro/Nanoscience, Micro/Nanotechnology fundamentals, and their modern-day applications in life sciences. Focus is on Micro/Nanodevices; Sensors’ fundamentals; NanoBioSensors; Microfluidics; Micro/Nanofabrication, detection system-level characterization; performance determination; solid-state materials; and more.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Bioinstrumentation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces instrumentation used in biomedical research, clinical medicine, and health monitoring. Interfacing of bioelectronics and biomedical sensing are taught with the most updated methods. The integration of bioinstrumentation with data science and cloud computing are introduced.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Digital Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Digital representation of information. Specification, analysis, design and optimization or combinational and sequential logic, register-transfer components and register-transfer systems with datapaths and controllers. Introduction to high-level and algorithmic state-machines and custom processors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( EECS 10 OR EECS 12 OR ENGRMAE 10 OR I&C SCI 31 )

allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to common digital integrated circuits: gates, memory circuits, MSI components. Operating characteristics, specifications, applications. Design of simple combinational and sequential digital systems (arithmetic processors game-playing machines). Construction and debugging techniques using hardware description languages and CAD tools.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Object-Oriented Systems and Programming
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Primitive types and expressions. The class and method definition. Information hiding and encapsulation. Objects and reference. Overloading. Constructors. Inheritance basics. Programming with inheritance. Dynamic binding and polymorphism. Exception handling. An overview of streams and file input/output. Programming laboratory.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Discrete-Time Signals and Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of discrete-time linear-time-invariant (DTLTI) systems in the time domain and using z-transforms.  Introduction to techniques based on Discrete-Time, Discrete, and Fast Fourier Transforms. Examples of their application to digital signal processing and digital communications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Probability
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sets and set operations; nature of probability, sample spaces, fields of events, probability measures; conditional probability, independence, random variables, distribution functions, density functions, conditional distributions and densities; moments, characteristic functions, random sequences, independent and Markov sequences.

allCourses.title: Network Analysis I

allCourses.description: Modeling and analysis of electrical networks. Basic network theorems. Sinusoidal steady state and transient analysis of RLC networks and the impedance concept.

allCourses.title: Case Studies in Environmental Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of real problems involving toxic chemicals and the human food, air, water supplies, occupational exposures, and lifestyles. Formal problems will be considered by small groups of students and discussed by the class.

allCourses.title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to basic principles of toxicology. Absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) of xenobiotics are covered and illustrated with specific examples.

allCourses.title: Psychosocial Occupational Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Importance of psychosocial work environment for workers’ health and productivity has increased with changing technology, work organization, demographics, and occupation/industry structures. This advanced occupational epidemiology course focuses on psychosocial work environment as exposures, and workers’ health and productivity as outcomes.

allCourses.title: Neurotoxicology
allCourses.description: The effects of various harmful chemicals upon nervous system function. Emphasis given to the molecular events underlying neurological damage and to the relation of such processes to basic mechanisms of neurobiology.

allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanistic analysis of responses occurring in various organ systems of experimental animals and humans exposed to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation. Review distinctive cellular and tissue structure and physiological function of the various organ systems.

allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanistic analysis of responses occurring in various organ systems of experimental animals and humans exposed to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation. Review of distinctive cellular and tissue structure and physiological function of the various organ systems.

allCourses.title: Experimental Design and Interpretation of Toxicology Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to methods of structuring toxicology experiments and analyzing data, including experimental design, data distributions, sample sizes, hypothesis testing, linear regression, analysis of variance, multiple comparison testing, and non-parametric tests.

allCourses.title: Inhalation Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The principles and practice of laboratory inhalation toxicology.  Topics include aerosols, gases, respiratory tract structure and function, lung defenses, aerosol deposition exposure techniques, characterization of exposure atmospheres, experimental designs, animal models, and regulations and guidelines.

allCourses.title: Industrial Toxicology
allCourses.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only. Environ Health Sci and Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Convergence of agents (chemical, physical, biological, or psychosocial) in environment can emerge as diseases influenced by social, political, and economic factors, allowing them to become rooted in society. How these agents from various spheres come together and impact human health.

allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

allCourses.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Surveys the general principles, basic mathematical methods, and practices of environmental modeling and human health risk assessment. Topics include advection-dispersion models, risk management, and risk perception. Students conduct an original risk assessment as a final group project.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Environmental Toxicology
allCourses.description: With consent from a faculty member who will supervise the program, a student may receive credit for individual study in some area of toxicology, culminating in the completion of a scholarly paper on the subject.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Occupational Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to psychological and social factors in the workplace that affect health and productivity. Goal is to support redesign of the workplace and social situations that can reduce stress-related illness risks, and increase humane forms of productivity and competence development.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Occupational Toxicology
allCourses.description: Discussions with clinical and research faculty in environmental toxicology and occupational medicine on current toxicology problems in the workplace and critical review of current publications in the field.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Environmental Health Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research problems and issues by students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and guests, covering the broad research and policy areas of environmental health sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
