allCourses.description: Analysis, modeling, and management of civil engineering systems. Statistics and system performance studies, probabilistic models and simulation, basic economics and capital investments, project elements and organization, managerial concepts and network technique, project scheduling. Emphasis on real-world examples. Laboratory sessions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Methods IV: Systems Analysis and Decision-Making
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis and optimization for decision-making in civil and infrastructural systems. Topics include linear programming formulations and solution algorithms, network models, and logistical models. Emphasis is on project-level and managerial decision-making and selection from alternative designs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 3D AND ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: GIS for Civil and Environmental Engineering
allCourses.description: GIS for CEE provides an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their various applications in civil and environmental engineering. Topics include GIS data formats, data queries, spatial and attribute data, spatial data analysis, coordinate systems, and raster data analysis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems I: Analysis and Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to analysis and design of fundamental transportation system components, basic elements of geometric and pavement design, vehicle flow and elementary traffic, basic foundations of transportation planning and forecasting. Laboratory sessions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems II: Operations and Control
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of urban traffic engineering, including data collection, analysis, and design. Traffic engineering studies, traffic flow theory, traffic control devices, traffic signals, capacity and level of service analysis of freeways and urban streets. Laboratory sessions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical foundations of transportation planning, design, and analysis methods. Theory and application of aggregate and disaggregate models for land use development, trip generation, destination, mode, and route choice. Transportation network analysis. Planning, design, and evaluation of system alternatives.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems IV: Freeway Operations and Control
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of traffic on urban freeways, including data collection analysis, and design. Traffic engineering studies, traffic flow theory, freeway traffic control devices, capacity, and level of service analysis of freeways and highways. Laboratory sessions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation and the Environment
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the impacts of motor vehicle transportation on the environment. Introduction to life cycle analysis applied to transportation. Basic economic tools for transportation externalities. Transportation planning, urban form, health, and the environment. Transportation sustainability.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Soil Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Mechanics of soils, composition and classification of soils, compaction, compressibility and consolidation, shear strength, seepage, bearing capacity, lateral earth pressure, retaining walls, piles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory procedures of soil testing for engineering problems.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Earthquake Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Nature of earthquakes, hazard analyses, structural dynamics for earthquake engineering, seismic design force determination methods: ELF, modal response spectrum, nonlinear time history analyses. Diaphragm analyses, redundancy, nonlinear response, ductile systems, hysteretic behavior. Basics of seismic design for steel, timber, concrete.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Stresses and strains, strain-stress diagrams, axial deformations, torsion, bending and shear stresses in beams, shear force and bending moment diagrams, combined stresses, principal stresses, Mohr's circle, deflection of beams, columns.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Experimental methods and fundamentals for mechanics of materials analysis.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 150 AND ( ENGR 30 OR ENGRCEE 30 OR ENGRMAE 30 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Structural Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of structural analysis and loading. Deformation of statically determinate and indeterminate structures. Influence lines. Structural systems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Structural Timber Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design of timber structures. Beams, columns, beam-columns, roof, and connections.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Ultimate strength design. Design of reinforced concrete beam sections. Design for shear and deflection. Design of columns. Design of isolated and combined footings. Laboratory sessions.   Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computer Methods in Structural Analysis and Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Matrix techniques for indeterminate framed structures. Computer implementation using the stiffness method. Software packages for design of reinforced concrete, steel, and/or timber structures.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Structural Steel Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design in steel of tension members, beams, columns, welded and bolted connections; eccentrically loaded and moment resistant joints; plate girders. Plastic design; load and resistance factor design. Composite construction; introduction to computer-aided design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Foundation Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Applications of soil mechanics principles to the analysis and design of shallow foundations, retaining walls, pile foundations, and braced cuts. Design criteria: bearing capacity, working loads and tolerable settlements, structural integrity of the foundation element. Damage from construction operations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Environmental Processes
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to environmental processes in air and water, mass balances, and transport phenomena. Fundamentals of water-quality engineering including water and wastewater treatment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 170 AND ( CHEM 1B OR CHEM H2B )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic concepts from general, physical, and analytical chemistry as they relate to environmental engineering. Particular emphasis on the fundamentals of equilibrium and kinetics as they apply to acid-base chemistry, gas solubility, and redox reactions. Laboratory sessions.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.description: Design of biological treatment processes. Topics include attached and suspended growth, aeration, anaerobic systems, process control, and economics. Design projects included.   Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Carbon and Energy Footprint Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Mass- and energy-balance analysis applied to water and wastewater treatment systems. Case studies include analysis of water supply, treatment, reclamation, and reuse.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Physical-Chemical Treatment Processes
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and dynamics of physical and chemical separation processes in water and wastewater treatment. Topics include coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, gas-transfer, membrane separations, and adsorption.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamental and applied principles of microbiology. Structures and functions of microorganisms, the microbiology of water, wastewater and soil used in environmental engineering, and the impact of microorganisms on human and environmental health.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Thermodynamic and mechanical fluid properties; fluid statics; control volume and differential approaches for mass, momentum, and energy; dimensional analysis and similarity.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Water Resources Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing the analysis and design of water resource systems including pressurized pipelines, pipe networks, channels, and ground water. Coverage of fluid mass, momentum and energy conservation, flow resistance, and related laboratory measurements in different systems. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Topics include conservation of fluid mass, storage properties of porous media, matrix compressibility, boundary conditions, flow nets, well hydraulics, groundwater chemistry, and solute transport. Design projects and computer applications included.

allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of hydrologic modeling are practiced. Concepts of watershed delineation, land use change impact, design studies, and GIS tools are discussed. Focus on the USACE (HEC) software tools (HEC-HMS, and HEC-RAS) along with their associated GIS interfaces.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Elements of the hydrologic cycle including precipitation, infiltration, evapotranspiration, ground water, and runoff. Unit Hydrograph theory and routing methods. Introduction to precipitation/runoff relationship and watershed modeling. Statistical methods and flood frequency analysis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fluid Mechanics of Open Channels
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of fluid motion in open channels. Navier-Stokes equations and one-dimensional momentum and energy principles. Topics include rapidly varied flow, flow resistance and turbulence, gradually varied flow, unsteady flow, and computational methods for channel flow modeling.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( CBE 120A OR ENGRCEE 170 OR ENGRMAE 130A ) AND ( BME 60B OR ENGRCEE 20 OR ENGRMAE 10 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Senior Design Practicum I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Civil Engineering Majors only. Environmental Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Team designs land development project including infrastructural, environmental, circulation aspects. Focus on traffic impact studies, design of roads, geometry, signals, geotechnical and hydrological analysis, design of structural elements, economic analysis. Oral/Written interim and final design reports. Laboratory sessions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 110 AND ENGRCEE 81A AND ENGRCEE 81B AND ( ENGRCEE 121 OR ENGRCEE 162 OR ENGRCEE 171 OR ENGRCEE 151C )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Senior Design Practicum II
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Civil Engineering Majors only. Environmental Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Team designs land development project including infrastructural, environmental, circulation aspects. Focus on traffic impact studies, design of roads, geometry, signals, geotechnical and hydrological analysis, design of structural elements, economic analysis. Oral/Written interim and final design reports. Laboratory sessions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Senior Design Practicum III
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Civil Engineering Majors only. Environmental Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Team designs land development project including infrastructural, environmental, circulation aspects. Focus on traffic impact studies, design of roads, geometry, signals, geotechnical and hydrological analysis, design of structural elements, economic analysis. Oral/Written interim and final design reports. Laboratory sessions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computational Problem Solving
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computer programming within a numerical computing environment (MATLAB or similar) including types of data representation, graphical display of data, and development of modular programs with application to engineering analysis and problem solving.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computational Problem Solving
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Engineering analysis and problem solving using MATLAB (or similar), including matrix algebra, solving systems of linear and nonlinear equations, numerical integration of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and coupled ODEs, and analysis of numerical errors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 3D AND ( BME 60B OR ENGRCEE 20 ) AND ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: GIS for Civil and Environmental Engineering
allCourses.description: GIS for CEE provides an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their various applications in civil and environmental engineering. Topics include GIS data formats, data queries, spatial and attribute data, spatial data analysis, coordinate systems, raster data analysis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Travel Demand Analysis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of transportation systems analysis. Theoretical aspects of travel demand. Travel behavior. Modeling of performance characteristics and costs of transportation modes. In-depth presentation of travel demand modeling techniques. Development of travel choice models including mode, route, and destination choice. Equilibrium.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Travel Demand Analysis II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Methods of discrete choice analysis and their applications in the modeling of transportation systems. Emphasis on the development of a sound understanding of theoretical aspects of discrete choice modeling that are useful in many applications in travel demand analysis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Travel Demand Analysis III: Activity-based Approaches
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The methodological underpinnings of activity-based travel demand modeling.  Presents methodologies within the context of a generalization of discrete choice modeling approaches, emphasizing the distinctions that separtate these two approaches and presenting appropriate mathematical and statistical tools to address these distinctions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems Analysis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to mathematical methods and models to address logistics and urban transportation problems. Techniques include stochastic models, queueing theory, linear programming, and introductory non-linear optimization.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems Analysis II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced mathematical methods and models to address logistics and urban transportation problems. Topics include network flows, advanced optimization techniques, network models, and heuristic algorithms.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transit Systems Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Planning methods for public transportation in urban areas. Technological and operating characteristics of vehicles, facilities, and systems.  Short-range planning techniques: data collection and analysis, demand analysis, mode choice, operational strategies, financial analysis.  Design of systems to improve performance.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical foundations of transportation planning, design, and analysis methods. Theory and application of aggregate and disaggregate models for land use development, trip generation, destination, mode, and route choice. Transportation network analysis. Planning, design, and evaluation of system alternatives.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Data Analysis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistical analysis of transportation data sources. Analysis of categorical and ordinal data. Regression and advanced multivariate analysis methods such as discriminant analysis, canonical correlation, and factor analysis. Sampling techniques, sample error and bias, survey instrument design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Transportation Planning Models II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and application of comprehensive transportation models. Network development, demand modeling, and equilibrium assignment. Model calibration, validation, prediction, and evaluation. Regional modeling, site impact analysis, and circulation studies. Design of transportation alternatives.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Traffic Flow Theory I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Traffic measurement and fundamental speed-density-flow relationships. Kinematic models. Shock waves. Statistical-kinetic theory of traffic. Introductory car-following principles and stability. Gap acceptance. Platoon dispersion.  Two-fluid model. Queueing process. Multi-regime and catastrophe models.  Higher-order continuum models. Microscopic and macroscopic simulation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Traffic Flow Theory II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced mathematical analysis of vehicular flow. Detailed treatise on car-following models. Fourier and Laplace analysis of stability problems. Perturbation analysis. Derivation of macroscopic traffic flow relationships from microscopic considerations. Advanced hydrodynamic theory.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Urban Transportation Networks I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analytical approaches and algorithms to the formulation and solution of the equilibrium assignment problem for transportation networks. Emphasis on user equilibrium (UE) comparison with system optimal, mathematical programming formulation, supply functions, estimation. Estimating origin-destination matrices, network design problems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Urban Transportation Networks II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced analysis, optimization, and modeling of transportation networks. Topics include advanced static and dynamic traffic assignment algorithms, linear and nonlinear multi-commodity network flow optimization, network simplex, and network control problems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Traffic Systems Operations and Control I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to operation, control, and analysis of arterial and freeway traffic systems.  Control concepts, traffic stream principles, detectors, local controllers, system masters, traffic signal and ramp metering timing principles, traffic measurement technologies, traffic delay principles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Traffic Systems Operations and Control II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics related to operation, control, and analysis of arterial and freeway traffic systems. Control concepts, traffic stream principles, detectors, local controllers, system masters, traffic signal and ramp metering timing principles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Foundation Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Essentials for design and analysis of structural members that transmit superstructure loads to the ground. Topics include subsurface investigations, excavation, dewatering, bracing, footing, mat foundations, piles and pile foundations, caissons and cofferdams, other special foundations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Geotech Earthquake Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In-situ and laboratory determination of dynamic soil properties, liquefaction of soil, cyclic softening of clays, seismic compression and settlement analyses, ground improvement methods, seismic slope stability, introduction to soil structure interaction.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: High Performance Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Part I: Linear and nonlinear fracture mechanics, methodology, real-world case studies; Part II: Composite material toughening, underlying micromechanics, materials engineering towards microstructure tailoring and new material design approaches; Part III: Emerging high-performance engineering materials for safety, energy and the environment.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Beams on elastic foundations. Combined axial and lateral loads. Curved beams. Unsymmetric bending. Shear center. Stresses and strains. Basic equations for theory of elasticity. Energy principles. Theory of torsion. Combined bending and torsion.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Composite Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Stress-strain relationship for orthotropic materials; invariant properties of an orthotropic lamina; biaxial strength theory for an orthotropic lamina; mechanics of materials approach to stiffness; elasticity approach to stiffness; classical lamination theory; strength of laminates; statistical theory of fatigue damage.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Structural Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Vibration of discrete and continuous mass elastic systems. Isolation and transmissability. Dynamic recording instruments. Introduction to nonlinear theory of vibration. Response of structures to earthquake, traffic, and wind loads. Response spectra concepts. Normal mode analysis. Numerical integration techniques.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Earthquake Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Nature of earthquakes, hazard analyses, structural dynamics for earthquake engineering, seismic design force determination methods: ELF, modal response spectrum, nonlinear time history analyses. Diaphragm analyses, redundancy, nonlinear response, ductile systems, hysteretic behavior. Basics of seismic design for steel, timber, concrete.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Finite Element Method in Structural Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Finite element concepts in structural engineering including variational formulations, shape functions, elements assembly, convergence and computer programming. Stiffness of truss, beam, and frame members, two- and three-dimensional solids, plate and shell elements. Static, vibration, stability, and inelastic analysis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Performance-Based Structural Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction and implementation of current approaches in performance-based assessment and design of building structures. Emphasis is on applied and evolving methods and tools for exercising performance-based engineering of building structures.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Multiscale Modeling of Materials and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to modeling materials and structures across length.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micromechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Micromechanics concepts in solid mechanics including eigenstrains, Eshelby equivalent inclusion theories, homogenization procedures, Mori-Tanaka method, self-consistent scheme, and effective mechanical behavior of composites.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Behavior and Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Flexural strength of reinforced concrete elements. Flexural ductility of unconfined and confined members with axial loads. Shear and torsional behaviors. Strength of reinforced concrete ductile frames and shear walls. Reinforced concrete detailing.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Behavior and Design of Steel Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced principles of structural steel design. Analysis and design of beam-column members, braced and unbraced frames for buildings, and plate girders. Review of seismic design provisions. Design of connections.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Earthquake Resistant Structural Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Objectives of seismic design. Cyclic load-distortion characteristics of typical structural elements. Desirable structural form. Ductility and methods of achieving it. Use of energy dissipators. Project involving design of multistory, multibay rigid-jointed plane frame.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Desalination
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction of state of technology, costs and benefits, environmental issues, and implementation issues related to desalination. Emphasis on membrane processes and biofouling prevention.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Applied Environmental Microbiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Microbes in the environment and their impact on human interactions. Microbiological  application in solving environmental engineering problems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Environmental Chemistry II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced concepts from physical and organic chemistry as they relate to environmental engineering. Emphasis on equilibrium and kinetics as they apply to redox reactions, coordination, absorption, gas phase reactions, and ion exchange.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Biological Treatment Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of biological processes in natural and engineered systems. Biological treatment processes, both aerobic and anaerobic, with emphasis on suspended growth systems including design consideration. Containment degradation or control covered. Includes laboratory on molecular tools used in wastewater treatment.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Carbon and Energy Footprint Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Mass- and energy- balance analysis applied to water and wastewater treatment systems. Case studies include analysis of water supply, treatment, reclamation, and reuse.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Physical-Chemical Treatment Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theory and dynamics of physical and chemical separation processes in water and wastewater treatment. Topics include coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, gas transfer, membrane separations, and absorption.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Drinking Water and Wastewater Biotechnology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Water and wastewater microbiology. Engineering principles, molecular aspects, and overview of microorganisms of importance to public health. Topics include aerobic and anaerobic wastewater treatment and disinfection of pathogens in water, wastewaters, and biosolids.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics and Turbulence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the nonlinear physics of turbulence flows with a focus on environmental applications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Beach Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Coastal erosion in California, human and natural influences on southern California beaches, and present-day challenges. Littoral cells and sediment budgets. Water wave theory. Littoral sediment transport and shoreline change modeling. Shoreline stabilization using green and gray infrastructure.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Flood Risk and Modeling
allCourses.description: Global and national trends in flooding and related impacts including disasters; flood risk management; theory and numerical methods for flood inundation modeling; flood risk communication strategies including flood hazard visualizations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Flow in Unsaturated Porous Media
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fluid flow in the unsaturated zone (zone of aeration) of the subsurface. Soil-water physics, flow in regional groundwater systems, miscible displacement, mathematical modeling techniques.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Groundwater Hydrology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include conservation of fluid mass, storage properties or porous media, matrix compressibility, boundary conditions, flow nets, well hydraulics, groundwater chemistry, and solute transport. Includes introduction to advanced topics in porous media. Design projects and computer applications included.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Watershed Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of hydrologic modeling are practiced. Concepts of watershed delineation, land use change impact, design studies, and GIS tools are discussed. Focus on the USACE (HEC) software tools (HEC-HMS and HEC-RAS) along with their associated GIS interfaces.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Climate Data Analysis
allCourses.description: Trend analysis; statistical indices for diagnosing and detecting changes in extremes; nonstationary processes; extreme value analysis; multivariate extreme value methods; tail dependence estimation; uncertainties in observed and projected changes in climate extremes.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Stochastic Hydrology
allCourses.description: Statistical analysis and modeling of hydrologic and geophysical data for decision making, frequency analysis of extreme precipitation and floods for hydrologic design, time series analysis for hydrological simulation, spectral analysis, and geostatistical analysis of spatially correlated fields.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Hydrology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Elements of the hydrologic cycle including precipitation, infiltration, evapotranspiration, ground water, and runoff. Unit Hydrograph theory and routing methods. Introduction to precipitation/runoff relationship and watershed modeling. Statistical methods and flood frequency analysis. Discussion section covers advanced topics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Hydrologic Transport Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Process description, mathematical and numerical modeling of transport processes in surface and ground water. Topics include advection, molecular diffusion, Taylor dispersion, mechanical dispersion in porous media, shear flow dispersion in channels, and turbulent jets and plumes.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Environmental Transport Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Computational modeling of multi-dimensional flow and scalar transport problems in surface and ground water. Topics include mathematical model formulation, numerical method selection, serial and parallel implementation, model verification and validation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Structural Reliability
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Applications of probability theory to reliability analysis of engineering structures. Theory of structural reliability. Estimation of static random loads. Reliability analysis of structural components and system. Monte Carlo simulation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mathematical Methods in Engineering Analysis
allCourses.description: Matrices; vector calculus; eigenvalue problems; Fourier analysis; partial differential equations; special functions; numerical analysis; finite difference method.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Analysis of Hydrologic Systems
allCourses.description: Application of systems theory in hydrologic, land surface, biogeochemical modeling. Design, identification, and calibration of conceptual models. Principles of dynamic systems, modeling approaches, theory of linear systems, mathematical concepts of differential calculus, theoretical concepts of parameter estimation and optimization theory.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Merging Models and Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to optimization and data assimilation methods for model calibration and uncertainty quantification. Local, global and multi-method search. Bayesian analysis using Monte Carlo simulation with Random Walk Metropolis, and adaptive samplers. Filtering methods for recursive inference. Illustration using environmental models.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Hydrologic Remote Sensing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of remote sensing and application in hydrology. Review of sensor systems, thermal and multispectral image processing, and image classification. Examples from remote sensing of hydrologic processes such as precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation are covered.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Wavelets in Hydrology, Engineering, and Geoscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Multiscale analysis of hydrologic, engineering, and earth system processes; energy decomposition in the time-frequency domain via wavelets; applications to fluid flows, climate and mechanical signals for feature extraction, trend analysis, coherent structures, and upscaling/downscaling.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Seminars in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminars scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation of the thesis required for the M.S. degree in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation of advanced topics and special research areas in civil and environmental engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Statics
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Economic Analysis for Scientists and Engineers
allCourses.description: Introduction to microeconomics and cost benefit analysis. Integration of economic, social, and behavioral considerations into the engineering design process. Applications to contemporary problems via case studies.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Contemporary and Emerging Environmental Challenges
allCourses.description: Introduces contemporary and emerging environmental challenges, illustrates links between human behavior, environmental policy, and engineering practices, examines policy options in the context of current institutions, and introduces tools and frameworks to reach sound economic, social, and environmental solutions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Civil Engineering Practicum I
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to civil engineering through presentations on structural, environmental, water, and transportation systems. Introduction to graphics. Graphical visualization and communication using hand and computer sketching. Fundamentals of Computer Aided Design (CAD) using AutoCad. Laboratory sessions. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Civil Engineering Practicum II
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of surveying; fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems (GIS); introduction to the state-of-the-art and future areas of the profession, including applications of advanced technology and computers; Introduction to visualization and communication of design concepts; laboratory sessions.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Honors Thesis
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Preparation of final presentation and paper describing individual research in Engineering. For participants in the Campuswide Honors Program.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR H199 AND LOWER DIVISION WRITING AND CAMPUSWIDE HONORS ONLY

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Study for Honors Students
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Supervised research in Engineering for participants in the Campuswide Honors Program. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Engineering Computations
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the solution of engineering problems through the use of the computer. Elementary programming, numerical analysis, and data visualization with a high-level programming language such as MATLAB.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"OR":["MATH 2A","MATH 5A","AP CALCULUS AB","AP CALCULUS BC","AP CALCULUS AB SUB"]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 2A OR MATH 5A OR AP CALCULUS AB OR AP CALCULUS BC OR AP CALCULUS AB SUB )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Systems Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Experiments in linear systems, including op-amp circuits, vibrations, and control systems. Emphasis on demonstrating that mathematical models can be useful tools for the analysis and design of electro-mechanical systems.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fluid Thermal Science Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fluid and thermal engineering laboratory. Experimental analysis of fluid flow, heat transfer, and thermodynamic systems. Probability, statistics, and uncertainly analysis. Report writing is emphasized and a design project is required. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Aerospace Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analytical and experimental investigation in aerodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer. Emphasis on study of flow over objects and lift and drag on airfoils. Introduction to basic diagnostic techniques. Report writing is emphasized.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Combustion and Fuel Cell Systems
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of gaseous, liquid, and coal-fired combustion and fuel cell systems. Fuels, fuel-air mixing, aerodynamics, and combustion and fuel cell thermodynamics. Operating and design aspects of practical systems including engines, power generators, boilers, furnaces, and incinerators.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Propulsion
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics to basic flow processes and cycle performance in chemical propulsion systems: gas turbines, ramjets, scramjets, and rockets. Introduction to electric and electromagnetic rocket thrusters, nuclear rockets, and solar sails.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Electric Propulsion
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Space propulsion requirements and maneuvers, stressing those best suited to electric propulsion. An introduction to plasma physics. Electrothermal, electromagnetic, and electrostatis accelerators, with emphasis in technologies (ion engines, Hall thrusters, and colloidal thrusters) belonging to the latter family.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions, and other characteristics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Applied Engineering Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of thermodynamic principles to compressible and incompressible processes representative of practical engineering problems; power cycles, refrigeration cycles, multicomponent mixtures, air conditioning systems, combustion, and compressible flow. Design of a thermodynamic process.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Solar and Renewable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of solar and other renewable energy systems including solar photo-voltaic, solar thermal, wind, and PEM fuel cell. Includes power generation and storage, and renewable fuels for transportation and stationary power generation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal, and next generation nuclear. Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Climate Solutions
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to climate change science and impacts on the health of people and the planet with a focus on the multi-dimensional aspects of solutions to the climate crisis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Heat and Mass Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer. Conduction, heat and mass transfer by convection in laminar flow, radiation heat transfer, and combined modes of heat and mass transfer. Practical engineering applications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fluid Dynamics I
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamental concepts; fluid statics; kinematics; incompressible and compressible flows; Bernoulli's equation; control-volume analysis; conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; differential analysis; introduction to potential flow and viscous flow.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D AND MATH 2E AND MATH 3D AND ENGRMAE 91 AND PHYSICS 7C AND ( ENGR 80 OR ENGRCEE 80 OR ENGRMAE 80 ) AND ( ENGR 30 OR ENGRCEE 30 OR ENGRMAE 30 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fluid Dynamics II
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis  of viscous flows: stress-strain rate, fully developed laminar and turbulent flows. Review of thermodynamics, sound speed, stagnation properties. One dimensional isentropic and non-isentropic compressible flows.  Normal and oblique shock waves. Two-dimensional supersonic  isentropic flow.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fluid Mechanics III
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in viscous and compressible flows. Viscous boundary layers, basic concepts in turbulent flow, separated flows, thermal transport, two-dimensional supersonic flow, shock polars, supersonic airfoils, conical flows.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors only. Mechanical Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computational fluid dynamics in simple engineering devices. The numerical simulations will be performed via the widely-used software ANSYS-Fluent. While Fluent is the choice of software, all major CFD packages are based on a similar numerical method.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Compressible Flow
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Compressibility effects in fluid mechanics. One-dimensional flow with area variation, friction, heat transfer, and shocks. Design of gas supply systems. Two-dimensional flow with oblique shocks and isentropic waves. Supersonic airfoil theory and design, wind tunnel design. Basic diagnostics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Aerodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Advanced potential flow, vorticity, and  circulation. Flow over aircraft wings and airfoils: Kutta-Joukowski theory, lift, moment, and drag. Flow similitude; three dimensional wing theory, compressibility, viscous effects. Source panel methods. Supersonic aerodynamics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Theory of Machines and Mechanisms
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents the basic mathematical theory of machines. Focuses on the principles of cam design, gearing and gear train analysis, and the kinematic and dynamic analysis of linkages, together with an introduction to robotics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 52 AND ( MATH 3A OR I&C SCI 6N ) AND ( ENGR 80 OR ENGRCEE 80 OR ENGRMAE 80 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Astronautics
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Motion in gravitational force fields, orbit transfers, rocketry, interplanetary trajectories, attitude dynamics and stabilization, navigation, reentry, the space environment.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Vibrations
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of structural vibrations of mechanical systems. Modeling for lumped and distributed parameter systems. Topics include single and multi-degree of freedom systems, free and forced vibrations, Fourier series, convolution integral, mass/stiffness matrices, and normal modes with design project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2E AND MATH 3D AND ( ENGR 80 OR ENGRCEE 80 OR ENGRMAE 80 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Smart Structures
allCourses.description: Introduction to modeling, numerical simulation, design, and control of axial, torsional, and bending actuators. Fundamentals of shape-changing trusses, frames, and panels. Introduction to the behavior and modeling of smart materials such as shape memory alloys/polymers.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Structures
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to mechanics of materials. Topics include stresses and strains, axial and torsional loading, bending, shear, combined loading, stress and strain transformation, failure theories, beam deflection, and buckling.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 3A AND ( ENGR 30 OR ENGRCEE 30 OR ENGRMAE 30 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Structures Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Experimental techniques for the measurement of mechanical properties of materials and structures. Methods for load, displacement, and strain measurements. Tension, bending, compression tests. Determination of strength. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( ENGR 150 OR ENGRMAE 150 ) AND ( ENGR 30 OR ENGRCEE 30 OR ENGRMAE 30 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Engineering Design
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A comprehensive group design project experience that involves identifying customer needs, idea generation, reverse engineering, preliminary design, standards, prototype development, testing, analysis, and redesign of a product involving fluid, thermal, and mechanical components.  Introduces design for manufacturing and the environment. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Elements and principles of computer-aided engineering with modern hardware and software are presented with a design focus. Case studies are used to assist in finite-element method techniques. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced BIOMEMS Manufacturing Techniques
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to BIOMEMS. Advanced biotechnology/biomedicine equipment based on MEMS and NEMS. Fundamentals of MEMS/NEMS sensing techniques and the biological and physics principles involved and the preferred MEMS and NEMS manufacturing techniques.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Composite Materials and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Micro and macro mechanical properties and failure mechanisms of lamina and laminates. Laminate theory, hygrothermal effects, failure analysis and design. Manufacturing methods, non-destructive evaluation, experimental characterization. Application of numerical modeling for analysis and design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 AND ( ENGR 150 OR ENGRCEE 150 OR ENGRMAE 150 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior and Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, yielding, necking, creep, and fracture of materials. Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize the properties of materials. Design parameters.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Lightweight Structures
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Mass minimization under stiffness, strength, and buckling constraints. Finite Element method and application to trusses. Three-dimensional bending. Thin-wall, composite, and functionally graded beams. Plates and shells, design of laminated and functionally graded plates. Stress analysis of aircraft components.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Aircraft Performance
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Flight theory applied to subsonic propeller and jet aircraft. Nature of aerodynamic forces, drag and lift of wing and fuselage, high-lift devices, level-flight performance, climb and glide performance, range, endurance, take-off and landing distances, static and dynamic stability and control.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Aircraft Design
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Preliminary design of subsonic general aviation and transport aircraft with emphasis on layout, aerodynamic design, propulsion, and performance. Estimation of total weight and weight distribution, design of wings, fuselage, and tail, selection and location of engines, prediction of overall performance.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Aviation Systems and the Environment
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors only. Aerospace Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Methods for analyzing aviation systems, flight and engine performance, and operations, and associated modern environmental challenges, including fuel burn, emissions, and noise are introduced. Analysis methods and technological and policy approaches for environmental impact mitigation examined.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Air Pollution and Control
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sources, dispersion, and effects of air pollutants. Topics include emission factors, emission inventory, air pollution, meteorology, air chemistry, air quality modeling, impact assessment, source and ambient monitoring, regional control strategies.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Control Systems
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Feedback control systems. Modeling, stability, and systems specifications. Root locus, Nyquist, and Bode methods of analysis and design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Digital Control Systems
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Methods for analysis and design of discrete-time control systems. Z-transforms, difference equations, discrete Fourier transforms. Sampling theorem and applications.  Z-plane stability, frequency response. Digital controller design. Introduction to digital filters.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Design of Computer-Controlled Robots
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students design a small robotic device and program it to exhibit sentient behaviors. The basic aspects of mechatronic design are covered, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, and microcomputer programming for the implementation of control paradigms.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Dynamics and Control of Aerospace Vehicles
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Equations of motion, linearization, stability derivatives, and longitudinal and lateral modes of motion. Handling qualities, sensors and actuators, and effects of various feedbacks on stability and performance. Stability augmentation. Autopilot design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles necessary to understand statistical learning methods. Introduction to the R programming language. Mathematical foundation for various machine learning algorithms. Computer implementation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computer-Aided Mechanism Design
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on design of planar, spherical, and spatial mechanisms using computer algebra and graphics. Topics include exact and approximate analytical design techniques. Students are required to use existing software (or develop new algorithms) to design various mechanisms for new applications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Design
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Review of statistics as applied to experimental research. Fundamentals and principles of statistical experimental design and analysis with emphasis on understanding and use of designed experiments, response surfaces, linear regression modeling, and process optimization.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Numerical Analysis in Mechanical Engineering
allCourses.description: Solution of mechanical-engineering equations by means of numerical methods. Errors in numerical analysis. Nonlinear equation and sets of equations. Numerical differentiation and integration. Ordinary differential equations. Boundary-value problems. Partial differential equations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2E AND MATH 3D AND ( EECS 10 OR EECS 12 OR ENGRMAE 10 )

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Design in Industry
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of engineering design in the context of an industrial application. Local manufacturing firms define an engineering design project to be completed in 10 weeks. Projects include initial brainstorming to final design, with a formal presentation.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Senior Project - Special Topics
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Mechanical Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Group or individual senior project of theoretical or applied nature involving design. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Topics in MAE Design
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides early-stage design/hands-on experience for upper-division students, and allows them to participate in senior design projects course ENGRMAE 189.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Seminars in Engineering
allCourses.description: Seminars by individual faculty in major fields of interest. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Analysis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Linear algebra, including vector spaces, matrices, linear systems of equations, least squares, and the eigenvalue problem. Ordinary differential equations, including analytical and numerical solution methods, stability, and phase portraits.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Analysis II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Review of ordinary differential equations, including Bessel and Legendre functions. Partial differential equations, including the diffusion equation, Laplace's equation, and the wave equation. Fourier series, Fourier and Laplace transforms and their applications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Integrated Thermal-Fluid Science Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The fundamentals of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer are first.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Design and Simulation: Tools and Process
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practical techniques and use of industry tools that improve the engineering design process by simulating the performance of design options prior to the costly steps of prototyping and manufacturing are covered. Applicable to a wide variety of engineering disciplines.
