allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Perturbation Methods in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Asymptotic Expansions of integrals. Regular and singular perturbations. Perturbation methods for ordinary and partial differential equations. Matched asymptotic expansions. Multiple-scale asymptotic expansion schemes. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A and ENGRMAE 200B. Knowledge of linear differential equations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nonlinear Optimization Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Numerical methods for constrained and unconstrained optimization. Necessary and sufficient conditions for optimimality. Conjugate gradient, variable metric algorithms. Gradient projection, penalty functions, and Lagrange methods. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Energy Efficiency in the Built Environment
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Energy and power for the built environment; building energy modeling; heat transfer and losses; heating and cooling cycles; control hardware and software; carbon neutrality, optimization.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Fundamentals of Combustion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Premixed, nonpremixed, and heterogenous reactions, with emphasis on kinetics, thermal ignition, turbulent flame propogation, detonations, explosions, flammability limits, diffusion flame, quenching, flame stabilization, and particle and spray combustion. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Combustion
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Premixed, nonpremixed, and heterogenous reactions, with emphasis on kinetics, thermal ignition, turbulent flame propogation, detonations, explosions, flammability limits, diffusion flame, quenching, flame stabilization, and particle and spray combustion.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Energy Storage Systems and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of energy storage systems and technology including lithium ion battery systems for transportation and stationary applications, for flow batteries (e.g., vanadium redox, sodium sulfur), and for reversible fuel cell electrolyzer systems and hydrogen energy storage.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Undergraduate-level knowledge of applied engineering thermodynamics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Electrochemistry: Fundamentals and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to engineering electrochemistry fundamentals and applications. Examine thermodynamics and transport principles in typical electrochemical systems. Electrochemical sensors, batteries, fuel cells, and supercapacitors. Manufacturing aspects will also be covered.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Electrochemistry: Fundamentals and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to engineering electrochemistry fundamentals and applications. Examine thermodynamics and transport principles in typical electrochemical systems. Electrochemical sensors, batteries, fuel cells, and supercapacitors. Manufacturing aspects are also covered.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Electric Propulsion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Space propulsion requirements and maneuvers, stressing those best suited to electric propulsion. An introduction to plasma physics. Electrothermal, electromagnetic and electrostatic accelerators, with emphasis in technologies (ion engines, Hall thrusters and colloidal thrusters) belonging to the latter family.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions and other characteristics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Systems and Degradation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fuel cell systems design; impacts of operating conditions; experimental and theoretical analysis methods for fuel cells systems; introduction to degradation mechanisms and mitigation techniques; provides broad insight into fuel-cell science, technology, system design and operation.  Offered every other year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: PEM Fuel Cells
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In-depth introduction to the fundamental principles of PEM fuel cells, including thermodynamics, kinetics, transport, cold start, manufacturing, and experiment.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions, and other characteristics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Combustion Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Pollutant formation and experimental methods. Formation of gaseous pollutants and soot; transformation and emission of fuel contaminants in gas, liquid, and solid fuel combustion; methods employed to measure velocity, turbulence intensity, temperature, composition, particle size; methods to visualize reacting flows.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Statistical Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistics of independent particles, development of quantum mechanical description of atoms and molecules, application of quantum mechanics, evaluation of thermodynamics properties for solids, liquids, and gases, statistical mechanics of dependent particles (ensembles).

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Generalized Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Generalized thermodynamics develops the laws of continuum thermodynamics from a set of plausible and intuitive postulates. The postulates are motivated qualitatively by a statistical description of matter and are justified by a posterior success for the resulting theory.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Generalized Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Generalized thermodynamics develops the laws of continuum thermodynamics from a set of plausible and intuitive postulates. The postulates are motivated qualitatively by a statistical description of matter and are justified by a posterior success for the resulting theory.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal and next generation nuclear.  Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal, and next generation nuclear. Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Solar and Renewable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of solar and other renewable energy systems including solar photo-voltaic, solar thermal, wind, and PEM fuel cell. Includes power generation and storage, and renewable fuels for transportation and stationary power generation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Knowledge of applied engineering thermodynamics.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Steady state and transient conduction heat transfer in one- and multi-dimensional geometries. Analytical methods, exact and approximate. Numerical techniques are also included.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Convective Heat and Mass Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental convective heat transfer for various cases, including flow conditions, flow phases, and boundary conditions. Analysis of heat convection by exact, approximate solutions, and similarity solutions. Boundary layer theory and equations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Radiative Heat Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Black body radiation.  Radiative transport equations for surfaces separated by non-participating media.  Radiant energy transfer through absorbing, emitting, and scattering media. Radiation-conduction interaction.  Radiation-convection interaction.  Introduction to finite-difference solutions.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Numerical Methods in Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transport (Laminar Flows) I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the discretization of various types of partial differential equations (parabolic, elliptic, hyperbolic). Finite-volume discretization for one- and two-dimensional flows. Use of a two-dimensional elliptic procedure to predict sample laminar flows.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced Transport Phenomena
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of transport phenomena. Covers the subjects of conservation equations, dimensionless numbers, fundamentals of diffusion, perturbation methods, ion transport, two-phase transport, and interfacial phenomena.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Thermal Resistance Analysis in Microdevices and Nanomaterials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Heat transfer and thermal resistance analysis relevant for microdevices and nanomaterials. Overview of recent progress in nanotechnology and materials science. Thermal modeling strategies for novel electronic devices and energy conversion systems.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nanoscale Phase Change Transport Physics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses a wide range of phase change processes (i.e., evaporation, boiling, condensation, and freezing) through the use of novel thermal metamaterials with the aim of enhancing phase change performances.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nanoscale Materials for Modern Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to design and synthesis of nanomaterials. Topics include thermal and liquid transport in materials systems, phase change heat transfer physics, and mechanical properties in materials systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Undergraduate-level knowledge of heat transfer.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Inviscid Incompressible Fluid Mechanics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Equations of motion. Vector notation. Flow kinematics. Potential flow and complex potential. Vorticity and circulation. Bernoulli's theorem. Crocco's theorem. Conformal, Joukowski, and Schwarz-Christoffel transformations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Viscous Incompressible Fluid Mechanics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Review of mass, momentum, energy equations. Stress tensor, constitutive relations. Laminar flows. Stokes and Oseen flows. Self-similarity. Boundary layer theory: thin-layer approximation, Falkner-Skan, Blasius solutions, integral methods. Jet, wake, cavity flows. Introduction to turbulence: instability, Reynolds averaging, mixing length.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Compressible Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: One-dimensional unsteady flow; Riemann invariants, acoustics, shock tube. Two-dimensional flow: shock polars, linear theory, similarity rules, method of characteristics. Three dimensional flow: slender-body theory.  Effects of viscosity and conductivity:  laminar boundary layer, Crocco-Busemann relations.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Turbulence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Phenomenon of turbulence. Reynolds equations. Dynamics of turbulence. Free turbulent shear flows. Wall-bounded turbulent shear flows. Turbulent transport of scalar quantities. Spectral dynamics. Mathematical models of turbulence.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Turbulent Free Shear Flows
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practical and theoretical aspects of turbulent free shear flows. Instability, global scaling laws, mixing, and noise generation in incompressible and compressible shear layers, jets, and wakes. Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, near- and far-field growth rates, effect of compressibility, aeroacoustics of jets.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nonequilibrium Gas Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Molecular description of fluid flow. Boltzmann equation. Chapman-Enskog expansion for flows with translational nonequilibrium. Shock structure. Inviscid flows with chemical and vibrational nonequilibrium. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mathematical, physical, and computational fundamentals of computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods for solving the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. Topics include: finite-difference and finite-volume discretization, time marching methods, von Neumann analysis, upwinding, flux splitting, TVD, and other high-resolution shock-capturing schemes.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Dynamics of Unsteady Flows
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Unsteady potential flow modeling (Kelvin's circulation theorem, unsteady Bernoulli's equation). Theodorsen's frequency response, Wagner's step response, and the Kussner sharp-edged gust. State Space approximations for Unsteady Loads. Vortex Lattice. Flutter.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Inertial Navigation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a basic understanding of 1) theory, operation, and performance characteristics of a strapdown inertial navigation system  (INS), (2) distinction between strap down and gimbaled INS, (3) Kalman filtering theory and its application to strap down INS aiding.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Kinematics and dynamics of three-dimensional motions. Lagrange's equations, Newton-Euler equations. Applications include robot systems and spinning satellites.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Robotics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Spatial rigid-body transformations.  Forward and inverse kinematics. Jacobian of serial and parallel chains.  Screw coordinates and transformations. Rate and static analyses using screw theory. Singularity analysis. Trajectory generation. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Theoretical Kinematics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Spatial rigid body kinematics is presented with applications to robotics. Orthogonal Matrices, Rodrigues' formula, Quaternions, Plucker coordinates, screw theory, and dual numbers are studied using modern projective geometry and multi-linear algebra. Applications include trajectory planning, inverse kinematics, and workspace analysis.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Spatial Mechanism Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental kinematic theory required for planar, spherical, and spatial mechanism design. The focus is on algebraic methods for the exact solution of constraint equations. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro-System Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro-System Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Smart Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Modeling, numerical simulation, design, and control of axial, torsional, and bending actuators. Structural analysis of shape-changing trusses, frames, and panels. Behavior and modeling of smart materials such as shape memory alloys/polymers.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale.  Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale. Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Biorobotics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Sensors, actuators, and neural circuits for biological movement control from an engineering perspective.  Current approaches to robotic and mechatronic devices that support and enhance human movement in health and following neurologic injuries like stroke and spinal cord injury.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Micro/Nano Robotics
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the emerging field of robotics at small scale (micro/nano robotics). Understanding different physical phenomena at small scales, the differences between nano and micro robotics, common fabrication, and different mechanisms of locomotion and environmental interaction.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces Engineering and Science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces engineering and science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Advanced BIOMEMS Manufacturing Techniques
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to BIOMEMS. Advanced biotechnology/biomedicine equipment based on MEMS and NEMS. Fundamentals of MEMS/NEMS sensing techniques and the biological and physics principles involved and the preferred MEMS and NEMS manufacturing techniques.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Solids and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Finite deformation kinematics; stress and strain measures; invariance in solid mechanics; objective rates; constitutive theory of elastic and inelastic solids; rate formulations; computational approaches; theories of plates and shells; applications to aerospace vehicles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanics of Solids and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Finite deformation kinematics; stress and strain measures; invariance in solid mechanics; objective rates; constitutive theory of elastic and inelastic solids; rate formulations; computational approaches; theories of plates and shells; applications to aerospace vehicles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Composite Materials and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Motivation for composite materials. Different classifications according to the nature of the matrix (PMC, MMC, CMC) and the reinforcement topology (fibers, whiskers, particulates). Mechanical properties. Failure mechanisms. Designing with composite materials. Advantages and limitations of homogenization techniques for numerical modeling.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nanomechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Nanoscale materials and the experimental and computational techniques used to measure their properties.  Mechanical behavior is the main focus, but other material properties such as diffusion and electron transport are discussed.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Materials Failure and Fracture
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces materials failure and fracture behaviors under mechanical, thermal, and environmental conditions. It aims to provide a solid foundation and basic understanding of classic fatigue and fracture problems, and their underlying physical mechanisms.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Nanomaterials
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to nanoscale materials and experimental and computational techniques. Topics materials synthesis techniques, thin film deposition, nanoparticle and nanowire growth, characterization with electrons and X-rays, forces and surface interactions at the nanoscale, structure-property scaling laws, and atomistic/multiscale computer modeling.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Continuum Theories
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents a continuum, macroscopic view of deformation and failure of solids. Covers elasticity, plasticity, visco-elasticity, visco-plasticity, fracture and fatigue. Topics include discussions of physical behavior, mathematical formalism and measurement techniques.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Atomistic Theories
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents atomistic mechanisms that control mechanical behavior of materials. Covers plasticity, dislocation theory, strengthening mechanisms, high-temperature diffusion and gain boundary sliding, shear localization, void formation, ductile rupture, brittle fracture and fatigue.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Atomistic Theories
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents atomistic mechanisms that control mechanical behavior of materials. Covers plasticity, dislocation theory, strengthening mechanisms, high-temperature diffusion and gain boundary sliding, shear localization, void formation, ductile rupture, brittle fracture, and fatigue.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Aviation Systems and the Environment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Methods for analyzing aviation systems, flight and engine performance, operations, and associated modern environmental challenges, including fuel burn, emissions, and noise are introduced. Analysis methods and technological and policy approaches for environmental impact mitigation examined.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Linear Systems I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Input-output and state-space representations of continuous-time linear systems. State transition matrices,  Controllability and observability. Irreducible realizations.  State feedback and observer design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Network Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides foundations on graph-theoretic, probabilistic and analytic techniques that have proven instrumental for studying networked dynamical systems. Applications are presented in diverse areas of science and engineering that include the coordination of vehicles and distribution of energy and resources.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Robust Control Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Methods for control design of systems with uncertainty. Feedback stability and small gain theorem. Multivariable stability margins and multiplier theory. H-infinity-optimal control, linear matrix inequalities. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Stochastic Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the tools stochastic differential equations and stochastic control. Focus on optimal control of dynamical systems in the presence of stochastic noise. Basic concepts are also central in various branches of theoretical physics and mathematical finance; examples are discussed.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Optimal Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and methods of optimal control. Topics include objectives and issues in controlling nonlinear systems; linear variational and adjoint equations; optimality conditions via variational calculus, maximum principle, and dynamic programming; solution methods; applications to control robots and aerospace vehicles.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Nonlinear Feedback Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced tools for feedback control system analysis and synthesis. Norms, operators, Lp spaces, contraction mapping theorem, Lyapunov techniques along with their extensions. Circle criterion positivity and passivity. Applications to nonlinear control methods, such as sliding mode or adaptive techniques.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Geometric Nonlinear Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Using the mathematics of differential geometry, a number of the concepts and results of linear systems theory have been extended to nonlinear systems. Describes these extensions and illustrate their use in nonlinear system analysis and design. Not offered every year.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Learning Control Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Supervised learning for classification and regression: perceptrons, support vector machines, feed-forward neural networks, Gaussian processes. Generalization and model selection: cross-validation, regularization, and Bayesian methods. Unsupervised learning: clustering and dimensionality reduction. Learning control systems. Introduction to reinforcement learning.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Parameter and State Estimation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Bayesian and frequentist approaches to parameter and state estimation. Properties of estimators. Linear Gaussian systems and the Kalman Filter. Nonlinear state estimation, extended and unscented Kalman Filters. Introduction to Monte Carlo methods and particle filtering. Application to tracking and navigation.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Selected topics of current interest in mechanical systems. Topics include robotics, kinematics, control, dynamics, and geometric modeling.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Design of Computer-Controlled Robots
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The basic aspects of mechatronic design are covered, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, inertial measurement units, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws. Students work in groups to create their own mechatronic device. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals and principles of statistical experimental design and analysis. Emphasis addresses understanding and use of designed experiments, response surfaces, linear regression modeling, process optimization, and development of links between empirical and theoretical models.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Engineering Design Under Uncertainty
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to statistical and ML methods used in engineering design under uncertainty. Students learn how to probabilistically formulate a design problem, translate the formulations into a computer, and systematically find the solution.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Design for Human Movement
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces techniques for analysis and modeling of human locomotion, with a focus on lower-limb rehabilitating and robotic assistive devices. Discusses background and current research, with assignments covering independent reading, computer simulations, and a final project.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Research Communication in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Guides students along research communication milestones by completion of a conference/journal publication, research proposal, MS thesis, or other significant publication. Peer review, response to reviewers, and a presentation are used to build skill and confidence.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Project
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Tutorial in which masters-level students taking the comprehensive examination option undertake a masters-level research project.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
allCourses.description: Special topics by individual faculty in major fields of interest.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the thesis required for the M.S. in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the dissertation required for the Ph.D. in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Seminars in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
allCourses.description: Presentation of advanced topics and reports of current research efforts in mechanical engineering. Required of all graduate students in mechanical engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Individual Research
allCourses.restriction: Consent of instructor to enroll
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Statics
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Computer-Aided Design
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Develops skills for interpretation and presentation of mechanical design drawings and the use of CAD in engineering design. An integrated approach to drafting based on sketching, manual drawing, and three-dimensional CAD techniques is presented. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Manufacturing Processes in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: With laboratory. Machines and processes of mechanical manufacturing. Safety and professional procedures emphasized.  Use of measuring instruments, hand tools, lathe, mill, drill press, bandsaw, grinder, welding equipment.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Electric Circuits
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of analog circuits based on lumped circuit elements with emphasis on the use of operational amplifiers. Sinusoidal and transient response. Constructional and laboratory testing of analog circuits, and introduction to data acquisition. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Introduction to Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Thermodynamic principles; open and closed systems representative of engineering problems. First and second law of thermodynamics with applications to engineering systems and design.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Topics in Design Project
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Early-stage design/hands-on experience for students, and allows them to participate alongside seniors in the design project.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Undergraduate Research in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides disciplinary research participation. Original or existing research options provide undergraduates the opportunity for faculty/mentor interactions including access to appropriate facilities. Medical Epidemiology research areas: Cancer, Genetic/Molecular, Environmental, Occupational, Biostatistics, and Infectious Disease.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, biostatistics, and epidemiological research. Topics include research methods of measuring health problems in populations, disease control and prevention in populations, how epidemiology contributes to knowledge of disease etiology, and biostatistical analysis and interpretation of epidemiologic data.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: College of Health Sciences students only. Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Epidemiology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Learn to design and conduct epidemiologic studies using common designs. Determine why bias and measurement error arise in observational studies, and how they influence effect estimates. Perform and interpret epidemiologic data analyses using statistical software.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 206A. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in the design and statistical analysis of epidemiologic studies. Topics include simulation methods, counter-matching and multiphase study designs, missing data, and Bayesian analysis. Published simulation studies are discussed and replicated using the R software package.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 200B. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 200B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Cancer Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on understanding how epidemiology plays a role in the search for cancer etiology, prevention, control, and treatment; gives an overview of cancer research with an appreciation of the multidisciplinary nature of the field.

allCourses.title: Genetic Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on the role of genetic factors in the etiology of disease in human populations with an objective of disease control and prevention and the role of interactions of genetic factors and environmental exposures in the occurrence of disease.

allCourses.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to help students develop an appreciation for statistician's view of the research process, emphasizing biomedical research. Instills an understanding of how statistical models are used to yield insights about data that form evidence-based understanding of the world around us.

allCourses.title: Biostatistics II: Intermediate Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and clinical research fields. Covers common regression-modeling techniques frequently used in biologic and medical applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204. EPIDEM 204 with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Biostatistics III: Advanced Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields.  Introduces statistical methods for analyzing survival and longitudinal/clustered data, and techniques to resolve missing data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204B. EPIDEM 204B with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Environmental Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on epidemiological approaches to the assessment of community environmental hazards; issues involved in environmental exposure estimation; interdisciplinary approaches to environmental epidemiology, including the use of biomarkers of exposures and susceptibility; epidemiological studies within the context of risk assessment.

allCourses.title: Methods for Design and Implementation of Epidemiologic Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields, and covers topics in subject recruitment, data collection, quality assessment and control, and sample-size estimation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 204A. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 204A with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Statistical Genetics
allCourses.description: Provides students with knowledge of the basic principles, concepts, and methods used in statistical genetic research. Topics include principles of population genetics, and statistical methods for family- and population-based studies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in statistical methods.

allCourses.title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology & Prevention
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Epidemiological aspects of chronic human diseases. Topics include methodologies for quantifying aspects of prevalent chronic diseases including risk factors, identification of susceptible groups, societal burdens, promising future research; and the intervention, prevention, and control of diseases in populations.

allCourses.title: Toxic Chemicals in Environment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Industrial ecology of toxicants and their impacts on environmental quality and human health. Explores theoretical basis of toxicity thresholds and regulatory issues. Uses classic and contemporary research articles to understand the legacy of traditional toxicants, and to identify emerging threats.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only. Environ Health Sci and Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Convergence of agents (chemical, physical, biological, or psychosocial) in environment can emerge as diseases influenced by social, political, and economic factors, allowing them to become rooted in society. How these agents from various spheres come together and impact human health.

allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents various topics and latest research in the broad field of epidemiology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Epidemiology Research Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Research journal club is a group discussion of recent publications in epidemiology and related fields.  Students rotate as lead discussants, guided by faculty.  All attendees are expected to be familiar with the papers at the start of class.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Epidemiology Department Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A forum for the presentation of recent research to epidemiology students, faculty, and other interested parties. The atmosphere is informal, yet rigorous. Speakers range from graduate students through distinguished visitors from other institutions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Biostatistics and Epidemiology for Medical Fellows
allCourses.description: Prepares medical fellows and other physicians for rotations in research programs. Understanding of basic biostatistics and study design, and interdependencies between the two. Application of principles in evaluation of medical literature for guidance on patient care and public health policy.

allCourses.title: M.S. Thesis Research and Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research and study necessary for a graduate student to prepare and complete the thesis required for the Master of Science (M.S.) degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: PhD Degree Dissertation Research & Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research and study necessary for a graduate student to prepare and complete the dissertation required for the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Directed Study in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed study with Epidemiology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Epidemiology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: University Supervised Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to students with active Teaching Assistant (T.A.) appointments.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Historical Foundations (1500-1800)
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of the European experience from its social, political, and cultural foundations to modern European issues and institutions in a globalized world. Topics include social, political, and cultural history up to the French Revolution.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: European Studies Core I - Early Europe (Pre-1789)
allCourses.description: Introduction to multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in European society, culture, art, literature, and politics; encourages students to explore intersections among disciplines. Possible themes: Concept of Europe in Renaissance, Self and Other: Europe and Islam, Hybrid Cultures in Medieval Europe.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: European Studies Core II: Modern Europe (Post-1789)
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in modern European society, culture, art, literature, and politics, encouraging students to see points of intersection among disciplines. Possible themes: Subjects, Citizens, and Representation; Europe in the World; European Revolutions in Art and Society.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Early European History and Culture: Pre-1789
allCourses.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts (art, literature, music, political theory) from the pre-1789 period in more than one European country.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern European History and Culture: Post-1789
allCourses.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts (art, literature, music, political theory) from 1789 to present in more than one European country.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Issues and Institutions in Modern Europe (1789-1945)
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of modern European societies in social, political, and cultural terms. Topics include shifting geopolitical borders, social movements, and various forms of cultural expression (film, art, literature) as they intersect with and shape issues and events after 1800.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: What is the Origin of Language?
allCourses.description: Teaches symbol-based logic and universal grammar in human language as tools to investigate the origin of language. Does language originate with reason? Is language inherently universal or diverse? Does it begin as something literal or figurative.

allCourses.title: Topics in Contemporary Europe (1945 – Today)
allCourses.description: Offers a perspective on contemporary politics and social and cultural life of today’s Europe. Introduces students to literature, film, and social theory crises of the contemporary world as they emanated from World War II, such as nationalism and populism.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Senior Seminar in European Studies
allCourses.restriction: School of Humanities students only.
allCourses.description: Capstone research seminar. Students engage in rigorous, in-depth, interdisciplinary exploration of specific topics, periods, or themes, investigating and analyzing the intersection of material and discursive culture in different historical periods and geographical locations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty advisor.  Substantial written work required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Core Seminar I: Foundations of European Thought and Culture
allCourses.description: Provides a historical, geographical, and methodological overview of foundational texts and issues in European thought and culture. Covering several historical periods between the Middle Ages and the present, students will see how ideas and institutions change over time.

allCourses.title: Core Seminar II: Theorizing Periods and Movements in European Thought and Culture
allCourses.description: Periods and movements still form basic units for organizing European thought and theory, even as such categories are problematized. This course will allow for greater focus on a specific time period or constellation of issues around a period or movement.

allCourses.title: Core Seminar III: European Thought and Culture Beyond Europe
allCourses.description: Studies the intersection and afterlives of European thought and culture with and in non-European contexts, the way European thought and culture has been translated and transformed, taken up and challenged, in colonial, postcolonial, and other global situations.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Studies
allCourses.description: Seminars on various topics related to European Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. School of Humanities students only.
allCourses.description: For students to do independent research with advisors on their master's thesis or master's examination reading lists.

allCourses.title: Topics in Europe in the Middle Ages
allCourses.description: Explores the literature, history, and thought of the European Middle Ages. Topics may include understandings of self and community, aristocratic power and courtly life, colonialism, crusading, religious beliefs and persecution, monasticism and reform, university culture, epic literature, and Arthurian romance.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Historical Foundations: Europe and the Foundations of the Modern World
allCourses.description: Encompasses a variety of perspectives in the social sciences and the humanities involving crucial developments coming out of Europe from roughly 1500 to 1800, (the Protestant Reformation through the French Revolution), that helped shape the modern (western) world.

allCourses.title: Europe's Futures: 1755-Present
allCourses.description: Introduces students to competing approaches from humanities and social sciences to conceptualizing the future in politics, art, and literature. From the enlightenment to today, investigates the cultural and political context of moments when new ideas emerged to secure Europe's futures.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Reporting for Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Financial reporting is concerned with the preparation and public dissemination of financial reports designed to reflect corporate performance and financial condition. Provides a base level of knowledge needed by corporate executives to understand and discuss corporate financial statements.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Investments Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to how securities are traded and how their prices are determined. Discussion of different market organizations, including some recently developed online financial markets. Study of pricing models, including Capital Asset, factor models, and Arbitrage Pricing Theory.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Foundations of Finance
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines foundations of finance. Teaches tools such as time value of money, capital budgeting techniques, cash flow analysis. Examines foundations of investment management and theory/empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, option pricing theory.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Master of Finance ProSeminar
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students in the Merage School Master of Finance program with information and practical skills for success in the program and for business career planning.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Research Methodology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction into the computational research methods necessary in modern finance, such as optimization, simulation methods, and finite difference and finite element methods. Some applications include quadratic programming for portfolio selection and option pricing.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Risk Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines modern techniques for managing financial risks, including market, credit, liquidity, and operational risks. Covers measurement techniques for different financial risks and instruments. Discusses how risk measurement tools can be used for management of the risk/return profile of financial institutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FIN 249. FIN 249 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a working understanding of the themes and concepts of portfolio management. Covers several disciplines, such as investment valuation, investment decision-making, investing styles, asset allocation, monitoring and re-balancing portfolios, risk management strategies, performance evaluation, and attribution analysis.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
allCourses.description: Addresses concepts covering a broad spectrum of debt securities with emphasis on qualitative and quantitative analysis of fixed income securities in many areas, including corporate (credit) debt, MBS/ABS, structured debt, and credit derivatives.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Multinational Finance
allCourses.description: Examines the history of the world’s foreign exchange markets, the macroeconomics of foreign exchange, major parity conditions, hedging of currency exposure and international investment. Gives students a basic understanding of foreign exchange market.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: FinTech
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Seminar in Management of the Real Estate Enterprise
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Capstone seminar. Looks beyond “The Deal” to management of the real estate enterprise itself. Explores aspects of decision-making focused upon strategic objectives: goal setting, legal/tax structures, public vs. closely-held entities, corporate ethics, capital structure, managing growth, diversification, technology. Guest professionals.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Applied Real Estate Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the public real estate investment trust (REIT) market and its place in modern investment strategies, presents methods for analyzing and valuing companies, and introduces basic concepts for constructing and managing a real estate investment portfolio.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Cases in Corporate Financial Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Case-based course in corporate finance. Introduces advanced analytical tools and techniques for value-based financial management in a broad range of corporate settings, including financial forecasting, mergers and acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, ownership and control, corporate restructuring, and financial distress.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Expands on concepts covered in introductory finance. Combines lectures and cases designed to confront students with real-world problems to enhance their understanding of the value and limitations of finance theory. Focuses on the value of firms/projects in diverse settings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FIN 210. FIN 210 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Covers major derivative instruments that are widely used for hedging, including forward, futures, swaps and options, speculation, and arbitrage. Focuses on understanding the instruments, how to use and price them, basic risk management principles, and how to implement investment strategies.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on mastering mergers and acquisitions concepts and techniques that will enable participants to practically apply them in related fields such as investment banking, consulting, and corporate development. Studies drivers of success in M&A with heavy attention on transactional review.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Behavioral Finance
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Describes the scientific evidence about where misvaluation comes from, how investors can trade profitably to exploit market inefficiency, how corporate managers should make financing and investment decisions in an inefficient market, and how managers can correct biases to avoid mistakes.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Wealth Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides overview of considerations needed to connect singular functional areas that comprise personal and business wealth management, including basic and advanced estate planning, investment management, tax management, life/liability and property/casualty insurance, medical and long‐term care coverage, retirement and philanthropy considerations.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of venture capital and private equity, which constitute the “alternative” asset class (as opposed to conventional investments). Many start-up and entrepreneurial firms require substantial capital, and venture capital and private equity organizations finance these high-risk but potentially high-reward companies.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Advanced Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Describes the scientific evidence about where misvaluation come from, how investors can trade profitably to exploit market inefficiency, how corporate managers should make financing and investment decisions in an inefficient market, and how managers can correct their own biases.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FIN 249. FIN 249 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Finance Internship
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with opportunities to apply knowledge obtained from classroom theory through actual practical work experiences. Also provides knowledge of career opportunities, understanding of finance in business environments, and preparation for the finance profession.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Finance
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of finance. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Master of Finance Capstone
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Students work in teams on an applied finance project associated with their area of focus to demonstrate knowledge and expertise. The project can involve experiential learning, collaboration with a faculty member, or association with an internship.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a select faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: History of Film I: The Silent Era
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from its invention to the adoption of synchronous sound. Includes early exhibition, developments in narrative and editing, the formation of the studio system, and avant-garde film movements. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: History of Film II: The Studio Era
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from the 1930s through the 1960s. Includes the Hollywood studio system, propaganda films, Italian neorealism, post-war Japanese cinema, and the French New Wave. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: History of Film III: The Contemporary Era
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from the late 1960s to the present. Includes New Hollywood and independent U.S. films, ethnic cinemas, postcolonial cinemas, East-Asian new waves, and digital filmmaking. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A and FLM&MDA 101B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Film and Media Theory
allCourses.description: Survey of major directions in film and media theory. Various theories of mass culture, realism, auteurism, semiotics, feminism, cultural studies, and theories of other media, with an emphasis on developing the student’s ability to analyze and articulate a theoretical argument. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A and FLM&MDA 85B and FLM&MDA 85C and (FLM&MDA 101A or FLM&MDA 101B or FLM&MDA 101C). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Film and Media Theory and Practice
allCourses.description: Seminar focusing on issues in film and media production and editing. Reading and exercises to understand aspects of film and media production (montage, sound, film movement, directing, and mise en scène), and how ideology works in tandem with style.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A and FLM&MDA 85B and FLM&MDA 85C and FLM&MDA 120A and (FLM&MDA 101A or FLM&MDA 101B or FLM&MDA 101C). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Genre Study
allCourses.description: Critical approaches to the serial productions we call "genre" films such as westerns, weepies, musicals, horror films, and others; televisual genres, such as sitcoms, drama, comedy, news, docudrama, police; Internet categories, such as chat-rooms, listservs, Web pages.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Narrative/Image
allCourses.description: What relations do sound, image, and story assume in film, television, video, and Internet narratives? In what ways do these media interact with and borrow from each other and traditional story-telling media? How have the new media explored non-narrative strategies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Film, Media, and the Arts
allCourses.description: A synthetic entity, film draws on both established and popular arts. Looks at visual media's exchanges with "high" and "low" culture, exploring its relation to areas such as photography, music, painting, and architecture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Authorship
allCourses.description: Theoretical and analytical discussions of visual media authorship, focusing on case studies of directors, producers, scriptwriters, and film, video, and digital artists.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Screenwriting
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technique and format of the screenplay, with a particular focus on its three act structural elements: coverage, treatment, and 60 beat outline. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Screenwriting
allCourses.description: Exercises in the development of screenplays, with emphasis on formal and structural considerations of character development. Students work with the hero structure and other character development methodologies, such as method acting. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 117A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Screenwriting Workshop
allCourses.description: Continuation and intensification of work initiated in 117B. Students complete a full-length screenplay. Concentrates on both practical and technical concerns, addressing pragmatic and aesthetic questions in intensive small-group discussions. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 117B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Writing Television I
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technique and format of the television screenplay. Focuses on character, storytelling, structure, and scene development; culminating in a one-hour drama series treatment and first act of the pilot.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Writing Television II
allCourses.description: Intermediate-level screenwriting class exploring the one-hour television drama format. Students write and workshop an original pilot, continuing work started in 118A, and finish a complete draft of the pilot script.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 118A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Basic Production
allCourses.description: Introduction to the basic apparatus of video/film production. The elementary essentials of production, including the use of camera and lenses, lighting, editing, and sound. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Production
allCourses.description: Students work on individual and group projects, utilizing skills and insights introduced in Film and Media Studies 120A. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 120A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Production Workshop
allCourses.description: As film and video are collaborative media, students form production groups and ultimately produce final 10-15-minute film/video projects. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 120B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Multicultural Topics in the Media
allCourses.description: Investigation of media representations of gender, race, and sexuality in the United States. Topics include media images of and by one or more minority groups in the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicano/Latinos, Native Americans, gays, and lesbians.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Writing on Film and Media
allCourses.restriction: Film and Media Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Writing on cinema, television, and/or digital culture, emphasizing identification of reliable sources, close readings, addressing academic, professional, and/or popular audiences. Requires at least 4,000 words of assigned composition.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A or FLM&MDA 85B or FLM&MDA 85C. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Critical Theory of Television
allCourses.description: Introduction to critical, theoretical, and scholarly understandings and analyses of television, which offer in-depth analyses of television programming, audience reception practices, and industry strategies of address.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Studies in New Media
allCourses.description: Advanced analysis of the technologies, texts, theories, and cultures of computers, video games, networks, or platforms.
