allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85C. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Popular Culture and Media
allCourses.description: Considers the forms, ideologies, consumption, and marketing of popular entertainment and technologies. May focus on cultural studies methods, transnational approaches, and synergy between media.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Sound Studies
allCourses.description: Focuses on the production, theories, and meanings of sound recordings, music, and/or audio technologies. Topics may include the cultures of popular music and audio devices, music television, and theories of film sound.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Audiences and Reception
allCourses.description: Explores the dynamics of address, interpretation, and appropriation between film and media texts and their viewers. Topics may include reception studies, fandom, audience-defined modes of production, demographics, spectatorial pleasure, and historical approaches to audiences.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Documentary and Experimental Film and Media
allCourses.description: Examines nonfiction and/or experimental cinemas and media, such as documentary, the historical avant-garde, video art, and activist media. Students consider the specific aesthetics and ideologies of forms distinct from narrative feature films.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FLM&MDA 85A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: National/Regional Cinemas and Media
allCourses.description: National schools, period styles, or cultural movements beyond U.S. cinema, as defined by national borders or by geographic regions, such as Latin America. May be approached from a comparative perspective.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Global/Transnational Cinemas and Media
allCourses.description: Analyzes the multinational production, circulation, and reception of film and media texts beyond singular national borders or specific geographic regions. Topics may include transnational co-productions, exports, and diasporic reception.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: US Cinema

allCourses.title: Data Analytics for Games and Interactive Media
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Survey of analysis methods for understanding player data, including playtesting, telemetry data collection and analysis, metrics visualization, and its application in development and business.

allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of game programming. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Games and Society
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of games and their relationship to society. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multiplayer Game Project
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors are given second consideration.
allCourses.description: Design and develop a multiplayer game using Unity or similar engine, with a focus on learning to work in a development team, writing design documents, working with platform features and limitations, developing engaging mechanics, playtesting, and post-mortems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: GDIM 27 and GDIM 33 and GDIM 51 and GDIM 61. GDIM 27 with a grade of C or better. GDIM 33 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Solo Game Project
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second consideration.
allCourses.description: Students work on their own to design, develop, and playtest a small game from scratch, taking into consideration psychology, narrative, platform features and limitations, marketing, computer science capabilities, human-computer interface principles, industry trends, aesthetic judgment, and other factors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: GDIM 27 and GDIM 33 and GDIM 51 and GDIM 61. GDIM 27 with a grade of C or better. GDIM 33 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Games Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second consideration.
allCourses.description: As the audiences for games continue to diversify so have the channels for game publishing and monetization. Explore connections between the business and creative side of games in context like esports, education, indie game development, mobile apps, and AAA studios.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Game Project I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Students work in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience. Emphasis on sound, art, and level design, building a community, production values, full utilization of hardware and software platform, and current industry trends.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ICS 168 or (GDIM 131 and GDIM 161). GDIM 161 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Game Project II
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Students continue work in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience. Emphasis on sound, art, and level design, building a community, production values, full utilization of hardware and software platform, and current industry trends.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: GDIM 167A or ICS 169A. GDIM 167A with a grade of C or better. ICS 169A with a grade of C or better. In Progress grade for GDIM 167A or ICS 169A also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Game Design Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration
allCourses.description: Explore the fundamentals of game design through the design and play of simple analog game systems. Students explore the principles and usage of game design elements through hands-on projects emphasizing iteration and playtesting in a creative game design community.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Intermediate Game Design
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: More advanced study of game design principles and systems design through the study of complex problems and play experiences. Topics include economies, game balancing, level design, prototyping, stat design, playtesting, and design documentation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming for Games
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Learn the fundamentals of programming for games through hands-on exercises in programming languages like C#, Processing, Visual Studio, .NET, and the Unity engine. Students build several small game prototypes. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Intermediate Programming for Games
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors will have second consideration.
allCourses.description: Students advance their skills with game programming, building on existing skills developed in Introduction to Programming for Games. Hands-on projects emphasize general procedural and problem-solving skills, as well as furthering knowledge of C# and the Unity3D/Unreal game engines.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Coding In Game Engines
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to visual scripting tools in game engines in the context of game design, level, design, and experience design. Students gain fluency in one or more visual scripting languages.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: GDIM 32. GDIM 32 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Games and Society
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: The study and critical analysis of computer games as art objects, cultural artifacts, gateways to virtual worlds, educational aids, and tools for persuasion and social change. Emphasis on understanding games in their historical and cultural context.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Games and Society
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of games and their relationship to society. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Visual Design Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: The principles, tools, and techniques of visual design for playable media. How do shape, line, color, composition, typography, and time work together to communicate information, emotion, and meaning in interfaces, game worlds, and stories. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Roleplaying and Improvisational Play
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: How do practices of performance, role-playing, and improvisation overlap with contemporary practices of game design? Connecting these forms of play to their contemporary uses within role-playing games, virtual worlds, and playable media more broadly.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Storytelling for Interactive Media
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: The history, theory, and practice of interactive storytelling for games and other interactive media. Starting with the emergence of electronic literature and hypertext narratives, students encounter and experience a compressed history of this emergent form through play, analysis, and design. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Game Development
allCourses.restriction: Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design and development of games. Includes core concepts in software development, team management, leadership, and project management.

allCourses.title: Feminism and Social Change
allCourses.description: Explores feminist modes of knowledge production in relation to histories and activist practices of various social movements. Examines the kinds of information, research, ideas, theories, and concepts that underlie feminist cultural analysis and social movement organizing.

allCourses.title: Feminist Theory
allCourses.description: Introduction to historical traditions in theory and various conceptual frameworks informing scholarship in gender studies, sexuality studies, and women's studies as a field of critical inquiry.

allCourses.title: Feminist Cultural Studies
allCourses.description: Investigation of the theories and methods that inform the feminist study of culture.  Focuses on the interpretation of the visual arts and literature created by, and predominately for, women.

allCourses.title: Queer Knowledges
allCourses.description: Explores the emergence of historical elaboration of non-normative sexual identities, practices, and communities; focuses on medical, legal, literary, aesthetic, scientific, and religious notions about homosexuality and appropriations and subversions of these notions by queer people.

allCourses.title: Gender, State, and Nation
allCourses.description: Examination of gender and sexuality in relation to the production of identities created through participation in state and nation. Examines complexity of relationship between feminism and nationalism, feminism and the state.

allCourses.title: Money, Sex, and Power
allCourses.description: Examination of gender and sexuality in relation to the emergence of the modern world, modernity, and capitalism; commodification, circulation, and transnational exchanges relating to race, gender, class, sexuality, religion, and nationality.

allCourses.title: The Politics of Health and Medicine
allCourses.description: Focuses on cultural and political-economic analysis and representations of disease both within the U.S. and globally.

allCourses.title: Histories of Sexuality
allCourses.description: Examines the historical production of non-normative sexual and gender identities, bodies, practices, and communities. Explores how past formations inform and shape the present and future.

allCourses.title: Image Problems
allCourses.description: Examination of scholarly approaches to gender stereotypes and politics of representation as they present possibilities for critical analysis and produce problems and limitations; how powerful ideas of gender intersect with other forms of social differentiation such as race and class.

allCourses.title: Practices of Embodiment
allCourses.description: Explores how science, medicine, and law have shaped the understanding of differentiated bodies; examines shifting norms and ideals about producing, shaping, adorning, and dressing gendered bodies across diverse historical, cultural, social, economic, and spatial contexts.

allCourses.description: Various topics in gender studies. Encompasses issues of gender, culture, race and class, including issues of sexualities and social justice.

allCourses.description: Examination of feminist approaches to militarism, war, and political violence; drawing on representations of women as both victims of and participants in military violence; effects of militarism on formations of gender; effects of military industrial complex on nationalism and identity.

allCourses.title: Gender and Feminism in Everyday Life
allCourses.description: What is gender? Why does studying it matter? Explores how feminism has understood not only gender as a category of social analysis, but how gender structures personal identities, family, citizenship, work and leisure, social policy, sexuality, and language.

allCourses.title: Gender and Power
allCourses.description: From workplace to home to schools to prisons, how are societal institutions and politics “gendered”? Examines power and inequalities around gender, race, class, and sexuality in national and transnational contexts.

allCourses.title: Gender and Popular Culture
allCourses.description: An investigation of gender, race, and sexuality in film, TV, video, music, and advertising, with attention to the ways that popular culture shapes understandings of technology, national identities, leisure and work, historical memory, international communication, and multicultural representation.

allCourses.title: Gender and Science
allCourses.description: Examines science from a variety of feminist viewpoints in order to explore how science influences everyday life.  Special attention is given to the ways science shapes our understanding of gender, race, and sexuality.

allCourses.title: Gender and Law
allCourses.description: Introduction to the relationship between gender, race, sexuality, and the law.  Critical thinking about how law defines citizenship, political representation, and democracy, focusing on the history of legal reform undertaken in the name of women as a social group.

allCourses.title: Gender and Religion
allCourses.description: Introduces the topic of religion in a feminist context by performing cross-cultural exploration of gender, authority, and faith in various traditions. Study includes (but is not limited to) writings of contemporary Jewish, Christian, and Muslim feminists.

allCourses.description: Examination of subjects relevant to the culture of Israel and Judaism in their historical and modern day contexts through the study of film, literature, religious texts, artistic representations, etc.

allCourses.title: The Holocaust
allCourses.description: Introduction to the history of European Jewish communities before the Holocaust; the origins of Nazi antisemitism; the implementation of the "Final Solution"; Jewish resistance to the Nazis; and attempts in film and literature to represent the Holocaust since 1945.

allCourses.title: Topics in Environmental History
allCourses.description: Explores the many historical interfaces between climate change, modes of production, and culture. Topics include the environmental history of warfare, imperialism, and famine in the nineteenth century and the history of environmental thought.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity Since WWII
allCourses.description: Investigates instances of genocide since 1945 (including Cambodia, Bosnia, Rwanda, and others); explores the history behind these mass murders; considers why people kill, how victims survive, and questions whether international agreements are enough to prevent crimes against humanity.

allCourses.title: Topics in Medieval Europe
allCourses.description: Theme-based approach to the main social, political, religious, and cultural developments in Europe between the 4th and 15th centuries. Topics include the Crusades, medieval towns, medieval visionaries, and the deadly sins.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Early Modern Europe
allCourses.description: Theme-based approach to the main social, political, and cultural developments in Europe between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries.  Topics included Renaissance humanism, Reformation and Counter-Reformation, scientific revolution, court culture and nation building, interactions with non-European peoples, cities and commerce.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern European History
allCourses.description: Course content changes with instructor. Topics include the Inquisition; science and religion in modern Europe; sex and society in modern Europe; French revolutions; culture in interwar Europe; the Holocaust; the fall of communism in Eastern Europe.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in History

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: War and Empire: France and the World in the 20th Century
allCourses.description: Examines French experience of World War I, the defeat and occupation by Germany in World War II, the violent struggles that came with the loss of the French empire in the 1950s and 1960s, immigration, French responses to globalization.

allCourses.title: Hitler and the Germans
allCourses.description: Focuses on Hitler's rise to power and Nazi society. Examines Germany's defeat in World War I; the political and cultural experimentation of the 1920s; the causes of Hitler's success; and life in Germany under the Nazis.

allCourses.title: Topics in Spanish History
allCourses.description: Topics include Spain in the nineteenth century, the Spanish Civil War, and dictatorship and democracy in modern Spain.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Twentieth-Century Russia

Topics include medieval religious anti-Judaism, persecution of Jews and Judaism during the Crusades and the Inquisition, the rise of modern racial antisemitism, Nazi antisemitism, and the persistence of antisemitism since 1945.

allCourses.title: Jews and Power
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority.

allCourses.title: History of Zoroastrianism
allCourses.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

allCourses.title: Ancient Persia

allCourses.title: Medieval Persia
allCourses.description: A survey of Persian history in the context of Late Antique and Medieval Islamic history.

allCourses.title: Modern Iran

allCourses.title: The Emergence of the Modern Middle East

allCourses.title: Women and Gender in the Middle East

allCourses.title: Armenians and Armenia in Modern World History
allCourses.description: Covers the most important themes in the history of Armenians and Armenia in the 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries within a regional (i.e., Middle East and Caucasus) and global context.

allCourses.title: History of the African Diaspora
allCourses.description: Examines the causes and consequences of the multiple diasporas of African peoples since the sixteenth century in the Atlantic world, especially the Americas and Europe.

allCourses.description: An examination of early modern European science from 1500-1700. allCourses.title: Crossing the World's Oceans: From Sail to Steam
allCourses.description: Explores the basics of oceanography, the evolution of ships and sailing in the ancient Mediterranean world, the North Atlantic, Polynesia, the South China Sea, the Arab Indian Ocean, the global oceanic world, and the discovery of celestial and terrestrial navigation.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Science and Technology

allCourses.description: Analyzes diverse social and cultural responses to epidemics from mid-nineteenth century to the present, including incarceration, caregiving, and disability rights. Using interdisciplinary materials and collaborative activities, students interpret strategies and outcomes of Indigenous, racialized, and marginalized communities surviving great illness.

allCourses.description: An exploration of why 13 continental colonies, whose commercial and cultural connections with Britain far exceed their interaction with one another, resisted imperial reform after 1763 to the point of war in 1775 and independence the following year.

allCourses.title: California Dreaming: Conquest, Conflict, and Globalization in the Golden State
allCourses.description: California as a case study of national trends and as a unique setting: its specific problems and culture. Major themes include: colonization, immigration, race relations, agricultural development, industrialization, urbanization, working class movements, social conflict, and political reform.

allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of American social and economic history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

allCourses.title: Education and the American Dream: Historical Perspectives on Democracy and Education
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between public schooling and the promotion of democratic ideals in American society over the past two centuries.

allCourses.title: Topics in Multicultural U.S. History
allCourses.description: Examines the variety of cultural expressions through which the people who came to inhabit the United States historically signify their collective identities.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Veterans in History and Society
allCourses.description: Explores key concepts, issues, and trends in the interdisciplinary field of veterans studies. Students gain a deep understanding of the ways that social scientists and historians have analyzed the identities, experiences, and worldviews of U.S. military veterans.

allCourses.title: Topics in African American History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of African American history.  Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Chicana/Chicano History: Twentieth Century
allCourses.description: Examines social history of the Southwest with emphasis on Mexican-origin people. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicana/Chicano history. Themes explored include: immigration, xenophobia, class struggle, leadership, generational cohorts, unionization, education, barrioization, ethnicity, patriarchy, sexuality.

allCourses.title: Latinas in the Twentieth Century U.S.
allCourses.description: Latinas in the U.S. from 1900 to present, offering a diversity of their cultures, regional histories, sexualities, generations, and classes.

allCourses.title: Latina/Latino Pop:  Latina/Latino Popular Culture
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. History Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: With a focus on the politics of language and space/place, prepares students to critically analyze sites of Latina/Latino popular culture including: music, film, performance, sports, media, and varied subcultures.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian-American History
allCourses.description: Introduction to important themes in the history of people of Asian ancestry in the United States from the nineteenth century to the present.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Labor
allCourses.description: Explores history of Asian Americans and work from the nineteenth century to the present. Areas of study include migration, colonialism, family, social organization, and work culture.

allCourses.title: American Urban History
allCourses.description: A study of urban communities in the United States, from colonial times to the present. Traces the impact of industrialization and urbanization on social and cultural life, and investigates the significance of urban life for U.S. democratic culture.

allCourses.title: Native American History
allCourses.description: Native American history in North America, emphasizing Indigenous perspectives and creative adaptations to changing historical circumstances. Topics may include sovereignty, settler colonialism, treaties, decolonization, Indigeneity; cultural, economic, religious, environmental practices and experiences; and intersections of U.S. and Native histories.

allCourses.title: Asian American Histories
allCourses.description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

allCourses.title: History of Sexuality in the US
allCourses.description: Explores intertwined histories of sexuality, race, and gender in the US. By examining how different cultures and times viewed sexuality, race and gender, it analyzes relationships between regulation of bodies/behaviors and construction of cultural, economic, and political norms.

allCourses.title: What to Eat? Immigrants and the Development of American Cuisines
allCourses.description: Relationship between immigration and changing American foodways; impact of several major culinary traditions of immigrants and racial minorities, such as African Americans, Asian Americans, Mexican Americans, Italian Americans, Irish Americans, and Jewish Americans, on America’s gastronomical and socioeconomic landscape.

allCourses.title: Racial Segregation in Modern U.S.
allCourses.description: Explores the history of racial segregation in the United States from the late 19th century to the present.

allCourses.title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
allCourses.description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

allCourses.title: Topics in Brazilian History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Brazilian history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: World of Coffee
allCourses.description: History of consumption and production of coffee over the centuries, and coffee's cultural, economic, social, political consequences. Coffee's social life as a drug, symbol of hospitality, religious rite, sociability and bourgeois lifestyle, commodity, source of livelihoods, imperial revenues, corporate profits.

allCourses.title: Caribbean History: Colonization to Emancipation
allCourses.description: Exploration of the history of the archipelago from pre-Columbian times to the end of slavery; examining the impact of European colonization, decimation of the indigenous populations, African slavery, resistance, and emancipation; the unity and diversity of experience in region.

allCourses.title: Caribbean History: Emancipation to Independence
allCourses.description: Post-emancipation and anti-colonial struggles ending with political independence for most of the region. Examines social, political, economic, cultural dimensions of post-emancipation period, including large-scale migration to Central America, the U.S., and Britain; the region's global cultural and political contribution.

allCourses.title: Race and Empire in Colonial Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores how native people of Latin America with enslaved and free African incorporated and defied Spanish and Portuguese colonization. Focuses on religious adaptions, resistance movements, legal systems, and the emergence of multicultural communities to explain how race shaped European empires.

allCourses.title: War and Revolution in Colonial Latin America
allCourses.description: Comparison of how Andeans resurrected the leaders of the Inca, a defeated indigenous empire, to contest the Spanish empire with how enslaved Africans, with their descendants and others, defeated Spanish colonial rule in what would become the Cuban nation.

allCourses.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

allCourses.title: Revolution and Reaction in Cold War Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores Latin American experiences of revolutionary change and military dictatorship during the Cold War (1945-1990). Pays particular attention to the lives of women, peasants, workers, and the urban middle classes. Case studies include Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, Argentina, Nicaragua, and Mexico.

allCourses.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
allCourses.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

allCourses.title: Revolution in Latin America
allCourses.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada.  Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

allCourses.title: Topics in Latin American History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Latin American history.  Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: World Religions I

allCourses.title: World Religions II
allCourses.description: An introduction to various religious traditions in selected areas of the world—including India and South Asia, East Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

allCourses.title: Religious Dialogue
allCourses.description: Lectures and discussion on controversial topics in religion: sexual morality; religious violence; science; treatment of women and girls; religious truth, American Constitutional matters; secularization; the future of religion, and other topics.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan.  Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.title: Chinese History to 1800
allCourses.description: A survey of the history of China to 1800.

allCourses.title: Chinese History: 1800-1949
allCourses.description: An examination of Chinese society and thought from the late-eighteenth century to the 1949 revolution. Focuses on the role of intellectuals; popular culture; women in Chinese society; developments in commerce and urban life; rebellion; foreign imperialism.

allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of China.

allCourses.description: Offers an overview of the Viet Nam War; explores the art of doing oral history and the use of oral testimony in research and writing the history of war through conducting oral history interviews with individuals of the war generation.

allCourses.description: Introduction to the diversity of Jewish cultures from ancient to modern times. Surveys the Jewish experience in various societies and civilizations: ancient Mediterranean, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

allCourses.title: Internships in Public History
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. History Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students will sharpen their abilities to research, critically interpret, and present history by “doing history” beyond the formal classroom. Internships, which introduce students to the field of “public history,” include working as archivists, oral historians, project advisers, and exhibit curators.

allCourses.description: Research and writing of a paper demonstrating command of historical methods explored in HISTORY 202A. Required of all first-year Ph.D. students and M.A. students.

allCourses.title: Second-Year Research Seminar

allCourses.title: World:  Innovations
allCourses.description: Treats major themes of world historical development through the mid-seventeenth century, focusing on the Eurasian world, but with secondary emphasis on Africa and the Americas.

allCourses.title: World: Empires and Revolutions
allCourses.description: Examines three major transformations that made the world of 1870 dramatically different from that of 1650: e.g., the scientific revolution, industrialization, and the formation of modern states and nations.

allCourses.title: World: Nation, War, and Rights
allCourses.description: Considers several major currents of modern history: technological change and its social effects; changes in gender relations; totalitarianism; peasant revolutions and the crisis of colonization; international migration; and ecological problems.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Early Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from its origins in the Bronze Age to the mid-Archaic period. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, religion, and archaeological remains.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society:  Late Archaic and Classical Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the Late Archaic period to the Classical period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Fourth-Century and Hellenistic Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the fourth century BCE through to the Hellenistic period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Origins to Roman Republic
allCourses.description: A survey of the development of Roman civilization from its eighth century BCE beginnings to the civil wars of the first century BCE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Roman Empire
allCourses.description: A survey of Roman civilization from Augustus’s consolidation of power following the civil wars of the first century BCE to the crisis of the third century CE. Includes social history, literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: The Fall of Rome
allCourses.description: A survey of Roman civilization from the crisis of the third century CE to the so-called “fall of Rome” in 476 CE.  Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Colonial America:  New Worlds
allCourses.description: Important themes in the social, economic, political, and cultural development in North America that transformed part of the geographical space into the U.S. Topics include Native Americans, European colonization, African enslavement, borderlands, gender, economic stratification, the American Revolution, the Constitution.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Nineteenth-Century U.S.: Crisis and Expansion
allCourses.description: Explores the transformation of American society, economy, and politics during the nineteenth century. Topics include industrial revolution, slavery, antislavery, women's rights, reform movements, Civil War and Reconstruction, immigration and ethnicity, and cultural and social transformation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Modern America:  Culture and Power
allCourses.description: Important themes in U.S. history in the twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. Topics include corporate capitalism, empire, immigration, race, gender, consumer society, World Wars, Progressiveness, New Deal, Great Society, civil rights, women's movements, Vietnam War, conservative politics, and economic stratification.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Truth, Lies, and History: The Uses of the Past
allCourses.description: Focuses on how struggles over the meaning of historical events have shaped and continue to shape our understandings of the world. Through guest lectures from history faculty, students explore debates about the meaning of the past.

allCourses.title: Crises and Revolutions
allCourses.description: Study of turning points in world history, illustrating themes and methods of historical analysis.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: The Making of Modern Science
allCourses.description: Surveys the history of science and mathematics since the Scientific Revolution, examining central developments both chronologically and thematically, as well as investigating their significance for contemporary philosophical debates about the role and status of current scientific theories.

allCourses.description: An introduction to the historical problems, the issues of interpretation, the primary sources, and the historical scholarship of the history of Asia, with an emphasis on developing skills in historical essay-writing.

allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of current issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. allCourses.description: A workshop seminar exploring the theory and practice of visual design, data visualization, and oral presentation. Designed to get students to think about, and hone their skills in, effective presentation of information in multiple media.
