allCourses.title: Exploring Memory
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Questions about human memory are central to a wide range of disciplines. Students will explore how historians, sociologists, social psychologists, legal experts, and neuroscientists understand human memory and apply their findings to understand and shape their own societies.

allCourses.title: The Vietnam War
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the origins, evolution, opposition against, conclusion, and legacy of the United States in the Vietnam War.

allCourses.title: How Nations Remember
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Just like people, nations select and organize what and how they want to remember. Compares how specific historical events (such as slavery and the Holocaust) are memorialized in various countries and represented in public art works, museums, literature, and film.

allCourses.title: Traveling East/West
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Traveling East/West presents a wide range of travel writings by Chinese, Indian, and Euro-American authors in which they contemplate the complexities of cross-cultural encounters and how knowledge about others and knowledge of ourselves are closely intertwined.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: How Computers Work
allCourses.restriction: May not be taken for credit after I&C SCI 31, I&C SCI 32, I&C SCI 32A, I&C SCI 51, I&C SCI 105, or IN4MATX 43.
allCourses.description: Introduction to digital computer and communication systems. Capabilities and limitations of information technology. Representing information in digital form. Overview of computer organization, internet, operating systems, software. Human-computer interaction and social impact.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: The Internet and Public Policy
allCourses.description: How the Internet works. Current public policy issues concerning the Internet. Introductory economics. Communications law. Interactions between information technology, economics, and law. Case studies about Internet and communications policy.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Critical Writing on Information Technology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study and practice of critical writing and oral communication as it applies to information technology. Each student writes assignments of varying lengths, totaling at least 4,000 words.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Game Engine Lab
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The use of an open source game or graphics engine in the design and implementation of a computer game. Principles of game engine design. Students work on teams to design, implement, and evaluate new computer games based on an engine.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 45C or CSE 45C or GDIM 32

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Modeling and World Building
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Use of 3D modeling software and related tools to design and create animated, textured models, and expansive virtual worlds incorporating objects, scenes, and venues for activity within game worlds and online environments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 33 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A) and I&C SCI 61

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Mobile and Ubiquitous Games
allCourses.description: Design and technology of mobile games, including mixed reality gaming, urban games, and locative media. Case studies of significant systems. Uses and limitations of location-based technologies. Infrastructures and their relationships to gameplay and design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 61 and (I&C SCI 10 or I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI 32A)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Game Design
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Game design takes into consideration psychology, narrative, platform features and limitations, marketing, computer science capabilities, human-computer interface principles, industry trends, aesthetic judgment, and other factors. Students focus on video game design through lectures, readings, presentations, implementation, and play testing.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multiplayer Game Systems
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Foundations and technologies that enable multiuser, networked, and persistent virtual environments. Emphasis on database design and management, network protocols, and concurrency control to accommodate large numbers of simultaneous users.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multiplayer Game Project
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors are given second consideration.
allCourses.description: Design and develop a multiplayer game using Unity or similar engine, with a focus on learning to work in a development team, writing design documents, working with platform features and limitations, developing engaging mechanics, playtesting, and post-mortems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: GDIM 27 and GDIM 33 and GDIM 51 and GDIM 61. GDIM 27 with a grade of C or better. GDIM 33 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Game Project I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Students work in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience. Emphasis on sound, art, and level design, building a community, production values, full utilization of hardware and software platform, and current industry trends.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 168 or (GDIM 131 and GDIM 161). GDIM 161 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Game Project II
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors given second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: Students continue work in teams to design and implement a unique game or interactive experience. Emphasis on sound, art, and level design, building a community, production values, full utilization of hardware and software platform, and current industry trends.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: GDIM 167A or I&C SCI 169A. GDIM 167A with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 169A with a grade of C or better. In Progress grade for GDIM 167A or I&C SCI 169A also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Industrial or Public Sector Field Study
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students participate in an off-campus, supervised internship for a minimum of 60 hours. Students apply classroom knowledge through internship projects in the private sector or nonprofit agencies.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Tutoring in ICS
allCourses.restriction: ICS Peer Tutoring Program students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and practice of providing technical assistance to novice learners in information and computer sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 18 units.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Invitation to Computing
allCourses.description: Foundational principles of computer science for students with no computing background that are interested in a related career. Big ideas of computing explored, including programming through use of sequential, conditional, iterative logic. Good computational practices, problem solving, and organization discussed.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Internet Technologies and their Social Impact
allCourses.description: Examines current Internet technologies and social implications at the individual, group, and societal level. Blogs, wikis, sharing of video, photos, and music, e-commerce, social networking, gaming, and virtual environments. Issues include privacy, trust, identity, reputation, governance, copyright, and malicious behavior.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts and techniques for writing software in a high-level programming language. Covers the syntax and semantics of data types, expressions, exceptions, control structures, input/output, methods, classes, and pragmatics of programming.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Programming with Software Libraries
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Construction of programs for problems and computing environments more varied than in I&C SCI 31. Using library modules for applications such as graphics, sound, GUI, database, Web, and network programming. Language features beyond those in I&C SCI 31 are introduced as needed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( CSE 41 OR I&C SCI 31 ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Python Programming and Libraries (Accelerated)
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces Python syntax and semantics for fundamental programming concepts.  Constructing programs for varied problems and environments. Using library modules for applications such as graphics, sound, GUI, database, Web, and network programming. Accelerated course for students with previous programming background.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: AP COMP SCI A AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Python Programming and Libraries (Accelerated)
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces Python syntax and semantics for fundamental programming concepts.  Constructing programs for varied problems and environments. Using library modules for applications such as graphics, sound, GUI, database, Web, and network programming. Accelerated course for students with previous programming background.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: AP COMP SCI A AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Intermediate Programming
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Intermediate-level language features and programming concepts for larger, more complex, higher-quality software. Functional programming, name spaces, modules, class protocols, inheritance, iterators, generators, operator overloading, reflection. Analysis of time and space efficiency.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 32 or CSE 42 or I&C SCI 32A. I&C SCI 32 with a grade of C or better. CSE 42 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 32A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Seminar
allCourses.description: Theories, methods, and resources for teaching computer science at the university level, particularly by teaching assistants. Classroom presentations, working with individuals, grading, motivating students. Participants will give and critique presentations and may be videotaped while teaching.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Teaching Assistant Seminar
allCourses.description: Teaching computer science at the university level, emphasizing issues in teaching an entire course. Course organization, designing examinations and projects, grading, motivating students. Participants will begin to assemble teaching portfolios.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Teaching assistants only.
allCourses.description: Involves on-the-job experience for Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Factors for the Web
allCourses.restriction: May not be taken for credit after IN4MATX 131.
allCourses.description: Principles of human-computer interaction in evaluating, designing, and developing information presented on the World Wide Web. User characteristics, usability analysis, navigation and organization. Color, typography, multimedia, information visualization, prototyping, user studies, evaluation strategies. Web accessibility.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Programming in C/C++ as a Second Language
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic characteristics of the C/C++ languages for experienced programmers. Emphasis on object-oriented programming, using standard libraries, and programming with manual garbage collection.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 33 or CSE 43 or EECS 40. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better. CSE 43 with a grade of C or better. EECS 40 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Programming in Java as a Second Language
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. I&C SCI 45J may not be taken for credit after I&C SCI 22, I&C SCI 23, or CSE 23.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic characteristics of the Java language for experienced programmers. Emphasis on object-oriented programming, using standard libraries, and programming with automatic garbage collection.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 33 or CSE 43. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better. CSE 43 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Data Structure Implementation and Analysis
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on implementation and mathematical analysis of fundamental data structures and algorithms. Covers storage allocation and memory management techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CSE 45C or I&C SCI 45C. CSE 45C with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 45C with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Global Disruption and Information Technology
allCourses.description: Explores how new forms of information technology may support transition to a sustainable civilization. Topics include design and implementation of IT systems, science of global change, online community building, and “green IT”. Activities involve reading, writing, discussion, and final project.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introductory Computer Organization
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multilevel view, design, and operation of computer system components. Machine-level data and instruction representation. Instruction sets and addressing modes. Memory organization. Laboratory work using low-level programming languages.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles in System Design
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic principles of system software: operating systems, compilers, and networking. Exposure to the following topics through theoretical and practical programming experiences: linking and loading, process and memory management, concurrency and synchronization, network communication, programming for performance, etc.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 46 and I&C SCI 51. I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 51 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles in System Design Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Required laboratory section and corequisite for I&C SCI 53.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Games and Society
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration.
allCourses.description: The study and critical analysis of computer games as art objects, cultural artifacts, gateways to virtual worlds, educational aids, and tools for persuasion and social change. Emphasis on understanding games in their historical and cultural context.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Game Design Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Computer Game Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Game Design and Interactive Media students have first consideration for enrollment. School of ICS majors have second right of consideration
allCourses.description: Explore the fundamentals of game design through the design and play of simple analog game systems. Students explore the principles and usage of game design elements through hands-on projects emphasizing iteration and playtesting in a creative game design community.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Game Technologies and Interactive Media
allCourses.description: Technologies for interactive media and game design. Web-based software systems, virtual world platforms, and game engines. Emphasis is on conceptual and architectural aspects of these technologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( CSE 41 OR I&C SCI 31 OR I&C SCI 32A )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Boolean Logic and Discrete Structures
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Relations and their properties; Boolean algebras, formal languages; finite automata.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering majors have second consideration.
allCourses.description: Covers essential tools from discrete mathematics used in computer science with an emphasis on the process of abstracting computational problems and analyzing them mathematically. Topics include mathematical induction, combinatorics, and recurrence relations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 6B AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Linear Algebra
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Matrices and linear transformations, systems of linear equations, determinants, linear vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonal matrices, diagonalization, and least squares. Topics taught primarily from an algorithmic perspective, including computational solutions, applications, and numerical error analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI 32A or AP Computer Science A. AP Computer Science A with a minimum score of 3

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Spreadsheets for Problem-Solving
allCourses.description: Features useful tools for building, solving, analyzing, and visualizing computational models in diverse areas. Covered features include data entry and protection; numerical, logical and relational computation; displaying, highlighting, and sorting data; storing, summarizing, and querying databases; and VB scripting.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of information and computer sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computation for Scientists and Engineers
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces principles, techniques, and computational tools for quantitative approach to basic problem solving in physics and engineering. Project-based course that actively explores how programing techniques are used for solving STEM real-world problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB or AP Calculus BC. AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 4. AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: New Students Seminar
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences. Focuses on advising students making the transition to UCI, community building, and mostly surveying the technical areas within departments in ICS, via talks by faculty on their research.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Bren School of ICS Honors students only. Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: An overview of computer science and selected recent trends in research. Students attend talks on current faculty research, with opportunities for discussion.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Concepts in Programming Languages I
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: In-depth study of several contemporary programming languages stressing variety in data structures, operations, notation, and control. Examination of different programming paradigms, such as logic programming, functional programming and object-oriented programming; implementation strategies, programming environments, and programming style.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 51 or CSE 31 or EECS 31) and (I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46). I&C SCI 51 with a grade of C or better. CSE 31 with a grade of C or better. EECS 31 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. CSE 46 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Concepts of Programming Language II
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: In-depth study of major programming paradigms: imperative, functional, declarative, object-oriented, and aspect-oriented. Understanding the role of programming languages in software development and the suitability of languages in context. Domain-specific languages. Designing new languages for better software development support.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Requirements Analysis and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Equips students to develop techniques of software-intensive systems through successful requirements analysis techniques and requirements engineering. Students learn systematic process of developing requirements through cooperative problem analysis, representation, and validation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 33 or CSE 43) and IN4MATX 43. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better. CSE 43 with a grade of C or better. IN4MATX 43 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Testing, Analysis, and Quality Assurance
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Preparation for developing high-quality software through successful verification and validation techniques. Fundamental principles of software testing, implementing software testing practices, ensuring the thoroughness of testing to gain confidence in the correctness of the software.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 45J or I&C SCI 45C or I&C SCI 46 or CSE 46) and IN4MATX 43. I&C SCI 45J with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 45C with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 46 with a grade of C or better. CSE 46 with a grade of C or better. IN4MATX 43 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Software System Design
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Specification, design, construction, testing, and documentation of a complete software system. Special emphasis on the need for and use of teamwork, careful planning, and other techniques for working with large systems.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Barter to Bitcoin: Society, Technology and the Future of Money
allCourses.description: Digital money has captured the broad imagination of speculators, coders, regulators, criminals and the mass media. Course puts this change in context: how do we understand money as a social, political and technological phenomenon?.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Design: Applications
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to application design: designing the overall functionality of a software application. Topics include general design theory, software design theory, and software architecture. Includes practice in designing and case studies of existing designs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 33 or CSE 43. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better. CSE 43 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Design: Structure and Implementation
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to implementation design: designing the internals of a software application. Topics include design aesthetics, design implementation, design recovery, design patterns, and component reuse. Includes practice in designing and case studies of existing designs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (I&C SCI 45J or I&C SCI 46 or IN4MATX 45) and (IN4MATX 101 or COMPSCI 141 or CSE 141)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Internet Applications Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concepts in Internet applications engineering with emphasis on the Web. Peer-to-Peer and Interoperability. Topics include HTTP and REST, Remote Procedure/Method Calls, Web Services, data representations, content distribution networks, identity management, relevant W3C/IETF standards, and relevant new large-scale computing styles.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Game Development
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the principles of interactive 2D and 3D computer game development. Concepts in computer graphics, algorithms, software engineering, art and graphics, music and sound, story analysis, and artificial intelligence are presented and are the basis for student work.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 112 or COMPSCI 171 or IN4MATX 121 or ART 106B or I&C SCI 163 or I&C SCI 166

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Computer Interaction
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of human-computer interaction (HCI). Introduces students to user interface design techniques, design guidelines, and usability testing. Students gain the ability to design and evaluate user interfaces and become familiar with some of the outstanding research problems in HCI.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 10 or I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI 32A or CSE 41 or ENGR 10 or ENGRMAE 10 or EECS 10. I&C SCI 10 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 31 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 32A with a grade of C or better. CSE 41 with a grade of C or better. ENGR 10 with a grade of C or better. ENGRMAE 10 with a grade of C or better. EECS 10 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Human-Computer Interaction Requirements and Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students undertake significant projects in the elicitation and specification of HCI requirements and the thorough evaluation of user interfaces.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Interaction Software
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to human-computer interaction programming. Emphasis on current tools, standards, methodologies for implementing effective interaction designs. Widget toolkits, Web interface programming, geo-spatial and map interfaces, mobile phone interfaces.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 45J or I&C SCI 45C. I&C SCI 45J with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 45C with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in User Interaction Software
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students complete an end-to-end user interface programming project based on an iterative design paradigm. Topics may include requirements brainstorming, paper prototyping, iterative development, cognitive walk-through, quantitative evaluation, and acceptance testing. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Retrieval
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to information retrieval including indexing, retrieval, classifying, and clustering text and multimedia documents.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( I&C SCI 45C OR I&C SCI 45J ) AND ( STATS 7 OR STATS 67 OR AP STATISTICS )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Visualization
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to interactive visual interfaces for large datasets, and to principles of human visual perception and human computer interaction that inform their design. Various applications for data analysis and monitoring are discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (IN4MATX 131 or IN4MATX 43) and (I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI 32A or CSE 41). IN4MATX 131 with a grade of C or better. IN4MATX 43 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 31 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 32A with a grade of C or better. CSE 41 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Ubiquitous Computing
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to ubiquitous computing research methods, tools, and techniques. Prototyping, design, and evaluation of physical computing applications, smart environments, embedded systems, and future computing scenarios. Includes hands-on in-class laboratory exercises. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 10 or I&C SCI 31 or CSE 41 or I&C SCI 32A. I&C SCI 10 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 31 with a grade of C or better. CSE 41 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 32A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces theoretical and practical aspects of project management. Topics include organizational theory, group behavior, project management skills, case studies, personal and group productivity tools, management of distributed work, stakeholders, consultants, and knowledge management. Students do a project exercise.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Supported Cooperative Work
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces concepts and principles of collaborative systems. Topics may include shared workspaces, group interaction, workflow, architectures, interaction between social and technical features of group work, and examples of collaborative systems used in real-world settings. Students develop a simple collaborative application.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (IN4MATX 161 or IN4MATX 43) and (I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI 32A or CSE 41). I&C SCI 31 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 32A with a grade of C or better. CSE 41 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Social Analysis of Computing
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction of computing as a social process. Examines the social opportunities and problems raised by new information technologies, and the consequences of different ways of organizing. Topics include computing and work life, privacy, virtual communities, productivity paradox, systems risks.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 10 or I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI 32A or CSE 41 or ENGR 10 or EECS 10 or ENGRMAE 10. I&C SCI 10 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 31 with a grade of C or better. I&C SCI 32A with a grade of C or better. CSE 41 with a grade of C or better. ENGR 10 with a grade of C or better. EECS 10 with a grade of C or better. ENGRMAE 10 with a grade of C or better. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Organizational Information Systems
allCourses.description: Introduction to role of information systems in organizations, components and structure of organizational information systems, and techniques used in information systems analysis, design, and implementation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 161. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in the Social and Organizational Impacts of Computing
allCourses.description: Students undertake projects intended to gather and analyze data from situations in which computers are used, organize and conduct experiments intended to test hypotheses about impacts, and explore the application of concepts learned in previous courses.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Children's Learning and Media
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only. Informatics Majors only. Informatics Minors only.
allCourses.description: Examines how popular media may impact how young people learn, develop, and communicate by looking at research related to the impacts of a wide range of popular media including television, video games, digital environments, mobile devices, and other multimedia.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.description: Broad overview of medical informatics for students with varied backgrounds. Electronic medical records, online resources, mobile technologies, patient safety, and computational design. Legal, ethical, and public policy issues. Health systems management. Evaluation and fieldwork for health systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( HUMAN 1C OR HUMAN H1C OR WRITING 30 OR WRITING 31 OR WRITING 60 OR WRITING 39C ) AND UPPER DIVISION STANDING ONLY

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Health Informatics
allCourses.description: Students undertake significant quarter-long projects related to health informatics. Topics may include field evaluations of health care technologies, prototypes, iterative design, and system implementations.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Consumer Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Health Informatics Minors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Consumer health informatics is a subfield of health informatics aimed to empower healthcare consumers through a variety of consumer-facing technologies. Covers health behavior change, health literacy, social support, and the design, evaluation, and implementation of major technological applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 171. IN4MATX 171 with a grade of C or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Health Data Analytics
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The increasing availability of electronic heath data provides an unprecedented opportunity to use data-driven approaches to improve human health. Equips students with essential skills in curating, managing, and analyzing health data, focusing on electronic health records.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 171. IN4MATX 171 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Informatics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of informatics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Senior Design Project
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Software Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Informatics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Group supervised project in which students analyze, specify, design, construct, evaluate, and adapt a significant information processing system. Topics include team management, professional ethics, and systems analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 113 and IN4MATX 121 and IN4MATX 131 and IN4MATX 151

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Senior Design Project
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Group supervised project in which students analyze, specify, design, construct, evaluate, and adapt a significant information processing system. Topics include team management, professional ethics, and systems analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 191A. In Progress (IP) grade for IN4MATX 191A is also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Methodology for Informatics
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategies and idioms of research in Informatics. Includes examination of issues in scientific inquiry, qualitative and quantitative methods, and research design. Both classic texts and contemporary research literature are read and analyzed.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Information Systems
allCourses.description: Introduction to qualitative research methods used to study computerization and information systems, such as open-ended interviewing, participant observation, and ethnography. Studies of the methods in practice through examination of research literature.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Quantitative Research Methods in Information Systems
allCourses.description: Quantitative research methods used to study computerization and information systems. Design of instruments, sampling, sample sizes, and data analysis. Validity and reliability. Longitudinal versus cross-sectional designs. Analysis of secondary data. Studies of the methods through examination of research literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 251 or IN4MATX 261. Basic knowledge of elementary statistics is also required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Doctoral Seminar on Research and Writing
allCourses.description: Doctoral seminar centered on original research and writing. Provides a chance for doctoral students at all levels to present original work, brainstorm ongoing issues, and learn to provide and receive critical feedback from peers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Informatics
allCourses.description: Current research and research trends in informatics. Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Interface Design and Evaluation
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design and evaluation of user interfaces, with an emphasis on methodology. Cognitive principles, design life cycle, on-line and off-line prototyping techniques. Toolkits and architectures for interactive systems. Evaluation techniques, including heuristic and laboratory methods.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research in Human-Centered Computing
allCourses.description: Introduction to contemporary topics in human-computer interaction, including methods, technologies, design, and evaluation. Emerging application domains and their challenges to traditional research methods. Advanced architectures and technologies. Critical issues.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Ubiquitous Computing
allCourses.description: The "disappearing computer" paradigm. Differences to the desktop computing model: applications, interaction in augmented environments, security, alternate media, small operating systems, sensors, and embedded systems design. Evaluation by project work and class participation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Ubiquitous Computing and Interaction
allCourses.description: Principles and design techniques for ubiquitous computing applications. Conceptual basis for tangible and embodied interaction. Interaction in virtual and augmented environments. Design methods and techniques. Design case studies. Examination by project work.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Embedded and Ubiquitous Systems
allCourses.description: Embedded and ubiquitous system technologies including processors, DSP, memory, and software. System interfacing basics; communication strategies; sensors and actuators, mobile and wireless technology. Using pre-designed hardware and software components. Design case studies in wireless, multimedia, and/or networking domains.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 and COMPSCI 152 and COMPSCI 161 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G or I&C SCI 6D). B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer-Supported Cooperative Work
allCourses.description: The role of information systems in supporting work in groups and organizations. Examines various technologies designed to support communication, information sharing, and coordination. Focuses on behavioral and social aspects of designing and using group support technologies.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Social Analysis of Computing
allCourses.description: The social and economic impacts of computing and information technologies on groups, organizations, and society. Topics include computerization and changes in the character of work, social control and privacy, electronic communities, and risks of safety-critical systems to people.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computerization, Work, and Organizations
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the influence of computerization and information systems in transforming work and organizations. Theories of organization and organizational change. Processes by which diverse information technologies influence changes in work and organizations over short and long time periods.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Theories of Information Society
allCourses.description: Social and economic conceptions of information technology. Macrosocial and economic conditions that foster changes in information technologies. Social construction of information and computer technology in professional worlds. Theories of information technology and large-scale social change.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Digital Media and Society
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the technological and social aspects of online interactions, and policy including online games, social media, electronic activism, e-commerce, and digital libraries. Media-theoretic approaches to digital technology. Architectures, infrastructure considerations, and their consequences.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Technology in Global Sustainability
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the relationship between recent developments in information technology and the global transition to sustainability. Topics include the role of IT systems in the provision of human needs and wants (e.g., smart grids, food systems, and other IT-enabled infrastructure).

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to human-computer interaction and user-centered design. The material is focused on laying the groundwork for understanding the history, importance, and methods of human-computer interaction and design.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Needs Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Understanding the user's context, needs, and preferences. Topics include interviews and observations, modeling the context, flow, culture, space, and artifacts involved in an endeavor, ways of aggregating what is found, and presenting these findings to others.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Design and Prototyping
allCourses.description: Introduction to user-centered design and prototyping. Focused on practical methods for interaction design. Topics include the nature of design and the challenges to creating and evaluating good designs, as well specific skills for designing interactive systems.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Experience Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Evaluating prototypes and completed systems. Topics include comparative analysis, laboratory experiments, heuristic evaluation, cognitive walkthroughs, surveys, clickstreams, and help-desk.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Design and Prototyping
allCourses.restriction: Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develop and communicate interactive technology design prototypes. Moving concepts from brainstorming and paper prototypes to wireframe and limited functionality mock-ups.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Interactive Technology Studio
allCourses.restriction: Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Technologies, languages, and skills required for creating prototypes to communicate interactive technology concepts. Topics include HTTP, CSS, CSS scripting, AJAX, Design Patterns, Javascript, Javascript libraries such as jQuery, SQL, MVC, and cloud architectures.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Innovations in HCI and Design
allCourses.description: Recent social and technological developments in human-computer interaction and design. Topics will vary as the field progresses but include novel input techniques, novel platforms, and innovations in theory and methods of design.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Project in HCI and Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Human Comp Interact and Design Majors only.
allCourses.description: Group project that reinforces all concepts learned in this program, including knowing where user experience work is most appropriate and essential, and executing the appropriate steps.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Project and Portfolio
allCourses.description: Completion of capstone projects and development of portfolios. Ideation, critique, development, and critique.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Applying Human-Computer Interaction and Design in Industry
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students only. Graduate students only. Human Comp Interact and Design Majors only.
allCourses.description: Selected topics related to understanding and applying human-computer interaction and design concepts and practices within the User Experience industry. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times as topics vary.

allCourses.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Literature Survey in Software Engineering
allCourses.description: Reading and analysis of relevant literature in Software Engineering under the direction of a faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of informatics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.
