allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concepts, methods, and current practice of software engineering. Large-scale software production, software life cycle models, principles and techniques for each stage of development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( CSE 42 OR I&C SCI 32 OR I&C SCI 32A ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Informatics
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed for informatics instructors to pilot new teaching materials and prototype new class. The format of the class is flexible based on the content to be offered in the future.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Research
allCourses.restriction: Bren School of ICS Honors students only. Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Directed independent research in Informatics for honors students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics, Technology, and Design
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a critical framework for how and why biases of many kinds are built into everyday digital tools. Reflections on ethics, technology, and design through case studies drawn from machine learning, CS education, engineering, social media, and criminal justice.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Leadership for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Assists experienced and inexperienced entrepreneurs with some of the challenges of managing others, and helps them build their understanding and skills so they can become more successful managers of people.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Accounting for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides the building blocks of financial accounting that are essential to entrepreneurs. Covers financial ratios and statements, including forecasting financial statements, basic transaction analysis, and generally accepted accounting principles.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develops familiarity with fundamental concepts, theories, and techniques in marketing, and acquaints students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers including customer targeting, product, pricing, placement, promotion, and research.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managerial Finance for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides the building blocks of finance knowledge that are essential to entrepreneurs.  Covers investment and financing decisions, including the time value of money, cash flow creation, cost of capital, and capital budgeting.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: MIE Pre-Accelerator
allCourses.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Prepares students for the New Venture Competition in spring quarter. Students form teams to create a startup, submit concept paper, pitch ideas, and attend workshops throughout the academic year.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Growth Strategies for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on management of growth opportunities in industries where applied innovation, usually in the form of technology, people, or processes, creates distinct competitive advantages.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teams develop a business plan to launch a new venture. Drafts of sections of the plan are due throughout the course.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Lean Startup
allCourses.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Exposes students to an entrepreneurial experience with the same pressures and demands of an early-stage startup to provide a real-world, hands-on learning experience in starting a company.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Venture Capital for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of venture capital and private equity, which constitute the alternative asset class (as opposed to conventional investments). Many start-up and entrepreneurial firms require substantial capital, and venture capital and private equity organizations finance these high-risk but potentially high-reward companies.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: New Product Development for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to introduce the new product development process and techniques to identify markets, develop new product ideas, measure consumer preferences, position and design new products, and test them prior to launch. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing on the Internet for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines impact of the internet on traditional methods of marketing. Discusses how to capitalize on and increase the internet's utility as a tool that can increase marketing effectiveness, efficiency, and competitiveness. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Innovation Internship
allCourses.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Students apply innovative and creative knowledge obtained from classroom theory through work experiences. Provides knowledge of career opportunities, an understanding of the role innovation plays in business environments, and preparation to become an entrepreneur.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Innovation and Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of innovation and entrepreneurship. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Law for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on educating individuals starting, or investing in, a new business in the U.S. Provides an overview to common legal issues faced by entrepreneurs, such as business formation and structure, governance and employment contracts, and intellectual property and taxation.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Edge: Innovation in the New Digital Age
allCourses.restriction: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the strategic and operational issues that business leaders face in adapting to the new business environment, what we call innovating, managing, and competing at the edge.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Merage Consulting Projects for Entrepreneurs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students the opportunity to put into practice concepts, skills, and tools acquired in other parts of the MBA program. Seminars augment internship experiences with analyses of relevant administrative issues.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Global Studies
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Ongoing historical processes that increase global integration, the social, economic, and political interdependence of different regions, cultures, and peoples. Topics include ancient empires, colonialism, nationalism, industrialization, modern imperialism and warfare, decolonization, global social movements, conflict, inequality, and global governance.

allCourses.title: Global Trials
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores landmark legal trials that have impacted both domestic and world affairs.The trials provide a lens through which to explore society at the time, as well as shed light on the historical legacies of current social, political, and legal values.

allCourses.title: Global Social Movements
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The evolution of global social movements over past 250 years. Age of Revolutions in America, France, and Haiti; nationalism and labor; 1960s global decolonization; 21st century Latin American indigenous movements; Occupy Wall Street, Arab Spring, and social media's #metoo, #BlackLivesMatter.

allCourses.title: Global Cities and Slums
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Cities as a window into contemporary challenges of the globalized world. Global cities such as Los Angeles, London, and Beijing compared with cities with slums in the global south such as Rio de Janeiro, Johannesburg, and Mumbai.

allCourses.title: Global Refugees and Stateless People
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the reason behind global refugee crises, and what it means to be a displaced migrant or stateless person in history and in contemporary society. Links case studies about refugees around the world.

allCourses.title: Global Asias and Orientalism
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines how the modern world is divided between East and West in the age of globalization. Through the postcolonial framework of Orientalism, it considers a pluralistic idea of Asia and the current notion of the new world order as one.

allCourses.title: Case Studies in Global and Planetary Health
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores critical global health and planetary health studies, linking past trends to current research of health inequalities. Case studies include maternal-fetal mortality, environmental contamination, disaster preparedness, pharmaceutical development and access, and humanitarian aid interventions.

allCourses.title: Global Trafficking
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores trafficking in different global contexts. Covers sex trafficking, labor trafficking, and organ trafficking. Tracks the use of the concept in policy, human rights, law, humanitarianism, and media. Provides a complex and nuanced understanding of the problem and its solutions.

allCourses.title: Global Gender and Sexuality
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Develops critical insights into gender and sexuality as products of the world around us and as lived experiences across the globe. Topics include agency and resistance, intersectionality, feminisms, colonialism, heteronormativity, gender violence, masculinities, media and popular culture, globalization and migration.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Global Political Ecology
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to political ecology and critical analysis of the global scale and globalization. Topics include current and historical climate change, fossil fuels, international trade and investment, soil erosion and pollution, deforestation, waste, ocean ecology, water crisis, wars, revolutions, and refugees.

allCourses.title: Global Food Environment
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the global political ecology of food, focusing on the U.S., China, and Brazil. Topics include the history of agriculture, imperialism/neocolonialism, Malthusianism, migration, agro-industrialization, deforestation, GMOs, agrochemicals, soil and water contamination, land struggles, food security/safety/sovereignty, dietary habits, and climate change.

allCourses.title: Global Cultures and Society
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Offers a general overview of the rise of global interdependence in political, economic, demographic, and cultural terms. Considers what drove people from relative isolation into intensified intercourse with one another, and investigates the consequences of this shift.

allCourses.title: World of Coffee
allCourses.description: History of consumption and production of coffee over the centuries, and coffee's cultural, economic, social, political consequences. Coffee's social life as a drug, symbol of hospitality, religious rite, sociability and bourgeois lifestyle, commodity, source of livelihoods, imperial revenues, corporate profits.

allCourses.title: International Business
allCourses.description: Introduction to conducting business in the international arena, decision making in the organization, and globalization of markets and production.  Topics covered range from tax and finance to ethics, marketing, and more.  Continuing corporate regulatory scandals discussed.

allCourses.title: Global Poverty and Inequality in the 21st Century
allCourses.description: Explores a multidisciplinary understanding of poverty and inequality in the 21st century and assesses impact of education, health, technology, and other interventions. Course offered online only.

allCourses.title: Global Political Ideologies
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.

allCourses.title: Nuclear Environments
allCourses.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Comparative Study of Legal Cultures
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Traces the anthropological and comparative cultural study of law from the nineteenth century to the present; briefly surveys the diversity of recorded legal cultures and critically examines key concepts which have been used to describe and classify them.

allCourses.title: Global Economy
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Acquaints students with the fundamental patterns of the global economy. Emphasizes the historical roots and political implications of economic choices.

allCourses.title: Transnational Gangs
allCourses.description: Examines the internationalization of U.S. domestic street gangs.  The relationship between California gangs Mara Salvatrucha and 18th Street and Mexico/Central American gangs is assessed.  Specified topics include:  mobilization, migration, territorialism, culture, organization, and use of technology.

allCourses.title: Introduction to International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of political relations between and among nations with emphasis on explanations of conflict and cooperation. The role of ideologies and their relation to international problems are also examined.

allCourses.title: Homeland Security
allCourses.description: Examines the 9/11 origins of the concept of homeland security; assess the evolution, structure, and operations of the Department of Homeland Security; critically examines the evolution of threat assessment to the U.S. and the utilization of risk management methodologies.

allCourses.title: Vietnam War
allCourses.description: Examines social structures and social changes in Vietnamese and U.S. societies through the study of the Vietnam War.

allCourses.title: International Law
allCourses.description: Examination of the origin, changing structure, application of international law, and the role of legal norms in regulating the behavior of states and maintaining international order.

allCourses.title: Global Indigeneity
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Situates the interdisciplinary fields of Native American and Indigenous Studies within a transnational context, focusing on the global dimensions of Indigeneity informing local histories, politics, and experiences. Examines settler colonialism, sovereignty, and the enduring legacies of colonialism as global phenomena.

allCourses.title: International Humanitarianism
allCourses.description: Examines, analyzes, and evaluates the humanitarian phenomenon, the actors involved in it (including states, international organizations (IOs), and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)), the rise of a body of international humanitarian law, and the problems and debates associated with international humanitarianism today.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Global Futures
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Develops critical insights into our collective future as it reflects different perspectives of the world. Topics include techno-orientalism, afro-futurism, feminist futures, indigenous cosmology, and environmental concerns.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Global Political Economy
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The global economy as an integrated system. The rise of world trade, capitalism, national economies, market cycles, competing economic ideologies, development, globalization, transnational labor, multinational corporations, and the role of UN, World Bank, WTO, and the IMF in global governance.

allCourses.title: Racism and Global Apartheid
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The concept of race has been used to draw a global color line dividing rich from poor, developed from developing, first from third worlds. Racism is used to justify slavery, colonialism, imperialism, eugenics, genocide, and extreme inequalities produced by globalization.

allCourses.title: Religion and World Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between religion and world politics historically and today, focusing on connections with peace/war, democracy, human rights, secularism(s), and globalization. Covers major debates, scholarship, concepts, and theories through class exercises, exams, and essays.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"OR":["INTL ST 11","INTL ST 12","REL STD 5A","REL STD 5B","REL STD 5C","POL SCI 41A"]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 41A or INTL ST 11 or INTL ST 12 or REL STD 5A or REL STD 5B or REL STD 5C

allCourses.title: Non-Government Organization (NGO) Fundamentals
allCourses.description: Introduction to non-governmental organizations, including their role in U.S. society and the international community. Explores varying definitions of NGOs and the characteristics held in common by all NGOs.

allCourses.title: Militarism and Gender
allCourses.description: Examination of feminist approaches to militarism, war, and political violence; drawing on representations of women as both victims of and participants in military violence; effects of militarism on formations of gender; effects of military industrial complex on nationalism and identity.

allCourses.title: Ethics and Justice in International Affairs
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analyzes choices regarding the use of force, resolving conflict, and promoting human rights and social justice. Special attention is given to the American experience as a principal case study of ethics and statecraft.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Racial Capitalism
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the historical relationship between racism and capitalism. Social movements such as Black Lives Matter highlight the contemporary political economy of racial capitalism, and the relationship between domestic policing and international militarization as twin sides of global racial hegemony.

allCourses.title: Comparing European and US Societies
allCourses.description: Society, culture, institutions of U.S. and European countries. Fertility to football, guns to government, work to welfare, health to housework. Cross-national approaches for understanding the world and thinking critically about taken-for-granted practices. Policies the U.S. might borrow for social issues.

allCourses.title: Peoples of the Pacific
allCourses.description: The cultural history and recent developments among the Pacific peoples of Polynesia, Micronesia, Melanesia, New Guinea, and Australia.

allCourses.title: China in the Global Age
allCourses.description: Chinese society from 1949 to present. Social change in the context of political control and ideological considerations. Focus on the power structure, political decision processes, and ideological legitimation, and interplay with the Chinese community and its culture.

allCourses.title: Human Rights and Global Governance
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.

allCourses.title: Political Islam
allCourses.description: Political Islamd is a diverse phenomenon. While noticeable barriers exist to "Islamist democracy," it is the Islamists who will define the political future of much of the Muslim world. Reviews the experience of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, and Indonesia.

allCourses.title: Peoples and Cultures of Post-Soviet Eurasia
allCourses.description: Examines the cultures and political conflicts of the more than 130 indigenous ethnic groups in the European and Asian territories of the former U.S.S.R. Emphasis is on the theoretical issues of ethnicity, nationalism, and conflict management.

allCourses.title: Global Inequalities
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An examination of various forms of social, economic, and political inequality within and between nations. Different approaches to understanding inequality and the intersections of poverty, race, ethnicity, class, gender, nationality, health, and violence.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
allCourses.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

allCourses.title: Global Environmental Issues
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines problems such as global climate change, growing human populations, fisheries depletion, ocean acidification, biodiversity loss, deforestation, and food security. Introduces political, social, and economic factors contributing to environmental issues and their disproportional impacts on the world’s poor and minorities.

allCourses.title: U.S. War on Terrorism
allCourses.description: Analyzes the United States war on terrorism by focusing on terrorism, the U.S. wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and changes in police powers through the Patriot Act, as well as the political leadership which directs the war.

allCourses.title: Political Power in Contemporary China
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analyzes the sources of political power in contemporary China, including historical legitimacy, political institutions, and Chinese Communist Party power. Identifies challenges to the CCP’s rule and rising socio-political issues such as mass protest, censorship, and the environment.

allCourses.title: Revolution in Latin America
allCourses.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada.  Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

allCourses.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

allCourses.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
allCourses.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

allCourses.title: Revolution and Reaction in Cold War Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores Latin American experiences of revolutionary change and military dictatorship during the Cold War (1945-1990). Pays particular attention to the lives of women, peasants, workers, and the urban middle classes. Case studies include Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, Argentina, Nicaragua, and Mexico.

allCourses.title: Ancient Civilization of Mexico and the Southwest
allCourses.description: The prehistory and cultural evolution of the civilization which originated in Mexico, including the Olmecs, Aztecs, Toltecs, Maya, and Zapotec, as well as the Pueblos of the Southwestern U.S. Topics include the origins of food production and of the state.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Geographic Focus in International Studies
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of international studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Global and International Studies Forum
allCourses.description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Mediation
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Humanities students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Student develop mediation skills and refine knowledge in the practice and theory of conflict resolution. Students who complete this course may serve as mediators in the Campus Mediation Program. Course is a prerequisite to completing Indep Study as an intern.

allCourses.title: Seminar Conflict Resolution
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed for seniors who are pursuing the International Studies major and/or minor. Provides a forum in which students will refine skills and theory in the study of cooperation and conflict, from local to global arenas. Students write research paper.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
allCourses.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Global Focus in International Studies
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of international studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Students participate in planned research and study under written contract with a supervising UCI instructor. Students may enroll for only one individual study course each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: What is Global Studies?
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces graduates to the field of global and international studies. Landmark studies outline the transition from globalization studies to contemporary global studies. Identify complex global issues, underlying processes of globalization, and the impacts they have on people around the world.

allCourses.title: Foundations of European Social Thought
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides graduate students with a broad overview of the major landmarks in the development of modern social thought. Introduces key philosophers and theorists Adam Smith, Marx, Durkheim, Weber, Freud, and Du Bois, focusing on the global dimensions of their work.

allCourses.title: Globalizing Social Theory in the Age of Extremes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines important developments in social theory between 1914 and 1991. The overarching goal is to synthesize from these various approaches a critical and transdisciplinary theoretical framework to analyze complex global issues.

allCourses.title: Theories of Globalization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theories of globalization engage deep historical transformations, keeping the interrelated dynamics of economics, politics, and culture in focus. Theories examine transformations emanating at transnational and state levels, and from below in the form of social movements led by everyday people.

allCourses.title: Theories from the Global South
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Looking beyond the theoretical traditions of the Euro-American academy scholars can begin to engage important theoretical contributions from the Global South. Explores alternative standpoints and interventions challenging dominant narratives and calling into question taken-for-granted assumptions, categories, concepts, values, and perspectives.

allCourses.title: Engaging Global Issues
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critical and interdisciplinary works on global issues serve as examples that graduates can use in their own research. Each week focuses on a different example of outstanding global research done by a scholar having an important impact on the field.

allCourses.title: Research Design and Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of empirical research design, strategies for global research, sampling logics, reliability, validity, mixed methods, integrating qualitative and quantitative methods. Introduction to basic data collection methods and examples of more advanced methodological strategies. Research ethics and the IRB review process.

allCourses.title: Grant Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on production, critique, and revision of student research proposals. A practical seminar designed to improve student proposals, help students through the application processes, and increase students' chances of obtaining support for their research.

allCourses.title: Proseminar in Global Studies I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Year-long intensive introduction to graduate students to a range of topics pertinent to the field of Global Studies. The guest speakers and topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times.

allCourses.title: Proseminar in Global Studies II

allCourses.title: Global Perspectives on Gender and Sexuality
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Selected readings introduce students to topics such as queer globalization, global sexual economy, Indigenous feminism, gender regimes, heteronationalism, the straight state, heteropatriarchy, feminist science and environmentalism, and global masculinities.

allCourses.title: Global Indigeneity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines issues impacting Indigenous peoples in local, national, and global contexts, including the cultural, political, and legal status of Indigeneity and geopolitical struggles over Indigenous territories, challenges such as climate change to Indigenous lifeways, and contemporary struggles for survivance.

allCourses.title: Directed Reading and Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Readings focused on specialized topics in consultation with, and with the consent of, a faculty member. Students are expected to produce a paper based on the readings.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times.

allCourses.description: Assists students to prepare a thesis prospectus for the Honors Program in International Studies. Students choose a topic, learn writing and research methods, write a prospectus and orally present and defend it, and conduct a literature review.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of Persia in antiquity.

allCourses.title: Medieval Persia
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey of Persian history in the context of Late Antique and Medieval Islamic history.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan. Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.description: Studies in grammars and texts of Old Persian and Avestan.

allCourses.description: Required of and limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: The Nature of Scientific Inquiry
allCourses.description: Investigates the nature, scope, and status of scientific knowledge and the methods used to acquire it. Uses concrete historical examples from a variety of scientific fields to identify distinctive features of the scientific enterprise and explore their significance.

allCourses.title: The Making of Modern Science
allCourses.description: Surveys the history of science and mathematics since the Scientific Revolution, examining central developments both chronologically and thematically, as well as investigating their significance for contemporary philosophical debates about the role and status of current scientific theories.

allCourses.title: The Philosophy of Sex
allCourses.description: Discusses the origins of biological sex, dynamics of sexual selection, sex differences in humans, and the construction of gender in human societies. Seeks to understand the role social values play in the creation of science.

allCourses.title: What is Disease?
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Explores philosophical issues associated with scientific efforts to understand and explain disease.

allCourses.title: What Is Time?
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Engages the question "what is time?" by drawing on physics, philosophy, fiction, film, and psychology. Organized around understanding and addressing the tension between time as represented in physics and our immediate temporal experience.

allCourses.title: Honors Philosophy of Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: An examination of the standard von Neumann-Dirac formulation of quantum mechanics. The quantum measurement problem is discussed along with several proposed solutions, including GRW, many-worlds, man-minds, and Bohm's theory.

allCourses.title: Scientific Realism and Instrumentalism
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Explores competing views of the character and status of theoretical knowledge in science, including challenges to and defenses of the view that contemporary scientific theories offer straightforward and accurate descriptions of how things stand in otherwise inaccessible domains of nature.

allCourses.title: What is Space?
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Historical, philosophical, scientific exploration of the concept of "space." Questions of interest include: What kind of a thing is space? How can we know what space is like? How is space different from time.

allCourses.title: The Philosophy and Biology of Sex
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the origins of biological sex, dynamics of sexual selection, the evolution and cultural creation of sexual behavior in humans, and the construction of gender in human societies.

allCourses.title: Jurisprudence and Constitutional Law
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Applies competing theories of the nature of law and legal reasoning to evaluate decisions of the U.S. Supreme Court in controversial areas of constitutional law such as free speech, privacy, sexual conduct, affirmative action, and political campaign contributions.

allCourses.title: Languages of the World
allCourses.description: The world has over 6,000 languages, with an exuberant variety of sounds, words, grammars. Introduction to a representative (about eight), drawn from every continent. Students not expected to learn these languages, but to explore and study their structure and complexity.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Phonology

allCourses.description: Formal aspects of describing and recognizing languages by grammars and automata.  Parsing regular and context-free languages. Ambiguity, nondeterminism. Elements of computability; Turning machines, random access machines, undecidable problems, NP-completeness.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ICS 46 or CSE 46) and MATH 2B and ICS 6B and ICS 6D. ICS 46 with a grade of C or better. CSE 46 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.description: Cellular and molecular basis of immune response and roles of the immune system in both maintaining health and contributing to disease.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. The main goal is to achieve a basic understanding of the cellular and molecular basis of innate and adaptive immunity, and how immune function is coordinated at a systems level.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology.  Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 215. PHYSIO 215 with a grade of B+ or better

allCourses.title: Pathogenic Microbiology
allCourses.description: Biochemical and genetic properties of infectious agents; identification and behavior of pathogens; activities of toxins; the chemotherapy, biochemistry, and genetics of drug resistance; and epidemiology of infectious diseases.

allCourses.title: Medical Virology
allCourses.description: Animal viruses as disease causing agents, including mechanisms of infection at both the cellular and organismic levels. Topics include comparative studies of different groups of viruses, viral transformation, and mechanisms of viral gene expression.

allCourses.title: Immunopathogenic Mechanisms of Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examination of the mechanisms underlying disease states mediated by immune dysregulation. Topics include mechanisms of immune evasion by cancer, diseases mediated by cytokine dysregulation, role of the microbiome of the GI tract and other disease sites, and adoptive T-cell therapy.

allCourses.title: Molecular Pathogenesis of Microbial Infections
allCourses.description: Features lectures by faculty on the molecular aspects of microbial pathogenesis, highlighting both microbe and cellular functions. In addition to lectures, students review papers and discuss them. There will be two written exams, one on viruses and one on microbes.

allCourses.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Disease
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the molecular mechanisms of human diseases, including neurologic, hematologic, neoplastic, and infectious diseases. Students gain an understanding of these mechanisms, as well as models of human diseases.

allCourses.title: Immunology Journal Club
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Stem Cells
allCourses.description: One-hour seminar presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer and open to the science community, followed by one-hour discussion of the lecture topic or related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.

allCourses.title: M.D./PH.D. Tutorial
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores a variety of topics that impact careers of medical scientists (M.D./Ph.D students). Topics range from scientific, such as recent advances in particular research areas, to ethical problems brought on by increased technology and intervention in the disease process.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Responsible Conduct of Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Each session includes a formal presentation by faculty/invited speaker followed by a discussion of case studies related to the topic under consideration.

allCourses.title: Career Development
allCourses.description: Topics include preparation of papers, grants and fellowships, scientific presentations, and curriculum vitae, and career opportunities.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Tutorial in Microbiology and Molecular Genetics
allCourses.description: Tutorial in Microbiology and Molecular Genetics. Presented by the department chair; relates current laboratory research to the literature.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Provided for MSTP students to synthesize the basic science information learned during the basic science years of medical school and learn how to apply that knowledge toward graduate research directed at understanding the basis of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Dissertation—Microbiology and Molecular Genetics
allCourses.description: Course provided for Ph.D. students to prepare and complete the dissertation required for a Ph.D. degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming for Data Science
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to Python for data science. Selecting appropriate data types; functions and methods; plotting; the libraries NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn. Foundations of machine learning.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 2D or MATH H2D) and (MATH 3A or MATH H3A) and MATH 9

allCourses.title: Numerical Analysis I
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of numerical computation with an emphasis on solving equations. Solving transcendental equations; linear systems, Gaussian elimination, QR factorization, iterative methods, eigenvalue computation, power method.

allCourses.title: Numerical Analysis II
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of numerical computation with an emphasis on topics from calculus and approximation theory. Lagrange interpolation; Gaussian quadrature; Fourier series and transforms; Methods from data science including least squares and L1 regression.

allCourses.title: Numerical Analysis Laboratory
allCourses.description: Provides practical experience to complement the theory developed in Mathematics 105A.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 105A AND ( NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER )

allCourses.title: Numerical Analysis Laboratory
allCourses.description: Provides practical experience to complement the theory developed in Mathematics 105B.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 105B AND ( NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER )

allCourses.title: Numerical Differential Equations
allCourses.description: Theory and applications of numerical methods to initial and boundary-value problems for ordinary and partial differential equations.

allCourses.title: Numerical Differential Equations Laboratory
allCourses.description: Provides practical experience to complement the theory developed in Mathematics 107.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 107 AND ( NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER )

allCourses.title: Optimization I
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to optimization, linear search method, trust region method, Newton method, linear programming, linear, and non-linear least square methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 2D or MATH H2D) and MATH 10 and MATH 121B

allCourses.title: Optimization II
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The simplex method, interior point method, penalty barrier method, primal dual method, augmented Lagrangian method, and stochastic gradient method.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 110A. MATH 110A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Applications I
allCourses.description: Introduction to ordinary and partial differential equations and their applications in engineering and science. Basic methods for classical PDEs (potential, heat, and wave equations). Classification of PDEs, separation of variables and series expansions, special functions, eigenvalue problems.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Applications II
allCourses.description: Introduction to partial differential equations and their applications in engineering and science. Basic methods for classical PDEs (potential, heat, and wave equations). Green functions and integral representations, method of characteristics.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Applications III
allCourses.description: Nonhomogeneous problems and Green's functions, Sturm-Liouville theory, general Fourier expansions, applications of partial differential equations in different areas of science.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Modeling in Biology I
allCourses.description: Discrete mathematical and statistical models; difference equations, population dynamics, Markov chains, and statistical models in biology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B or MATH 5B or MATH 7B or AP Calculus BC. AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4

allCourses.title: Mathematical Modeling in Biology II
allCourses.description: Linear algebra; differential equations models; dynamical systems; stability; hysteresis; phase plane analysis; applications to cell biology, viral dynamics, and infectious diseases.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B or MATH 5B or MATH 7B or AP Calculus BC. AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4

allCourses.title: Mathematical Modeling
allCourses.description: Mathematical modeling and analysis of phenomena that arise in engineering physical sciences, biology, economics, or social sciences.

allCourses.title: Dynamical Systems
allCourses.description: Introduction to the modern theory of dynamical systems including contraction mapping principle, fractals and chaos, conservative systems, Kepler problem, billiard models, expanding maps, Smale's horseshoe, topological entropy.

allCourses.title: The Theory of Differential Equations
allCourses.description: Existence and uniqueness of solutions, continuous dependence of solutions on initial conditions and parameters, Lyapunov and asymptotic stability, Floquet theory, nonlinear systems, and bifurcations.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra: Groups
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Axioms for group theory; permutation groups, matrix groups. Isomorphisms, homomorphisms, quotient groups. Advanced topics as time permits. Special emphasis on doing proofs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 3A or MATH H3A) and MATH 13. MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra: Rings and Fields
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic properties of rings; ideals, quotient rings; polynomial and matrix rings. Elements of field theory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 120A. MATH 120A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra: Galois Theory
allCourses.description: Galois Theory: proof of the impossibility of certain ruler-and-compass constructions (squaring the circle, trisecting angles); nonexistence of analogues to the "quadratic formula" for polynomial equations of degree 5 or higher.

allCourses.title: Linear Algebra I
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to modern abstract linear algebra. Special emphasis on students doing proofs. Vector spaces, linear independence, bases, dimension. Linear transformations and their matrix representations. Theory of determinants.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 3A or MATH H3A) and MATH 13. MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Linear Algebra II
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to modern abstract linear algebra. Special emphasis on students doing proofs. Canonical forms; inner products; similarity of matrices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 121A. MATH 121A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Abstract Mathematics
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to formal definition and rigorous proof writing in mathematics. Topics include basic logic, set theory, equivalence relations, and various proof techniques such as direct, induction, contradiction, contrapositive, and exhaustion.

allCourses.title: Probability I
allCourses.description: Combinatorial probability, conditional probabilities, independence, discrete and continuous random variables, expectation and variance, common probability distributions.

allCourses.title: Probability II
allCourses.description: Joint distributions, sums of independent random variables, conditional distributions and conditional expectation, covariances, moment generating functions, limit theorems.

allCourses.title: Stochastic Processes
allCourses.description: Markov chains, Brownian motion, Gaussian processes, applications to option pricing and Markov chain Monte Carlo methods.

allCourses.title: Fixed Income
allCourses.description: Overview of interest theory, time value of money, annuities/cash flows with payments that are not contingent, loans, sinking funds, bonds, general cash flow and portfolios, immunization, duration and convexity, swaps.

allCourses.title: Mathematics of Financial Derivatives
allCourses.description: General derivatives; call/put options; hedging and investment strategies: spreads and collars; risk management; forwards and futures; bonds.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 133C OR MATH 134A ) AND NO MATH 133A AND ( NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = F OR BETTER )

allCourses.title: Mathematical Models for Finance
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: General properties of options: option contracts (call and put options, European, American and exotic options); binomial option pricing model, Black-Scholes option pricing model; risk-neutral pricing formula using Monte-Carlo simulation; option greeks and risk management; interest rate derivatives, Markowitz portfolio theory.

allCourses.title: Elementary Analysis I
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to real analysis, including convergence of sequence, infinite series, differentiation and integration, and sequences of functions. Students are expected to do proofs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 2D or MATH H2D) and (MATH 3A or MATH H3A) and MATH 13. MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Elementary Analysis II
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to real analysis including convergence of sequences, infinite series, differentiation and integration, and sequences of functions. Students are expected to do proofs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 140A. MATH 140A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Analysis in Several Variables
allCourses.description: Rigorous treatment of multivariable differential calculus. Jacobians, Inverse and Implicit Function theorems.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Topology
allCourses.description: The elements of naive set theory and the basic properties of metric spaces. Introduction to topological properties.

allCourses.title: Complex Analysis
allCourses.description: Rigorous treatment of basic complex analysis: analytic functions, Cauchy integral theory and its consequences, power series, residue calculus, harmonic functions, conformal mapping. Students are expected to do proofs.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Logic
allCourses.description: First order logic through the Completeness Theorem for predicate logic.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 13 or (ICS 6B and ICS 6D). MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better. ICS 6B with a grade of C- or better. ICS 6D with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Modern Geometry
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Euclidean Geometry; Hilbert's Axioms; Absolute Geometry; Hyperbolic Geometry; the Poincare Models; and Geometric Transformations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 13 or (ICS 6B and ICS 6D). MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better. ICS 6B with a grade of C- or better. ICS 6D with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry I
allCourses.description: Applications of advanced calculus and linear algebra to the geometry of curves and surfaces in space.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry II
allCourses.description: Applications of advanced calculus and linear algebra to the geometry of curves and surfaces in space.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 162A. MATH 162A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cryptology I
allCourses.description: Introduction to some of the mathematics used in the making and breaking of codes, with applications to classical ciphers and public key systems. Includes topics from number theory, probability, and abstract algebra.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 2B or MATH 5B or MATH 7B or AP Calculus BC) and (MATH 3A or MATH H3A) and (MATH 13 or (ICS 6B and ICS 6D)). AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cryptology II
allCourses.description: Introduction to some of the mathematics used in the making and breaking of codes, with applications to classical ciphers and public key systems. The mathematics which is covered includes topics from number theory, probability, and abstract algebra.

allCourses.title: Combinatorics
allCourses.description: Introduction to combinatorics including basic counting principles, permutations, combinations, binomial coefficients, inclusion-exclusion, derangements, ordinary and exponential generating functions, recurrence relations, Catalan numbers, Stirling numbers, and partition numbers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 2B or MATH 5B or MATH 7B or AP Calculus BC) and MATH 13. AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4. MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Mathematics of Finance
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: After reviewing tools from probability, statistics, and elementary differential and partial differential equations, concepts such as hedging, arbitrage, Puts, Calls, the design of portfolios, the derivation and solution of the Blac-Scholes, and other equations are discussed.

allCourses.title: Number Theory I
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to number theory and applications. Divisibility, prime numbers, factorization. Arithmetic functions. Congruences. Quadratic residue. Diophantine equations. Introduction to cryptography.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 3A or MATH H3A) and MATH 13. MATH 13 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Number Theory II
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to number theory and applications. Analytic number theory, character sums, finite fields, discrete logarithm, computational complexity. Introduction to coding theory. Other topics as time permits.

allCourses.title: History of Mathematics
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Topics vary from year to year. Some possible topics: mathematics in ancient times; the development of modern analysis; the evolution of geometric ideas. Students will be assigned individual topics for term papers.

allCourses.title: History of Mathematics Lesson Lab
allCourses.description: Aspiring math teachers research, design, present, and peer review middle school or high school math lessons that draw from history of mathematics topics.

allCourses.title: Studies in the Learning and Teaching of Secondary Mathematics
allCourses.description: Focus is on historic and current mathematical concepts related to student learning and effective math pedagogy, with fieldwork in grades 6-14.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Problem Solving Seminar
allCourses.description: Develops ability in analytical thinking and problem solving, using problems of the type found in the Mathematics Olympiad and the Putnam Mathematical Competition. Students taking the course in fall will prepare for and take the Putnam examination in December.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Writing
allCourses.restriction: Mathematics Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Techniques of mathematical writing and communication. Covers effectively writing mathematical papers, creating effective presentations, and communicating mathematics in a variety of media. Focuses on utilizing LaTeX for typesetting mathematics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 120A or MATH 121A or MATH 140A. MATH 120A with a grade of C- or better. MATH 121A with a grade of C- or better. MATH 140A with a grade of C- or better. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Health, Wellness, and Conception of the Body
allCourses.description: Asks what is health and who gets to have it? What is considered a “healthy” or “sick” body? We analyze historical and contemporary experiences of illness, medicine, and caregiving, including how patients represent their bodies and healing.

allCourses.title: Surviving Epidemics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sophomores only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes diverse social and cultural responses to epidemics from mid-nineteenth century to the present, including incarceration, caregiving, and disability rights. Using interdisciplinary materials and collaborative activities, students interpret strategies and outcomes of Indigenous, racialized, and marginalized communities surviving great illness.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Capstone Seminar: The Clinical Moral Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the clinical encounter, and the importance of meaning making in these “moral laboratories.” Students enter the clinical space as participant observers, and reflect on how the clinical site informs and challenges reading practices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MED HUM 1 or MED HUM 3 or GEN&SEX 60A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Critical Perspectives in Medical Humanities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes social and cultural understandings of the body, health, illness, medicine, and disease. Themes include critical histories of the body; non-compliant subjects interacting with medicine; racial-sexual hierarchies of health; and theories and expressions of pain and suffering.

allCourses.title: Art and Medicine
allCourses.description: Analyzes the relationship between medicine and the visual arts from the late medieval to modern periods, covering topics such as anatomy, optical medical technologies, gender and race in medicine, and popular representations of disease and doctors.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Introduction to Business and Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Rigorous overview of major business functions and management topics. Addresses the global and fast-changing environment in which modern business enterprises operate as well as the challenges posed by concerns about sustainable growth, ethics, and social responsibility.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Management Science
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concepts and methods of management science, which applies mathematical modeling and analysis to management problems. Topics include linear and integer programming, project scheduling, inventory management, queuing analysis, decision analysis, and simulation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 7 OR MGMT 7 OR STATS 7 OR ECON 15A OR ECON 15B OR AP STATISTICS )

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managing Organizational Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic theory and concepts which provide the manager with tools for understanding behavior of people in organizations. Areas such as individual, group, and organizational determinants of attitudes, turnover, and job performance.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Introduction to Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic marketing concepts; discussion of the role marketing plays in modern society. Topics include industrial and consumer marketing, promotion, distribution, and pricing theory.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Introduction to Management Information Systems
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Information Technology (IT) continues to drive rapid productivity growth and structural changes in the economy. Topics include what IT is, and how companies can use IT to improve business processes, enhance customer services, and gain competitive advantage over rivals.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Introduction to Managerial Finance
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basics of financial administration. Capital budgeting, cost of capital, cash budgeting, working capital management, and long-term sources of funds. Provides a basic understanding of issues and techniques involved in financial decision making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( ECON 25 OR MGMT 30A ) AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC )

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Strategic Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses management of the entire business.  Role of the general manager in organizations, industry analysis, core competencies, growth through vertical integration, innovation, acquisition and diversification, globalization, strategy implementation, and the ethical and moral responsibility of a manager.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: China and the Global Order
allCourses.description: Introduces students to China's economic and military relations with the world, assessment of likelihood for conflict, and how to strategically manage business risk from regional conflict. Includes an original documentary series and engaging discussion.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: New Ventures: A Course in Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the survival and growth of new ventures. Methods include analysis of live cases, guest speakers, discussion, and field projects with contemporary new ventures to learn about new venture management and surviving the liabilities of newness.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Lean Startup
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Based on the well-known Lean Launchpad course currently used by a growing segment of the startup world. Students work in teams to ideate, develop a Business Model Canvas, and gather customer/market feedback.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managing Organizational Change
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the implementation of change. Identifies the features of successful changes in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Creativity and Leadership in Entrepreneurial Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Learn about your own thinking process; develop the ability to think both logically and creatively and to understand how emotions affect your thinking. Class sessions involve discussion and experiential exercises. Business problems and issues are used for discussion and exercises.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
