allCourses.restriction: Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and practice of managing human resources. Students identify and analyze HR dilemmas, apply labor law, and design systems and processes to develop the human resources needed to help organizations achieve their goals.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Negotiations
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The objective is to assist students in developing an understanding of different theoretical perspectives and develop their skills in negotiating. Exploration of feelings and beliefs about negotiation, negotiation skills, and putting theory into action by practicing new negotiation skills.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Foundations of Teams
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Social and psychological processes that detract from effective teamwork and collaboration. Tools to understand how to be a better team member are introduced. Provides the foundation for students to become effective team leaders and to manage difficult team situations.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Comprehensive introduction to ethical considerations in business with a focus on awareness to the complexity of ethical decision-making and how to make choices from a standpoint of ethical consciousness.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: International Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Impact of different cultures and political/economic systems on assumptions, expectations, and organizational practices relevant to conducting business in different national settings. Understanding of the challenges of cross-national management and resources utilized to work and conduct business outside the United States.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Case analyses, free-form discussion, and written assignments designed to develop critical thinking skills, as well as knowledge of approaches to differing leadership challenges. Experiential exercises encourage students to develop their ability to innovate, foster collaboration, manage conflict, and value diversity.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting I
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First course in a series of two intermediate-level courses in financial accounting theory and practice. Concepts include the measurement, valuation, and reporting of current and long-term assets, current liabilities, and revenue recognition issues.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting II
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Second course in a series of two intermediate-level courses in financial accounting theory and practice. Concepts include the measurement, valuation, and reporting of long-term liabilities and contingencies, accounting for stockholders' equity, and the Statement of Cash Flows.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting III
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Third in a three-part series (A, B, and C). Focuses on developing knowledge related to investments, debt/equity issues, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and revenue recognition.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Individual Taxation
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of federal income taxation pertaining to individuals. Topics include income, deductions, credits, property transactions, and the impact of taxes on business and investment decisions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Corporate and Partnership Taxation
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of federal income taxation pertaining to partnerships and corporations, including subchapter S corporations. Emphasis on the tax issues associated with formation, operation, and termination of these entities.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Data Analytics in Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of data types and sources and how to apply and leverage analytical techniques in making financial and managerial accounting decisions.  Business and ethical issues surrounding the collection and use of Big Data are also discussed.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Accounting Information Systems & Spreadsheets
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of accounting information systems including internal controls and transaction processing cycles. Development of efficient spreadsheets as applied to financial and managerial accounting concepts.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Advanced Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers advanced concepts in accounting theory and practice. Topics include business combinations, consolidated financial statements, foreign exchange transactions, international, and governmental/nonprofit accounting standards.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Auditing
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to auditing practice with emphasis on the verification of financial statements and related information. Topics include professional ethics, assessment of audit risk, study and evaluation of internal control, gathering and evaluating audit evidence, and audit reporting.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Investments
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Foundations of investment management.  Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, and option pricing theory. Students are expected to combine market research results and electronic information sources to create optimal investment strategies.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Multinational Finance
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on financial issues facing multinational corporations, the most important of which is the management of foreign exchange risk. Introduction to investments and financing decisions in international capital markets.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 109 and (ECON 20A or MGMT 4A) and (ECON 20B or MGMT 4B)

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: FinTech
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of economic mechanisms in areas of FinTech. Identifying and analyzing important issues through a balance of qualitative analysis and quantitative applications. Topics covered include Bitcoin, Blockchain, Crowdfunding, peer-to-peer lending, robo-advisor, and their economic and social impacts.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Introduction to the Real Estate Process
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory survey course providing a working knowledge of the real estate market, both residential and commercial. Topics include real estate economics, appraisal, feasibility, investment, tax considerations, financing, and development. Lectures and cases, with supplemental presentations by real estate professionals.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Applied Financial Valuation
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Case study course designed to confront students with real-world financial valuation problems. Situations are chosen to enhance students’ understanding of the application of finance theory. The principal focus is on estimating the value of firms and projects in diverse settings.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to financial derivatives. Covers forward contracts, futures, swaps, and options. Applications of these instruments, including pricing and risk management, are emphasized.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Consumer Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of the behavioral sciences to understanding buyer behavior.  Topics include perception, memory, affect, learning, persuasion, motivation, behavioral decision theory, social and culture influences, and managerial implications.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing Research
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Research to aid managerial decisions for products and services; problem formulation, research design, data collection, sampling, statistical analyses, managerial recommendations, and implementation in several real-world settings.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Sales Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed for students interested in learning about sales force management and personal selling by firms engaged in business-to-business and consumer goods/services marketing. Covers advantages of personal selling, how to perform sales calls, challenges of sales managers, roles of buying centers.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Global Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students are exposed to the challenges and opportunities facing marketers in the international marketplace. Special attention is given to the management of cultural differences in product development, distribution systems, pricing, and promotion.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Brand Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to issues in planning, implementing, and evaluating brand strategies, relevant theories, models, and tools for the making of brand decisions; application of these principles.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Pricing Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides a framework for designing and analyzing pricing strategies. Emphasizes role of pricing in the marketing-mix decisions and broader marketing strategy of a firm. Incorporates study of various economic, psychological, competitive, and organizational foundations that enter into effective pricing decisions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Digital Media Marketing Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Entails developing digital marketing strategy across numerous digital marketing platforms; understanding digital native consumers and newer consumer.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Analysis of Marketing Data
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunity to learn and apply analytical skills to marketing datasets to unveil hidden patterns and truths, to measure and quantify the performance differences between different initiatives, and to inform decision-making in an increasingly digital world.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: U.S. Healthcare Systems
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Providers, suppliers, payers, consumers, and the unique market dynamics among these players. Structure, organization, and financing of health care. The health care industry's relationship to the overall economy will be explored.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business of Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: In order to improve the quality and efficiency of health care delivery one must understand the design and management of health care operations. Opportunities for innovation and changes needed to design a simple, accessible, fair, and effective health care system.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Social Media
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers theoretical aspects and business applications of social media tools including blogs, wikis, social networking platforms, immersive environments, and other social computing technologies. Also covers business value of social-media-enabled processes.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students how to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Previous experience with programming languages (preferably Python).

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Intelligence for Analytical Decisions
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: BI from both managerial and technical perspectives. Learn to apply a variety of data mining techniques to learn business intelligence embedded in data, and apply that intelligence to run your business more efficiently. These techniques are useful in different areas.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Query, manipulate, and understand data and learn about leading edge applications for databases.  Database fundamentals including entity relationship design, creating database tables, normalization, and data querying.  Contemporary applications of database using case studies.  Applications include data warehousing, data mining.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Digital Strategies
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Covers business strategies for firms that make technology products. Insights are applicable not only to industries that make information and technology goods but also to industries that leverage digitization and network effects for their products.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Management of Information Technology
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Strategic use and impact of information technology (IT) in organizations. Covers what IT is, and how it works, business value of IT, and IT strategies that organizations can employ to create value.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Supply Chain Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Flows of materials and information among all of the firms that contribute to a product or service. Forecasting, demand management, logistical networks, inventory management, supplier contracting, sourcing, information technology, flexibility, globalization, and performance management.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Operations Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Managing the productive resources, from which raw materials as inputs are being transformed into useful outputs of final products and services. Explanation of issues pertaining to both manufacturing and services-oriented systems.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of management. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Communication
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a solid foundation in business communication. Emphasis is placed on improving students' written and oral communication skills to help them succeed in (1) upper-division Business Administration courses, (2) graduate school, and (3) work and career activities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Law
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A study of the legal environment of business.  Topics include contracts, agency, partnerships, corporations, and other basic principles of law as they relate to business transactions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of financial statements and their related footnotes; tools and procedures common to financial statement analysis; relationships among business transactions, environmental forces (political, economic, social), and reported financial statement information; how financial statement information can help solve certain business problems.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Decision Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Use of decision analysis digital technologies for multiple objective decisions under certainty; decision-making under risk using decision trees; fitting probability distributions to judgments or data; and Monte Carlo simulation, applied to business, government, not-for-profit, and personal decisions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Administrative Internship
allCourses.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Administrative Internship
allCourses.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Administrative Internship
allCourses.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Principles of Accounting I
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First in a two course introductory series. Emphasis on financial accounting concepts and practices essential to the administration of business enterprises; including recording and valuation of financial transactions, and preparation, analysis, and interpretation of financial statements.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Principles of Accounting II
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Second in a two-course introductory series. Emphasis is on the introduction of managerial accounting concepts and techniques as tools to aid management in carrying out the primary internal functions of planning, control, and decision-making.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Basic Economics for Managers I
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4A may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20A.
allCourses.description: Microeconomic principles for managers. Useful applications of basic economic principles to situations in business as well as in various professions. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Basic Economics for Managers II
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4B may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20B.
allCourses.description: Macroeconomic principles for managers. Useful applications of basic economic principles to situations in business as well as in various professions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Management of Contemporary Organizations
allCourses.description: Equips students with working knowledge of several major subject areas within the context of business and society studies. Topics include:  role of management in organizations, corporate social responsibility and responsiveness, ethics and values in business, government regulation, and international business.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Statistics for Business Decision Making
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basics of data analysis and the fundamental notion of statistical inference emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Classical estimation and hypotheses testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, nonparametric methods, and statistical probability.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of management. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Thinking Strategically in the Digital Age for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the strategic and organizational challenges that a rapidly changing environment poses to the firm’s management and frames them according to Merage’s strategic emphasis on analytical decision making, innovation, and information technology.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Analytics: Decision-Making for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Topics include classical estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Organizational Leadership for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops a better understanding of individual and group behavior in and across organizations, and the frameworks by which to analyze and understand behavior in complex organizations. Enhances the skills required to manage collaboration and lead. Every other weekend course.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Reporting Policies for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Involves the development, analysis, and interpretation of financial accounting information for external reporting purposes. Emphasis on measurement and valuation issues in decision-making problems and cases. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managerial Accounting for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Involves developing and using internal financial and non-financial information to help organizations make planning, budgeting, control, operating, and performance evaluation decisions. Every other weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 203A. MGMT EP 203A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Microeconomics for Executives in the Digital Age
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions of consumers and firms. Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, market failures, and introductory game theory.  Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Macroeconomics for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces use of macroeconomic analysis to manage the business cycle for competitive advantage. "Business cycle-sensitive" management is explored within the context of marketing, operations management, HRM, merger and acquisition activity, and capital financing and expenditures. Every other weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 204A. MGMT EP 204A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to marketing. Topics include developing familiarity with fundamental marketing concepts, theories, and techniques; acquainting students with the type of decisions made by executives, including customer targeting, product, pricing, place, promotion, and research. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Competing with Digital: Technology, Analytics, Business Models
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how information technology is used to create value in organizations through product, process, and strategy innovation. Aims to help managers understand the strategic role of key information technologies in managing organizations. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Operational Excellence: Processes, Strategy, and Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management. A blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations. Topics include product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, just-in-time manufacturing, and quality management. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managerial Finance for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to financial theory and concepts. Topics include time value of money, valuation of stocks and bonds, capital budgeting, portfolio theory, and capital structure choice. Every other weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 201A and MGMT EP 203A and MGMT EP 204A. MGMT EP 201A with a grade of C or better. MGMT EP 203A with a grade of C or better. MGMT EP 204A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Strategy for Executives: Foundations and Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides conceptual frameworks and techniques to analyze and develop firm strategies. Through case analysis/discussion, helps improve strategic thinking by developing frameworks by which to assess, evaluate, and respond to different business situations. Every other weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 200 and MGMT EP 202 and MGMT EP 205 and MGMT EP 209A. MGMT EP 200 with a grade of C or better. MGMT EP 202 with a grade of C or better. MGMT EP 205 with a grade of C or better. MGMT EP 209A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Practice of General Management for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches the graduating MBA how the best managers actually manage. Students develop a toolkit of proven concepts and practices that will help them succeed as managers at any level.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Negotiations For Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of business. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Global Business I for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of global strategy, economics, and financial issues. Topics include global manager’s environment, global strategy, impact of national culture on business systems, strategies and practices, foreign direct investment, corporate governance, human resources, and international marketing. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Global Business II for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes and reinforces international perspectives contained in the M.B.A. curriculum by providing a week-long intensive seminar abroad in the second year. Scholars and business people from the host country instruct Executive M.B.A. students in designed class sessions and company visits.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Executive Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the conceptual, practical, and personal dimensions of executive leadership. Past and current leadership theories are addressed. Individual personal assessment and diagnosis. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Individual Study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Thinking Strategically in the Digital Age for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the strategic and organizational challenges that a rapidly changing environment poses to the firm’s management and frames them according to Merage’s strategic emphasis on analytical decision making, innovation, and information technology.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Analytics: Decision-Making for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Topics include classical estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Management Science for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Uses both prescriptive analysis and risk analysis to explore linear programming models, network problems, and simulation. The goal is to introduce and help students acquire some skills of logical thinking with formal models and improve students’ decision making capability.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Organizational Leadership for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops a better understanding of individual and group behavior in and across organizations; the frameworks by which to analyze and understand behavior in complex organizations; and enhances the skills required to manage collaboration and lead. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Reporting for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Involves the development, analysis, and interpretation of financial accounting information for external reporting purposes. Emphasis on measurement and valuation issues in decision-making problems and cases. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Driving Profitability Through Managerial Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches skills for making vital strategic and tactical decisions (e.g., outsourcing; adding/dropping product lines), to maximize profitability while managing risk. Also covers managerial tools (e.g., budgeting, cost-volume-profit analysis) to drive strategy implementation and incentivize employees. Taught in an evening/weekend format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A or MGMTMBA 203A. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of C or better. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Microeconomics for Managers in the Digital Age
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions, the determinants and consequences of market structure and market failure. Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, and introductory game theory. Evening and weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Macroeconomics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces use of macroeconomic analysis to manage the business cycle for competitive advantage. "Business cycle-sensitive" management is explored within the context of marketing, operations management, HRM, merger and acquisition activity, and capital financing and expenditures. Evening and weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to marketing. Develops familiarity with fundamental concepts, theories, and techniques in marketing and acquaints students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers including customer targeting, product, pricing, placement, promotion, and research. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Competing with Digital
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the technological and managerial issues surrounding the development and use of IT in organizations. Examines how technology can be used to execute an organization's business strategy and to enable new, innovative business strategies. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Operational Excellence: Processes, Principles, and Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management. Blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations. Topics include product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, distribution management, just-in-time manufacturing, quality management. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Finance for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to financial theory and concepts. Topics include time value of money, valuation of stocks and bonds, capital budgeting, portfolio theory, and capital structure choice. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 201A and MGMT FE 203A and MGMT FE 204A

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Investments for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Foundations of investment management. Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, and valuation models for equities, bonds, and options. Emphasis on practical applications, including optimal investment strategies. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MGMT FE 209A OR MGMTMBA 209A ) AND ( ADMIN - FULLY EMPLYD MAJORS ONLY OR BUSINESS ADMIN MAJORS ONLY OR DIGITAL LEADERSHIP MAJORS ONLY OR BIOTECHNOLOGY MGMT MAJORS ONLY OR ADMIN - EXECUTIVE MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides conceptual frameworks and techniques to analyze and develop firm strategies. Through case analysis and discussion, helps improve strategic thinking by developing frameworks by which to assess, evaluate, and respond to different business situations. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 200 and MGMT FE 202 and MGMT FE 205 and MGMT FE 209A

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Networks, Platforms, and Ecosystems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on unique strategic issues raised by multi-sided platform businesses that facilitate interaction among different parties. Combining economic theory and case examples to unpack subtle factors making multi-sided businesses different. From value propositions to pricing strategies to design decisions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Corporate Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how firms should assemble resources in-house, ally with partners, or acquire firms to grow and thrive. Learn the tools necessary to develop and evaluate a corporate strategy and to become an effective strategist, consultant, or analyst.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: A project course in which student teams develop a business plan to launch a new venture. Drafts of sections of the plan are due throughout the course. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Strategy in a Digital Age
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on applying unchanging basic principles of strategy, economics, and organization to digital technologies. Studies historical and contemporary competitive situations to work out key underlying digital mechanisms that shape competition over time.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Competitive Intelligence for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how to design a competitive intelligence program, which is a core foundation upon which competitive strategies and execution tactics are developed, assessed, and modified. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Practice of General Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to teach the graduating M.B.A. students how the best managers actually manage. Students will develop a toolkit of proven concepts and practices that will help them succeed as managers at any level.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Organizational Change in a Digital World for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the implementation of change. Identifies the features of successful changes in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Performance Management in 21st Century Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The key to sustained competitive advantage in a 21st century organization. Performance management is all about aligning employee attitudes and behaviors with firm goals and performance.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Negotiations For Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Global Negotiations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes economic, political, social, and cultural environments of international business negotiations. Topics include self-assessment/analysis, environmental analysis, international team building, negotiation processes and strategies, resources, skills, pre-negotiation preparations, agreements, and post-contract negotiations. Specific emphasis will be placed on cross-cultural problem-solving.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: International Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the effects of different national cultures, and political and economic systems on the assumptions, expectations, organizational practices, and organizational forms needed to conduct cross-national organizational work. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation for Managers I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develops skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis by examining financial information quality, profitability and risk analysis, earnings management, revenue recognition, asset recognition and valuation, and how financial reporting is related to the business environment and managerial incentives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A or MGMTMBA 203A. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of C or better. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation for Managers II
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the financial statement analysis of liabilities and stockholders' equity. Topics include forecasting financial statements, earnings-based valuation models, accounting analysis of mergers and acquisitions, leases, bankruptcy prediction, and derivatives. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A or MGMTMBA 203A. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of C or better. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Wealth Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Aims to integrate behavioral finance, psychology, personal financial planning, risk management, and asset management to provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge to effectively build and manage wealth.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: FinTech and the Digital Economy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Introduction to the Real Estate Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory survey course providing an understanding of the real estate market. Topics include real estate economics, valuation, feasibility, investment, tax considerations, financing, development, and corporate real estate asset management. Hands-on lectures, with guest lectures by real estate professionals.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: International Real Estate
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of international real estate investment opportunities. Topics include size and breadth; opportunities and challenges (tax treatment, currency/political/market risks, transaction costs, lack of local knowledge); ownership vehicles (REITs, joint ventures, equity funds, etc.). Global cast of guest lecturers supplements lectures.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Real Estate Capital Markets
allCourses.description: Understanding the four sectors of real estate capital markets: pubic debt, private debt, public equity, private equity; estate investment, key players, investment types drive capital solutions, underwriting strategies, and vehicle structuring, debt versus equity source characteristics and implications for returns.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: The Real Estate Development Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Nature and composition of development community and development process. Emphasis on role of conflicting interests, values and goals, and market uncertainty. Special attention paid to deal structuring and risk management. Lectures, guest lecturers, team projects evaluating actual development project.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Seminar in Management of the Real Estate Enterprise
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Beyond "The Deal" to management of the real estate enterprise itself. Explores aspects of decision-making focused upon strategic objectives: goal setting, legal/tax structures, family-owned firms, going public, corporate ethics, capital structure, diversification, core competencies, technology. Guest professionals.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Applied Real Estate Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the public real estate investment trust (REIT) market and its place in modern investment strategies, presents methods for analyzing and valuing companies, and introduces basic concepts for constructing and managing a real estate investment portfolio.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Geared to students who are seeking a career in finance and/or in working with venture capital firms, private equity/buyout firms, investment banks, commercial lenders, mezzanine fund investors, corporate finance, and entrepreneurial firms.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Derivatives for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies financial derivatives instruments, including forward contracts, futures, swaps, and options. Advanced applications of these instruments, including pricing and risk management, are emphasized. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing Research for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Qualitative and quantitative marketing techniques that generate customer insights. Discusses problem formulation, data collection, statistical analyses, formulating managerial recommendations, implementation, and how research is used by companies. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managing Advertising and Communications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Integrated marketing communications, including advertising, sale promotions, public relations, and direct mail. Exposure to elements of a communications plan; marketing research, including copy testing and tracking; creating brand value; media strategies; metrics. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business to Business Selling and Sales Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Sales is the interpersonal process where the needs of the buyer are uncovered and satisfied, to the long-term benefit of both parties. Students explore sales force management and personal selling in a dynamic, digital environment.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing on the Internet for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the Internet's impact on traditional methods of marketing. Discusses how to capitalize on and increase the Internet's utility as a tool that can increase marketing effectiveness, efficiency, and competitiveness. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Strategic Brand Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Addresses important branding decisions faced by organizations. A computer simulation allows students hands-on experience in making decisions about their brand and seeing the results of those decisions. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Machine Learning Analytics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods to mine data repositories for business intelligence to facilitate analytical decision-making. Topics include clustering for market segmentation; association rules to discover relationships between different purchase decisions; Naive-Bayes classification techniques for decision-making using decision-trees. Evening or weekend format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Digital Strategies and Markets
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how online social media are impacting organizations and markets. Topics include collective intelligence, online social influence, social networks, and social media monetization. The target audience consists of students interested in IT consulting, competitive strategy, marketing, and entrepreneurship.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Analytical Decision Models for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction of analytics tools for decision making. Topics include linear and non-linear optimization and simulation models. Excel Solver is used as the optimization tool and Risk Solver Platform is used as the simulation tool. Evening or weekend.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Decision Analysis for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Models of preferences and uncertainty; exercises in creative problem solving. Assessment and use of preference models for private, public, and not-for-profit decision making. Assessment and use of subjective probabilities in decision making. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Supply Chain Analytics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to fundamental analytics tools to manage business uncertainties, meet customer needs, and drive business disruptions through supply chain innovations. Example topics include forecasting, inventory management, capacity planning, profit analysis, supply chain coordination, risk management, simulation-based performance analysis.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Predictive Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deals with predicting entities, such as demand for a product or service (forecasting) and predicting membership of known groups (classification). Blends methodologies of forecasting and data mining and focuses on the application of these methods to managerial problems and decision-making.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Business
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Business. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business

allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Detailed study from a business viewpoint of contract theories, assignments, delegation of duties, third-party beneficiary contracts, defenses to consensual contracts, types of conditions, methods of excusing conditions, remedies, and types of damages. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business

allCourses.description: Use of contextual inquiry and ethnographic methods to assess real world contexts.  Exploring culture, power, physical layout, and the role of artifacts in information flow, communication practices, and coordination through qualitative fieldwork in an organization.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business

allCourses.description: Explores the crucial roles of external forces: globalization, technology, shifting demographics - as transformative catalysts for change - opening markets, erasing boundaries, and transforming industries. allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business

Evening and weekend course format.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
