allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Operational Excellence: Processes, Models, and Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management. A blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations. Topics include product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, distribution management, just-in-time manufacturing, quality management.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managerial Finance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to financial theory and concepts.  The main topics covered are time value of money, valuation of stocks and bonds, capital budgeting, portfolio theory, capital structure choice.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Investments
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Foundations of investment management. Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, and option pricing theory. Students are expected to combine market research results and electronic information sources to create optimal investment strategies.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Strategy: Foundations and Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides conceptual frameworks and techniques to analyze and develop firm strategies. Through case analysis and discussion, helps improve strategic thinking by developing frameworks by which to assess, evaluate, and respond to different business situations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 200 and MGMTMBA 202 and MGMTMBA 205 and MGMTMBA 209A

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: MBA Proseminar
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students in the Merage School Full-time MBA Program with information and practical skills for success in the MBA program, and for business career planning.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: New Venture Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches students how to launch and manage a new business by providing an overview of the start-up process, including how to identify new business opportunities and how to develop a sound operating model, value new ventures, and understand capital financing.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Entrepreneurship: Planning the New Venture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Project course in which student teams develop a business plan to launch a new venture. The final business plan is presented to an expert panel.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MGMTMBA 202 or MGMT FE 202) and (MGMTMBA 205 or MGMT FE 205) and (MGMTMBA 210 or MGMT FE 210)

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Competitive Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: The course focuses on how to design a competitive intelligence program which is a core foundation upon which competitive strategies and execution tactics are developed, assessed, and modified.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Enhances students' analytical skills by analyzing complex challenges that businesses face and to quickly implement a winning response.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Organizational Change
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the implementation of change, including identifying the features of successful change in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Negotiations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: International Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the effects of different national cultures, political and economic systems on the assumptions, expectations, organizational practices, and organizational forms needed  to conduct cross-national organizational work.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develops skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis by examining financial information quality, profitability and risk analysis, earnings management, revenue recognition, asset recognition and valuation, and how financial reporting is related to the business environment and managerial incentives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 203A or MGMT FE 203A. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of C or better. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Multinational Finance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on financial issues facing multinational corporations, the most important of which is the management of foreign exchange risk. Other topics include investments and financing decisions in international capital markets.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: FinTech and the Digital Economy for Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Geared to students who are seeking a career in finance and/or in working with venture capital firms, private equity/buyout firms, investment banks, commercial lenders, mezzanine fund investors, corporate finance, and entrepreneurial firms.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies cases that expand concepts covered in the introductory corporate finance course and focuses on estimating the value of firms and projects in diverse settings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MGMTMBA 209A or MGMT FE 209A) and (MGMTMBA 209B or MGMT FE 209B)

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Consumer Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the consumer decision-making process with an emphasis on application of concepts and research findings from behavioral sciences for solution of marketing problems. Includes models of consumer decision-making, information processing theories, and sociological influences on consumer decision-making.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Marketing Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Covers conducting marketing research to generate consumer insights that will drive sales, market share, and profitability and/or realize other quantitative objectives. Discusses problem formulation, data collection, statistical analyses, formulating managerial recommendations, implementation, and how research is used by companies.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: New Product Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to introduce the new product development process and techniques to identify markets, develop new product ideas, measure consumer preferences, position and design new products, as well as test them prior to launch. Analytical thinking and techniques are emphasized.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Global Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the problems and perspectives of marketing across national boundaries, and develops analytical abilities for structuring and controlling marketing programs related to overseas business. Financial, legal, and cultural barriers to international marketing are emphasized.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Managing Nonprofits
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the similarities and differences between for-profit and nonprofit organizations, with emphasis on the management of nonprofits.  Topics include: marketing, fundraising, staffing, management/director relationships, use of volunteers, and emerging career opportunities.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Economics of Information
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of fundamental economic principles governing information technology industries. Particularly, implications for optimal pricing strategies, determinants/consequences of market structure, and the role and rationale for government intervention and the implications for business strategy.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Data Camp for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of R for basic data analytics and visualization with hands-on training using Data Camp. This project is meant to foreshadow the analysis that students will be doing in their electives.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Machine Learning Analytics for Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods to mine data repositories for business intelligence to facilitate analytical decision-making. Topics include clustering for market segmentation; association rules to discover relationships between different purchase decisions; Naive-Bayes classification techniques for decision-making using decision-trees.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Analytics and Technology Consulting
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on elements of analytics and personalized engagement. Students work on a project using a real-life business problem and data to get hands-on understanding.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Digital Strategies and Markets
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how online social media are impacting organizations and markets. Topics include collective intelligence, online social influence, social networks, and social media monetization. The target audience consists of students interested in IT consulting, competitive strategy, marketing, and entrepreneurship.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Decision Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Models of preferences and uncertainty; exercises in creative problem solving.  Assessment and use of preference models (von Neumann-Morgenstern expected utility and measurable value functions) for private, public, and not-for-profit decision making. Assessment and use of subjective probabilities in decision making.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Supply Chain Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the use of advanced analytics and data-driven methods to successfully manage uncertainty in supply chains, meeting customer needs in the most timely and cost effective manner, and driving business disruptions through innovations.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the fundamental components of project management and its role in the modern corporation. Emphasis on how to initiate, implement, control, and terminate a project. Use of computer package for project management.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Predictive Analytics for Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deals with predicting entities, such as demand for a product or service (forecasting) and predicting membership of known groups (classification). Blends methodologies of forecasting and data mining and focuses on the application of these methods to managerial problems and decision-making.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Field Studies in Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Each quarter a number of special topic seminars are offered in the 290 series.  Examples of possible topics include Communication in Organizations, Power and Authority in Organizations, International Management, Health Care Administration, Real Estate Development.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Detailed study from a business viewpoint of contract theories, assignments, delegation of duties, third-party beneficiary contracts, defenses to consensual contracts, types of conditions, methods of excusing conditions, remedies, and types of damages.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Biotech Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Taught jointly by Bio Sci and Merage School faculty, the course addresses fundamental aspects within, and associated with, the biotechnology industry. Curriculum is focused largely on management issues, including finance, product development, pharmaceuticals, project management, regulatory affairs, and ethics.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Edge
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Edge explores the crucial roles of external forces - globalization, technology, shifting demographics - as transformative catalysts for change - opening markets, erasing boundaries, and transforming industries. This course prepares future business leaders to innovate and compete successfully.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Miicromarketing with Digital Footprints
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: How businesses use digital footprints from household data and point-of-purchase data to customize product offerings and delivery, store locations, advertising, and promotions to households and neighborhoods with the highest market potential. Hands-on experience with Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping software.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Merage Consulting Projects
allCourses.restriction: Second-year MBA students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students the opportunity to put into practice concepts, skills, and tools acquired in other parts of the M.B.A. program. Seminars augment internship experiences with analyses of relevant administrative issues.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of the selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Ph.D. Special Topics Seminar
allCourses.description: Each quarter a number of special topic seminars are offered in the 291 series for Ph.D. students. Examples include topics such as methods seminar, experimental design, qualitative research, structural equation modeling.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Pre-Colloquium Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Management Majors only.
allCourses.description: Seeks to facilitate discussion of upcoming Colloquium research papers increasing the likelihood that Ph.D. students are active participants in all of the Colloquia. Active participation enhances exposure of Ph.D. students to visiting scholars.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Doctoral Proseminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the central theories and theoretical controversies in the field of management. Examination of the formal education for managerial careers and exploration of issues relating to professional careers in research and scholarship in the field of management.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to prepare students for teaching career; incorporates seminars addressing topics of classroom dynamics, syllabus preparation, teaching techniques; establishes mentor relationship with faculty member in student’s teaching area, provides classroom experience and includes option of videotape analysis of teaching style.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Philosophy of Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides exposure to fundamental issues regarding how knowledge is created, defended, and replaced both in the natural and social sciences. Covers current debates on the meaning of the term “scientific” and the validity of the scientific method.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Doctoral Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Management Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of social science research: theory development, research design, methods, data management, and writing for scholarly publications; for doctoral students intending scholarly research careers. Involves hands-on practice in formulating hypotheses, designing research, and conducting journal reviews.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Experimental Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced course provides experience in planning and implementing an experiment or quasi-experiment, including choice of topic, study design, data analysis, and manuscript preparation.  Data analysis topics include ANOVA, ANCOVA, repeated measures, logistic regression, chi-square, and tests of mediation.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Applied Multivariate Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the most common techniques for multivariate analysis: principal component analysis, factor analysis, cluster analysis, MANOVA, regression with continuous variables, and regression with discrete variables.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Writing for Scholarly Publication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods for planning and carrying out scholarly writing.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: SAS Boot Camp
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches basics of SAS programming for empirical research. No prior knowledge of SAS or other computer programming language is required. Provides knowledge and tools to replicate an empirical study and learn how to perform very advanced data procedures.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Game-Theoretic Models for Management Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces some classic game-theoretic models for management research. It is about modeling strategic interactions between business competitors and/or partners in an analytical framework.  Various applications will be discussed, e.g., pricing strategies, business alliances, e-commerce, negotiations, and contracts, etc.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Business Economics Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches mathematical and conceptual basics of microeconomics and application. Covers basics of consumer/firm behavior, static and dynamic imperfect competition. Building of simple mathematical models to gain economic insights into business practices and decisions.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Decision Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Decision theories and preference models: How models are elicited or theories are experimentally tested, relevance to different management research areas, alternative theories, applications in management practice, and interpretations for the general public.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Foundational Theories of Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers major economic and sociological perspectives guiding the study of organizations (i.e., transaction cost economics, agency theory, institutional theories, organizational ecology, network and diffusion theories, behavioral theories, resource dependence), and examines how different theoretical perspectives are tested.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Information, Psychology, and Social Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In the marketplace for ideas, which succeed and which fail? How do ideas and information spread between individuals, and how do populations of ideas evolve? This course reviews recent research on these issues and applications to business.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Establishing Your Academic Career
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of the best practices for succeeding in an academic career. Presenting oneself in conversation, in written documents, in research talks, and in teaching.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: Individual Directed Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.school: The Paul Merage School of Business
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units.

allCourses.title: Research in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Molecular Biology and Biochemistry faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Research in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Molecular Biology and Biochemistry faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Research in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research with Molecular Biology and Biochemistry faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Research in Developmental & Cell Biology for First-year Students
allCourses.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry for first-year Ph.D. students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Molecular Biology & Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Presentation of research from department laboratories or, when pertinent, of other recent developments.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Molecular Biology & Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Presentation of research from department laboratories or, when pertinent, of other recent developments.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Molecular Biology & Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Presentation of research from department laboratories or, when pertinent, of other recent developments.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Tutorial in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Tutorials in the area of research of a particular professor which relate current research to the literature. May be conducted as journal clubs.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Tutorial in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Tutorials in the area of research of a particular professor which relate current research to the literature.  May be conducted as journal clubs.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Tutorial in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Tutorials in the area of research of a particular professor which relate current research to the literature. May be conducted as journal clubs.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Nucleic Acid Structure and Function
allCourses.description: Structure and chemistry of nucleic acids. Relationship between these properties and the mechanisms of fundamental processes such as replication and repair, RNA-mediated catalysis, formation and regulation of higher order chromatin structure and recombination.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C

allCourses.title: Protein Structure and Function
allCourses.description: The structure and properties of proteins, enzymes, and their kinetic properties.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51C

allCourses.title: Molecular Virology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Primary research data on the major DNA and RNA viruses emphasizing strategies of regulation of gene expression. Utilization of viruses as molecular biological tools. Graduate-level knowledge of the biochemistry and molecular biology of macromolecules is required.

allCourses.title: Structural Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, Xray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.

allCourses.title: Literature in Nucleic Acid Structure and Function
allCourses.description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in structure, properties, and biological mechanisms involving nucleic acids.

allCourses.title: Literature in Protein Structure and Function
allCourses.description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in structure and properties of proteins, enzymes, and their kinetic properties.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. The main goal is to achieve a basic understanding of the cellular and molecular basis of innate and adaptive immunity, and how immune function is coordinated at a systems level.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology.  Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 215. PHYSIO 215 with a grade of B+ or better

allCourses.title: Principles of Cancer Biology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes are studied from molecular viewpoints. Also studies their role in cancer; viral carcinogenesis. Designed for graduate students interested in cancer research. Format includes lectures and student-led discussions.

allCourses.title: Principles of Cancer Biology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include cancer cell growth and metastasis, chemical carcinogenesis, and cancer genetics and epidemiology. Designed for graduate students interested in cancer research. Format includes lectures and student-led discussions.

allCourses.title: Clinical Cancer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to acquaint students in basic life science with clinical cancer.

allCourses.title: Structure & Synthesis of Biological Macromolecules Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in macromolecular struture and synthesis as related to biological problems.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Literature-based, interactive discussions focused on review of seminal historic and recent immunology literature. Student responsibilities include reading, critical evaluation, and discussion of manuscripts.

allCourses.title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced course in immunology for graduate students enrolled in the Biotechnology master's program. Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, immunofluorescent staining assays.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
allCourses.concurrent: BIO SCI M123 and COMPSCI 183 and BME 132.

allCourses.title: Immunlology Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 15 times.

allCourses.title: Research-in-Progress Seminars
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Two half-hour presentations by graduate students and postdoctorals to the department on their current research projects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 15 times.

allCourses.title: Literature in Chemical and Structural Biology
allCourses.description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in chemical and structural biology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Stem Cells
allCourses.description: Presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer that is open to the science community, followed by discussion of the lecture topic or a related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.

allCourses.title: Principles of Genomics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey course of the principal subfields of genomics and their applications to biological and health sciences that will cover genome assembly and annotation, genome structure, comparative genomics, population genomics, functional genomics, and medical genomics.

allCourses.title: Metallobiochemistry
allCourses.description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Biotechnology - Nucleic Acids
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Supplements laboratory curriculum with scientific background behind experimental methods. Format consists of lectures and the presentation and analysis of relevant papers from the scientific literature.

allCourses.title: Biotechnology Laboratory - Nucleic Acids
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Nucleic acid techniques and recombinant DNA technology. Extraction and purification of nucleic acids, cloning and subcloning, PCR, site-directed mutagenesis, nucleic acid hybridization, additional associated procedures. Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebook) detailing experience and results.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Biotechnology - Protein Purification and Characterization

Explore the effects of composition, bonding, and confinement on physical properties of nanomaterials, their chemical syntheses, and their device physics in electronic, optoelectronic, and energy technologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and ENGR 54 and MSE 69

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Synthesis and Properties of Biological, Biomimetic, and Bio-Inspired Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Synthesis of biological materials, including self-assembly and biomineralization, and translational processing to engineered materials via additive manufacturing, freeze casting, and other methods. Subsequent functional properties of these materials are reviewed.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Polymeric Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including polymer molecular size and configuration, solution and bulk phase structural properties, mechanical properties including viscoelasticity and rheology, polymer synthesis methods, characterization techniques, processing methods, and examples from existing and emerging polymeric materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (MSE 165A or CBE 40C or MAE 91)

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior and Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, yielding, necking, creep, and fracture of materials. Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize the properties of materials. Design parameters.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize mechanical properties of materials. Emphasis on correlations between property and microstructure. Experiments include: plastic stability in tension, effect of grain size on flow stress, microstructural engineering.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering
allCourses.title: Ceramic Materials for Sustainable Energy
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A technical elective for students interested in materials. Topics covered include structure and properties of ceramic materials, and design for sustainable energy applications.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors only.

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.description: Treatment of the laws of thermodynamics and their application in understanding properties and equilibrium states of engineering materials. allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (MSE 165A or CBE 40C or MAE 91). ENGR 54 with a grade of C- or better. MSE 165A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Treatment of the kinetics of solid-state reactions and reactions at interfaces. Thermodynamics and kinetics of phase transformations, including solidification processes, diffusional and diffusionless phase transformations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (MSE 165A or CBE 40C or MAE 91) and (MSE 165B or BME 150 or MAE 120 or (CBE 120B and CBE 120C)). MSE 165A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (MSE 165B or (CBE 120B and CBE 120C) or MAE 120). MSE 165B with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: The Henry Samueli School of Engineering

Students apply those concepts to music from a wide range of historical and cultural origins.

allCourses.description: Introduces students with no musical background to the dramatic and performance conventions of opera, and suggests ways of developing a critical stance vis-a-vis the social, political, gender-related and moral conflicts that are presented by composers and librettists.

allCourses.description: An introduction to the analysis of musical styles and forms, to the sources for constructing music history and reconstructing historical music, and to J.S. Bach.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts

allCourses.restriction: Music Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Music - Performance Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the analysis of musical styles and forms, and to the sources for constructing music history and reconstructing historical music, to Richard Wagner.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MUSIC 40B. MUSIC 40B with a grade of D or better. Recommended: MUSIC 16D

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: 20th Century Music

allCourses.description: Survey of principal composers, movements, and compositional techniques of Western art music of the modern era.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MUSIC 16C. MUSIC 16C with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Major Composer
allCourses.description: Study of the works of an important composer with emphasis on their significance in historical and social contexts. Composers selected represent a wide variety of historical periods, nationalities, and stylistic orientations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music and Gender
allCourses.description: Explores various intersections between music and gender. Examines ways in which gender and sexuality have played a vital role in the creation, dissemination, and consumption of music ranging from medieval Christian mysticism to contemporary hip-hop artists.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Classical Music in Society
allCourses.description: Examines some ways in which classical music has played an integral role in aspects of society. Studies pieces from different cultural, political, and historical contexts in order to understand how musical meaning is created and interpreted.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: History of Film Music
allCourses.description: Course provides an overview of film music history. Special emphasis will be placed on developing an analytic vocabulary for musical elements and cultivating an understanding of how music can function within a film.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music in Multimedia
allCourses.description: Students explore intersections between music and other media forms through creating multimedia projects, readings, lectures, and discussion. Students produce music, edit video, increase media literacy, and study theories behind how music communicates meaning.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in Music Technology
allCourses.description: Introductory topics in electronic music, digital audio, and other aspects of music technology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in Music and Culture
allCourses.description: Examines music and musical practices in different historical periods, societies, and cultural settings.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Popular Music in the United States
allCourses.description: Examines the cultural, social, political, and economic dimensions of popular music in the United States over the last century and a half, with an emphasis on matters related to class, race, ethnicity, and gender.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music Technology and Computers
allCourses.description: A study of the influence of technology on the musical culture and aesthetics from the 20th century to the present, with particular emphasis on the role of the computer. Work includes lectures, readings, listenings, discussions, demonstrations, writing, and experimentation.

allCourses.description: Development of jazz from African and African American folk origins through blues, early jazz, swing, bebop, "cool" jazz, fusion, free jazz, and contemporary trends.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Beatles and the Sixties
allCourses.description: Through a study of the music of the Beatles, students are introduced to selected broader historical and cultural themes (e.g., race and music, gender and music, music and the counterculture) while developing an understanding of the basic elements of music.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: MAHUR-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
allCourses.description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on MAHUR modal system and different instruments of classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: HOMAYUN-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
allCourses.description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on HOMAYUN modal system and famous musicians and performers of classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: SHUR-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
allCourses.description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on the SHUR modal system and different poetic rhythms in classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Rock: The Early Years
allCourses.description: Surveys the social and cultural fabric of the post-World War II United States (from the late 1940s through the early 1970s) as seen through the prism of music - rock and roll music.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Experiments in Music
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Scientists explain the cognition of music using experimental methodology; artists expand the domain of music by trying previously unknown ways of making it. These two types of experiment deepen our understanding of music, from both scientific and artistic vantage points.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Communication Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Networking Laboratory
allCourses.description: A laboratory-based introduction to basic networking concepts such as addressing, sub-netting, bridging, ARP, and routing. Network simulation and design. Structured around weekly readings and laboratory assignments.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Networks
allCourses.description: Design principles of networked systems, advanced routing and congestion control algorithms, network algorithms, network measurement, management, security, Internet economics, and emerging networks.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NET SYS 201 or COMPSCI 232 or EECS 248A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Wireless and Mobile Networking
allCourses.description: Introduction to wireless networking. The focus is on layers 2 and 3 of the OSI reference model, design, performance analysis, and protocols. Topics covered include: an introduction to wireless networking, digital cellular, next generation cellular, wireless LANs, and mobile IP.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
allCourses.description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Middleware for Networked and Distributed Systems
allCourses.description: Discusses concepts, techniques, and issues in developing distributed systems middleware that provides high performance and Quality of Service for emerging applications. Also covers existing standards (e.g., CORBA, DCOM, Jini, Espeak) and their relative advantages and shortcomings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: An undergraduate-level course in operating systems and networks.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences

allCourses.description: Study of Networked concepts.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.description: Current research in networked systems. Includes talks by UCI faculty, visiting researchers, and Networked Systems graduate students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Neuroscience
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Neuroscience
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.

allCourses.title: Molecular Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Surveys molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in neuronal function, including control of gene expression, post-transcriptional and post-translational processing, RNA and protein targeting, cell death mechanisms, and molecular genetic basis of neurological disorders. Overview of the molecular aspects of developmental neurobiology.

allCourses.title: Cellular Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Neurophysiological and neurochemical mechanisms of electrical and chemical signaling in neurons. Topics include generation of resting- and action-potentials, voltage- and ligand-gated ion channels, second messenger systems, and synaptic transmission and integration.

allCourses.title: Cellular Neuroscience Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intensive hands-on laboratory experience of contemporary techniques for studying ion channels and synaptic function. Experiments include microelectrode recording, patch clamp, quantal analysis of synaptic transmission, heterologous expression of genes for channels and receptors, brain slice, and fluorescence calcium imaging.

allCourses.title: Systems Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Study of the mammalian nervous system at the systems level. Anatomy and physiology of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of fundamental conceptual and experimental issues in the neurobiology of learning and memory. The approach is a cross-level integration of research in molecular-genetic, cellular, circuit, systems, and behavioral analyses.

allCourses.title: Neural Coding, Computation, and Dynamics
allCourses.description: Theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, compute adaptive responses to external inputs, and how knowledge is extracted from experience to generate an internal model of the world.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: At least one upper-division course in the field of Neuroscience or one upper-division course in Cognitive Science or Machine Learning.

allCourses.title: Scientific Presentation Skills
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A tutorial seminar on developing skills for presenting research to scientific audiences.

allCourses.title: Rigor, Reproducibility, and Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Understanding key concepts in experimental design, execution, and analysis that enhance or detract from scientific rigor.

allCourses.title: Bioinformatics and Systems Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics, genomic approaches, and Linux and R program in order to analyze RNA-sequencing data.

allCourses.title: Psychophysiological Methods in Clinical Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the principal signals of psychophysiology and outlines how measures calculated from these signals can be applied in clinical research and practice.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One graduate or undergraduate course in statistics.

allCourses.title: Epigenetics in Health and Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the role of chromatin/nuclear structure organization (histone and DNA modification, chromatin remodeling, higher order chromatin structure and nuclear organization) on gene regulation, DNA replication and repair, relevant to development, metabolism, learning and memory, and human disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 203 or MOL BIO 204 or NEURBIO 206

allCourses.title: Clinical and Epidemiological Aspects of Neurodegenerative Diseases
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Clinical and epidemiological aspects of neurodegenerative disorders causing dementia will be reviewed, including AD, PD, FTD, HD and cerebrovascular disease. Seminar format will include student presentations and group discussion.

allCourses.title: Regenerative Neurobiology
allCourses.description: Surveys the latest research on regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders will be examined.

allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Drug Addiction
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.

allCourses.title: Cortex: Structure, Function, and Plasticity
allCourses.description: Structured to include lectures and presentation of papers about cortex with emphasis on sensory-motor cortex. Both historical and current perspectives on cortical structure-function relationship will be critically evaluated.

allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Brain Aging
allCourses.description: Outlines some of the significant changes that occur in the aging brain, with a special emphasis on risk factors and protective strategies that promote successful brain aging. Topics include changes in synaptic plasticity, neurotrophic factors, and molecular mechanisms in aging.

allCourses.title: Functional Imaging of the Nervous System
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of technical and applied aspects of imaging techniques available for studying the nervous system. The areas emphasized are cellular and subcellular imaging of neural function, systems-level imaging of brain function, and imaging of the human brain.

allCourses.title: Advanced Analysis of Learning and Memory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Advanced analysis of contemporary research concerning the nature and neurobiological bases of learning and memory. Special emphasis is given to time-dependent processes involved in memory storage.

allCourses.title: Programming for Neuroscience Research
allCourses.description: A neuroscience-specific introduction to programming and data analysis using either MATLAB or Scientific PYTHON. Students will learn general programming skills and effective use of programming for data management, statistical analysis, and image analysis.

allCourses.title: Topics in Neurobiology and Behavior
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Neurobiology and Behavior. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Electronics for Biologists
allCourses.description: Basic principles of electricity; properties and use of discrete components and integrated circuits; circuit analysis and design. Intended for advanced students in the life sciences.

allCourses.title: Molecular Neurobiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: The application of genetic and recombinant DNA technology to neurobiology.  Topics include the study of neuronal proteins which play important roles in the formation of synapses and synaptic transmission.

allCourses.title: Perspectives in Neuroscience: Past, Present, and Future
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: An overview of the conceptual and technical foundations of contemporary neuroscience from ancient times to the present. The subjects include synapses, neurons, brain organization, sensory, motor and regulatory systems, learning and memory, human brain function and dysfunction.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Statistics for Neurobiologists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to common methods for statistical analysis used in neurobiology. Topics covered include t-tests, ANOVAs, correlations and regressions, general linear model, power analysis, and non-parametric tests.

allCourses.title: Auditory Neuroscience
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary overview of brain mechanisms of hearing. Emphasizes breadth of auditory function and research: single neurons to psychoacoustics, the chochlea to the cortex, and basic science to clinic.

allCourses.title: Colloquium in Neurobiology and Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Presentation of contemporary research problems in neurobiology and behavior and related areas by invited speakers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Proposals for Neuroscience Trainees
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students learn how to effectively communicate scientific ideas and results. Activities include learning how to effectively write a scientific proposal, how to perform a coherent, persuasive slide presentation, and how to give meaningful, constructive review critiques.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Introduction to Nursing Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: Covers topics relevant to evidence-based practice; nursing informatics as a specialty; electronic health records and clinical informatics; clinical decision support and decision analysis; using informatics to promote community/population health; telenursing and remote access telehealth; and ethical issues in nursing informatics.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Frameworks for Professional Nursing Practice
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Nursing Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: Conceptual frameworks for professional practice. Scope of professional nursing, jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and health care delivery systems in the context of the social, political, and economic environments. Socialization of the student for professional roles in nursing.
