allCourses.title: Medical Surgical Nursing 2
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines nursing assessment and advanced nursing management for acute and chronic health problems within the inpatient hospital setting. Theory content emphasizes assessment, health history, diagnostic reasoning, and nursing prioritization of care in medically complicated patients.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 209B and NUR SCI 217 and NUR SCI 221A. NUR SCI 209B with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 217 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 221A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Seminar in Clinical Translational Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of clinical translational science methods in the context of nursing science research. Emphasis placed on interdisciplinary and community participatory research approaches.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Consent of the instructor is required.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Seminar in Clinical Translational Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of clinical translational science methods in the context of nursing science research. Emphasis placed on interdisciplinary and community participatory research approaches.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Biostatistics for Health Sciences I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Helps students to develop skills necessary for applying statistical principles and practices in health research. This is achieved through in-depth review of existing research articles and hands-on statistical programming exercises.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Biostatistics for Health Sciences II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces advanced methods of statistical analysis and research design used in health research. These include linear, logistic, Poisson regression, and a brief introduction to regression models for correlated data.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Research Designs in Nursing Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Nursing Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research designs, methods, and analyses in nursing science. Evaluation of measurement and population issues, data management, ethics, analytical approaches, mixed methods work, and translational potential in the context of research.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Advanced Pharmacology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology that serve as a foundation for the pharmacotherapeutic management of patients evaluated and treated by advanced practice nurses.  Emphasis includes the application of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Advanced Pharmacology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology that serve as a foundation for the pharmacotherapeutic management of patients evaluated and treated by advanced practice nurses.  Emphasis includes the application of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 225A. NUR SCI 225A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Theoretical and Conceptual Frameworks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the history, roles, and uses of theory in nursing and health scholarship. Students examine, analyze, and utilize the components of theory, theory construction, concept analysis, and theory evaluation.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Grant Writing I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the principles and methods of proposal writing used in preparing grant proposals. Provides content on the process for good proposal development, key elements and sections of proposal, necessary information to include in grant proposal and development of budget.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Grant Writing II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a continuation of skill building in preparing a grant proposal, with emphasis on developing the educational training plan, budget and budget justification, the IRB and ethics component, and letters of support for a career-development grant.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 227A. NUR SCI 227A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Human Behavior and Mental Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on nursing management of individuals across the lifespan with alterations in mental health. Mental health promotion and crisis intervention, chemical dependency, acute and chronic care for psychiatric conditions, rehabilitation, and recovery are addressed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 209B and NUR SCI 217 and NUR SCI 221A. NUR SCI 209B with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 217 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 221A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Pain: Symptoms, Science, and Treatment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Ph.D. graduate standing is required.
allCourses.description: Covers theory, assessment, experience, and management of pain.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Application of theoretical concepts related to comprehensive health assessment of patients across the lifespan. Analysis, synthesis, and application of comprehensive health assessment data.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Clinical laboratory course for the application of concepts related to comprehensive health assessment of patients across the lifespan.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Prologue
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An onsite 2 1⁄2 day immersive experience that provides an introduction to DNP scholarship and foundations essential for academic success in a doctoral program. Preparatory activities and onsite individual and group assignments are completed.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Leadership and Professional Collaboration in Healthcare
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explore and debate the relationship between various leadership and collaboration models, theories health care practice, and outcomes. Prepares DNP graduates to assume leadership roles across the healthcare spectrum.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Appraisal and Translation of Evidence for Practice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides advanced concepts on research methods and measurement strategies that are applicable to support the advanced practice nurse to access, evaluate, and utilize data from various sources including research, quality improvement initiatives, and information technology origins to achieve improvements.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Consent of the instructor is required.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Health Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Participants analyze, apply, and evaluate current health policy-related literature, engage in the process of health policy development within professional, regulatory, or administrative environments, and develop an evidence-based health policy proposal across the spectrum of health care systems.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Scholarly Project I: Conceptualization and Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students gain the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to develop an evidence-based project plan and proposal. Structured didactic content and application of the Student's DNP Scholarly Project. First of four DNP Scholarly Project courses.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Social Determinants of Health and Health Equity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The four components of the Clinical Prevention and Population Health Framework: evidence-based practice, clinical preventive service and health promotion, health systems and policy, and population health and community aspects of practice with emphasis on ethical care delivery.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Intersession
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides DNP students an opportunity to present and receive faculty and peer feedback on their DNP project plan. Recommendations related to practical data collection and information gathering approaches and data analysis are also emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 235. NUR SCI 235 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Foundations of Health Systems and Health Economics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Foundational understanding of how healthcare is financed in the U.S. Explores economic theories and policies, various types of healthcare organizations, and healthcare delivery systems. Healthcare finance is discussed at national and practice levels.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: The Science of Change, Quality Improvement, and Program Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intro to science of quality improvement and program evaluation. Focus on info system technology and its application in quality improvement. Focus placed on the role of the advanced practice nurse leader in developing and leading clinical quality and safety initiatives.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Scholarly Project II: Proposal
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Developing a full proposal that reflects synthesis of the student's knowledge from prior coursework and work in an area of interest or expertise under the direction of a faculty mentor. Second of four DNP Scholarly Project course sequence.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Scholarly Project III: Implementation and Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Continued development of knowledge, skills, and abilities to implement the chosen DNP proposal. Students receive direction from a faculty mentor and peer feedback as they become engaged in the microsystem where they are implementing their DNP Scholarly Project.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Scholarly Project IV: Implications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Selection and implementation of evidence-based interventions supported through informatics and technological advances and measurement of outcomes in a selected practicum site as applicable. Includes reflection and mapping of the DNP Scholarly Project with DNP Essentials as published.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Epilogue
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: DNP students develop DNP competency through the presentation of their project and development of a professional manuscript. Individual direction from the DNP Project Team and peer feedback are provided throughout the course.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: A Systems Approach to Health and Well-Being
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on using a systems approach to promote individual and population wellness. The key topics include complex/dynamic system, analytic tools to measure dynamic/ interrelated processes, critical analysis of literature that utilizes the systems approach to promote holistic well-being.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Primary Care Adult/Gerontology Acute Common Conditions
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting patients and families across the lifespan. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics are integrated. Concepts of quality health care, resource management, and shared-decision making are emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 210 and NUR SCI 230. NUR SCI 210 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 230 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Designs in Nursing Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar in qualitative research philosophies, methods, and analysis in nursing science clinical research. Consideration of population access and sampling, ethics, data management, analytical approaches, and translational potential.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Quantitative Research Designs in Nursing Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar in experimental and survey research designs, methods, and analysis in nursing science clinical research. Consideration of measurement issues, mixed methods models, population access and sampling, data management, analytical approaches, and translational potential.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Curricular Design for the Health Professions
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the theoretical foundations, essential components, and accreditation standards for curriculum development at the program level. Outcome competencies are addressed as they apply to the development and evaluation of an educational program to meet society’s diverse healthcare needs.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Transformational Leadership in Education for the Health Professions
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students are introduced to the role of the nurse educator as change agent, leader, and scholar and are provided experience in planning learner-centered learning activities that are engaging and effective in achieving desired student performance.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Primary Care Women's Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Primary health care needs of women including adolescent, adult, and aging adults.  Emphasizes assessment, diagnosis, prevention, management, and education of common gynecologic and family planning health care needs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 210 and NUR SCI 230. NUR SCI 210 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 230 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Nursing Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of nursing informatics topics for practice.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Applied Data Science for Clinical Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides hands-on training in applied data science for clinical research.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Primary Care Obstetrics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Assessment and management of women during pregnancy. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology and therapeutics are integrated. Includes assessment, differential diagnosis, management, patient/family education, and counseling related to normal pregnancy care.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Primary Care Adult/Gerontology Chronic Conditions
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting adult and geriatric patients and their families. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutic are integrated.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 245. NUR SCI 245 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative and Mixed Methods Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion and application course on design and implementation of qualitative, mixed methods research. Emphasis on data analysis and management skills, interpretation of findings, reflexivity and ethical considerations in field work, and the development of.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Enrollment in a UCI Ph.D. program and at least one introduction qualitative course.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Foundations of Professional Nursing Practice
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development of skills in therapeutic communication, interviewing, functional assessment across the lifespan, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment. Faculty-facilitated, participatory peer group, and self-learning laboratory activities are included.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Frameworks for Professional Nursing Practice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A theory-intensive course focused on conceptual frameworks for professional nursing practice. Topics address the professional, political, and economic contexts of nursing practice, with an emphasis on jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and nursing’s role in the care delivery system.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Applied Pharmacology I
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology applied to intervention in pathophysiologic states across the life span. Discussion of the major drug groups with implications for monitoring, drug administration, toxicity, and patient education included. Physical, psychological, social, and cultural factors affecting drug administration.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Applied Pharmacology II
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology applied to intervention in pathophysiologic states across the life span. Discussion of the major drug groups with implications for monitoring, drug administration, toxicity, and patient education included. Physical, psychological, social, and cultural factors affecting drug administration.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Older Adult Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes the interaction of physical, pathophysiological, psychological, social, cultural, and health care policy factors influencing the health and health care of older adults. Topics include health risk factors, health assessment, acute illness and chronic conditions, and ethical issues.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Adult Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the restorative, peri-operative, and supportive nursing management of adults with acute or chronic alterations in oxygenation, regulation, immune response, elimination, metabolism, mobility, cognition, and substance abuse. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics will be integrated.

allCourses.title: Human Behavior and Mental Health Nursing
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on nursing management of individuals across the lifespan with alterations in mental health. Mental health promotion and crisis intervention, chemical dependency, acute and chronic care for psychiatric conditions, rehabilitation, and recovery will be addressed.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Pathophysiology I
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on pathologic alterations in physiologic processes in cells, tissues, organs, and systems across the life span. Content includes disease processes, linkage of relevant physiology to disease states, and factors that influence epidemiology and pathophysiology.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Pathophysiology II
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on pathologic alterations in physiologic processes in cells, tissues, organs, and systems across the life span. Content includes disease processes, linkage of relevant physiology to disease states, and factors that influence epidemiology and pathophysiology.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Primary Care Pediatrics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting pediatric patients and their families. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics are integrated.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 210 and NUR SCI 230. NUR SCI 210 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 230 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Community-Based Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Epidemiology, primary health care promotion, and disease prevention applied to nursing care of individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes sociocultural, political, economic, and environmental influences. Concepts and methods of assessing populations and communities incorporated in concurrent practicum.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 215 and NUR SCI 274 and NUR SCI 276

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Pediatrics: Care of Children and Families
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of infants, children, and adolescents with acute, chronic, and/or life-threatening conditions. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Maternity and Women’s Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of women’s wellness across the lifespan, the childbirth process, and newborn care. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Critical and Specialty Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the restorative, supportive care of individuals with life-threatening alterations in health status utilizing technology and pharmacology for life support. The course includes pathophysiology, diagnostics, monitoring, pharmacology, therapeutics, and evidence-based management interventions will be integrated.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Clinical Preceptorship
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Independent study course focusing on in-depth clinical nursing practice in a selected clinical area of interest to the graduate student. Students are mentored by a preceptor who is an expert clinician in the area.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 215 and NUR SCI 274 and NUR SCI 276

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Leadership and Management in Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores the professional nurse as leader and manager of a health care team. Principles and theories related to organizations, leadership, decision-making, and group process are applied to the delivery of health care at the individual and population levels.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Implementation Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on dissemination and implementation (D&I) science. Emphasizes the types of questions D&I research seeks to answer, commonly used models and frameworks, methods employed, and outcomes examined.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Frameworks for the Advanced Practice Registered Nursing Role: Nurse Practitioner
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Orientation to the scope and standards of advanced practice registered nursing pertinent to the APRN role. Principles of jurisprudence, ethics, and advocacy will be introduced along with conceptual frameworks for advanced nursing practice.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Professional Issues in Nursing
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides an orientation to the scope and standards of professional nursing practice for master's students. The social, political, and economic environments affecting health care delivery systems and the ethics of professional nursing practice are analyzed.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Compassionate Care with Underserved Populations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Addresses theory/research on health risk factors (e.g., psychiatric illness, sociocultural and economic characteristics) that impact patient health and well-being across the lifespan. Emphasis is on cultural awareness, lifestyle modification, community resources, and communication/coping strategies to promote well-being.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Primary Care Procedures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Introduces the theoretical basis for common procedures performed in primary care clinical practice. Focus includes EKG interpretation, x-ray interpretation, minor surgery, and orthopaedic procedures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 245. NUR SCI 245 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Scholarly Concentration
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Independent study focusing on critique, analysis, and synthesis of research evidence as a basis for graduate practice nursing in an area of interest to the student.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP APRN Practicum I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Clinical application of theory and research related to the advanced assessment and health promotion of patients across the lifespan.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 210 and NUR SCI 230 and (NUR SCI 230L or NUR SCI 231L). NUR SCI 210 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 230 with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 230L with a grade of B or better. NUR SCI 231L with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP APRN Practicum II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Clinical field study applying theory, research, and developing clinical skills related to the provision of care to patients and their families in increasingly complex clinical situations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 285. NUR SCI 285 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP APRN Practicum III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Clinical application of theory and research through clinical experiences in selected primary care settings designed to provide students with competencies in the assessment, diagnosis, management, and education/counseling in selected populations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 286. NUR SCI 286 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP APRN Practicum IV
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Continued clinical application of theory and research through clinical experiences in selected primary care settings designed to provide students with competencies in the assessment, diagnosis, management, and education/counseling in selected populations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 287. NUR SCI 287 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP APRN Practicum V
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Culminating clinical experience serves as a transition from the student role to that of the advanced practice nurse.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 288. NUR SCI 288 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP APRN Practicum VI
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Through continued clinical experience, students demonstrate increased responsibility and accountability for performance as an advanced practice nurse and clinical scholar, synthesizing knowledge of pathophysiology and disease management, evidence-based guidelines, anticipatory guidance, models of provider-patient communication, and provision of educational resources.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 289. NUR SCI 289 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Practicum I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, DNP project in an area of advanced practice in partnership with a selected agency or organization that solves a practice problem or improves population health, educational, or performance outcomes.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Practicum II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, DNP project in an area of advanced practice in partnership with a selected agency or organization that solves a practice problem or improves population health, educational, or performance outcomes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 291. NUR SCI 291 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: DNP Practicum III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Consent of instructor required to enroll.
allCourses.description: Implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, DNP project in an area of advanced practice in partnership with a selected agency or organization that solves a practice problem or improves population health, educational, or performance outcomes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NUR SCI 292. NUR SCI 292 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Directed Study in Vulnerable Populations
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science, Community and Population Health Nursing Majors only.
allCourses.description: Independent study that focuses on individually designed clinical learning experiences and goals within a selected vulnerable population, such as the homeless, veterans, minority groups, etc. Students work in a clinical setting addressing health care needs of the vulnerable population(s).
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Doctoral Dissertation Reading and Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Nursing Sciences faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Sue and Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Nursing Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed study with Nursing Science faculty.

allCourses.title: Immunopathogenic Mechanisms of Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examination of the mechanisms underlying disease states mediated by immune dysregulation. Topics include mechanisms of immune evasion by cancer, diseases mediated by cytokine dysregulation, role of the microbiome of the GI tract and other disease sites, and adoptive T-cell therapy.

allCourses.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Disease
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the molecular mechanisms of human diseases, including neurologic, hematologic, neoplastic, and infectious diseases. Students gain an understanding of these mechanisms, as well as models of human diseases.

allCourses.title: Experimental Pathology Journal Club
allCourses.description: Graduate-level course, which is open to all years, will involve the reading and discussion of papers, preferably written by the invited seminar speaker. Discussions will cover advanced topics in experimental pathology as related to an understanding of human disease.

allCourses.title: Neuropathology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers genetic and molecular mechanisms of neurological diseases. A grounding in neuroanatomy and prior or simultaneous enrollment in Anatomy 210A or the equivalent is strongly recommended. Resident physicians and clinical fellows can audit the course.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Provided for the preparation and completion of the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Genetics and Cytogenetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers current concepts regarding mitosis, meiosis, the cell cycle, and chromosome ultrastructure and function. Clinical disorders caused by chromosomal aneuploidy, duplication, and deletion, and principles of Mendelian, chromosomal, and multifactorial and nontraditional inheritance are presented and illustrated.

allCourses.title: Genetic Screening, Prenatal Development, and Human Teratology
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Principles and techniques of prenatal, neonatal, and carrier screening. Infertility, pregnancy, and delivery. Normal and abnormal prenatal growth and development. Reproductive and fetal effects of drugs, radiation, infections, and other environmental factors.

allCourses.title: Human Genetic Disorders
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Inheritance, diagnosis, natural history, management, and counseling considerations for commonly encountered genetic diseases, birth defects, and dysmorphic syndromes.

allCourses.title: Disorders due to Inborn Errors of Metabolism
allCourses.description: Aspects of biochemistry and metabolism are reviewed with special emphasis on genetic abnormalities which lead to inborn errors of metabolism. Diagnostic procedures, heterozygote detection, treatment, counseling issues, and prenatal diagnosis are reviewed.

allCourses.title: Molecular Genetics, Gene Mapping, and Genetic Linkage
allCourses.description: Derivation of different types of DNA probes and DNA libraries, restriction endonuclease polymorphisms, assignment of genes to chromosomes, and genetic linkage.  Emphasis on the use of recombinant DNA technologies and genetic analysis for diagnosis of human genetic disease.

allCourses.title: Quantitative Genetics
allCourses.description: Quantitative aspects of human genetics, including population studies, segregation analysis, linkage, mapping, and genetic risk determination.

allCourses.title: Hereditary Cancer Counseling
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Issues in genetic counseling for cancer. Cancer biology; genetic mechanisms and environmental influences in carcinogenesis; tumor pathology; cancer gene mapping; epidemiology. Features natural history, diagnosis, prevention, surveillance, and management of heredity cancers. Psychosocial, ethical, legal aspects of cancer risk assessment.

allCourses.title: Genetic Counselin Research Design
allCourses.description: Quantitative and qualitative methods for genetic counseling research. Reference management; statistics: sample size, power, and data analysis; reliability and validity; surveys, questionnaires, interviews, focus groups; quality of life and genetic epidemiology research; designing a research protocol; IRB issues; grant writing.

allCourses.title: Cytogenetics Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practicum introducing methods of specimen collection, short-term lymphocyte and bone marrow culture, long-term fibroblast and amniocyte culture, harvesting and slide preparation, chromosome staining, microphotography, and darkroom techniques. Microscopic chromosome analysis, photographic karyotyping, and appropriate use of cytogenetic nomenclature are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Genetic Counseling
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Through directed readings, observing patient evaluations, role-playing, and conducting intake interviews, students are introduced to the process of diagnosis, management, and counseling for genetic disease. Psychosocial issues, interviewing techniques, pedigree construction, clinical photography, and various other skills are addressed.

allCourses.title: Clinical Rotation I
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides extensive supervised experience in history taking, interviewing, and psychosocial assessment in the clinical genetics setting. Students independently perform telephone, office, and home-visit intake interviews, participate in counseling, and present cases at patient management conferences.

allCourses.title: Clinical Rotation II
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides further supervised experience in genetic counseling, case management, clinic administration and organization, and the use of community resources. Emphasis is on sharpening counseling skills and on developing a professional identity and code of ethics.

allCourses.title: Prenatal Diagnosis Counseling
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: A practicum with extensive supervised experience in prenatal diagnosis counseling which provides the student with the opportunity to conduct genetic counseling sessions semi-independently and to further develop clinical skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200A and PED GEN 200B and PED GEN 200C

allCourses.title: Counseling in Human Genetics: Theory and Methods
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical approaches, counseling models and methods, and bio-psychosocial assessment strategies are examined in the context of genetic counseling. Contract-setting, working alliance, the use of self and evaluation methods. Beginning counseling and peer supervision skills are practiced in class.

allCourses.title: Community Resources
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Lectures, guest speakers, and community visits acquaint genetic counselors with public and private health care and funding agencies, parent support and advocacy groups, and other resources to assist individuals and families confronted with genetic disorders, developmental disabilities, and birth defects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Ethical Issues in Human Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores major social, legal, and ethical issues in genetic counseling including those arising in genetic screening, prenatal diagnosis, informed consent, privacy and confidentiality, rights of the disabled, new genetic and reproductive technologies, treatment, and access to services.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Counseling in Human Genetics: Putting Thought to Practice
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Builds upon the skills learned in previous courses emphasizing advanced counseling methods such as listening, empathy, and collaboration. The counselor's own self-awareness, ethical behaviors, and limits are explored. Individual, team, and group exercises are performed.

allCourses.title: Professional Skills Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Hones and augments existing competencies in genetic counseling through ongoing clinical experiences. Develops skills using computers for genetics applications, provision of community and professional education, and clinic administration. Further experience in genetics laboratories or specialty clinics may be elected.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.description: Exploring modern Iran through film, literature, photography, travel writing, and philosophy and social science texts that introduce students to important concepts in post-colonial studies, social thought, war culture, religion, and media as experienced through the paradigm of a non-Western modernity.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Application of pharmacological principles in disease therapy.  Advanced pharmacological mechanisms and in-depth study of drug action.  Discussion of several major drug classes/therapeutic strategies:  molecular mechanisms of action, physiological consequences of administration, and clinical use.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in pharmacological science. Molecular biology, quantitative and biochemical pharmacology, fluorescent probes, behavior, genetics, animal handling, anatomical and receptor binding analysis, methods for ion channel study, the absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination of drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Ligand-gated ion channels, G protein-coupled receptors, receptor tyrosine kinases, ligand-regulated transcription factors, their signaling mechanisms, trafficking, macromolecular complexes, and physiological responses.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and periphery. Molecular biology, signal transduction, transmitter synthesis, and inactivation of major neurotransmitter systems. Drugs that act on these major neurotransmitters.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Design for Pharmacologists
allCourses.description: Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, experimental design, power, and the use of statistical computer software.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics in Research
allCourses.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, handling of misconduct.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: One week (five days, 40 hours) in-residence course offered on the UCI campus. Introduction to pharmacological techniques and current research problems; includes laboratory demonstrations and research seminars.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology: pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, pharmacogenetics, drug interactions, and toxicity.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Receptors and Drug Targets
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Molecular basis of drug-receptor interaction. Receptor properties including gene and protein structure, signaling mechanisms, trafficking and physiological effects: G-protein linked receptors, ligand-gated ion channels, receptor tyrosine kinases, nuclear receptors, and ligand regulated transcription factors.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Techniques in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Experimental techniques and model systems used in pharmacological research. Receptor analysis, bioassay, molecular biology, in vitro pharmacology, biochemical pharmacology, imaging, electrophysiology, in vivo pharmacology, disease models.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Design and Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, and power calculations.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics in Scientific Research
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, and handling of misconduct.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Concepts in Drug Discovery
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Critical steps involved in discovery and optimization of a new drug. Target selection, relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activities, screening methods, strategies to identify lead compounds, and preclinical characterization necessary for development of the drug for clinical trials.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Topics of current interest in pharmacology; discussion of recent research publications.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Master's Project in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Capstone research paper on topic of interest in pharmacology.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Autonomic and central nervous system pharmacology, including major drug classes and therapeutic uses. Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and peripheral nervous system, including neurotransmitter synthesis, inactivation, and receptor action.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Pharmacology of integrative function and behavior. Drug treatment of pain. Mechanisms of reward, addiction, and drugs of abuse.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Cardiovascular Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Basic understanding of drugs used in the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular disease. Mechanisms of action, clinical and adverse effects.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Endocrine, Respiratory, and Gastrointestinal Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Basic understanding of drugs used in endocrine, respiratory, and gastrointestinal conditions, including hormone replacement, contraceptives, and drugs for diabetes, asthma, obesity, ulcer, and gastric reflux. Mechanisms of drug action, clinical and adverse effects.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation and discussion of current problems and methods in teaching and research in pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Pharmacology and Toxicology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
allCourses.description: A selection of philosophical problems, concepts, and methods, e.g., free will, cause and substance, personal identity, the nature of philosophy itself. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy
allCourses.description: Examination of the central philosophical themes developed by the pre-Socratics, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, the Stoics, the Epicureans, and the Skeptics.

allCourses.title: Writing Philosophy
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of those aspects of writing of special importance in philosophy, e.g., philosophical terminology, techniques for evaluating arguments, philosophical definitions and theories. At least 4,000 words of assigned composition based on philosophical readings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Metaphysics
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the problems of "first philosophy," e.g., substance, free will, causation, abstract entities, identity.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Theory of Knowledge
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the basic issues in epistemology, e.g., the role of perception in the acquisition of knowledge, the nature of evidence, the distinction between belief and knowledge, and the nature of truth and certainty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Moral Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the problems of contemporary moral philosophy, e.g., the nature of justice, liberalism versus conservatism, happiness and its relation to virtue and right conduct, the objectivity of moral standards.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Logic
allCourses.description: Introduction to sentence logic, including truth tables and natural deduction; and to predicate logic, including semantics and natural deduction.

allCourses.title: Elementary Set Theory
allCourses.description: An introduction to the basic working vocabulary of mathematical reasoning. Topics include sets, Boolean operations, ordered n-tuples, relations, functions, ordinal and cardinal numbers.

allCourses.title: Metalogic
allCourses.description: Introduction to formal syntax (proof theory) and semantics (model theory) for first-order logic, including the deduction, completeness, compactness, and Löewenheim-Skolem theorems.

allCourses.title: Undecidability and Incompleteness
allCourses.description: Introduction to the formal theory of effective processes, including recursive functions, Turing machines, Church's thesis, and proofs of Göedel's incompleteness theorem for arithmetic, and Church's undecidability theorem for first-order logic.

allCourses.title: Topics in Logic
allCourses.description: Selected topics in mathematical or philosophical logic.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Induction, Probability, and Decision Theory
allCourses.description: Selected topics in induction, probability, and decision theory.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Medieval Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of some of the major theological and philosophical texts from the Medieval period.

allCourses.title: Topics in Ancient Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics from the writings of Plato and Aristotle, e.g., Aristotle's criticisms of Plato's metaphysics, ethics, or politics.

allCourses.title: Topics in Medieval Philosophy
allCourses.description: Studies of some of the major issues of concern to Medieval philosophers, e.g., universals, the nature and existence of God, faith, and reason.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Nineteenth-Century Philosophy
allCourses.description: Studies of some of the major figures after Kant (e.g., Hegel, Nietzsche, Marx, Kierkegaard), especially in German idealism and social thought.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in History of Analytic Philosophy
allCourses.description: Review of central theories or figures in the history of analytic philosophy. Emphasis on writings of Frege, Russell, Schlick, Carnap, and Quine. Topics include the nature of meaning and truth, the synthetic/analytic distinction, and scientific knowledge.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian Philosophy

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Modern Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of major developments in western philosophy from Descartes to Kant with readings from Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, Berkeley, Hume, and Kant.

allCourses.title: Topics in Metaphysics
allCourses.description: Examines central philosophical questions concerning our own fundamental nature and that of the world around us (e.g., causation and necessity, determination, free will, personal identity, the mind-body problem).
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Theory of Knowledge
allCourses.description: One or more topics in the theory of knowledge, e.g., the nature of rational justification, of perceptual knowledge, of a priori knowledge.

allCourses.description: Analysis of epistemological issues concerning medical research and health care. Topics may include medical evidence, transmission of medical knowledge, medical expertise, the epistemology of medical disagreement, classification of illnesses, well-being, philosophy of pain, and medical decision making.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Mind
allCourses.description: Selected topics involving the concept of mind, e.g., the relation between mind and body, the self, personal identity, consciousness, the unconscious.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Religion

allCourses.title: Topics in Feminist Epistemology
allCourses.description: Investigates the nature of knowledge from a feminist standpoint. Emphasizes the relevance of the knower’s gender and social situatedness in knowledge practices against a traditional account of knowledge as a detached activity of an independent, neutral subject.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Contemporary Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of recent philosophical developments in Anglo-American and Continental philosophy with readings from such figures as Russell, Moore, Wittgenstein, Quine, Heidegger, and Sartre.

allCourses.description: Selected topics in ethics.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Applied Ethics

allCourses.title: Medical Ethics
allCourses.description: Analysis of moral issues concerning health care. Topics may include just allocation of scarce medical resources, the doctor/patient relationship, genetic engineering, surrogate motherhood, abortion, euthanasia, or social policy concerning AIDS.

allCourses.title: Topics in Political and Social Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics in social and political philosophy, e.g., the functions of government, the justification of political authority, the nature of democracy, the varieties of liberty, and social justice. Readings from classical and contemporary sources.

allCourses.description: Selected topics concerning legal systems and the concept of law, e.g., the nature and purpose of law, the nature of authority, the relationship between law and morality, law and political-economic systems.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Gender and Race

allCourses.title: The Scientific Revolution
allCourses.description: An examination of early modern European science from 1500-1700. Includes primary readings from central figures (Copernicus, Harvey, Bacon, Descartes, et al.); themes include the impact of printing, humanism, patronage, technology, and discussion of the term "revolution" in this context.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Science
allCourses.description: Selected topics in contemporary philosophy of science, e.g., the status of theoretical entities, the confirmation of theories, the nature of scientific explanation.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Geometry and Spacetime
allCourses.description: An examination of the foundations of the special theory of relativity, with emphasis on the geometry of Minkowski spacetime, and its relation to both Euclidean and non-Euclidean (hyperbolic) plane geometries.

allCourses.title: Probability and Determinism
allCourses.description: An examination of a cluster of interrelated issues concerning probability, determinism, logic, and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Social Science
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of the social sciences, e.g.: Is their goal to understand behavior or to predict and control it? Are they normative and the natural sciences not? Do they incorporate philosophical doctrines about language and mind?.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Language

allCourses.title: Well-Being
allCourses.description: Examines what it is that makes a life good (or bad) for the person who lives it. Topics include hedonism, desire-satisfaction theories of well-being (as well as other such theories), the notion of harm, the possibility of posthumous harm.

allCourses.title: Philosophy of Action
allCourses.description: Philosophy of action is specifically concerned with questions concerning the nature of acting, and related phenomena such as intending, willing, trying, and trusting. It deals both with individual and group action and their moral and epistemological  underpinnings.
