allCourses.description: The second course in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics and interconnections with the pharmacist patient care process. Topics include drug substances, dosage forms, and therapeutic effects. Includes laboratory.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmaceutics III
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The final course in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics,and interconnections with the Pharmacist Patient Care Process. In laboratory, students perform pharmacokinetic modeling, drug screening, and comprehensive therapeutic efficacy.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry I
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Application of organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, physical chemistry, pharmacology, and physiology to understand the theory and mechanics of modern day medicinal chemistry. Topics include receptor-protein structure, dynamics, and interactions; drug development and design; and pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry II
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Walks students through medicinal chemistry, broadly defined. Students utilize the knowledge gained in organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, physical chemistry, pharmacology and physiology in an integrated fashion as applied to modern medicinal chemistry. Continuation of Medicinal Chemistry I.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Scholarly Project I
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students an opportunity to develop independent thinking, with particular focus on maturing analytical skills. Students are encouraged to develop an independent project, with a mentor, to study pharmacy-related aspects of multiple areas. First phase identifies project focus.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Scholarly Project II
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students an opportunity to develop independent thinking, with particular focus on maturing analytical skills. Students develop an independent project, with a mentor, to study pharmacy-related aspects of multiple areas. Phase 2 focuses on final evaluation of project.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Doctor of Pharmacy Epilogue
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reinforces and assesses student pharmacist’s performance on cumulative learning outcomes; pre-APPE and APPE knowledge, skills, and attitudes; entrustable professional activities; team- and practice-readiness; and to demonstrate that student pharmacists are achieving outcomes required by the ACPE.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to engage students and expose them to seminar speakers that come to discuss research or case studies in pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: New Student Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors only. New students only.
allCourses.description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the Pharmaceutical Sciences major, campus resources, learning skills, and special programs and opportunities.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Physiology
allCourses.description: Covers the function of the human body. All major organ systems are discussed. Designed to prepare students for healthcare careers, such as medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, and for research careers which require basic knowledge of how the human body functions.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Physiology Lab
allCourses.description: Designed to complement PHRMSCI 120. Computer-based lab simulations are used to study the function of the human body. Class physically meet for review sessions and exams.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medical Microbiology Laboratory
allCourses.description: An introduction to the structure, metabolism, cultivation, isolation, classification, and identification of the major groups of bacteria. Additional focus on identification of infection and use of antibiotics in diseased patients.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51C. CHEM 51C with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Healthspan Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the complex and multi-factorial process of aging and increases the understanding of factors that contribute to enhanced lifespan, including basic principles of health and wellness and scientifically proven interventions, both pharmacological and non-pharmacological.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropsychopharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the nervous system. Fundamental knowledge for understanding the cellular and molecular actions of drugs and their mechanisms of action on synaptic transmission. Applied neuropsychopharmacology including major drug classes and therapeutic uses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 170A. PHRMSCI 170A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacogenomics and Epigenetics
allCourses.description: Survey of the genetic and epigenetic basis of inter-subject variability in response to drugs. Covers drug efficacy, safety, and need for their optimization in pharmacotherapy. Emphasizes genetic mechanisms of polymorphisms in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of representative therapeutic drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Pharmacology I
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Molecular basis of drug-receptor action at the molecular and cellular levels. Structure-function of drug targets emphasizing enzymes, ion channels, and membrane transport proteins. Understanding how the drugs' mechanisms of action contribute to the development of more efficacious and safer drugs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C) and (PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109)

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Pharmacology II
allCourses.description: Introductory survey covering the molecular mechanisms of drugs that target the nervous system, such as anxiolytics, antidepressants, antipsychotics, hypnotics, muscle relaxants, and recreational drugs; drugs related to the immune system, including antibiotics, antihistamines, and immunosuppressants; drugs used to treat cancer.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Physical Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Thermodynamics and kinetic fundamentals as applied to problems relevant to pharmaceutical sciences such as receptor/enzyme-ligand interactions. Fundamentals of biophysical methods used in the pharmaceutical sciences including structure determination and biomolecular spectroscopy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 AND PHYSICS 3C AND ( CHEM 1C OR CHEM H2C ) AND ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.description: Presents information about various fields of research, study, careers, and graduate school opportunities in pharmaceutical sciences. Taught by guest lecturers from various disciplines including 199 research course faculty. Helps Pharmaceutical Sciences students select electives appropriate to their future goals.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and (CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C)

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacotherapy
allCourses.description: An exploration of the clinical application of medications to selected disease states. Focus is on an understanding of underlying principles of pharmacology and how this knowledge can be applied to treatment of diseases.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biopharmaceutics and Nanomedicine
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces theories and tools of new drug formulations. Particularly new novel therapeutics based on biological materials, pathological characteristics utilized to achieve the maximum efficacy and specificity, and drug delivery systems based on emerging nanotechnology are extensively discussed.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biopharmaceutics and Nanomedicine Lab
allCourses.description: Introduction to cancer drug screening using cellular models, and confirmation of comprehensive therapeutic efficacy using a live animal model. Includes basic cell culture, cytotoxicity assays, cell analysis, drug circulation test, and tumor eradication and imaging experiments. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Drug Discovery Computing Techniques
allCourses.description: Techniques used in computer-aided drug discovery, including theory behind these techniques and practical applications. Topics include scientific computing; python; classical force fields and simulations; visualization and movie-making; quantum mechanics in drug discovery; molecular dynamics; solvation models; and several others.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CSE 41 or I&C SCI 31. CSE 42 or I&C SCI 32 is recommended.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction of the basics of drug activity and mechanisms. Strategies used to identify lead compounds such as natural product chemistry, combinatorial chemistry, molecular modeling, and high-through put screening.  Relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C and (BIO SCI 98 or CHEM 128)

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction of the basics of drug activity and mechanisms. Strategies used to identify lead compounds such as natural product chemistry, combinatorial chemistry, molecular modeling, and high-through put screening.  Relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activity. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 100 AND ( CHEM 128 OR BIO SCI 98 ) AND ( CHEM 177 OR PHRMSCI 177 ) AND ( CHEM 51C OR CHEM H52C ) AND LOWER DIVISION WRITING

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Emerging Technologies in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine
allCourses.description: Introduces emerging, ground-breaking technologies in pharmaceutical sciences and medicine, including pharmacogenomics, genome editing, and stem cell and engineered T cell therapies. Explores these novel technologies with both their underlying theories and forward-thinking applications.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Professional Internship
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with opportunity to develop leadership and professional skills necessary for competitive placement in their chosen industry. Students gain new and field-specific skills outside the classroom environment while participating in a supervised internship for a total of 100 hours.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Independent Study in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.description: Students interested in independent study should arrange with a faculty member to sponsor and supervise such work. A time commitment of three hours per week per unit is expected. A written report is required at the end of each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Undergraduate Research
allCourses.description: Original research in the laboratory of Pharmaceutical Sciences faculty. Attendance at regular research group meetings is also generally expected, and a quarterly written report is required. Strongly recommended for students considering research careers and/or graduate degree programs.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biological Macromolecules
allCourses.description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Application of pharmacological principles in disease therapy.  Advanced pharmacological mechanisms and in-depth study of drug action.  Discussion of several major drug classes/therapeutic strategies:  molecular mechanisms of action, physiological consequences of administration, and clinical use.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Math and Computational Biology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Math and Computational Biology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Math and Computational Biology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in pharmacological science. Molecular biology, quantitative and biochemical pharmacology, fluorescent probes, behavior, genetics, animal handling, anatomical and receptor binding analysis, methods for ion channel study, the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination of drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ligand-gated ion channels, G protein-coupled receptors, receptor tyrosine kinases, ligand-regulated transcription factors, their signaling mechanisms, trafficking, macromolecular complexes, and physiological responses.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and periphery. Molecular biology, signal transduction, transmitter synthesis, and inactivation of major neurotransmitter systems. Drugs that act on these major neurotransmitters.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Design for Pharmacologists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, experimental design, power, and the use of statistical computer software.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics in Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, handling of misconduct.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacogenomics and Epigenetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the genetic and epigenetic basis of inter-subject variability in response to drugs. Covers drug efficacy, safety, and the need for their optimization in pharmacotherapy.Emphasizes genetic mechanisms of polymorphisms in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of representative therapeutic drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: The RNA World: From Discovery to Mechanism
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of RNA in biology. Use of knowledge gained in organic chemistry, biochemistry, genomics, and molecular biology to understand how RNA is integrated into contemporary biology.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: New Frontiers in Chemical and Synthetic Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores new developments in chemical and synthetic biology that span the areas of chemistry, molecular biology, genetics, bioengineering, systems biology, and computational genomics.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a mechanism-based overview of pharmacology with strong emphasis on clinical application of pharmacology. Students learn the most recent advances in pharmacology as they relate to drug discovery, development, and clinical application.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reserved for current topics of particular interest in areas of pharmaceutical sciences that are not covered by other courses. The subject will vary from year to year, highlighting, for example, significant emerging fields or highly specialized but vital research areas.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Drug Discovery Computing Techniques
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Techniques used in computer-aided drug discovery, including theory behind these techniques and practical applications. Topics include scientific computing; python; classical force fields and simulations; visualization and movie-making; quantum mechanics in drug discovery; molecular dynamics; solvation models; and several others.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of medicinal chemistry covering diverse aspects of drug design, discovery, synthesis, and development. Molecular basis of drug action with an emphasis on the structure-to-function continuum.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Emerging Technologies in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine
allCourses.description: Introduces emerging, ground-breaking technologies in pharmaceutical sciences and medicine, including pharmacogenomics, genome editing, and stem cell and engineered T cell therapies. Explores these novel technologies with both their underlying theories and forward-thinking applications.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation and discussion of current problems and methods in teaching and research in pharmaceutical sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Graduate Research
allCourses.description: Supervised original research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Professional Development and Careers in the Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to help Pharmaceutical Science majors select a career track and prepare for graduate program applications and careers in industry.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Life 101
allCourses.description: Covers the latest scientific work on the impact of nutrition, exercise, and lifestyle choices on mental and physical health. Motivates students to make positive changes by fostering personal growth.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethical Conduct of Research
allCourses.description: Covers the ethical responsibilities of biomedical scientists. Topics include, as discussions and case studies, the high standards of science, the responsible conduct of research, animal experimentation, and clinical trials as they relate to the pharmaceutical sciences.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: The Art of Public Speaking
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students learn to effectively prepare and present public speeches and slide presentations. Included are storytelling, informative, commemorative, and persuasive speeches, and scientific presentation. Evaluating speeches and strategies to reduce speaker apprehension is also covered.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Research in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.description: Undergraduate honors research in Pharmaceutical Sciences. A student time commitment of 10-15 hours per week is required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Drugs and Society
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Where drugs come from, how drugs work, how and why people abuse drugs, the costs of drug abuse on society, which drugs are commonly abused, and how drug abuse can be prevented and treated. Course intended for non-science majors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: High school chemistry and biology.

allCourses.title: California Teach 2: Middle School Science and Mathematics Teaching
allCourses.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Second in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies for grades 6-8. Includes supervised field experience in a middle school classroom.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PHY SCI 5 OR BIO SCI 14 ) AND NO REPEATS ALLOWED

allCourses.title: Technical Writing and Communication Skills
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Physical Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Workshop in writing technical reports, journal articles, proposals. Oral presentations. Communicating with the public. May not be used in satisfaction of any School or departmental requirement.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Science Communication Skills
allCourses.description: Development of effective communication skills, oral and written presentations. Topics range from the art of creating keynote slides to strategically crafting a personal story, culminating in a live presentation to an invited audience.

allCourses.title: California Teach 1: Introduction to Science and Mathematics Teaching
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Physical Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies. Includes supervised field experience in a K-12 classroom.

allCourses.title: Skills Development
allCourses.restriction: School of Physical Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Undergraduates identify, cultivate, and practice relevant soft skills applicable to careers in mathematics and science. The focus is on career readiness, how to market oneself to future employers, and what to expect from the professional world.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Computation for Scientists and Engineers
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces principles, techniques, and computational tools for quantitative approach to basic problem solving in physics and engineering. Project-based course that actively explores how programing techniques are used for solving STEM real-world problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB or AP Calculus BC. AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 4. AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3

allCourses.title: Computational Methods
allCourses.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2E AND ( MATH 3A OR MATH H3A )

allCourses.title: Advanced Data Acquisition, Analysis, and Scientific Writing
allCourses.description: Introduces modern practical laboratory techniques for developing data interface devices, acquiring and analyzing data, and writing up results in manuscript format. Experiments include interfacing with instruments through software and hardware development, PID controller, Fourier analysis, and lock-in amplifier.

allCourses.title: Classical Mechanics
allCourses.description: One-dimensional motion and oscillations; three-dimensional motion, non-inertial coordinates, conservation laws, and Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics; rigid body motion and relativity.

allCourses.title: Classical Mechanics
allCourses.description: One-dimensional motion and oscillations; three-dimensional motion, non-inertial coordinates, conservation laws, and Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics; rigid body motion and relativity.

allCourses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
allCourses.description: Electric, magnetic, and gravitational fields and potentials; electrodynamics; mechanical and electromagnetic waves and radiation.

allCourses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
allCourses.description: Electric, magnetic, and gravitational fields and potentials; electrodynamics; mechanical and electromagnetic waves and radiation.

allCourses.title: Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: The wave function and its interpretation; time independent and time dependent Schrödinger equation; Hilbert space and the uncertainty principle; systems in one to three dimensions; the hydrogen atom, angular momentum and spin.

allCourses.title: Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: Identical particles in quantum systems; atoms and the periodic table; theories of solids; time-independent perturbation theory; fine structure of hydrogen, the Zeeman effect and hyperfine structure; the variational principle; the WKB approximation and tunneling.

allCourses.title: Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: Symmetries and conservation laws in quantum mechanics; degeneracy; quantum dynamics and selection rules; scattering theory; time-dependent perturbation theory; emission and absorption of radiation; Fermi's golden rule; selected contemporary topics.

allCourses.title: Statistical Physics
allCourses.description: Microscopic theory of temperature, heat, and entropy; kinetic theory; multicomponent systems; quantum statistics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 50 and (PHYSICS 60 or CHEM 1C or ENGRMAE 91)

allCourses.title: Relativity and Black Holes
allCourses.description: Introduces students to both special and general relativity; includes the formalism of four-vectors, equivalence principle, curved space-time, and modern issues with black holes.

allCourses.title: Science Fiction and Science Fact
allCourses.description: An introduction to fundamental physics principles, the scientific process, and the mathematical language of science, used to analyze topics drawn from superheroes, science fiction works, and current science news to distinguish science fiction and science fact.

allCourses.title: Electronics for Scientists
allCourses.description: Applications of modern semiconductor devices to physical instrumentation. Characteristics of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, analog and digital circuits. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Advanced Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Physics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Experiments in atomic, condensed matter, nuclear, particle, and plasma physics. Introduction to instrumentation and a first experience in the research laboratory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PHYSICS 51B or PHYSICS 61B or PHYSICS 61C) and (PHYSICS 52C or PHYSICS 193) and (PHYSICS 194 or EDUC 143BW)
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Physics
allCourses.description: Complex variables; Legendre and Bessel functions; complete sets of orthogonal functions; partial differential equations; integral equations; calculus of variations; coordinate transformations; special functions and series.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Physics
allCourses.description: Complex variables; Legendre and Bessel functions; complete sets of orthogonal functions; partial differential equations; integral equations; calculus of variations; coordinate transformations; special functions and series.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics
allCourses.description: Phenomena of solids and their interpretation in terms of quantum theory.

allCourses.title: Physical and Geometrical Optics
allCourses.description: Focuses on the practical aspects of optics and optical engineering, starting at the fundamentals. Topics include geometrical optics, ray tracing, polarization optics, interferometers, and diffractive optics.

allCourses.title: Plasma Physics
allCourses.description: Basic concepts, orbits, kinetic and fluid equations, Coulomb collisions, fluctuations, scattering, radiation.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Particle Physics
allCourses.description: Experimental techniques and theoretical concepts of high-energy phenomena: accelerators and detectors; classification of particles and interactions; particle properties; symmetries and mass multiplets; production and decay mechanisms.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cosmology
allCourses.description: Solution of the differential equations governing the expansion of the Universe. Observational determinations of the parameters governing the expansion. Big Bang inflation, primordial nucleosynthesis, and cosmic microwave background. Dark matter, dark energy, and large-scale structure of the Universe.

allCourses.title: Astrophysics of Galaxies
allCourses.description: Introduction to the solar neighborhood, Milky Way, and other galaxies. Interstellar medium. Star formation. Stellar populations. Evolution of spiral, elliptical, and irregular galaxies. Supermassive black holes, quasars, and active galaxies. Galaxies as probes of the expansion rate of the Universe.

allCourses.title: Observational Astrophysics
allCourses.description: Telescopes and astronomical observations, imaging with CCD detectors and image processing techniques. Photometry and spectroscopy of stars, galaxies, and quasars. Advanced imaging techniques such as deconvolution, adaptive optics, and interferometry.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 194 AND PHYSICS 52A AND PHYSICS 52B AND PHYSICS 52C AND ( EECS 12 OR PHYSICS 53 OR I&C SCI 45C )

allCourses.title: Energy and the Environment
allCourses.description: The physics of society’s energy production and consumption, and of their influences on the environment. Topics include fossil and renewable energy resources; nuclear power; prospects for a hydrogen economy; efficient and environmentally benign transportation; efficient home and commercial energy usage.

allCourses.title: Stellar Astrophysics
allCourses.description: Stars: their structure and evolution; physical state of the interior; the Hertzprung- Russell diagram, stellar classification, and physical principles responsible for the classification; star formation; nuclear burning; giant and dwarf stars; neutron stars and black holes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PHYSICS 51A or PHYSICS 61A) and PHYSICS 111A and PHYSICS 112A

allCourses.title: High-Energy Astrophysics
allCourses.description: Production of radiation by high-energy particles, white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. Evolution of galactic nuclei, radio galaxies, quasars, and pulsars.  Cosmic rays and the cosmic background radiation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PHYSICS 51A or PHYSICS 61A) and PHYSICS 111A and PHYSICS 112A

allCourses.title: Biophysics of Molecules and Molecular Machines
allCourses.description: Physical concepts and experimental and computational techniques used to study the structure and function of biological molecules and molecular machines with examples from enzyme action, protein folding, molecular motors, photobiology, chemotaxis, and vision.

allCourses.title: Biophysics of Molecules and Molecular Machines
