allCourses.restriction: Physics Majors only. Campuswide Honors Collegium students only. Honors Program in Physics students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis in Physics II
allCourses.restriction: Physics Majors only. Campuswide Honors Collegium students only. Honors Program in Physics students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis in Physics III
allCourses.restriction: Physics Majors only. Campuswide Honors Collegium students only. Honors Program in Physics students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research for seniors conducted under the guidance of a faculty member. Students’ research results are discussed in oral presentations, and a written proposal, progress report, and thesis are submitted.

allCourses.title: Impact of World War I on Science
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to science in 1914 and WWI. Participants in groups of two or three will pick a preferred science; find out what happened to it during and after the war; write reports and present what they learned.

allCourses.title: The Idiom and Practice of Science
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: A series of fundamental and applied scientific problems of social relevance. Possible topics include Newton's Law, calculus, earthquake physics, and radiation.

allCourses.title: Research in Physiology and Biophysics
allCourses.description: Individual research directed toward doctoral dissertation and supervised by a particular professor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Research in Physiology and Biophysics for First-Year Students
allCourses.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Physiology and Biophysics for first-year Ph.D. students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Physiology Research
allCourses.description: Introduction to research in physiology and related sciences. Concentrates on techniques emphasized in the various laboratories of the Department of Physiology and Biophysics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Concepts of Biophysics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of crystallography; introduction to time-resolved absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy; the concepts of kinetic order and kinetic rate theory.

allCourses.title: Electronics for Biologists
allCourses.description: Basic principles of electricity; properties and use of discrete components and integrated circuits; circuit analysis and design. Intended for advanced students in the life sciences.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Vertebrate physiology with emphasis on humans and on the relationship between the function of normal tissues and the processes of disease. Fundamental principles of physiology and the interrelationships which control organ function.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Vertebrate physiology with emphasis on humans and on the relationship between the function of normal tissues and the processes of disease. Fundamental principles of physiology and the interrelationships which control organ function.

allCourses.title: Approaches in Circuit Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces modern methods in circuit neuroscience and how they are used to explore questions relating to the neurological basis of animal behavior. Emphasis is on rodent models but other model systems are incorporated where relevant.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Medical Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: One of the cornerstones of the MS1 Molecular Basis of Medicine block. Includes temporal coordination of lecture material, regular course director meetings, and combined exams with PHYSIO 544: Medical Immunology.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to immunology, but focuses on providing in-depth analysis of selected topics within the broader field of immunology, including relevant research techniques, while improving critical thinking skills.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology.  Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 215. PHYSIO 215 with a grade of B+ or better

allCourses.title: The Physiology of Ion Channels
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses how ion channels work (molecular/structural biophysics level) and what ion channels do in diverse cell types (cell physiology level).

allCourses.title: Introduction to Proteomics
allCourses.description: Introduces students to concepts and methods of proteomics including protein identification, expression proteomics, and protein-protein interactions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Eye: Health and Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the anatomic and physiological basis of vertebrate vision and disease states in which the structure and function of the eye is disrupted with emphasis on current and developing research areas.

allCourses.title: Topics in Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Contemporary research problems in physiology. Students review research articles in current literature and present ideas contained therein, focusing on groundbreaking discoveries and methodologies. Students present results of their own research and attend presentations given by other students and departmental researchers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Dissertation in Physiology and Biophysics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Preparation and completion of the dissertation required for the Ph.D.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Political Science I
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the variety of statistical applications in the social sciences.  Descriptive statistics.  Measures of central tendency and dispersion.  Percentile ranks.  Standardization and normal approximation.  Basic probability theory focuses on application to statistical inference and binomial distribution.  Laboratory required.
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10A, ECON 15A, PSYCH 10A, SOCECOL 13, SOC SCI 9A, SOCIOL 10A.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Political Science II
allCourses.description: Introduction to statistical inference, sampling distribution, standard error.  Hypothesis tests for proportions and means. Inferential techniques for nominal variables including chi-square, study measures of strengths, significance of relationships between variables, assumptions, data requirements, and types of error in significance tests.
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10B, ECON 15B, PSYCH 10B, SOCECOL 13, SOC SCI 9B, SOC SCI 10B.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Political Science III
allCourses.description: Focus on correlation, regression, and control for effects of variables.  One-way and two-way factorial analysis of variance.  A priori and a posteriori comparisons.  Introduction to repeated measures design and non-parametric statistics. Discusses use of statistics in newspapers and popular magazines.
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10C, PSYCH 10C, SOCECOL 13, SOC SCI 9C, SOC SCI 10C, SOCIOL 10C.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Political Analysis
allCourses.description: Presents various modes of understanding politics. Emphasis on basic approaches to political analysis, their uses in constructing theories, and their application to particular national political systems.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Micropolitics
allCourses.description: Introduction to political behavior of individuals and groups within national systems. Three questions addressed: How do individuals come to understand the political world? How do individuals behave within this world? How do groups and individuals engage in the political process.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theories concerning sources of public opinion, processes by which it is altered, organization of citizens’ belief systems, and role of public opinion in government policy. Students analyze survey data as a research project.

allCourses.title: The American Presidency
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents a comprehensive survey of the American presidency and considers the question of political power.

allCourses.title: U.S. Elections and Voting Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines how voters evaluate political parties, candidates, and issues in electoral campaigns to reach their decisions. Numerous controversies concerning the degree of issue voting, sophistication of candidate evaluations, and the decline of political parties are discussed.

allCourses.title: Presidents Since World War II
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Reviews the actions and character of presidents from Harry Truman through Bill Clinton.  Each week a different president is examined from a variety of perspectives.  Students are expected to write a substantial original research paper.

allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.title: Writing for the President of the United States
allCourses.description: Imagines how White House staffers can help presidents with clear, focused, and effective writing. Through a variety of formats, students study, hone, and practice writing skills that will prove useful in and out of the White House.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 21A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: American Metropolitan Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the politics of urban and suburban America, including the policy making process; the exercise of political power; local politics, federalism and the problems of metropolitanism; and major policy problems facing urban areas.

allCourses.title: California Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the structure and function of California government, traces historical development of political power, with constantly changing casts of power-brokers and seekers. Explores California exceptionalism and the roles played by the electorate, legislature, executive, and organized interests in policy making.

allCourses.title: California Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the structure and function of California government, traces historical development of political power, with constantly changing casts of power-brokers and seekers. Explores California exceptionalism and the roles played by the electorate, legislature, executive, and organized interests in policy making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Representation
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Deals with classical theories of representation: issues of racial and political representation in U.S. legislatures and city councils; proportional representation models; and comparative election systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI 3A or SOC SCI 10A or SOC SCI 10B

allCourses.title: The Politics of Protest
allCourses.description: Examines the Civil Rights, Black Power, and women’s movements in relationship to the Asian American movement. Uses social movement theories to illuminate the cases, and the cases to critique and revise the theories.

allCourses.title: Latinos in U.S. Politics
allCourses.description: Comparing the political issues facing Latino groups by examining their migration histories, voting behavior, nonelectoral participation, and policy issues.  Latino issues are examined on the national, state, and local levels, including formal representation, immigration, affirmative action, and language policy.

allCourses.title: Comparative Minority Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the political experiences of Blacks, Latinos, and Asian Americans in the United States from roughly 1950 to the present. Focuses on how each group has pursued political empowerment via both conventional political channels and social movements.

allCourses.title: African American Politics
allCourses.description: Examines politics of African Americans in order to gain a broader perspective of the American political process. Major developments in African American politics (including the civil rights movement, Black presidential bids), continuing problem of racism, responsiveness of key governing institutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 61A AND NO POL SCI 129

allCourses.title: The United States Congress
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Does the Congress do a good job of representing the American citizenry? Is it the most appropriate mechanism for the creation, resolution, and implementation of public policy.

allCourses.title: Constitutional Convention
allCourses.description: Analyzes the Constitution, its amendments, and periods of Constitutional reform as a foundation for a critical evaluation of the Constitution with an eye both to necessary reforms and to elements of the Constitution that should be maintained.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 21A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: U.S. Immigration Policy
allCourses.description: Examines selected immigration policy debates since the nineteenth century, rationale and consequences of immigration law since 1965, problems of administration, implementation and enforcement, impact of immigration policy on foreign relations, and contemporary debate regarding the future of U.S. policy.

allCourses.title: Urban Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines economic limits of cities and welfare policy. Addresses such issues as why are the poor concentrated in the central cities? Which anti-poverty programs will work best in cities? Which level of government can best combat poverty in the U.S.

allCourses.title: Politics of Animal Rights
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Asian American Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines animal rights/welfare movement’s efforts to transform moral, practical, and legal standing of nonhuman animals in contemporary U.S. Explores intersection of racism, sexism, and speciesism informed by theories of race and ethnicity, including Asian American Studies.

allCourses.title: Sex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll: The Politics of Prohibition
allCourses.description: Why and how does the U.S. government prohibit, regulate, or try to control sex, drugs, and rock and roll? Reveals the motivations and politically strategic decisions that underpin these governmental efforts.

allCourses.title: Political Ideologies: The Way We View Our World
allCourses.description: Politics has become divisive and ideological. But ideologies are poorly understood and have become mere labels for identifying friends and enemies. Course analyzes the nature of ideology, focusing on liberalism, conservatism, fascism, socialism, and contemporary "liberation" ideologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Political Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Majors only. POL SCI 128C may not be taken for credit if taken after POL SCI 137C.
allCourses.description: Examination of how psychological theory and research may be used to better understand political thought and behavior. Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses such topics as the formation of political attitudes, and the process of political decision-making.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in American Politics and Society
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of American politics and society. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics I
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics II
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: More advanced game theory and its political applications, beginning where Game Theory and Politics I ends.  Examples of topics covered include revolutions; arms race; spatial models of party competition; political manipulation; political coalitions and their power.

allCourses.title: Modern Political Theory
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines major thinkers and intellectual movements in the political thought of the 17th and 18th centuries.

allCourses.title: 20th Century Political Theory
allCourses.description: Examines major thinkers and intellectual movements in the political thought of the 20th century.

allCourses.title: Social and Political Theory
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focus is on recent major work in social and political theory. An in-depth analysis of a relatively small body of writing. Authors discussed include Jurgen Habermas, Anthony Giddens, and Richard Rorty.

allCourses.title: Origins of Liberalism
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the ideals, social forces, and historical events that gave rise to liberal political theory. Topics include patriarchal authority, the divine right of kings, religious toleration, slavery, colonialism, political economy, the evolution of law, and tensions between liberty and equality.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( POL SCI 6B OR POL SCI 6C OR POL SCI 31A )

allCourses.title: Just War Revisited
allCourses.description: Examines the evolution of the doctrine of the just war across the history of Western political thought, the importance of changes in the doctrine and whether it applies today; examines international relations case studies to determine today's relevancy.

allCourses.title: Cannibals and Conquistadores: The Philosophy of the Other
allCourses.description: Examines critically the notion of the "other" by looking at the philosophical challenges difference poses in the context of the European discovery of the New World. Seeks to understand the naissance of the concept of human rights and tolerance.

allCourses.title: Cannibals and Conquistadores: The Philosophy of the Other
allCourses.description: Examines critically the notion of the "other" by looking at the philosophical challenges difference poses in the context of the European discovery of the New World. Seeks to understand the naissance of the concept of human rights and tolerance.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: France and You: Trans-Atlantic Problems and Partnerships - Past, Present, Future
allCourses.description: Co-taught by professors from UC and Sciences Po, French and UCI students are brought together in a virtual classroom. Students engage in joint projects on issues of global import: democratic fragility, race relations, international security, and climate change.

allCourses.title: Types of Political Representation
allCourses.restriction: Recommended: Upper-Division students. Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Political representation plays an important role in democratic systems, but is elusive once examined closely.  Students delve into the concept and relate different views to political life. Half of the course is spent on writing instruction.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The Moral of the Story: Introductory Seminar in Ethics
allCourses.description: Introduces major theories and classic texts in ethics, from Plato and Aristotelian virtue ethics to utilitarianism and Kant and contemporary moral psychology.

allCourses.title: Moral of the Story: Introduction to Ethics
allCourses.description: Focuses on how we learn about ethics from stories, in the form of fables, bedtime stories, religious stories, soap operas, television, and movies as adults. Students bring in stories that informed their own ethical development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Ethics of Difference
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines differences traditionally judged politically salient—race, ethnicity, religion, gender. Personal interviews with an elderly person encourage students to understand the social construction of difference and to reexamine their own attitudes by putting themselves in the place of another.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The Moral Life During War
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Can people keep their humanity during war? What does the term humanity signify when simply surviving requires faith, courage, and desperation? When facing wartime brutality, must we abrogate morality? What does it mean to compose a moral life during war?.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Political Theory and Methods
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of political theory and methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: International Political Economy
allCourses.description: Examination of problems in global political-economic relations through competing conceptual lenses or grand theories: mercantilism, liberalism, and Marxism. Surveys North-North and North-South issues relating power and wealth.

allCourses.title: International Political Economy of East Asia
allCourses.description: Integration of theoretical perspectives in international political economy with the study of economic development in East Asia, with special emphasis on regional integration.

allCourses.title: US Foreign Policy Toward Asia
allCourses.description: U.S. policy toward the countries of East Asia: bilateral and regional security relationships, U.S. economic relations with the major Asian countries, the development of regional institutions, and human rights.

allCourses.title: The International Relations of East Asia
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys various aspects of relations between the nations of East Asia. Topics include the historical development of the region; current political and security relations, including the impact of the American military presence.

allCourses.title: U.S. Foreign Policy I: Globalism and Cold War
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Looks at changing international perspectives, policy responses, and military strategies of presidential administrations from Truman to Reagan. In assessing the motives and objectives of U.S. foreign policy leaders during the “Cold War” era, the concept of “national interest” is examined.

allCourses.title: US Coercive Diplomacy
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the theory of compellence and the U.S. practice of coercive diplomacy - the power to change behavior of other governments. Specific case examples: the Cuban missile crisis, bombing of North Vietnam, the Nicaraguan Contras, Desert Shield/Desert Storm, and Libya.

allCourses.title: Human Rights and Foreign Policy
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analyzes theories, patterns, and cases of human rights foreign policy. How do countries pursue the values and standards of human rights in their foreign relations. How does the U.S. fit into worldwide trends? Examines historical and contemporary cases.

allCourses.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

allCourses.title: East Asian Security
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of issues in East Asian security including U.S.-China relations, economic interdependence, global supply chains, South China Sea, environmental cooperation, COVID-19, and others. Includes Oxford-style debates.

allCourses.title: Homeland Security
allCourses.description: Examines the 9/11 origins of the concept of homeland security; assess the evolution, structure, and operations of the Department of Homeland Security; critically examines the evolution of threat assessment to the U.S. and the utilization of risk management methodologies.

allCourses.title: Approaches to International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Reviews theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of international relations using contending perspectives to analyze power and influence, capabilities, interdependence, reciprocity, international regimes, anarchy, cooperation, imperialism, and hegemony.

allCourses.title: Ethics in an Age of Terror and Genocide
allCourses.description: Original sources document personal impact of wars on genocides, from World War II to the Bosnian and Rwandan genocides and current wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. Students train for and conduct personal interviews with someone who lived through a war.

allCourses.title: Religion and World Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between religion and world politics historically and today, focusing on connections with peace/war, democracy, human rights, secularism(s), and globalization. Covers major debates, scholarship, concepts, and theories through class exercises, exams, and essays.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"OR":["INTL ST 11","INTL ST 12","REL STD 5A","REL STD 5B","REL STD 5C","POL SCI 41A"]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 41A or INTL ST 11 or INTL ST 12 or REL STD 5A or REL STD 5B or REL STD 5C

allCourses.title: International Humanitarianism
allCourses.description: Examines, analyzes, and evaluates the humanitarian phenomenon, the actors involved in it (including states, international organizations (IOs), and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)), the rise of a body of international humanitarian law, and the problems and debates associated with international humanitarianism today.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: International Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Active learning course that examines origins, decision-making processes, activities, and evolution of leading international organizations (e.g. U.N., NATO, EU, AU, WTO, World Bank, IMF). Activities include drafting reforms, applying theory, assessing dysfunctions, and participating in U.N. negotiation simulations.

allCourses.title: Critical Investigations into Humanitarianism in Africa
allCourses.description: Explores the complex phenomenon of aid to Africa (emergency and development aid), and the representational, cultural, historical, and other reasons why some participants and many observers critique it. Students occasionally engage with peers and faculty in African institutions.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Political Power in Contemporary China
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analyzes the sources of political power in contemporary China, including historical legitimacy, political institutions, and Chinese Communist Party power. Identifies challenges to the CCP’s rule and rising socio-political issues such as mass protest, censorship, and the environment.

allCourses.title: Chinese Politics: Policy, Leadership, and Change
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines major policies from 1949 to the present, and considers the changing role of the Communist Party and its shifting treatment of various social groups; the era of Mao Zedong, reforms under Deng, and post-Deng politics.

allCourses.title: Voting and Political Manipulation
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

allCourses.title: West European Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores four main themes: (1) thinking scientifically about politics; (2) understanding the linkages between different political structures and spheres of activity; (3) evaluating some theories about politics; (4) learning about three countries: Britain, France, and Germany.

allCourses.title: Immigration Politics in Western Europe
allCourses.description: Examines immigration politics in Western Europe, analyzing trends and policy from the postwar period through to today. Topics include citizenship, immigrant integration, asylum, the far-right, and a rotating focus on contemporary issues, e.g., terrorism, Islamophobia.

allCourses.title: Canadian Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses the basic structures and processes of contemporary Canadian government and politics. Additional topics may include regionalism, federalism, western alienation and oil, Canadian solutions to social welfare policy questions, developments in Quebec, and other issues associated with French-English relations.

allCourses.title: Human Rights
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the causes and consequences of human rights violations with a focus on Latin America. What are human rights? When and where are they violated? What political mechanisms are available to deal with human rights problems? How effective are they.

allCourses.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
allCourses.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

allCourses.title: Comparative Politics: Four Nations, Three Continents
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies four countries in a comparative fashion: their respective political histories and cultural traditions; actual differences among their superficially similar party, parliamentary, and executive institutions; contemporary economic policy. The countries represent three continents and varying levels of economic development.

allCourses.title: Peoples and Cultures of Post-Soviet Eurasia
allCourses.description: Examines the cultures and political conflicts of the more than 130 indigenous ethnic groups in the European and Asian territories of the former U.S.S.R. Emphasis is on the theoretical issues of ethnicity, nationalism, and conflict management.

allCourses.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
allCourses.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

allCourses.title: Jews and Power
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority.

allCourses.title: US Government in Comparative Perspective
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the United States in comparative perspective, covering general features of the United States and other countries, such as institutional design and policy choices. Addresses the debates about American exceptionalism and American decline.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: How bureaucracies, formal organizations, and voluntary associations work, how/why they grow, and where they are going. History and structure of organizational rationality; dynamics of organized groups; behavior in organizations; limits of bureaucratization and attempts to overcome these limits through decentralization.

allCourses.title: Political Participation
allCourses.description: The ways in which people in various political systems take part in politics, especially in activities directed toward affecting outcomes.  Who is active, what they do, why they do it, and what difference it makes.

allCourses.title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1

allCourses.title: International Divided Cities
allCourses.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
allCourses.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of comparative politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Race and Ethnicity Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of race and ethnicity. Topics vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Law and its various roles in society. The nature and meaning of law; legality and power in the American system; law as a mechanism for social change; the role of law in dispute processing, social control, compliance with judicial decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Comparative Constitutional Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the impact of constitutional courts on politics and policy-making in Canada, France, Germany, and the United States. Cases may focus on the constitutional politics of free speech, abortion, rights to property, and the conduct of foreign relations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: American Constitutional Law
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: American constitutional interpretation of cases involving separation of powers, federal-state relations, rights of property, free expression, privacy, criminal due process, political participation, and equality. Includes legal research methods, development of judicial review, legal reasoning, and impact of Supreme Court decisions.

allCourses.title: Law in the Twenty-First Century
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the complex relationship between law, the social sciences, and modern society.  Lectures explore such issues as the interplay between technology and constitutional rights, the impact of science on law, and the evolving roles of attorneys and judges.

allCourses.title: Legal Implications of the Drug Trade
allCourses.description: Examines United States policy to combat domestic and international narcotics trafficking. Analyzes the national drug policy and program implementation by federal and state agencies. Considers the effects of these policies on our individual constitutional rights and the criminal justice system.

allCourses.title: International Law
allCourses.description: Examination of the origin, changing structure, application of international law, and the role of legal norms in regulating the behavior of states and maintaining international order.

allCourses.title: Civil Liberties
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Political analysis of selected Supreme Court cases involving claims under the Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment. Topics include:  race, sex, and other forms of discrimination; criminal justice; privacy; freedom of speech and related claims.

allCourses.title: U.S. Supreme Court
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview and analysis of the role played by the U.S. Supreme Court in the American political system. Judicial review, appointment of justices, judicial activism and judicial restraint, process of case selection, court deliberation, land decision-making, impact of Supreme Court decisions.

allCourses.title: U.S. Supreme Court
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview and analysis of the role played by the U.S. Supreme Court in the American political system. Judicial review, appointment of justices, judicial activism and judicial restraint, process of case selection, court deliberation, land decision-making, impact of Supreme Court decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The Bill of Rights in Film
allCourses.description: Focuses on ways American cinema has portrayed, represented, and analyzed U.S. Bills of Rights. Juxtaposes cinematic presentations on specific Bill of Rights clauses, treating films as cultural texts, with pertinent judicial decisions and more scholarly appraisals of those same provisions.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Public Law
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of public law. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Senior Thesis
allCourses.description: Thesis research with Political Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.description: Thesis research with Political Science faculty.

allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.description: Field study with Political Science faculty.

allCourses.description: Directed group study with Political Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Independent study or research with a Political Science faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. POL SCI 209A may not be taken for credit if taken after SOCIOL 229.
allCourses.description: Skills critical to professional success. Students learn and practice professional presentation skills, develop substantive knowledge in the field by attending talks and panels, and interact with scholars and professionals in the field.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. POL SCI 209B may not be taken for credit if taken after SOCIOL 229 Democracy.
allCourses.description: This colloquium teaches students skills critical to professional success. Students learn and practice professional presentation skills and develop substantive knowledge in the field by attending talks and panels and interacting with scholars and professionals in the field.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. POL SCI 209C may not be taken for credit if taken after SOCIOL 229 Democracy.
allCourses.description: This colloquium teaches students skills critical to professional success. Students learn and practice professional presentation skills and develop substantive knowledge in the field by attending talks and panels and interacting with scholars and professionals in the field.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and discussions regarding research with departmental faculty.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This year-long workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and casual conversations with departmental faculty.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This year-long workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and casual conversations with departmental faculty.

allCourses.title: Colloquium
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This year-long workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and casual conversations with departmental faculty.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the study of U.S. public opinion. Provides an overview of the theories regarding opinion formation, the methodologies employed, and the role of public opinion in democratic governments.

allCourses.title: Ethics Workshop
allCourses.description: Students find an important question in ethics, search literature to assess topic's importance, post question to be researched, propose method of analysis and type of data, analyze data, and note how their works contribute to knowledge in the field.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Politics and Society
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in politics and society.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to American Government
allCourses.description: Introduction to American political processes and institutions. Topics include elections, political participation, parties, interest groups, the Presidency, Congress, the bureaucracy, and the judiciary.

allCourses.title: Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst.  Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the study of U.S. public opinion. Provides an overview of the theories regarding opinion formation, the methodologies employed, and the role of public opinion in democratic governments.

allCourses.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in American Politics
allCourses.description: Current research in American Politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Political Epistemology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on fundamental issues of knowledge in the study of politics, especially interconnections and tensions between politics and knowledge.  Counts as the Field Seminar in Political Theory.

allCourses.title: Theories of Textual Interpretation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examination of different theories of textual interpretation, including Straussian, hermeneutical, poststructuralist, feminist, postcolonial, and critical race theories. Key questions include: How does one go about the task of interpreting texts? What makes one interpretation better or more insightful than another.

allCourses.title: The Moral Life During War
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Can people keep their humanity during war? What does the term humanity signify when simply surviving requires faith, courage, and desperation? When facing wartime brutality must we abrogate morality? What does it mean to compose a moral life during war?.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Political Theory
allCourses.description: Current research in political theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar in International Relations Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of the major theories guiding research and scholarship in international relations.  Focus on major conceptual approaches (realism, neoliberalism, marxism) and levels of analysis (systemic, state, and subnational), as well as on methodological/epistemological debates engulfing the field.

allCourses.title: Research Design in International Relations
allCourses.description: Surveys research design primarily through substantive readings in international relations. The purpose is to familiarize students with choices/dilemmas relevant to IR-specific research. Students at various stages in the graduate program and with different methodological orientations are welcome.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Voting Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to voting models. Substantive topics include majority rule, voting methods and their properties, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

allCourses.title: Theories and Practice of Migration and Citizenship
allCourses.description: Examines theories of migration and citizenship. In examining these themes, the course includes discussion of theory development, multi-method testing, and case study comparison with a focus on Western Europe and other advanced democratic receiving states.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Game Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to non-cooperative games.  The prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, sequential games, subgame perfection. Applications include collective action, agenda-setter models, spatial competition of political parties, models of revolution and arms race.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in comparative politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Political Participation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theoretical approaches to the explanation of the pattern of participation and consideration of the results of empirical studies of such activity by mass publics (mainly in Europe and North America).  Addresses issues in both comparative politics and political behavior.

allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

allCourses.title: Predictive Models in Social Sciences
allCourses.description: Basic numeracy (logarithms, fixed-exponent and exponential formats, graphing). Models based on ignorance and logical constraints. Logical quantitative models (how things should be) to complement and guide statistical analysis (how things are).

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Psychology I
allCourses.description: Reviews theoretical questions regarding the relationship between the analytical and normative and the polity. Considers relationships between the analytical and normative concerns of psychology and political science, addressing empirical literatures on political socialization, ideology and public opinion, identity and nationality.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Political Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Independent research with Political Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Theory
allCourses.description: Types of questions:  What is politics?  What are the theoretical and philosophical bases for different types of political arrangements?  How do these perspectives get translated into reality?  Among others, the works of Rousseau, Locke, Mill, and Marx are read.

allCourses.title: Dilemmas of Diversity
allCourses.description: Focuses on racial, ethnic, and gender diversity, multiculturalism, and their impact on our social and political ideals. Traces the sources of ideas about difference, equality, and toleration, and examines tensions that occur when forms of identity conflict with one another.

allCourses.title: Introduction to International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of political relations between and among nations with emphasis on explanations of conflict and cooperation. The role of ideologies and their relation to international problems are also examined.

allCourses.title: Global Political Ideologies
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.

allCourses.title: Human Rights and Global Governance
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.

allCourses.title: Lower-Division Special Topics in International Relations
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Politics Around the World
allCourses.description: Introduces comparative politics. Compares political systems in a variety of countries. Includes elections, parties, parliaments, presidents, protest movements, and other aspects of national politics. Addresses how to make meaningful comparisons across countries.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnicity in Political Science
allCourses.description: Examines major theories that attempt to explain the roles of race and ethnicity in U.S. politics.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Law
allCourses.description: An introduction to the study of judicial politics.  Questions include:  what is law?; what is a court?; who are the judges? Analysis of a wide range of judicial decisions illustrates the political importance of courts in the U.S. and elsewhere.

allCourses.title: Honors Seminar in Political Science
allCourses.description: Course for students enrolled in the Honors Program in Political Science.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Only open to students in the Political Science Honors Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis Workshop
allCourses.restriction: Open only to students in the Political Science Senior Thesis program.
allCourses.description: A weekly seminar/workshop to facilitate the exchange of ideas and research strategies among students and to review their progress in writing the thesis.

allCourses.title: Globalization and Human Security
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Emerging issues of human security in the globalized world, including personal human security, physical integrity, human trafficking, global climate change, food. Challenges of these complex human security problems for a multi-scalar system (international, national, local).

allCourses.title: Topics in Luso-Brazilian Literature
allCourses.description: In English. Contextualized study of a major author, current, or genre in Brazilian, Portuguese, and/or Lusophone African literature. Examples: Gender, Race, and Sexualities in Postcolonial Lusophone Literatures; Women and Writing in Brazil and Portugal; The Short Story.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Luso-Brazilian Literature and Culture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critical analysis of selected literary works from Portugal and/or Brazil. Contextualizes the works within their historical and literary specificity, and discusses pertinent theoretical issues raised by them. Taught in Portuguese.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Course content varies with interest of instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Life Span Developmental Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses the major issues, concepts, and methods of life span developmental psychology. The fundamental theories, distinctive methods, and the physical, perceptual, cognitive, social, motivational, and emotional development for each developmental phase of the life course are considered.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B.

allCourses.title: Abnormal Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Survey of disorders organized by the diagnostic categories of the American Psychiatric Association. Interdisciplinary orientation combines environmental, psychological, and organic perspectives on etiology and treatment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9C) and SE 10.

allCourses.title: Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and research are considered as they contribute to an understanding of the role of psychological processes in health and illness. The distinction between prevention and treatment of illness is established, and a variety of psychosocial interventions are elaborated.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11C OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11C )

allCourses.title: Social Animal: An Introduction to Social Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theories and research exploring social behavior and social influences on behavior. Topics include methods of social research, attitude formation and change, social perception, the social self, stereotypes and prejudice, conformity, obedience, altruism, aggression, interpersonal relationships and love, and group behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11C OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11C )

allCourses.title: Infant Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of human development from conception through the first two years of life, covering processes and events in the domains of physical, social, and cognitive development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B.

allCourses.title: Child Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines social, emotional, and intellectual growth and development between the ages of 2 and 12 years.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11B OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11B ) AND ( PSYCH & SOC BEHAVIOR MAJORS ONLY OR PSYCHOLOGICAL SCI MAJORS ONLY OR SOCIAL ECOLOGY MAJORS ONLY OR PUB HEALTH POLICY MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.title: Advanced Research Methods
allCourses.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SE 10 and SE 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Adolescent Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines current research on the biological, social, and cultural contexts of adolescent development. Topics include the impacts of puberty, adolescents' decision-making competencies, changes in family and peer relationships, identity development, and psychosocial problems such as depression and problem behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B.

allCourses.title: Adult Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines why and how we change (with attention to gains as well as losses) from ages 18-65 and the nature and sources of continuity over time. Topics include physical and intellectual functioning, personality, coping strategies, and social roles and relationships.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines theories on nature of cognitive development. Discusses behaviorist theories on role of the environment including those of Vygotsky and Piaget, and recent evidence from cognitive psychologists stressing the importance of knowledge and skills within specific domains.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B.

allCourses.title: Human Development and Cross-Cultural Perspectives
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Human development in diverse cultures (e.g., Asian, American, and African). Special emphasis on East-West contrasts and when East meets West (i.e., Asian-American experiences). Topics include parenting, family relations, language and cognition, schooling and academic achievement, and morality.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B) and SE 10.

allCourses.title: The Psychology of Gender
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discussion of gender identity development and examination of gender differences and similarities across the life span. Consideration of the biology and psychology of gender in relation to physical, behavioral, personality, and intellectual capabilities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSCI 9 or PSYC 9B or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A

allCourses.title: Human Sexuality
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A broad survey of human sexuality encompassing genetic factors, physiological and anatomical development, customary and atypical forms of behavior, reproductive processes, and cultural determinants.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9B.

allCourses.title: Psychology Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. PSCI 9 and PSYCH 7A may not be taken for credit if taken after PSCI 11A, PSCI 11B, PSCI 11C, PSYCH 9A, PSYCH 9B, or PSYCH 9C.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide freshman with an in-depth survey of general psychology. Topics include biological bases of behavior, sensation, perception, cognition, development, personality, psychopathology, and social psychology.
