allCourses.description: Introduction to psychopathology and behavioral deviations, and the concepts of theories regarding these conditions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11C OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9C OR AP PSYCHOLOGY ) AND NO PSY BEH 102C AND NO PSCI 102C

allCourses.title: Developmental Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A general introduction to the study of the physical, intellectual, social, and emotional development of the child from birth to adulthood.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11A OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9A OR AP PSYCHOLOGY ) AND NO PSCI 111D

allCourses.title: History of Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A history of the development of various schools and systems of psychological thought.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9) or (PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A) and (PSYCH 9B or PSCI 11B) and (PSYCH 9C or PSCI 11C)

allCourses.title: Personality Theories
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of the evolution of personality theory during this century. An overview of major perspectives in the field, with special attention to Freud, Jung, and Adler.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9 or PSYCH 9C or PSCI 11C

allCourses.title: Theories of Motivation
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Factors affecting the behavioral performance of organisms. A survey of theoretical and empirical approaches to the physiological, psychological, and social factors which generate behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9) or (PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A) and (PSYCH 9B or PSCI 11B) and (PSYCH 9C or PSCI 11C)

allCourses.title: Psychology of Sleep and Consciousness
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the physiology, neurochemistry, and neuroanatomy associated with sleep, contemporary sleep theory, REM and NREM, phenomenology, sleep disorders, examination of differences between conscious and unconscious cognitive function, the history of sleep and dream theories from ancient time to present day.

allCourses.title: Clinical Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides overview of the clinical psychology field including theories and techniques used in counseling and testing.

allCourses.title: Organizational/Industrial Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to applied psychology in organizations, including personnel testing, selection, training and evaluation, job and classification analysis, job satisfaction and motivation, organizational development, leadership, market research, and consumer psychology. Potential ethical problems are discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9A OR PSYCH 9B OR PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11A OR PSY BEH 11B OR PSY BEH 11C OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: Clinical Psychophysiology
allCourses.description: Psychophysiology investigates the relationships between physiological processes and psychological phenomena. Technologies examined include reaction times, heart rate variability, EEGs, ERPs, magnetoencephalography, and eye tracking. Applications include diagnosis, the longitudinal assessment, and the identification of individuals at risk of disease onset.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Philosophy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of psychology, e.g., the nature of psychological explanation, reductionism, issues in cognitive, behavioral, and neuroscience.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Sports Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discusses the field of sports psychology with an emphasis on clinical practice including motivation, goal setting, performance skills, and mental skills. Discusses and utilizes a wide range of techniques designed to enhance performance and manage problems among athletes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11C OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: Psychology of Violence
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discusses the psychology of violence and aggression with an emphasis on understanding the psychological, social, and physiological roots of violent and aggressive behavior. Psychological treatment techniques and strategies for prevention of aggressive and violent behavior are also discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSY BEH 9) or (PSYCH 9C or PSY BEH 11C)

allCourses.title: Personality Disorders
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Psychology Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: The history of personality disorder classification; defining characteristics of each disorder; the causes, courses, and outcomes of personality disorders; and information regarding assessment, prevention, and treatments of these disorders.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in General Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of general psychology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Perception and Sensory Processes
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A general introduction to the scientific study of sensory processes and perceptual phonomena, with special emphasis in the visual systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9A OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11A OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: Vision
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.

allCourses.title: Hearing
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Auditory perception, the anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, and the physics of sound. Topics include neural transduction of sound, sensitivity, sound localization, complex sound perception, and hearing loss.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 11A OR PSYCH 9A OR PSY BEH 11A ) AND ( PSCI 11B OR PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 11B OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: The Mind/Body Problem
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: What is consciousness and what is matter and how are the two related? How can brains have minds? This multidisciplinary course draws on information from the fields of computer vision, artificial intelligence, cognition, neurophysiology, philosophy, and psychophysics.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Perception and Sensory Processes
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of perception and sensory processes. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Science
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the investigations of the structure and function of the mind, from viewpoints of computation, neuroscience, philosophy, and cognitive psychology. Topics include perception, attention, knowledge representations, learning and memory, action, reasoning, and language.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSY BEH 9 OR AP PSYCHOLOGY OR ( ( PSYCH 9A OR PSY BEH 11A ) AND ( PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 11B ) ) )

allCourses.title: Judgment and Decision Making
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The psychology of human decision making. Theories, models, experiments, and data that inform how people make choices, judgments, and other decisions. Topics include optimality and bias, mental simulation, learning and feedback, expertise, emotional effects, and group decision making.

allCourses.title: Principles of Learning Theory
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Investigation of the learning and memory processes of human and animals.  Basic experimental approaches to learning and memory, empirical results, and theoretical interpretations of the evidence are discussed.

allCourses.title: Human Memory
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Developments in the area of memory; history of memory research; theories of the nature of memory. Visual memory, recognition memory, high-speed scanning, free recall, short-term memory, mnemonics, retrieval, relationship of memory to thinking. Selected theoretical formulations for memory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11B OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: Human Problem Solving
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Modern developments in the psychology of human problem solving. Topics include concept identification, arithmetic, sets, logic puzzles, story problems, group problem solving, and theorem proving.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11B OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: Writing about Memory
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers a broad range of texts, literary, philosophical, and scientific, each probing the nature of memory and its meaning in human life. Readings are drawn from across many disciplines and many perspectives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11B OR AP PSYCHOLOGY ) AND LOWER DIVISION WRITING

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Cognition and Learning
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of cognition and learning. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 2B OR ECON 15B OR PSYCH 10C ) AND NO PSYCH 139 AND NO ECON 109
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: MATLAB Programming
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: MATLAB is a mathematical software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology. Topics include rudiments of programming, statistical analysis of data, matrix algebra, signal processing, graphic visualization, and simulated models of cognitive and perceptual processes.

allCourses.title: Scientific Python for Research
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces Python for data analysis and modeling encountered in cognitive science and neuroscience. Topics include data structures, execution control, graphic visualization, and interaction with sound and display interfaces. Application in statistical analysis, model simulation, and stimulus presentation and experimental control.

allCourses.title: Psychology of Language
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Language Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines language using the tools of experimental psychology. From sounds to words to spoken and written sentences, explores how language is used in real time, and how its use reveals how it is represented in the mind.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9 or PSYCH 9B or PSCI 11B or LSCI 3

allCourses.title: Acquisition of Language II
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on native language learning, exploring the way in which infants and very young children unconsciously uncover the rich systematic knowledge of their native language. Examines both experimental and computational studies that quantitatively investigate the "how" of language acquisition.

allCourses.title: Computational Methods for Language Research
allCourses.description: Focuses on computational methods useful for language research. Students become familiar with software and programming languages used for extracting information from electronic datasets and for creating basic simulations of linguistic cognition. No prior programming experience assumed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 150 or LSCI 155 or PSYCH 156A or LSCI 151

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Language
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of language sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the neural basis of human perceptual, motor, and cognitive abilities. Topics include sensory perception, motor control, memory, language, attention, emotion, frontal lobe function, functional brain imaging, and neuropsychological disorders.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 11B OR PSYCH 9B ) AND ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11A OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9A OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )

allCourses.title: Brain Disorders and Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9) or ((PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A) and (PSYCH 9B or PSCI 11B)) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

allCourses.title: History of Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies of the human mind from ancient cultures to the innovation of modern methods of brain imaging. Logic of valid and invalid brain hypothesis are examined. Recurring theme is the competition between holistic and localized views of brain function.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 9A or PSY BEH 11A or PSYCH 7A or PSY BEH 9

allCourses.title: Language and the Brain
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Research analysis on biological bases of human linguistic capacity. Development, focusing on hemispheric specialization, plasticity; localization of specific linguistic functions in adults, with emphasis on study of aphasias; relation of linguistic capacity to general cognitive capacity, considering research on retardation.

allCourses.title: Hearing and the Brain
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of brain mechanisms of hearing, including perception of simple sounds, speech, and music. Begins with sound itself, and looks at processing by the ear, auditory pathways, auditory cortex, and beyond. Also auditory development, learning, and clinical issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 160A or BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.title: Human  Neuropsychology
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of cognitive neuroscience. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSCI 11B OR PSYCH 9B ) AND ( PSCI 9 OR PSCI 11A OR PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9A OR AP PSYCHOLOGY )
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Psychological Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Cultural differences and similarities in personality and behavior.  Child-rearing practices and consequent adult personality characteristics, biocultural aspects of child development and attachment, culture and behavior evolutionary models, politically linked personality, cognitive anthropology, psychology of narrative forms, comparative national character studies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR ANTHRO 2A OR PSY BEH 9 OR AP PSYCHOLOGY OR ( ( PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 11C ) AND ( PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 11B ) AND ( PSYCH 9A OR PSY BEH 11A ) ) )

allCourses.title: African American Psychology
allCourses.description: Historical overview of the development of black psychology and the African American frame of reference. Topics include personality development, psychological assessment, issues in education, black mental health, and the role of the African American psychologist in the community.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latino Families
allCourses.description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

allCourses.title: Political Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Majors only. POL SCI 128C may not be taken for credit if taken after POL SCI 137C.
allCourses.description: Examination of how psychological theory and research may be used to better understand political thought and behavior. Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses such topics as the formation of political attitudes, and the process of political decision-making.

allCourses.title: Deviance
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.

allCourses.title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C) and PSCI 102C and (PSCI 178S or CRM/LAW C149)

allCourses.title: Social Psychology of Networks
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Review of network methods used in small group and organizational research. Discussion of social psychological literature relevant to the network of study of cognitive social structure, exchange/communication, identity negotiation, and social control. Case study of network datasets exemplifies research issues.

allCourses.description: Directed study with Cognitive Sciences faculty.

allCourses.description: Independent research with Cognitive Sciences faculty.

allCourses.description: Focuses on psychosocial dynamics of today's adolescents in America emphasizing the quest for identity, independence, values, and sexual orientation. The influence of society, family, school, and peers is analyzed. Strategies for helping troubled adolescents are discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR ( PSYCH 9A AND PSYCH 9B AND PSYCH 9C ) )

allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of psychology, e.g., the nature of psychological explanation, reductionism, issues in cognitive, behavioral, and neuroscience.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on computational models of native language learning, exploring how probabilistic learning and inference fare on difficult case studies within language acquisition. In all cases, grounds the learning models in available empirical data and considers their psychological plausibility.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: LSCI 251. LSCI 251 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Human Memory
allCourses.description: Covers the core concepts of modern research and theorizing about human memory, including structural subdivisions (e.g., perceptual memory, short-term memory, long-term memory), different measures of memory (e.g., recall, reorganization), and some practical applications of memory research (e.g., mnemonics).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 7A OR PSY BEH 9 OR ( ( PSYCH 9B OR PSY BEH 11B ) AND ( PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 11C ) AND ( PSYCH 9A OR PSY BEH 11A ) ) )

allCourses.title: Acquisition of Language
allCourses.description: What children say, what they mean, and what they understand. Theories about the learning of language by one-, two-, and three-year-olds. Comparison of kinds of data on which these theories are based.

allCourses.title: Self-Identity and Society
allCourses.description: Studies sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology, with focus on the social influences on personality, attitudes, beliefs, and behavior; socialization, human groups, and social interaction.

allCourses.description: Introduction to field of psychology, addressing the application of scientific methods to the study of human development, learning, memory, problem solving, perception, biological mechanisms, emotions and motivation, personality, psychopathology, and effects of diverse social and cultural contexts on human behavior.

allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Honors students only. Psychology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the research activities and honors thesis research projects of each student and the research of various Cognitive Sciences faculty. Students discuss their research interests in the early and later stages of their projects. Research projects and write-ups required.

allCourses.title: Honors Experimental Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology and Cognitive Sciences Honors Program students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasis on design of experiments and analysis of results. Experiments are conducted in laboratory sections.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND":[{"OR":["PSYCH 9C","PSY BEH 11C"]},{"OR":["ECON 15B","PSYCH 10C","ANTHRO 10C","SOCIOL 10C","POL SCI 10C","SOC SCI 10C",{"AND":[{"OR":["MATH 2B","AP CALCULUS BC"]},{"OR":["MATH 7","STATS 7","AP STATISTICS"]}]}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 11C ) AND ( ECON 15B OR PSYCH 10C OR ANTHRO 10C OR SOCIOL 10C OR POL SCI 10C OR SOC SCI 10C OR ( ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( MATH 7 OR STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS ) ) )

allCourses.title: Honors Advanced Experimental Psychology Laboratory
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of multivalent, factorial, and correlational studies. Students prepare proposals for independent research.

allCourses.title: Honors Research in Experimental Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors only. Social Science Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Each student conducts a research project in experimental psychology. The projects are discussed in a seminar format. Written reports on each project are submitted at the end of the quarter.

allCourses.title: Principles of Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the major concepts and principles of public health and the determinants of health status in communities. Emphasizes the ecological model that focuses on the linkages and relationships among multiple natural and social determinants affecting health.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
allCourses.description: Introduction to emerging topics in public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Course may be offered online when topic is Public Health in the Corporate World.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The distribution of disease and injury across time, space, and populations. Covers basic concepts and methods of descriptive epidemiology including the natural history of disease, data, and indices of health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( STATS 7 OR STATS 8 OR PUBHLTH 7 OR PUBHLTH 7A OR AP STATISTICS )

allCourses.title: Social Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overviews evidence linking environmental factors to mental and physical disorders including such variables as socioeconomic status, income inequality, work stress, job loss, social capital, location, and other demographic characteristics. Measurement and research design issues of both individual and aggregate levels.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 AND SOCECOL 13 AND ( PSYCH 7A OR PSYCH 9C OR PSY BEH 9 OR PSY BEH 11C )

allCourses.title: Introduction to Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.description: Broad overview of medical informatics for students with varied backgrounds. Electronic medical records, online resources, mobile technologies, patient safety, and computational design. Legal, ethical, and public policy issues. Health systems management. Evaluation and fieldwork for health systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( HUMAN 1C OR HUMAN H1C OR WRITING 30 OR WRITING 31 OR WRITING 60 OR WRITING 39C ) AND UPPER DIVISION STANDING ONLY AND ( NO REPEATS ALLOWED IF GRADE = C OR BETTER )

allCourses.title: Project in Health Informatics
allCourses.description: Students undertake significant quarter-long projects related to health informatics. Topics may include field evaluations of health care technologies, prototypes, iterative design, and system implementations.

allCourses.title: Epidemiology of Drug Use and Misuse
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Applies epidemiologic concepts to the use and misuse of licit/illicit substances. Emphasizes descriptive aspects of drug use and determinants of progressing from experimental use to misuse. Assesses subgroups of abusers, risk factors, trends, and surveillance techniques for estimating drug prevalence.

allCourses.title: Community, Social Justice, and Health Equity Research for Action
allCourses.description: Focuses on community as a unit of identity, community, well-being, and social justice perspectives and initiatives to promote community health. Addresses community change and improvements in community well-being, with a focus on health equity research for action.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 or PUBHLTH 2 or CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Epidemiology and Genetics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of epidemiology and genetics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Nutrition and Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Global issues related to nutrition and public health. Evaluation of nutritional risk factors associated with the development of chronic diseases and the role of nutritional medicine in prevention. Topics include food safety, communicable diseases, supplements, and regulatory issues.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Complementary and Alternative Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines health and disease in contemporary American culture/society with definitions, models, and practices of what has come to be known as "orthodox" or "conventional" medicine. Selected "alternative" or "complementary" modes of promoting health and well-being including homeopathy, herbology, and chiropractic.

allCourses.title: Health Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States.  What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care?  International comparisons will be made wherever possible.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Community Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Public Health Law: Fundamentals in Action
allCourses.description: Addresses the relationship of U.S. public health law to health systems at the individual and population levels. Examines legislative and judicial concepts and how they are applied to disease prevention strategies, health services, management, and policy.

allCourses.title: Public Health Programs for the Corporate World
allCourses.description: International perspective on workplace health promotion. Strategies for developing programs to improve employee health and to decrease risks of chronic degenerative diseases. Case studies include assessment of employee health, program design, implementation, and evaluation. Emphasis on disease prevention.

allCourses.title: Public Health Administration
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines historical aspects of public health administration including policies, procedures, trends, and development of organizations. Addresses information and skills necessary to succeed in public health leadership roles. Discusses strategic planning, collaborations, and ethical considerations for successful management in public health.

allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.title: Medical Sociology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Current problems in U.S. health-care system and proposals for reform. Examines  financial barriers to access; problem of patient dumping; underinsurance; prenatal and perinatal care; child services; preventative care and needs of the elderly; minorities; low-income people; undocumented.

allCourses.title: Tobacco Control Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only. Public Health Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines the challenges that governments encounter in regulating the marketing, sales and acquisition, and use of tobacco products. Students assess the supply and demand for tobacco from the perspectives of the industry and consumer.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Health Policy and Administration
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of health policy and administration. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Clinical Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Behavioral role in etiology, treatment, and prevention of certain diseases. Behavioral intervention including biofeedback, stress-, pain-management, health habit counseling, and other skills to assist patients make cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes needed to cope with disease or achieve better health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Health Behavior Theory
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces theoretical perspectives from the social sciences to understand health behavior from the vantage point of individuals, their interpersonal contacts, communities, and ecological contexts. Application of theory to public health problems is a central focus.

allCourses.title: Health Promotion Programs
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines ecological perspectives of health promotion programs and risk factors related to mortality/morbidity.  Analyzes effectiveness of health promotion strategies and issues in the existing healthcare systems in light of sociocultural beliefs and economical/political conditions.

allCourses.title: Drug Abuse and its Prevention
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and practical underpinnings of drug abuse and its prevention at the individual and population levels. Students practice developing drug abuse prevention schemes for specific populations. Recent developments in pharmacological and biobehavioral theories of drug dependence are explored.

allCourses.title: Public Health Communication
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical underpinnings and practical applications of communication sciences in public health practice. Techniques of effective communication, including fear appeal and deterrence; social marketing; public-private partnerships; health service delivery; and outreach in rural and urban settings, and for international health strategies.

allCourses.title: Public Health and Wellness
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents information about wellness from both science and policy perspectives in order to demonstrate the role of wellness in public health. Emphasizes the conditions that create wellness in the individual, the community, the nation, and the world.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social and Behavioral Health Science
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social and behavioral health sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Environmental Geology
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to geologic principles and applications to environmental problems. Topics include: tectonic processes, earth materials, soils, river processes, groundwater, the coastal environment, slope failures, seismic hazards, mineral resources, and land-use evaluation based on geologic conditions. Examples from case studies.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on processes of exposure to environmental toxins/agents and their impact to human health and the environment. Media transport, exposure assessment, susceptibility, behavior, and health effect of several toxins are discussed.

allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to how air pollutants are emitted into the atmosphere, how people are most exposed to air pollutants in developed and developing areas, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and the influence of air pollutants on global warming.

allCourses.title: Nuclear Environments
allCourses.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Global Health
allCourses.description: Provides a foundational interdisciplinary understanding of global health issues and their importance to various societal goals, including poverty reduction, economic productivity, and peace promotion. Covers major communicable and non-communicable diseases and demographic patterns of disease burden.

allCourses.title: Human Exposure to Environmental Contaminants
allCourses.description: Introduces origins of human's realization that chemicals in the environment may adversely affect health. Introduces the theory and principles of exposure assessment. Covers estimation of exposure, variability of measures, the way exposure assessment is incorporated into the risk-assessment paradigm.

allCourses.title: Climate Change and Disaster Management
allCourses.description: Examines the social, economic, environmental, and health impacts of anthropogenic climate change through engaged learning that integrates practice and theory.

allCourses.title: Health and Global Environmental Change
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of scientific underpinnings of global environmental change and human health consequences. Provides  an understanding of the fundamental dependency of human health on global environmental integrity. Encourages disciplinary cross-fertilization through interaction of students in environmental, health, and policy sciences.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One upper-division course in environmental science, public health, environmental policy, and/or environmental management.

allCourses.title: Global Health Ethics
allCourses.description: Provides a foundation for understanding and application of key issues.

allCourses.title: War and Public Health
allCourses.description: Explores how war impacts public health both globally and domestically in the United States. Focus on the link between war and the burden that it ultimately places on physical, mental, environmental, and societal health as well as on health systems.

allCourses.title: Global Health Policy and Diplomacy
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles and consequences of global health policy and diplomacy, including governance structure, functions, analysis, advocacy, and outcomes. Emphasizes practical application of multilateral policies for global health security and responses to transnational threats such as pandemics, climate, pollution, and migration.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Environmental and Global Health Science
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of environmental and global health sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Epidemiology of Infectious Disease
allCourses.description: Examines the distribution of infectious disease and the health and disease risk among human populations. Introduces basic methods for infectious disease epidemiology. Case studies of important diseases, including HIV and malaria, are conducted.

allCourses.title: Infectious Disease Dynamics
allCourses.description: Learn how the immune system interacts with infectious diseases, in particular with viral infections. An introduction to basic virology and immunology, it concentrates on the way in which the immune system is critical to the prevention of infections.

allCourses.title: Evolutionary and Ecological Principles in Medicine
allCourses.description: Explore the dynamics of populations on an ecological, epidemiological, and medical level. Considers the dynamics of competition, predation, and parasitism; the spread and control of infectious diseases; and the in vivo dynamics of viral infections and the immune system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Infectious Diseases
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of infectious diseases. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
allCourses.description: Provides a broad introduction to the use of Geographic Information Systems software to carry out projects for visualizing and analyzing spatial data to address significant issues of health care and policy-planning.

allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Ethics and Responsible Conduct of Research in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Sciences Majors only. Public Health Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Issues of scientific integrity and satisfies the requirements for training in public health ethics. Includes guidelines for responsible conduct of research, federal and international codes, administrative review and approval, conflict of interest, and privacy and safety of research participants.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory I
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides training for students with an interest in clinical and translational research in the health care setting. Cultivates skills for study design, research literature review, ethics, responsible conduct of research, and cultural competence while emphasizing professionalism and personal responsibility.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and BIO SCI 194S and CHEM 1C and CHEM 1LC and CHEM 1LD. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory II
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunities for students to participate in clinical and translational research through rotations in at least two health care settings. Builds on preparation through the first course (194A) in the sequence to support exploration of various research topics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 194A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory III
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunities for students to work closely in a particular clinical and translational research setting. Builds on preparation through the didactic instruction presented in first course of the sequence (194A) to support deeper engagement on a particular research topic.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 194B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory IV
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunities for students to participate in clinical and translational research through placement in a research laboratory. This course is a continuation of 194C in which students have the opportunity to participate in a permanent research rotation.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Public Health Practicum and Culminating Experience
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Sciences Majors only. Public Health Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides direct opportunities for Public Health majors to observe and participate in public health activities and/or research; and to cultivate skills for verbal and written communication of contemporary public health topics for an integrative culminating experience.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory I - Community-Based Research and Evaluation
allCourses.description: Provides training for students with an interest in clinical and translational research in a community-based setting. Cultivates skills for study design, research literature review, ethics, responsible conduct of research, and cultural competence while emphasizing professionalism and personal responsibility.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory II - Community-Based Research and Evaluation
allCourses.description: Provides the unique opportunity for students to participate in research in two or more community-based settings. Builds on preparation through PUBHLTH 196A to support exploration of various research topics.

allCourses.title: Clinical and Translational Research Preparatory III - Community-Based Research and Evaluation III
allCourses.description: Final course in the 196 series where students have the unique opportunity to participate in permanent research rotation. Instructs students how to design, perform, interpret, and discuss independent research in a collaborative atmosphere.

allCourses.title: Field Studies in Public Health
allCourses.description: For students who may either accompany faculty members on field trips or engage in post-practicum work at a field agency.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Directed Studies
allCourses.description: Student participation in a series of research-related activities performed in an individual or small-group setting under the guidance of a faculty advisor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Undergraduate Research
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Original research with Public Health faculty. Attendance at regular research group meetings is also generally expected, and a quarterly written report is required. Strongly recommended for students considering research careers and/or graduate degree programs.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Case Studies in Public Health Practice
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents case studies in various themes of public health practice to demonstrate how the principles of public health were established and continue to evolve.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Public Health
allCourses.restriction: College of Health Sciences students only. Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Presents the overarching framework, principles, and core responsibilities of public health research and practice from a multidisciplinary perspective. Provides necessary foundation for further studies toward advanced cross-cutting approaches essential for public health practice.

allCourses.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to help students develop an appreciation for statistician's view of the research process, emphasizing biomedical research. Instills an understanding of how statistical models are used to yield insights about data that form evidence-based understanding of the world around us.

allCourses.title: Biostatistics II: Intermediate Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and clinical research fields. Covers common regression-modeling techniques frequently used in biologic and medical applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204. EPIDEM 204 with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Biostatistics III: Advanced Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields.  Introduces statistical methods for analyzing survival and longitudinal/clustered data, and techniques to resolve missing data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204B. EPIDEM 204B with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, biostatistics, and epidemiological research. Topics include research methods of measuring health problems in populations, disease control and prevention in populations, how epidemiology contributes to knowledge of disease etiology, and biostatistical analysis and interpretation of epidemiologic data.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: College of Health Sciences students only. Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Epidemiology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Learn to design and conduct epidemiologic studies using common designs. Determine why bias and measurement error arise in observational studies, and how they influence effect estimates. Perform and interpret epidemiologic data analyses using statistical software.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 206A. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in the design and statistical analysis of epidemiologic studies. Topics include simulation methods, counter-matching and multiphase study designs, missing data, and Bayesian analysis. Published simulation studies are discussed and replicated using the R software package.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 200B. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 200B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to probability and statistical methods, using examples in public health. Topics include descriptive statistics, laws of probability, discrete and continuous probability distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and power calculations for one- and two-sample comparisons.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 206A. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Analysis of Public Health Data Using Statistical Software
allCourses.restriction: Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of common statistical methods in public health and how to implement them in R. Topics include linear regression, ANOVA, the Kruskal-Wallis test, logistic regression, missing data and censoring, Kaplan-Meier survival curves, log-rank tests, and Cox regression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 207A. PUBHLTH 207A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Advances in Social Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advances understanding of social distribution and social determinants of disease through multiple risk factor models and mechanisms that emphasize developmental and socio-environmental risk factors on mental and physical health across the life span.

allCourses.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic demographic methods used in social science and public health research. Topics include sources and limitations of demographic data; components of population growth; measures of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, and population mobility projection methods; and demographic models.

allCourses.title: Theory-Driven Secondary Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Learn how to develop and test theoretically-driven research questions in secondary data sources. Logic of theory building and testing, how to conduct statistical analyses on testable research questions, and interpret results. There is also a lab component.

allCourses.title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
allCourses.description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.

allCourses.title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
allCourses.description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.

allCourses.title: Epidemiology in Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines major topics in epidemiology and global health. Research topics within these two disciplines are focused on resource-poor communities, with an application to the global world.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in biostatistics, epidemiology, and health informatics. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Public Health Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Master of Public Policy Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban and Regional Planning Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

allCourses.title: Risk Communication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theory and research related to the communication of scientific information in risk communication contexts, risk perceptions, and behavior as related to decision-making under risk.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in health policy and management. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Environmental Policy and Global Sustainability
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Organized around four transcendent questions: does the world value sustainability, what challenges must be met to move toward it, what are the roots of inequality, and is capitalism compatible with sustainability.

allCourses.title: Theories of Health Communication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the concepts, constructs, and theories of communication in health and risk contexts. Examines interpersonal, family, organizational, and mediated communicative processes about health care and conditions from a global perspective.

allCourses.title: Health Behavior Theory
allCourses.restriction: Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the field of Health Behavior and segues into major theoretical perspectives. Focus on health behavior change from the vantage point of individual health behavior and theoretical abstraction. Explores how to relate theory to behavior-change intervention programs.

allCourses.title: Health Promotion Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces strategic planning integral to intervention planning in public health practice and research, emphasizing the fundamental domains of social and behavioral health science and practices. Students develop an intervention plan for a specific health problem, health behavior, and target population.

allCourses.title: Social Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An interactive graduate seminar covering topics related to the research process and study design. Begins with conceptualizing research questions, hypotheses, and then turns to topics in measurement and concludes with experimental, quasi-experimental, and observational study designs.

allCourses.title: Program Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods, tools, and procedures for systematic investigation of the effectiveness of programs in health and social services for disease intervention, prevention, and health promotion. Includes development of program evaluation plans, logic models, contextual frameworks, study designs, and data analyses.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Maternal and Child Health - Programs, Problems, and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of issues facing women, children, and families from a public health perspective.  Discusses role of socio-economic, political, biological, environmental factors on population health. Studies historical foundations and current factors impacting Maternal Child Health programs and legislation in the US.

allCourses.title: Health Status and Care Disparities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Expert health care providers present viewpoints and interdisciplinary strategies for addressing sociocultural, economic, gender, age, and other disparities in population health status and care provision.

allCourses.title: Models of Practice and Intervention at the Community Level
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines and critiques current models, frameworks, theories for.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Human Exposure Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the basic principles and methods in estimating human exposure to environmental pollutants. Topics include source emissions, spatial/temporal aspects of human exposures, air pollution exposure modeling, time-activity patterns, micro-environmental exposure assessment, the uncertainty/variability analysis.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only. Environ Health Sci and Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Convergence of agents (chemical, physical, biological, or psychosocial) in environment can emerge as diseases influenced by social, political, and economic factors, allowing them to become rooted in society. How these agents from various spheres come together and impact human health.

allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

allCourses.title: Occupational Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to psychological and social factors in the workplace that affect health and productivity. Goal is to support redesign of the workplace and social situations that can reduce stress-related illness risks, and increase humane forms of productivity and competence development.

allCourses.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Surveys the general principles, basic mathematical methods, and practices of environmental modeling and human health risk assessment. Topics include advection-dispersion models, risk management, and risk perception. Students conduct an original risk assessment as a final group project.

allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanistic analysis of responses occurring in various organ systems of experimental animals and humans exposed to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation. Review distinctive cellular and tissue structure and physiological function of the various organ systems.

allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanistic analysis of responses occurring in various organ systems of experimental animals and humans exposed to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation. Review of distinctive cellular and tissue structure and physiological function of the various organ systems.

allCourses.title: Industrial Toxicology
allCourses.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Environmental & Occupational Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in environmental and occupational health. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Global Burden of Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces composite measures of disease burden, including Disability Adjusted Life Years and their use in prioritizing disease burden at local, regional, and global levels. Focuses on WHO's landmark assessments and introduces DISMOD software for specific analyses.

allCourses.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Geographical distribution of infectious diseases and the health and disease risk in diverse human populations. Introduces basic methods for infectious disease epidemiology and case studies of important diseases. Includes surveillance, outbreak investigation, emerging pathogens, traditional and molecular epidemiology.

allCourses.title: Climate Change and Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed for students to examine major topics in climate change and global health. Draws heavily on the literature in order to develop an understanding of micro- and macro-level impacts and drivers with regard to climate change and health.

allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a broad introduction to the use of Geographic Information Systems software to carry out projects for visualizing and analyzing spatial data to address significant issues of health care and policy-planning.

allCourses.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems and Spatial Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students expand their current knowledge of the ArcGIS software to develop advanced geographic-related research questions, learn how to apply spatial epidemiologic methods to public health data, and integrate their skills in a GIS project of their design.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: General introduction to qualitative research methods for investigating public health questions at various scales from community level to global populations. Emphasizes systematic approaches to the collection, analysis, interpretation of qualitative data.

allCourses.title: Research Proposal Writing in Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of financial support for research in global health and disease prevention. Collaborative agreements, guidelines for proposal writing, team building, budgeting, peer-review process, and transitioning from proposal to research project implementation.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Global Health and Disease Prevention
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in global health and disease prevention. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice.  Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health

allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice.  Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
