allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Ethics and Responsible Conduct of Research in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Issues of scientific integrity and satisfies the requirements for training in public health ethics. Includes guidelines for responsible conduct of research, federal and international codes, administrative review and approval, conflict of interest, and privacy and safety of research participants.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Clinical and Translational Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces rationale and imperative for clinical translational science and various approaches being developed to speed-up discoveries and their transformation into health care practices. Compares and contrasts current impediments to clinical research with the potential and transformative power of translational science.

allCourses.title: Research Communication in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Strategies for effective writing and oral presentation of research characteristics and results to various audiences. Includes exercises in writing for the public, for scholarly journals, and at conferences.

allCourses.title: Graduate Practicum and Culminating Experience in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunities for hands-on experience for graduate students at agencies or organizations engaged in public health practice. Students are matched with placement sites based on academic preparation and students' career goals. The practicum report is integrated into the culminating experience.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 200 and PUBHLTH 244 and PUBHLTH 222 and PUBHLTH 264 and PUBHLTH 207A. PUBHLTH 200 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 244 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 222 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 264 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 207A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Research Design and Proposal Writing
allCourses.restriction: College of Health Sciences students only. Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Evaluate strengths of research findings based on methods used by researchers to develop research proposals. Components such as collaborative agreements, guidelines for proposal writing, budgeting, peer-review process, and transitioning from proposal to research project implementation are addressed.

allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed study with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Urban Environmental Health
allCourses.description: Study of natural and physical components of earth's environmental problems due to human activities. Topics include global air, water, soil, biodiversity, rainforests, energy, demographics, agriculture, and urbanization. Theme is sustainability. Integrated into the science are social, legal, and economic considerations.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Environmental Quality and Health
allCourses.description: Overviews how pollution in the environment affects human health. Topics are toxicology, epidemiology, risk assessment, water, food, air, radiation, pesticides, solid and hazardous waste. Included are interdisciplinary elements of environmental regulations, education, and consumer protection.

allCourses.title: Public Health Statistics I
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the development and application of statistical reasoning and methods in addressing, analyzing, and solving problems in public health, health care, and biomedical, clinical, and population-based research and practice.

allCourses.title: Public Health Statistics II
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only. Public Health Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the development and application of statistical reasoning and methods in addressing, analyzing, and solving problems in public health, health care, and biomedical, clinical, and population-based research and practice.

allCourses.title: AIDS Fundamentals
allCourses.description: Considers the biological and sociological bases of the AIDS epidemic. Topics include the history of AIDS, current medical knowledge, transmission, risk reduction, and how the community can respond.

allCourses.title: Natural Disasters
allCourses.description: Natural disasters are natural Earth processes that adversely affect humans. Topics include tectonics, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanoes, landslides, severe weather, flooding, coastal processes, wildfire, related topics, and use of GIS for hazard and risk assessment.

allCourses.title: Disparities in Health Care
allCourses.description: Student participatory course practicing initiation, planning, and coordination of various speakers on the subject of Disparities in Health Care.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides an opportunity for selected students to pursue advanced work in research and earn Public Health Honors. Students will conduct their honors research project with faculty through lectures, guest speakers, creating timelines and assignments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 199 AND SCHOOL OF PUBHLTH ONLY
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis II
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students initiate and complete data collection for the honors thesis. In addition, students begin data analysis and summarize results at a class symposium at the end of the quarter. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.

allCourses.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis III
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students write their honors research project (PUBHLTH H192A-PUBHLTH H192B) and prepare an oral report to be presented at a class symposium at the end of the quarter. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Study of Religion
allCourses.description: The intersection of religious belief and practices with selected subjects of continuing interest.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Philosophy of Religion
allCourses.description: Critical examination of philosophical concepts in religious scripture and theology, e.g., the nature and existence of God, miracles, the problem of evil, and divine command theories in ethics. May include any religious tradition.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Thinking about Religion: Theories and Methodologies
allCourses.restriction: Religious Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey and investigation of the major thinkers, theories, and methodologies in the study of religions. Designed to develop the student's ability to analyze and articulate theoretical arguments; includes a paper on relevant Religious Studies topics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( REL STD 5A OR HISTORY 16A ) AND ( REL STD 5B OR HISTORY 16B ) AND ( REL STD 5C OR HISTORY 16C )

allCourses.title: Thinking about Religion: Theories and Methodologies
allCourses.restriction: Religious Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey and investigation of the major thinkers, theories, and methodologies in the study of religions. Designed to develop the student's ability to analyze and articulate theoretical arguments in writing; includes a paper on relevant Religious Studies topics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( REL STD 5A OR HISTORY 16A ) AND ( REL STD 5B OR HISTORY 16B ) AND ( REL STD 5C OR HISTORY 16C ) AND LOWER DIVISION WRITING

allCourses.title: Religion and World Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between religion and world politics historically and today, focusing on connections with peace/war, democracy, human rights, secularism(s), and globalization. Covers major debates, scholarship, concepts, and theories through class exercises, exams, and essays.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Studies involving (but not limited to) Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Jainism, Sikhism, Daoism, Shinto or Shamanism, including both elite and doctrinal aspects and forms of more popular religiosity.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan.  Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern Indian Religion
allCourses.description: Topics in religions of the Indian subcontinent including, but not confined to, Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism, Islam, and Buddhism from the founding of the Mughal Empire in 1526 to the creation of the several modern states of the Indian subcontinent.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Character and evolution of Egyptian, Jewish, Zoroastrian, Muslim, and other religious communities of the region from their formative periods to the present era.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Antisemitism
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of antisemitism, ancient to modern. Topics include medieval religious anti-Judaism, persecution of Jews and Judaism during the Crusades and the Inquisition, the rise of modern racial antisemitism, Nazi antisemitism, and the persistence of antisemitism since 1945.

allCourses.title: Jews and Power
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority.

allCourses.title: History of Zoroastrianism
allCourses.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

allCourses.title: Early Western Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Religious perspectives of the Mediterranean and European regions from the earliest times to approximately 1500 C.E.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Religion in the Americas
allCourses.description: Religious belief and social context in North and South America from the earliest human societies to the present.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Diaspora Religions
allCourses.description: Examination of what happens to belief and practice as religious communities are scattered geographically.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: An Economic Approach to Religion
allCourses.description: Introduction to how basic economic concepts such as demand, supply, consumption, production, competition, free-riding, innovation, regulation, and rent-seeking can be applied to understand observed religious behavior.

allCourses.title: Topics in Comparative Studies in Religion
allCourses.description: Literary, historical, or philosophical comparison of selected religious and quasi-religious traditions, their beliefs and practices.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty member.  Substantial written work required.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Philosophy and Religion
allCourses.description: Examines the intersection of religion and philosophy from a standpoint that does not presuppose previous academic study of either.  Both Western and Eastern traditions and perspectives may be explored.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: World Religions I
allCourses.description: An introduction to the history, doctrine, culture, and writing of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

allCourses.title: World Religions II
allCourses.description: An introduction to various religious traditions in selected areas of the world—including India and South Asia, East Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

allCourses.title: Religious Dialogue
allCourses.description: Lectures and discussion on controversial topics in religion: sexual morality; religious violence; science; treatment of women and girls; religious truth, American Constitutional matters; secularization; the future of religion, and other topics.

allCourses.title: Gender and Religion
allCourses.description: Introduces the topic of religion in a feminist context by performing cross-cultural exploration of gender, authority, and faith in various traditions. Study includes (but is not limited to) writings of contemporary Jewish, Christian, and Muslim feminists.

allCourses.title: Aspects of Religion
allCourses.description: A presentation of selected issues in the study of religion.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.description: Focuses on life skills such as physical fitness, nutrition, and time management while providing an introduction to military knowledge, customs, and skills.

allCourses.description: Uses increasingly intense situational leadership challenges to build cadet awareness and skills in leading small units. Skills in decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members when "under fire" are explored, evaluated, and developed.

allCourses.title: Leadership III

allCourses.description: Transitions the focus of student learning from being trained, mentored, and evaluated as a cadet to learning how to train, mentor, and evaluate cadets. Cadets begin to learn the duties and responsibilities of an Army staff officer.

allCourses.title: Developmental Leadership II
allCourses.restriction: For students with a service obligation to the U.S. Army.
allCourses.description: Requires students to continue to train, mentor, and evaluate underclass cadets. Cadets learn to safely conduct training by understanding and employing the Composite Risk Management Process and the Comprehensive Soldier Fitness (CSF) program.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ROTC 131 and ROTC 132 and ROTC 133 and ROTC 141

allCourses.title: Officership

allCourses.description: Explores the dynamics of leading in the complex situations of current military operations in the OE. Cadets examine differences in customs and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ROTC 131 AND ROTC 132 AND ROTC 133 AND ROTC 141 AND ROTC 142 AND ROTC 100L

allCourses.title: Military History
allCourses.description: Develops an understanding of the role military officers have played in the defense of our country and the advancement of its military.

allCourses.description: Examines the evolution of the American military establishment and the progression of military professionalism in terms of social, political, economic, military, and technological developments from the end of the Civil War through World War II.

allCourses.title: United States Military History-1945 to 2001
allCourses.description: Examines the evolution of the American military establishment and the progression of military professionalism in terms of social, political, economic, military, and technological developments from the Cold War to the War on Terrorism.

allCourses.description: Examines the challenges of leading tactical teams in the OE. Highlights dimensions of terrain analysis, patrolling, and operation orders.

allCourses.title: Topics in Russian Culture
allCourses.description: Study of varied topics in Russian culture, area studies, and society, both in the present and in historical perspective.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Studies Russian
allCourses.description: Special studies under faculty supervision.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Social Ecology
allCourses.description: Introduction to the ecological paradigm through a consideration of the classic and recent works in human, cultural, and social ecology. Emphasis on the use of the ecological paradigm as an aid in analyzing societal problems and prescribing for their amelioration.

allCourses.title: Research Design
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only. Environmental Science and Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the logic behind and methods of designing and conducting research studies in Social Ecology. Topics include how to measure variables of interest, identifying causal relationships, sampling, survey research methods, experiments, quasi-experimental designs, and ethics in research.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Ecology
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: Special topics courses are offered from time to time. In general they will focus on a topic from interdisciplinary perspectives. Course content varies with the interest of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Community Archiving in Social Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: Students are trained in community archiving, oral history, and ethnography in order to produce material for submission to a student-initiated Social Ecology community archive housed in the UC Irvine Special Collections section of the UC Irvine libraries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Field Study authorization required for enrollment.

allCourses.title: Building, Analyzing, and Sustaining a Digital Media Archive
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students are trained in contributing to and managing a digital media archive. Provided an opportunity to use resources in the archive to develop policy proposals to solve real-world problems at the intersection of crime, law, and society.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Authorization for field study.

allCourses.title: Advanced Research Methods
allCourses.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Domestic Violence
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: General perspectives about domestic violence and theoretical accounts about what causes such behavior.

allCourses.title: Violence in Intimate Relationships
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Responses to various forms of domestic violence, such as intimate partner violence and child abuse. Covers barriers to reporting to the police, and prosecutors and courts. Human services, such as safety planning for victims, treatment programs, and restorative justice approaches.

allCourses.title: Statistical Analysis in Social Ecology
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. No credit for SOCECOL 13 if taken concurrently with or after PSYCH 10A, SOCIOL 10A, POL SCI 10A, SOC SCI 10A, STATS 7, STATS 8, STATS 67, EDUC 15
allCourses.description: Introduction to the techniques of statistical analysis in Social Ecology. Topics include probability, statistical inference, significance testing, univariate descriptive statistics, and multivariate analysis from an interdisciplinary perspective.
allCourses.overlap: PSYCH 10A, SOCIOL 10A, SOC SCI 10A, POL SCI 10A, STATS 7, STATS 8.

allCourses.title: Global and International Studies Forum
allCourses.description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Mediation
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Humanities students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Student develop mediation skills and refine knowledge in the practice and theory of conflict resolution. Students who complete this course may serve as mediators in the Campus Mediation Program. Course is a prerequisite to completing Indep Study as an intern.

allCourses.title: Seminar Conflict Resolution
allCourses.description: Designed for seniors who are pursuing the minor in Conflict Resolution and/or International Studies major. Provides a forum in which students will refine skills and theory in the study of cooperation and conflict, from local to global arenas.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Global Sustainability Minors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations.  Prepare bibliography.

allCourses.title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability II
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations.  Prepare research proposal.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 191A or SOCECOL 186A or EARTHSS 190A

allCourses.title: Writing/Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability III
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability.  Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum also is required.  Seminar utilized to analyze Forum presentations and to prepare senior research paper.  Prepare/write research paper under direction of faculty member.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B. BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Global Service Scholars Advanced Seminar
allCourses.description: For students who are accepted into the Global Service Scholars Program. Provides advanced training in empathy and compassion, and prepares students for their summer international field experience.

allCourses.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.

allCourses.title: Naturalistic Field Research
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to alternative models of experiential learning and to various methods of observation, assessment, and evaluation. Introduction to the nature of organizations and ethical issues that emerge from research and intervention in natural settings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Field Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: Community engagement to facilitate civic education through field research experience, social intervention, and professionalization. Small group instruction, discussion, writing, and presentations synthesizing students’ experiences in the field with theory, paradigms, and ideas learned about in their course work.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Advanced Field Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: While completing 10 hours of field work per week, students become acquainted with the goals and activities of their placement and will work closely with the placement supervisor and AFS instructor to identify the scope of a research project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Field Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: While completing 10 hours of field work per week, students implement their research project through data collection and observations which allow them to reflect on, apply, and synthesize their academic training through observations and experiences at the placement.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 195A. Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Field Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Ecology students only.
allCourses.description: While completing 10 hours per week of field work, students write and finalize their AFS Client Project in consultation with the placement and the FS instructor, and make a final written and oral presentation to the placement and invited guests.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 195B. Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Field Study Writing Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Environmental Science and Policy Majors only. Psychological Science Majors only. Criminology, Law and Society Majors only. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only. Urban Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Community engagement to promote civic education through field research experience, and the opportunity to study social issues and the environments where they occur. Develop discipline-specific writing and communication skills, methodology, and integrate information from multiple sources.   Course may be offered online.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10. Cumulative UC GPA of 2.0. Authorization is required. Successful completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an appreciation and understanding of statistics necessary to conduct applied research. Topics include approaches to and presentation of data, robust statistics, standardization techniques, multivariate regression, and analysis of variance.

allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to survival analysis methods for the analysis of change in discrete dependent variables. Focuses on data collection strategies for obtaining longitudinal data and continuous-time hazards models. Communicates the variety and power of multivariate hazard models.

allCourses.title: Structural Equation Modeling I
allCourses.description: The general structural equation model is developed including path models, recursive and nonrecursive structural models, multiple indicator models, and confirmatory factor models. Use of LISREL and other software for estimating model parameters is covered.

allCourses.title: Structural Equation Modeling II: Longitudinal and Advanced Topics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides hands-on experience with longitudinal and advanced structural equation models and is of interest to students from a range of disciplines. Topics covered include confirmatory factor, latent growth curve, general growth mixture, and multi-level modeling.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics covered vary with interests of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Program Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students are introduced to the use of research techniques and statistical methods in assessing the effectiveness of social programs. Different evaluative models are discussed using examples of actual program evaluations.

allCourses.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Sociology
allCourses.description: Considers major sociological concepts, theories, and research findings illuminating processes of interpersonal interaction, social differentiation and stratification, integration and conflict, and change, with attention to variation in class, race/ethnic, gender, multicultural, and cross-national perspectives and experiences.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.

allCourses.description: Methods of data collection and analysis used by sociologists. Experimental methods, surveys, and interviews, field research and participant observation, demographic methods, historical and comparative approaches.

allCourses.title: Sociological Theory
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: What a theory of society is and is not. Historical and contemporary models, perspectives, and schools.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Theory
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics I
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.

allCourses.title: Social Psychology of Networks
allCourses.restriction: Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Review of network methods used in small group and organizational research. Discussion of social psychological literature relevant to the network of study of cognitive social structure, exchange/communication, identity negotiation, and social control. Case study of network datasets exemplifies research issues.

allCourses.title: Religious Traditions of Asian Americans
allCourses.description: Studies the religious traditions of Asian Americans, focusing on the transplantation of religious institutions, establishment of sacred spaces, celebration of religious holidays, socialization of children, as well as birth, marriage, gender relations, death, family.

allCourses.title: Business Decisions
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys normative and descriptive models of decision-making behavior, with an emphasis on organizational and policy contexts. Topics include rational choice theory, biases and heuristics, framing effects, and overconfidence. Management fads, panics, and herd behavior are also discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ANTHRO 10A and ANTHRO 10B and ANTHRO 10C) or (SOCIOL 10A and SOCIOL 10B and SOCIOL 10C) or (SOC SCI 10A and SOC SCI 10B and SOC SCI 10C) or (MATH 2A and MATH 2B and (STATS 7 or MGMT 7)) or (STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C) or (ECON 15A and ECON 15B)

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Social Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social psychology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: How bureaucracies, formal organizations, and voluntary associations work, how/why they grow, and where they are going. History and structure of organizational rationality; dynamics of organized groups; behavior in organizations; limits of bureaucratization and attempts to overcome these limits through decentralization.

allCourses.title: White-Collar Crime
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines criminal activity in business and corporate enterprise, organizations, and the professions. Theories regarding the causes and control of white-collar and corporate crime are covered as well as the numerous definitions of these terms.

allCourses.title: Social Networks and Social Support
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the manner in which behaviors/attitudes of individuals are affected by their network ties to others. How are peoples' opportunities and well-being increased/decreased by their social networks? May include studies in mental/physical health, job seeking, separation and loss, and aging.

allCourses.title: Politics, Power, and Society
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Includes an examination of the major theoretical approaches to political sociology, and the application of these ideas to the politics of advanced capitalist societies. Also considers stability and change in power structures.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Structures
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of structures. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Sociological Lens on Religion
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the effects of religious beliefs, belonging, and institutions on social dynamics, including class, gender, and racial stratification, politics, and social movements. Additional topics: the sociological significance of conversion, commitment, and secularization/sacralization.

allCourses.title: Social Inequalities and Health
allCourses.description: Introduces ways in which social inequalities produce health disparities. Begins with general perspectives on social causation of health, and then considers how particular individual attributes (e.g., gender, SES, race/ethnicity, nativity) and social contexts (e.g., neighborhoods) can get “under the skin.”.

allCourses.title: Global Peace
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Why do countries fight wars? Will world peace ever be possible? Focuses on social structures that might lead to global peace, with an emphasis on the role of culture and narrative in bringing peace locally, nationally, and globally.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Medical Sociology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Current problems in U.S. health-care system and proposals for reform. Examines  financial barriers to access; problem of patient dumping; underinsurance; prenatal and perinatal care; child services; preventative care and needs of the elderly; minorities; low-income people; undocumented.

allCourses.title: Medical Sociology

allCourses.description: An examination of baseball's role in American social life over the last 150 years. Issues of fraternal organizations, national development, capitalism, rationalization, race and ethnicity, gender, economic organization, labor relations, and politics are discussed.

allCourses.description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Education
allCourses.description: Focuses on education’s role in creating and redressing inequality, and in shaping how we understand our place in society. Education from cross-national and historical perspectives, and education as a vehicle for examining and solving social problems.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.title: Comparing European and US Societies
allCourses.description: Society, culture, institutions of U.S. and European countries. Fertility to football, guns to government, work to welfare, health to housework. Cross-national approaches for understanding the world and thinking critically about taken-for-granted practices. Policies the U.S. might borrow for social issues.

allCourses.title: Money, Work, and Social Life
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sociological perspective on issues related to money and work. Consumption practices and lifestyles, jobs and organizations, issues of money in intimate relations, marriage, and households, illegal work, discrimination, economic globalization are discussed.

allCourses.title: Money, Work, and Social Life

allCourses.description: Explores complex processes contributing to social construction of gender and sexuality in the U.S. with focus on intersection of gender, race, ethnicity, sexuality, and class; evaluates how men and women are differentially constituted in family, education, work, politics, media, language.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Aging
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to sociology of age, aging, and the aged. Problems posed by aging population. Life course transitions and how social organizations influence the life course. Addresses work, health, and family in later life.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Aging
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to sociology of age, aging, and the aged. Problems posed by aging population. Life course transitions. How social organizations influence the life course. Work, health, family in later life.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Inequality
allCourses.description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

allCourses.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.

allCourses.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Vietnam War
allCourses.description: Examines social structures and social changes in Vietnamese and U.S. societies through the study of the Vietnam War.

allCourses.title: U.S. War on Terrorism
allCourses.description: Analyzes the United States war on terrorism by focusing on terrorism, the U.S. wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and changes in police powers through the Patriot Act, as well as the political leadership which directs the war.

allCourses.title: Environment and Society
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines society's changing relationship to the natural world. Delineates different models of "nature" and then explores their institutional roots, the social responses they have generated, and their implications for social inequality.

allCourses.title: Revolution and Social Transformation in China
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the major political events in Mao’s communist revolution and the social transformations afterward. Helps students understand the historic and political landscape from which China is now departing.

allCourses.title: Chicanx/Latinx Education
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latinx low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

allCourses.title: Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.

allCourses.title: Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1

allCourses.title: China in the Global Age
allCourses.description: Chinese society from 1949 to present. Social change in the context of political control and ideological considerations. Focus on the power structure, political decision processes, and ideological legitimation, and interplay with the Chinese community and its culture.

allCourses.title: International Divided Cities
allCourses.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Social Policy
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explains how people decide to migrate and how they are incorporated into a host society (both historically and currently), examines the effects of immigration on the U.S., analyzes how the framing of immigration shapes the discourse about the issue.

allCourses.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
allCourses.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Social Policy
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explains how people decide to migrate and how they are incorporated into a host society (both historically and currently), examines the effects of immigration on the U.S., analyzes how the framing of immigration shapes the discourse about the issue.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Sociology Majors Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.

allCourses.description: Field study with Sociology faculty.

allCourses.title: Directed Group Study
allCourses.description: Directed study with Sociology faculty.

allCourses.description: Independent research with Sociology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Globalization
allCourses.description: Examines globalization and international issues from the perspective of sociology and related fields. Issues include economic globalization and global inequality, international environmental problems, international politics, trends in global culture, and global conflict.

allCourses.title: Proseminar I in Sociology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces first-year graduate students in Sociology to the current research interests of Sociology faculty, as well as to other aspects of graduate life at UCI and to the profession of sociology more generally.

allCourses.title: Proseminar II in Sociology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focus is on second-year research projects, design, development, data gathering, analysis, and preparing oral and written presentations of the results. Students learn analytic and writing skills, gain experience with research processes, and become socialized about professional standards, customs, and institutions.

allCourses.title: Classical Social Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the development of classical sociological theory through the writings of Karl Marx, Emile Durkheim, Max Weber, Georg Simmel, and George Herbert Mead.

allCourses.title: Contemporary Social Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Familiarizes students with 20th-century developments in social thought that have influenced sociological research, suggesting "what is living and what is dead" in the "classics" and offering an overview of the main outlines of recent sociological theorizing.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Gender
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the sociology of gender in the U.S. and globally. The social construction of gender and sexuality; theoretical perspectives and feminist frameworks. Theories of economy, patriarchy, and race, and the social positions of women and men.

allCourses.title: Network Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to theoretical work in the field of social networks. Topics include baseline models, homphily, and propinquity, exchange and power, balance theory, diffusion and social influence, equivalence, and cohesion. Deductive use of theory to make novel predictions is emphasized.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Data collection, organization, and analysis in ethnographic or quasi-experimental settings, including interviewing, participant observations, behavior observations, and questionnaires. Research design issues include sampling, longitudinal research, and comparative research. Emphasis on the integration of qualitative and quantitative data.

allCourses.title: Graduate Statistics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.

allCourses.title: Graduate Statistics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.

allCourses.title: Graduate Statistics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.

allCourses.title: Comparative and Historical Sociological Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include the logic of comparative and historical analysis techniques and the examination of exemplar works in representative problem areas.

allCourses.title: Interview Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Hands-on introduction to the use of interviews in social scientific research. Topics include when to use interviews and/or focus groups; how to design an interview-based study, how to conduct interviews, analyze interview data, and write up and publish interview-based results.

allCourses.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic demographic methods used in social science and public health research. Topics include sources and limitations of demographic data; components of population growth; measures of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, and population mobility projection methods; and demographic models.

allCourses.title: Seminar Ethnographic & Qualitative Field Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Comprehensive and critical discussion of the traditions of qualitative fieldwork; detailed examination of the collection, coding, analysis, and presentation of ethnographic/qualitative field data; and close mentoring of student projects culminating in an original research paper.

allCourses.title: Seminar Ethnographic & Qualitative Field Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Comprehensive and critical discussion of the traditions of qualitative fieldwork; detailed examination of the collection, coding, analysis, and presentation of ethnographic/qualitative field data; and close mentoring of student projects culminating in an original research paper.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Race and Ethnicity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An examination of central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity through a critical analysis and discussion of the principal theoretical perspectives and paradigms that have framed much of the scholarship in the area.

allCourses.title: Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and empirical approaches to the study of social and economic inequality, with special attention to race/ethnicity, class, and gender.

allCourses.title: Ethnic America
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines critically the meaning and measurement of ethnicity, race, and nation in sociological theory and research. Theories of ethnicity are explored, along with empirical studies of the construction of ethnic and pan-ethnic identities in historical and contemporary contexts.

allCourses.title: Poverty and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

allCourses.title: Educational Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on macro-level explanations of inequality of schooling, particularly in the U.S. context. Explores traditional models, such as conflict, functionalism, status-attainment, cultural reproduction, and newer synthetic accounts. Emphasis on higher education access and the intersection of education and work.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Social Movements
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey of the field of Social Movements, oriented around critical themes in the major theoretical traditions and contemporary exemplars.

allCourses.title: Political Sociology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Begins with an examination of the three major orientations to the State (Pluralist, Elitist, and Class). Next considers current topics in political sociology including the Welfare State, the New Deal, political behavior, social movements, participation, and democracy.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Culture
allCourses.description: Major perspectives in the sociology of culture. Topics include the role of cultural dynamics in the reproduction of inequality, collective action, political and organizational decision making, emotional experience, and the social impacts of new technologies.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Political Sociology and Social Movements
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of political sociology and social movements. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Global Urbanization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the 20th century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Global Studies and Comparative Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of global studies and comparative development. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Population
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the interrelationships between population and social organization. Considers measurement and explanation of historical and contemporary trends in birth rates, death rates, migration, and marriage and divorce. Case material is drawn primarily from the U.S. and other industrialized nations.

allCourses.title: Immigrant America
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The study of the causes and consequences of international migration has become one of the most vital fields of sociological theory and research. Examines principal theoretical perspectives and empirical research on contemporary immigration flows and the processes of incorporation.

allCourses.title: DASA Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Data collection, organization, and analysis in population studies and demography. Research design issues include sampling, longitudinal research, and comparative research.

allCourses.title: Crimmigration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the criminalization of immigration, with an emphasis on U.S. enforcement procedures and outcomes. Analyzes the devolution of federal immigration law to local authorities, the rise in immigrant detention and deportation, and the militarization of the U.S.-Mexico border.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Social Demography
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social demography. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social organizations and institutions. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Analysis of Social Network Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview and application of methods for analyzing social network data. Topics include: data structures, visualization, graph theory, centrality, subgroups, positions, blockmodels, local properties, and statistical models. Social network analysis software is used to analyze a range of examples.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Social Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a broad overview of the history, concepts, and applications of social networks. Students have the opportunity to delve deeply into applications of the network approach in their individual areas of interest.

allCourses.title: Theorizing Illegality and the Experiences of Undocumented Immigrants
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theories of illegality and citizenship, historical and contemporary undocumented immigrant experiences, and methodological concerns in this area of study.

allCourses.title: Special Topics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Social Sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Theory
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
