allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Sociology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 10 times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Sociology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Social Problems
allCourses.description: Focuses on how institutional and organizational features of societies generate problems for people. Particular attention directed at a set of problems related to political and economic inequality: poverty, racism, sexism, urban and population problems, the environment, the criminal justice system.

allCourses.title: Self-Identity and Society
allCourses.description: Studies sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology, with focus on the social influences on personality, attitudes, beliefs, and behavior; socialization, human groups, and social interaction.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Social Psychology
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social psychology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Small Group Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Deals with models for understanding behavior in small groups, including coalition formation, socialization, group norms and decision rules, leadership, conformity, group structure, and communication processes.

allCourses.title: City and Community
allCourses.description: Examines nature, causes, and consequences of urbanization along with changing scale and complexity, demographic/ecological city growth patterns, quality of life in urban areas, processes of decision-making, and bearing of sociological investigation on public policy concerns in contemporary urban society.

allCourses.title: Births, Deaths, and Migration
allCourses.description: Introduction to the analysis of human population including fertility, mortality dispersion, sex distribution. Attention is focused on the effects of these variables on, e.g., over-population, social disorganization, and the stability of social institutions.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Structures
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of structures. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Family & Community
allCourses.description: Briefly examines the history of different Asian American groups and provides an in-depth analysis of issues related to family composition, mate selection, changing gender roles, and intergenerational conflict.

allCourses.title: Religion and Society
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A critical and personal examination of the varieties of religious and spiritual experiences human beings are undergoing in contemporary society. The role of conscious understanding and unconscious conditioning regarding religion and spirituality.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Social Institutions and Culture
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social institutions and culture. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Families and Intimate Relations
allCourses.description: Sociological theories/research on marriage, kinship, intimacy, and divorce. Emphasis on comparing family patterns in different social classes, ethnic groups, and societies, and on relating family life to the economy and other social institutions. Topics include gender roles, child-rearing, historical change.  Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Race and Ethnicity
allCourses.description: Focuses on racial and ethnic relations in the United States and compares them with those found in other societies. Analyzes the conditions that favor either cooperation and integration or rivalry, tension, and conflict. Appraises strategies for reducing and resolving conflicts.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Sexuality
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to and overview of the sociology of sex and sexuality. Considers the social meanings of sex and sexuality, the social contexts of sex and sexuality, and the social regulations of sex and sexuality.

allCourses.title: Gender and Race Inequality in the Workplace
allCourses.description: Analysis of current state and trends in major inequality measures including the wage gap, occupational segregation, and access to managerial positions. Theories that purport to explain such differences, and the related empirical evidence, are also covered.

allCourses.title: Ethnic and Immigrant America
allCourses.description: Focusing on Asian, Latino, and Black immigrant groups, examines the second generation's experience of straddling two cultures and growing up American. Covers topics such as assimilation, bilingualism, race relations, education, bicultural conflicts, interracial marriage, and multiracial identities.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Age, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of age, gender, race, and ethnicity. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Honors Research and Thesis
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the design and implementation of individual research projects undertaken by senior Sociology majors. Writing projects consist of a proposal and paper on some empirical research.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems in Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Hands-on laboratory course introduces students to the fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) technology using social science applications.  Students learn to organize, manipulate, and display spatial data leading to the design of their own GIS research project.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Geographic Information Systems in Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Expands Geographic Information Systems (GIS) skills to more advanced theories and concepts in the spatial analysis of social science issues and particularly to analyzing and interpreting spatial data.  Students develop and complete a GIS research project of their own choosing.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics I
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics II
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: More advanced game theory and its political applications, beginning where Game Theory and Politics I ends.  Examples of topics covered include revolutions; arms race; spatial models of party competition; political manipulation; political coalitions and their power.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences I
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SOC SCI 10A may not be taken for credit if taken after or concurrently with ECON 15A.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the variety of statistical applications in the social sciences. Descriptive statistics. Measures of central tendency and dispersion. Percentile ranks. Standardization and normal approximation. Basic probability theory focuses on application to statistical inference and binomial distribution. Laboratory required.
allCourses.overlap: PSYCH 10A, SOCECOL 13, POL SCI 10A, SOCIOL 10A, ECON 15A.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences II
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to statistical inference, sampling distribution, standard error.  Hypothesis tests for proportions and means. Inferential techniques for nominal variables including chi-square, study measures of strengths, significance of relationships between variables, assumptions, data requirements, and types of error in significance tests.
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10B, POL SCI 10B, SOCECOL 13, SOCIOL 10B, PSYCH 10B.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences III
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focus on correlation, regression, and control for effects of variables. One-way and two-way factorial analysis of variance. A priori and a posteriori comparisons.  Introduction to repeated measures design and non-parametric statistics. Discuss use of statistics in newspapers and popular magazines.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( ECON 10B OR PSYCH 10B OR ANTHRO 10B OR SOCIOL 10B OR SOC SCI 10B )
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10C, POL SCI 10C, PSYCH 10C, SOCECOL 13, SOCIOL 10C.

allCourses.title: International Business
allCourses.description: Introduction to conducting business in the international arena, decision making in the organization, and globalization of markets and production.  Topics covered range from tax and finance to ethics, marketing, and more.  Continuing corporate regulatory scandals discussed.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Geography
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of geography. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Barter to Bitcoin: Society, Technology and the Future of Money
allCourses.description: Digital money has captured the broad imagination of speculators, coders, regulators, criminals and the mass media. Course puts this change in context: how do we understand money as a social, political and technological phenomenon?.

allCourses.title: Global Political Ideologies
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.

allCourses.title: Transnational Gangs
allCourses.description: Examines the internationalization of U.S. domestic street gangs.  The relationship between California gangs Mara Salvatrucha and 18th Street and Mexico/Central American gangs is assessed.  Specified topics include:  mobilization, migration, territorialism, culture, organization, and use of technology.

allCourses.title: Voting and Political Manipulation
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

allCourses.title: Veterans in History and Society
allCourses.description: Explores key concepts, issues, and trends in the interdisciplinary field of veterans studies. Students gain a deep understanding of the ways that social scientists and historians have analyzed the identities, experiences, and worldviews of U.S. military veterans.

allCourses.title: Veterans’ Transitions
allCourses.description: Provides veteran and non-veteran students with a comprehensive and academically rigorous overview of the ways and means through which diverse communities of veterans have made and continue to make the complex and multi-faceted transition from active military.

allCourses.title: Veterans’ Voices
allCourses.description: Uses the medium of academic writing to develop a broad understanding and appreciation for the wide range of worldviews, priorities, and values embodied in the creative production and activism of diverse U.S. military veterans.

allCourses.title: Global Political Economy
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The global economy as an integrated system. The rise of world trade, capitalism, national economies, market cycles, competing economic ideologies, development, globalization, transnational labor, multinational corporations, and the role of UN, World Bank, WTO, and the IMF in global governance.

allCourses.title: Non-Government Organization (NGO) Fundamentals
allCourses.description: Introduction to non-governmental organizations, including their role in U.S. society and the international community. Explores varying definitions of NGOs and the characteristics held in common by all NGOs.

allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.title: Human Rights and Global Governance
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.

allCourses.title: Urban America
allCourses.description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

allCourses.title: Chicanx/Latinx Education
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latinx low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

allCourses.title: Domestic Gangs
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the history and development of California street gangs and the role of historical events in that development. Students will be able to contrast and compare gang cohort behaviors between some of the major gangs in California.

allCourses.title: Prison Gangs
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the growth and spread of prison gangs throughout the country. Relationships between prison and street gangs, and possible relationships with foreign drug trafficking organizations studied. Violence examined as the standard to establish dominance in and out of prison.

allCourses.title: Juvenile Gangs
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines risk factors that can be used to predict gang membership. Compares generational with non-generational gangs and develops a working sociological definition that can be used to identify street gangs. Myths about juveniles, street gangs.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latino Families
allCourses.description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Inequality
allCourses.description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

allCourses.title: Global Environmental Issues
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines problems such as global climate change, growing human populations, fisheries depletion, ocean acidification, biodiversity loss, deforestation, and food security. Introduces political, social, and economic factors contributing to environmental issues and their disproportional impacts on the world’s poor and minorities.

allCourses.title: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines how interdisciplinary social science research questions are formulated and studies several research methods including: experimental method, quasi-experimental methods, survey research, field research, evaluation research, and meta-analysis. Parametric and non-parametric statistical methods are illustrated using the SPSS program.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI 1A and SOC SCI 2A and SOC SCI 3A and (SOC SCI 10A or STATS 7)

allCourses.title: American Culture
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of the historical development of dominant American culture and society; emphasis on a close reading of key cultural texts, with weekly text as a model of writing, examining its use of language and rhetoric.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Law in the Twenty-First Century
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the complex relationship between law, the social sciences, and modern society.  Lectures explore such issues as the interplay between technology and constitutional rights, the impact of science on law, and the evolving roles of attorneys and judges.

allCourses.title: Latinos in a Global Society
allCourses.description: Examines interconnections between diverse Latino groups in the U.S. and the effects of globalization on their social, cultural, and political realities. Topics include immigration, demographics, socioeconomic differentiation, familial relations, political protest/resistance, law and policy, and links to "homeland" issues.

allCourses.title: Revolution in Latin America
allCourses.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada.  Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

allCourses.title: Asian American Women
allCourses.description: Examines the representations and experiences of Asian American women from diverse perspectives. Explores the commonalities and differences among various groups of Asian American women, with particular focus on history, culture, values, and family roles.

allCourses.title: Korean American Studies
allCourses.description: Explores the factors that have distinctly shaped the Korean American experience, including patterns of racial domination, the profile of immigrant flow, immigrant roles in the urban political economy, politics in Korea, and the role of the church.

allCourses.title: Vietnamese American Studies
allCourses.description: Studies the resettlement of Vietnamese in the United States following their exodus from Southeast Asia. Topics include the Vietnam War, the 1975 evacuation, boat and land refugees, the shaping of Vietnamese communities, and Vietnamese American literature.

allCourses.title: Japanese American Studies
allCourses.description: Studies the settlement of Japanese in Hawaii and the continental United States since the late 19th century. Topics include sugar plantations, development of rural Japanese America, World War II internment, post-War community development, and persistence of Japanese American identity.

allCourses.title: South Asian American Studies
allCourses.restriction: Asian American Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines and compares the experiences of South Asian immigrants in the U.S. over time. Looks at the economic, political, and social positions of the immigrants, with special emphasis on religious changes and the changes in the second and later generations.

allCourses.title: Southeast Asian American Studies
allCourses.description: Analyzes experiences of refugees and immigrants from Southeast Asia, which may include those from Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Examines political and economic factors for their exodus and how they reconstruct their identities, histories, and communities.

allCourses.title: Chinese American Studies
allCourses.description: Analyzes the experiences of Chinese in the United States. Immigration, Chinese exclusion, racial and gender identity. Historical overview and contemporary issues covered.

allCourses.title: Filipina/Filipino American Studies
allCourses.description: Explores the experience of Filipina/Filipino Americans from the era of Spanish colonization of the Philippines to present-day community formations in the United States, with special emphasis on the 20th century. Topics include colonialism, nation, migration, gender, and culture.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Asian American Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Ethical Leadership
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores historical and contemporary theories of ethical and unethical leadership.  Examines models of "good leadership" such as cardinal and monastic virtues; and models of "bad leadership," such as Machiavelli's Prince.  Explores the philosophies, styles, and accomplishments of leaders.

allCourses.title: Global and International Studies Forum
allCourses.description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Mediation
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Humanities students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Student develop mediation skills and refine knowledge in the practice and theory of conflict resolution. Students who complete this course may serve as mediators in the Campus Mediation Program. Course is a prerequisite to completing Indep Study as an intern.

allCourses.title: Seminar Conflict Resolution
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed for seniors who are pursuing the International Studies major and/or minor. Provides a forum in which students will refine skills and theory in the study of cooperation and conflict, from local to global arenas. Students write research paper.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
allCourses.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

allCourses.title: Sage Leader Research I
allCourses.restriction: SAGE Scholars Program students only.
allCourses.description: Participants in the SAGE Scholars Program learn to define leadership concepts, discover various leadership styles, and develop strong leadership and communication skills resulting in strengthened ability to contribute to and interact with UCI and the Orange County community.

allCourses.title: Sage Leader Research II
allCourses.restriction: SAGE Scholars Program students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a survey of contemporary topics and challenges in the fields of management and leadership. Case studies and text by leading authors are used to analyze key leadership issues in twenty-first century, with particular emphasis on current events.

allCourses.title: Media Writing
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed to teach reporting and news writing basics.  Students learn how to gather and organize information, ask effective questions, develop story ideas, research facts, and write stories on deadline.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: People in Society
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Through readings about people in distinctly different societies throughout history, students learn concepts that cross the boundaries of the social science disciplines. Such themes as democracy, elitism, power, social class, and gender are the basis for discussion and writing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Twenty-First-Century Graduate Education
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Graduate and professional education in twenty-first century United States. Examines  strategies for admission to postbaccalaureate programs and success in graduate study culture. Introduction to processes including planning and preparation, school selection, entrance examination preparation, submission of applications, writing personal statements.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
allCourses.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

allCourses.title: Political Islam
allCourses.description: Political Islamd is a diverse phenomenon. While noticeable barriers exist to "Islamist democracy," it is the Islamists who will define the political future of much of the Muslim world. Reviews the experience of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, and Indonesia.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Graduate-Mentored Study in the Social Sciences
allCourses.description: Offers a hands-on research experience while increasing awareness of the various disciplines in the social sciences and of the requirements of graduate school.  Features graduate-mentored study under the supervision of the Associate Dean.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Identification of a graduate student (who is in good standing) as a mentor.

allCourses.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors only.
allCourses.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI 70C or SOCIOL 63. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
allCourses.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

allCourses.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
allCourses.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

allCourses.title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
allCourses.restriction: Social Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and under-served communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.

allCourses.title: Public Service Internship
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the role of etiquette and leadership in the professional environment. With a two-unit (50 hours) or four-unit (100 hours) credit option, students intern at a nonprofit agency exploring their roles as community leaders and improving their professional skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Management and Leadership Practicum-Social Science
allCourses.description: Social Sciences Academic Resource Center (SSARC) Resource Mangers (RMs) report directly to the Director and Associate Director, serving as frontline resource consultants, assisting visitors with resume development, graduate and professional school planning, internship placement, and professional development.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Educational Policy Field Studies
allCourses.description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Educational Policy Field Studies
allCourses.description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Educational Policy Field Studies
allCourses.description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Global Connect
allCourses.description: Identifies factors of change that influence the twenty-first century. Students serve as mentors at high schools to introduce globalization issues through workshops and lectures. Students must submit an application and have a 3.0 or higher overall GPA.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Professional Internship
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Students apply classroom knowledge through research projects in nonprofit agencies (local, state, and government) and the private sector. They pose solutions to agency-posed questions. Students gain field experience through 50 hours (for 2 units) or 100 (for 4 units).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Directed Group Study
allCourses.description: Directed study with Social Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Opportunities to do research and learn new skills outside the normal classroom environment. Students participate in planned research and study activities under a written contract with a supervising UCI instructor. Students may enroll for only one 199 each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 16 units.

allCourses.title: Principles in the Social Sciences
allCourses.description: Introduction to various disciplines within the social sciences. Provides an interdisciplinary perspective on understanding human behavior and social institutions, including interpersonal, economic, and cultural activities.

allCourses.title: Model United Nations
allCourses.description: Focuses on simulations of the foreign policy pursuits of selected countries in the international community. Emphasis placed on understanding the rules of debate, as well as the policy positions of the student's selected country in the United Nations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Behavioral Sciences Colloquium
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Behavioral Sciences Colloquium
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Behavioral Sciences Colloquium
allCourses.description: Weekly reports and colloquia by faculty, students, and visitors.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A required writing-intensive seminar conducted by an instructor affiliated with the Race and Justice Studies emphasis. Students with manuscripts on relevant topics will read and critique peer manuscripts, and revise manuscripts toward completion of articles, dissertation chapters, and other publications.

allCourses.title: Transnational Migration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

allCourses.title: Origin and Evolution of Marxist Social Thought
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the genesis and evolution of Marxist social thought The "systemic" method of Marx and Engels to questions of economic production and reproduction is compared and contrasted with modern world-system grand visions, feminist-theoretic approaches, and postmodern critiques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate course in political theory or equivalent.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Science
allCourses.description: Current research in Social Science.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Social Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Social Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Social Science Analysis
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to social science research and analytical models. Theory construction and use of research methods in an interdisciplinary context.  Discussion of the application of social science research to public policy.  Computer laboratories develop creative thinking, graphing, and data presentation skills.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Computer-Based Research in the Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the data manipulation, data visualization, and information searching techniques. Hands-on experience in hypothesis testing, mapping, graphics, and data arrays.

allCourses.title: Social Policy and Public Service
allCourses.description: An introduction to the basic theories and principles of public policy. Students examine various influences on the development of public policy and the principle actors in the process, and learn to identify tools and techniques employed in policy making.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Global Studies
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Ongoing historical processes that increase global integration, the social, economic, and political interdependence of different regions, cultures, and peoples. Topics include ancient empires, colonialism, nationalism, industrialization, modern imperialism and warfare, decolonization, global social movements, conflict, inequality, and global governance.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Human Geography
allCourses.description: Human behavior in a geographical context. Spatial patterns and organization of the cultural, social, and economic activities of man as imposed on and influenced by the earth's physical setting.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
allCourses.description: An introduction to the physical world we live in. Distribution and dynamics of the earth's air, water, and solid crust. Concepts and principles from climatology and geology. Selected examples from North America and beyond.

allCourses.title: US & World Geography
allCourses.description: Survey of general geographical principles and facts on a world scale, as well as introduction to the broad regional and resource geography of the U.S., emphasizing in particular the interactions of physical and cultural factors.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Gangs
allCourses.description: Introduces students to street gang subculture and explores risk factors associated with gang membership. Students develop a working definition for street gang and understand the difference between social and legal definitions. Also explores the connection between prison and street gangs.

allCourses.title: Comparing Cultures
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the scope of cross-cultural comparisons by analyzing the theories, methodologies, and facts utilized by anthropologists, sociologists, social psychologists, political scientists, and historians in comparing cultures.

allCourses.title: Asian American Histories
allCourses.description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

allCourses.title: Asian American Communities
allCourses.description: Examines the renewal of Asian immigration following World War II. Explores contemporary Asian American populations and communities in the U.S., and the impact of contemporary Asian immigration on the U.S. political economy and social order.

allCourses.title: Asian Americans and Race
allCourses.description: Analyzes the Asian American experience in comparative perspective, which includes comparisons of different ethnic and racial groups, and across gender and class. Possible topics include labor, economy, politics, migration, nation, popular culture, gender, family, sexuality, and multiraciality.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Sciences
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Social Sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Honors Research Workshop
allCourses.restriction: Social Science Majors only. Social Policy/Public Service Majors only. Social Science Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Student develops a 10–15-page prospectus of research for the honors thesis which includes: the research question, literature review, methods of investigation, and bibliography. Student selects a faculty mentor who will supervise thesis research and writing in winter and spring.

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis Research
allCourses.description: The student initiates and completes data collection for the honors thesis. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI H190A or SPPS H190A

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis
allCourses.description: The student completes, with the approval of the faculty mentor, an honors thesis containing: statement of the problem, literature review, research hypotheses, methods of investigation, results, discussion, and bibliography.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI H190B or SPPS H190B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

allCourses.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI H1E or SOCECOL H20A

allCourses.title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI H1F or SOCECOL H20B

allCourses.title: Introduction to Iberian Literature and Culture
allCourses.description: Introduction to the major authors and movements of Iberian literature and culture from the Middle Ages to the present.

allCourses.title: Introductory Studies to Latin American Literature and Culture
allCourses.description: A historical overview of Latin American literature and culture mainly focused on canonical texts. Topics include colonialism and postcolonialism, the nation, indigenismo, gender, and literary movements. Also introduces literary analysis, research methods, and cultural critique.

allCourses.title: Writing in Spanish
allCourses.description: Focuses on the use of writing as a medium to encourage critical thinking and the practical analysis of literary texts, as well as the study of historical and social issues in the Spanish-speaking world.

allCourses.title: Spanish Communication
allCourses.description: Designed to help students develop Spanish oral skills by exposing them to different verbal Spanish language registers. Special emphasis placed on abilities essential to professional or academic careers. Intended for Spanish majors as an important component of their overall education.

allCourses.title: Advanced Spanish Grammar
allCourses.description: Designed for students who have demonstrated a substantial level of proficiency in their studies of the Spanish language. Takes thorough approach to advanced grammatical problems, in order to assist students in their mastery of the elements of the Spanish language.

allCourses.title: Topics in Spanish for the Professions
allCourses.description: Taught in Spanish to promote linguistic competencies, intercultural awareness, and understanding of local Latino communities’ needs. Provides resources to carry out professional tasks and build meaningful community-based relationships in the health, legal, and business fields.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Peninsular Literature and Cultures
allCourses.description: Topics in Peninsular literature and cultures.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Latin American Literature and Cultures
allCourses.description: Topics in Latin American literature and cultures.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: U.S. Latino Literature and Cultures
allCourses.description: Focuses on aspects of literature, art, cultural production, and history of the multifaceted Latino cultures that have developed within the United States.  Focuses on one group, such as Caribbean Americans, Chicanos, Central Americans, or a comparative perspective of several groups.

allCourses.title: Spanish Phonetics
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamental notions of Spanish phonetics. Particular attention paid to problems of pronunciation that arise in native and non-native speakers of Spanish due to interference between Spanish and English. Phonology (the system that underlies phonetics) and Spanish dialectology included.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the scientific study of the Spanish language with a focus on its sound system, word components, word order as well as second language acquisition and language variation. Class is delivered in a hybrid format.

allCourses.title: Textual Analysis and Interpretation
allCourses.description: Focus on analysis and interpretation of literary texts. Emphasis on narrative, poetry, theater/performance, and visual media. Introduces students to major currents in theoretical thought, such as cultural studies, postmodernism, and others. Oral presentations and short essays required. Taught in Spanish.

allCourses.title: Topics in Golden Age Literature and Culture
allCourses.description: Golden Age Literature in Spain, including the Renaissance and Baroque periods. Works of poetry, narrative, and theater. Historical and cultural background.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in 18th and 19th Century Spanish Literature and Culture
allCourses.description: The main literary and ideological trends in 18th and 19th century Spain, including the enlightenment, romanticism, realism, and naturalism.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in 20th and 21st Century Spanish Literature and Culture
allCourses.description: 20th century Spanish authors. Works of poetry, narrative, or theater. Historical context of the period and principles of literary theory.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture of the 20th Century
allCourses.description: Topics in Latin American literature and culture of the 20th century.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Statistical Computing Methods
allCourses.description: Numerical computations and algorithms with applications in statistics. Topics include optimization methods including the EM algorithm, random number generation and simulation, Markov chain simulation tools, and numerical integration.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in probability and statistics.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Modern Data Analysis Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces selected modern tools for data analysis. Emphasizes use of computational and resampling techniques for data analyses when the data do not conform to standard toolbox of regression models and/or complexity of modeling problem threatens validity of standard methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: STATS 120C and STATS 205 and (STATS 201 or STATS 210)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
allCourses.description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, and factor analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and dimension reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, factor analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Time Series Analysis
allCourses.description: Statistical models for analysis of time series from time and frequency domain perspectives. Emphasizes theory and application of time series data analysis methods. Topics include ARMA/ARIMA models, model identification/estimation, linear operators, Fourier analysis, spectral estimation, state space models, Kalman filter.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Time Series Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistical models for time series. Topics include linear models for trends; stationary time-series; non-stationary time series; forecasting and Kalman filtering; time-series smoothing; seasonal models; ARCH, GARCH and stochastic volatility models; multivariate time series; vector autoregressive models; spectral analysis; case studies.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Biostatistics
allCourses.description: Statistical methods commonly used to analyze data arising from clinical studies. Topics include analysis of observational studies and randomized clinical trials, techniques in the analysis of survival and longitudinal data, approaches to handling missing data, meta-analysis, nonparametric methods.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Statistical Methods for Survival Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistical methods for analyzing survival data from cohort studies. Topics include parametric and nonparametric methods, the Kaplan-Meier estimator, log-rank tests, regression models, the Cox proportional hazards model and accelerated failure time models, efficient sampling designs, discrete survival models.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Statistical Genetics
allCourses.description: Provides students with knowledge of the basic principles, concepts, and methods used in statistical genetic research. Topics include principles of population genetics, and statistical methods for family- and population-based studies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in statistical methods.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Inference with Missing Data
allCourses.description: Statistical methods and theory useful for analysis of multivariate data with partially observed variables. Bayesian and likelihood-based methods developed. Topics include EM-type algorithms, MCMC samplers, multiple imputation, and general location model. Applications from economics, education, and medicine are discussed.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Theory and Practice of Sample Surveys
allCourses.description: Basic techniques and statistical methods used in designing surveys and analyzing collected survey data. Topics include simple random sampling, ratio and regression estimates, stratified sampling, cluster sampling, sampling with unequal probabilities, multistage sampling, and methods to handle nonresponse.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Theory and Practice of Sample Survey
allCourses.restriction: Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic techniques and statistical methods for designing surveys and analyzing collected survey data. Topics include simple random sampling, ratio and regression estimates, stratified sampling, cluster sampling, sampling with unequal probabilities, multistage sampling, and methods to handle nonresponse.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Causal Inference
allCourses.description: Various approaches to causal inference focusing on the Rubin causal model and propensity-score methods. Topics include randomized experiments, observational studies, non-compliance, ignorable and non-ignorable treatment assignment, instrumental variables, and sensitivity analysis. Applications from economics, politics, education, and medicine.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Stochastic Processes
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and application of stochastic processes. Topics include Markov chains, continuous-time Markov processes, Poisson processes, and Brownian motion. Applications include Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and financial modeling (for example, option pricing).

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Stochastic Processes
allCourses.restriction: Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and application of stochastic processes. Topics include Poisson processes, Markov chains, continuous-time Markov processes, and Brownian motion. Applications include Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and financial modeling (e.g. option pricing).

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Statistical Consulting
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Training in collaborative research and practical application of statistics. Emphasis on effective communication as it relates to identifying scientific objectives, formulating a statistical analysis plan, choice of statistical methods, and interpretation of results and their limitations to non-statisticians.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: STATS 203 or STATS 212 or STATS 210C. STATS 203 with a grade of B or better. STATS 212 with a grade of B or better. STATS 210C with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Periodic seminar series covering topics of current research in statistics and its application.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Axiomatic definition of probability, random variables, probability distributions, expectation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Point estimation, interval estimating, and testing hypotheses, Bayesian approaches to inference.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Contingency table analysis, linear regression, analysis of variance, model checking.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Statistics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of statistics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Thesis Supervision
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Data Science
allCourses.restriction: Information Computer Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the field of Data Science; intended for entering freshman and transfers.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Data Science
allCourses.description: Introduces the full data cycle. Topics include data collection and retrieval, data cleaning, exploratory analysis and visualization, introduction to statistical modeling, inference, and communicating findings. Applications include real data from a wide-range of fields with emphasis on understanding reproducible practices.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. STATS 67 may not be taken for credit concurrently with or after STATS 120B.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics with discussion of applications to computer science.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ( MATH 2B OR AP CALCULUS BC ) AND ( SCHOOL OF I&C SCI ONLY OR COMPUTER SCI & ENGR MAJORS ONLY )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Statistical Computing and Exploratory Data Analysis
allCourses.description: Introduces key concepts in statistical computing. Techniques such as exploratory data analysis, data visualization, simulation, and optimization methods, will be presented in the context of data analysis within a statistical computing environment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 31 AND ( STATS 7 OR AP STATISTICS )

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Basic Statistics
allCourses.restriction: STATS 7 may not be taken for credit concurrently with or after STATS 110, STATS 111, STATS 112.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic inferential statistics including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing on means and proportions, t-distribution, Chi Square, regression and correlation. F-distribution and nonparametric statistics included if time permits.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Biological Statistics
allCourses.restriction: STATS 8 may not be taken for credit concurrently with or after STATS 110, STATS 111, STATS 112.
allCourses.description: Introductory statistical techniques used to collect and analyze experimental and observational data from health sciences and biology. Includes exploration of data, probability and sampling distributions, basic statistical inference for means and proportions, linear regression, and analysis of variance.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Engineering
allCourses.description: Study of the concepts, methods, and tools for the analysis, design, construction, and measurement of complex software-intensive systems. Underlying principles emphasized. State-of-the-art software engineering and promising research areas covered, including project management.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Analysis of Programming Languages
allCourses.description: Concepts in modern programming languages, their interaction, and the relationship between programming languages and methods for large-scale, extensible software development. Empirical analysis of programming language usage.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Requirements Engineering and Specification
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Rigorous techniques in requirements engineering - the requirements definition phase of software development - with a focus on modeling and specification. Topics include notations and models for requirements specification; and methods, tools, and processes for software requirements elicitation, representation, analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Program Analysis
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers principles and concepts of automated program analysis. Topics include program representations; intra-procedural data-flow analysis; call-graph construction; pointer analysis; alias analysis; inter-procedural analysis; inter-procedural finite distributive subset problems; inter-procedural distributive environment problems; symbolic execution; and program-analysis applications.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Dynamic Analysis, Testing, and Debugging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies techniques for developing confidence in software from traditional testing techniques to state-of-the-art dynamic analysis and debugging techniques. Emphasis is on assisting developer comprehension of runtime behavior.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of the concepts, representation techniques, development methods, and tools for architecture-centric software engineering. Topics include domain-specific software architectures, architectural styles, architecture description languages, software connectors, and dynamism in architectures.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Retrieval, Filtering, and Classification
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Algorithms for the storage, retrieval, filtering, and classification of textual and multimedia data. The vector space model, Boolean and probabilistic queries, and relevance feedback. Latent semantic indexing; collaborative filtering; and relationship to machine learning methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CS 161 and CS 171 and (ICS 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Intelligent User Interfaces
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores example software systems and their underlying concepts that leverage computing to empower and augment human individuals in their activities. Topics span the fields of user interface design, human-computer interaction, software engineering, and cognitive computing.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Aspects of Software Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Selected topics about the cooperative and human aspects of software engineering from the perspective that software engineering is inherently an endeavor involving human stakeholders. Topics may include but are not limited to collaboration, trust, emotion, language, gender, and software tools.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Data Structures
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of well-known data structures to represent computational problems. Topics include linked lists, graphs, binary trees, stacks, queues, heaps, and hash tables, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Data Structures and Algorithms
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of strategies to tackle computational problems whose solutions include well-known algorithms and data structures. Topics include sorting, searching, and indexing, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of networking principles and concepts for the development of distributed software. Topics include programming against well-known network protocols, ports and sockets, and network APIs.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Database Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of software development with substantial reliance on a database for storage and retrieval of data. Topics include relational databases, structured query language, relational database management systems, APIs and libraries for database programming, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Concurrent Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of concepts and mechanisms for the development of concurrent software.  Topics include threads, locks, race conditions, and deadlocks, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: GUI Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of interactive software with substantial graphical user interface elements.  Topics include libraries and frameworks for GUI programming, layout design and alternatives, event-driven programming, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Mobile Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of contemporary libraries and frameworks for construction of mobile applications. Topics include emulators, mobile development standards and patterns, energy consumption issues, screen layout, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Information Retrieval
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of principles and concepts for textual information retrieval. Topics include tokenization, inverted indexes, scored retrieval, and precision and recall.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Neural Network Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and processes for training and using deep neural networks for classification problems. Topics include tensors and tensor operations, gradient-based optimization, feature engineering and learning, and workflow of learning systems.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Data Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and processes used in supervised and unsupervised learning for classification and clustering, from a software engineering perspective. Topics include K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, K-Means, and model assessment.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Web Programming
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and popular frameworks for developing full-stack web applications. Students develop simple applications using multiple development stacks, and deploy them on the cloud.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Testing and Debugging
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to teach students how to ensure high-quality software by means of testing, debugging, and other quality assurance activities. Students learn a combination of both theoretical and practical skills, including hands-on experience with modern tools and approaches.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Programming Styles
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to teach students the various ways software can be decomposed and put back together. Students are exposed to a variety of different programming styles and composition mechanisms.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Experience and Interaction
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to the basic principles of human-computer interaction (HCI) and the pragmatic aspects of usability engineering. Topics include the fundamentals of interaction, user experience, design for usability, and evaluation of products for their usability.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Distributed Software Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of software system architectures and architectural styles for large-scale distributed applications, and contemporary technologies and standards for their construction. Topics include client-server, peer-to-peer, publish-subscribe, REST, cloud computing, content distribution networks, scalability, latency, caching, and security, among others.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Reverse Engineering and Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces theories, concepts, representations, techniques, and case studies in understanding large-scale, complex software systems. Topics include static and dynamic modeling notations, manual and (semi-)automated reverse engineering techniques, APIs, patterns, and styles. A significant, hands-on project is included.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Security and Dependability
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and concepts for the design and construction of secure software. Topics include common types of software security vulnerabilities, methods for detecting vulnerabilities, design and process methodologies to improve security of software, and techniques for assessing security properties of software.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Cloud and Security Foundations
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Cloud and security foundations provides students fundamental design and security principles about cloud computing and information security. Topics include cloud concepts and architectures; cloud security; data protection and privacy compliance and governance; and security by design, amongst other topics.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Career and Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches practical skills for spoken, written, and electronic communication in a range of business and technical contexts, including promoting project ideas and portfolio development. Students practice their skills in classroom presentations and written exercises.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to project management in software engineering from several perspectives. Topics include team behavior; globally distributed work; and resource estimation, scheduling, and budgeting. Students apply their knowledge in an ongoing class project.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Curricular Practical Training
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mandatory internship in which students individually work at an outside organization to gain experience with the challenges involved in the practice of software engineering.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Project in Software Engineering
