allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Quarter-long software-intensive project focusing on the design and implementation of a novel software system. Students are expected to bring to bear the concepts acquired during the program.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advisement
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mandatory weekly meetings with a faculty advisor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Software Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of software engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Thesis Supervision
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Master of Software Engineering Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Supervised individual practical project in Software Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Washington DC Internship
allCourses.description: Supervised internship (20-40 hours per week) in Washington DC government, nonprofit, or private institution consistent with student's interest.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Selected for Washington DC Center Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Washington-Themed Seminar
allCourses.description: UCDC core course (multiple topics offered each quarter). Enhances students' experiential learning and imparts knowledge and skills to help them transition into public service/private sector positions. One core course per quarter mandatory for all participants in Washington DC Center Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Washington DC Elective
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas related to the UC Washington, DC Center Program (UCDC).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Selected for Washington DC Center Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Student Participation
allCourses.description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Project must be approved by a Student Affairs Department head and the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Student Participation
allCourses.description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Student Participation
allCourses.description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Freshman Experience
allCourses.description: An introduction to the freshman experience provides an overview of the University's aims and resources and exploration of developmental theories and skills necessary for academic success. Attention is also paid to questions of personal development and major choice.  Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Civic and Community Engagement and Community Research
allCourses.description: Provides a foundation for understanding the role of public scholarship, civic engagement, and social action, and the relationship between service learning and engaged citizenship. Introduces key theoretical and research methodologies on the traditions and innovations of civic and community engagement.

allCourses.title: Doing Research in the Community
allCourses.description: Critically reimagines the research endeavor and its participants/outcomes. Grapples with methods, values, and relationships involved in research. Explores alternative conceptions of research; focus is community-based. Students work in teams on real-world community research projects with faculty mentors and community partners.

allCourses.title: Philanthropy in the Community
allCourses.description: Introduces the role of community engagement, social action and philanthropy. Examines theories and practices of philanthropy, and strategies for social change. Involves hand-on engagement with philanthropy in the form of students making decisions about the distribution of a real fund.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Global Sustainability III
allCourses.description: Introduces Earth as a system and living planet. Examines physical and biological resources as well as energy, water, climate, and ecosystems. Introduces and applies analytic lens of environmental, social, and economic sustainability to examine human impacts and resource use.

allCourses.title: Advanced Internship in Undergraduate Education
allCourses.description: Advanced interns have a year's internship experience and return to contribute to Undergraduate Education programs in a leadership position. Students work three-five hours per week in a DUE office to coordinate or lead less-experienced interns and/or events.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: UNI AFF 1A and UNI AFF 1B and UNI AFF 1C
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 6 units.

allCourses.title: Methods and Application in Small Group Instruction
allCourses.restriction: Learning and Academic Resource Center employed tutors only.
allCourses.description: Explores various theories and methods of learning and development and their practical application in small group settings. Peer tutors receive instruction in the design, implementation, and evaluation of an effective learning environment for undergraduate students.

allCourses.title: Pedagogy of Small Group Facilitation - LAs
allCourses.description: Overview and readings in evidence-based instruction for undergraduate learning assistants. LAs receive instruction, training, and feedback on effective small group facilitation and active learning. To be taken while serving as a learning assistant in a course.

allCourses.title: Student Leadership Institute for Climate Resilience
allCourses.description: An overview of some of the major challenges and opportunities we face in building community climate resilience, as well as tools for action.

allCourses.title: Internship in Civic and Community Engagement
allCourses.description: Provides an opportunity to extend learning into a community-based setting addressing important social, environmental, and public issues. The internship project has a creative and scholarly component where students initiate their own action or inquiry experience.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Teaching Seminar: Theory and Practice
allCourses.description: For students selected to be discussion leaders for University Studies 2. Models of teaching, developmental theory applied to college freshmen, curriculum development. Practice of teaching techniques and group management skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Group Project for Discussion Leaders
allCourses.restriction: Discussion leaders only.
allCourses.description: For discussion leaders for University Studies 2. Weekly discussion group training for leading effective groups in addition to evaluations of weekly discussion sections and completion of a special project on issues of freshman development.  Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Internship
allCourses.description: Enables students from all majors to receive credit for an approved internship on or off-campus.  Internship sites may be public or private, for profit or non-profit agencies, organizations, companies, or corporations offering paid or unpaid learning experiences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Undergraduate Education
allCourses.description: Students do directed study (research, readings, etc.) on a topic related to Undergraduate Education under the supervision of one of the faculty who serve as Deans or Faculty Directors in the Division of Undergraduate Education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: UTeach Special Study
allCourses.restriction: UTeach Program students only.
allCourses.description: Students accepted to teach a UTeach course in spring quarter enroll in Special or Independent Study with their faculty mentor during the preceding fall quarter to develop their detailed course syllabus.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: UTeach: Teaching Theory and Practice
allCourses.restriction: UTeach Program students only.
allCourses.description: Students accepted to teach a UTeach course in spring quarter enroll during the winter to develop their teaching skills in preparation for teaching the following quarter.

allCourses.title: UTeach: Teaching Practicum
allCourses.restriction: UTeach Program students only.
allCourses.description: Students selected to teach in the UTeach Program teach their courses and meet weekly in a seminar to continue to develop and enhance their teaching skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Study Abroad Experiential Learning
allCourses.description: Study abroad on an approved program. Complete critical reflection (written paper, blog, etc.) submitted no later than the end of the quarter following the completion of the study abroad program. Enroll while studying abroad or the quarter immediately following return.

allCourses.title: Reflections While Abroad
allCourses.description: For students while they are studying abroad; maximizing learning outcomes by critically reflecting on learning experiences while abroad. Topics include cultural observations, professional issues, cultural competence, etc. Participants are located in different countries around the world.

allCourses.title: Internship Plus
allCourses.description: Provides training and development of career readiness competencies in parallel with a student’s internship experience. Internship sites may be public or private, for profit or non-profit agencies, organizations, companies, or corporations offering paid or unpaid learning experiences.

allCourses.title: Mentored Learning Assistant Field Work
allCourses.description: Oversight of trained learning assistants by the course instructor, including training in the discipline and responsibilities associated with supporting active group work. Instructor mentors LAs in how assisting small groups supports their career goals.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 9 units.

allCourses.title: NIH Fellowship Writing Skills
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed for graduate students in biomedical science departments who are preparing to write applications for NRSA (F30/F31) fellowships from the NIH. It involves a mixture of lectures, panel discussions, and peer review of writing samples.

allCourses.title: Graduate Legal Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Law students only.
allCourses.description: Monthly faculty/student colloquium to present and discuss socio-legal related research/issues. Course convened by Law School faculty with other faculty participation. Required for PLGS students enrolled in Law portion of degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: California Community College Internship
allCourses.restriction: MFA or Doctoral students who have advanced to candidacy.
allCourses.description: The California Community College Internship offers graduate students the opportunity to learn about faculty life, governance, and teaching at local community colleges. Structures fieldwork for students to participate in and reflect on the educational mission of community colleges.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 10 units.

allCourses.title: Mini-Seminars
allCourses.description: Designed primarily for freshmen as introduction to scholarly inquiry. Each section is taught by a faculty member from one of the academic disciplines and presents interesting and challenging topics representing the instructor's interest. Students participate in discussions, presentations, and projects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
allCourses.restriction: Must be a pedagogical fellow.
allCourses.description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
allCourses.restriction: Must be a pedagogical fellow.
allCourses.description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
allCourses.restriction: Must be a pedagogical fellow.
allCourses.description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Developing Teaching Excellence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to evidence-based instructional design and methods, specifically for higher education courses. Students practice, observe, and design instruction based on pedagogical literature. Meets most of the requirements for the Certificate in Teaching Excellence Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Advanced Course Design for Instructors of Record
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Confirmed instructors of record who have earned the Certificate in Teaching Excellence design their course (syllabus, lesson plans, activities, assessments, assignments) using best practices in pedagogy. By the end of the course, participants have their full course mapped.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Certificate of Teaching Excellence required, proof of instructor of record appointment required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Seminar for Teaching as Research
allCourses.description: Preparation and implementation of a teaching as research project in higher education. Participants learn research, experimental design, human subjects, and statistical analysis.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Illuminations
allCourses.description: This course connects students to Illuminations, the Chancellor’s Arts and Culture Initiative. Students will attend five Illuminations-sponsored events and engage in brief preparatory and reflective activities in response to these events.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Graduate School Opportunities and Preparation
allCourses.description: Explores the opportunities associated with graduate school by considering a wide range of disciplines and career paths. Reviews professional and academic paths in graduate school and the ways to prepare for a chosen path.

allCourses.title: University Studies International Village Seminar
allCourses.description: Seminars held in International Village that are specifically designed to either (a) introduce visiting international students to the U.S. and/or local area and institutions or (b) engage both international and U.S. students in discussion of topics of international interest.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: UTeach: Student-Taught Seminar
allCourses.description: Student-taught seminar courses on selected topics. Topics vary each year according to the interest of the students teaching the classes.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Pathways to University Success
allCourses.description: Helps first-year students transition to UC Irvine and promotes a successful University experience. Students learn about academic resources and programs that support acclimation to the campus and enhance academic development through lectures, discussions, and a range of co-curricular activities.

allCourses.title: Bridges to University Success
allCourses.description: Helps first-year students transition to UC Irvine and promotes a successful University experience. Students learn about academic resources/programs that support acclimation to the campus and enhance academic development through lectures, writing laboratories, discussions, and a range of co-curricular activities.

allCourses.title: Leading from Within
allCourses.description: Students examine characteristics and behaviors of effective leaders. Study the history and theoretical framework for understanding effective leadership. In addition, examine their own leadership strengths and weakness and become familiar with the theory behind and use of comprehensive self-assessment tools.

allCourses.title: Leading Others
allCourses.description: Students examine best practices within a team environment. They learn goal setting, diagnosing performance problems, designing solutions, and recognizing relevant differences in culture, priorities, and values within a team through lectures, writing, discussions, and practical activities.

allCourses.title: Leading Change
allCourses.description: Focused on a global viewpoint, students learn the theoretical framework behind innovation and change management. Develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges, design strategies to bring an expansive vision into fruition, and learn to communicate a vision and strategies.

allCourses.title: Strategies for Success
allCourses.description: Designed to develop good study skills in technical fields and the participation of students as active learners in their education. Topics include time management, analytical thinking, text analysis, academic survival strategies, and goal setting.

allCourses.title: Campuswide Honors Thesis Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Supports the honors thesis research activities of Campuswide Honors Collegium students. Students set research goals, discuss, and develop their research interests.
allCourses.corequisite: Students must sign up separately for 8 units of independent study with faculty mentors.

allCourses.title: Campuswide Honors Thesis Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Supports the honors thesis research activities of Campuswide Honors Collegium students. Students work with each other to improve both written and spoken presentations of their results.
allCourses.corequisite: Students must sign up separately for 8 units of independent study with faculty mentors.

allCourses.title: Critical Analysis of Health Science Literature
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on evaluation of scientific literature. Aspects of scientific inquiry include scientific method, scientific research design, statistical analysis, and publication processes. Addresses why scientific inquiry cannot be separated from sociocultural influences and concerns. Examples drawn from research on health-related issues.

allCourses.title: Environmental Issues Affecting the Sustainability of Societies I
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on several environmental challenges facing the world today, and explores the problem, possible solutions, and their scientific, technical, and social constraints. Models for systems, their assumptions, predictive uncertainty, and interpretation, play a large role.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: UNI STU H30A. UNI STU H30A with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Environmental Issues Affecting the Sustainability of Societies II
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how we can use Earth’s resources, e.g., food and water, in a more sustainable way, exploring their scientific, technical, and social constraints.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: UNI STU H30B. UNI STU H30B with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Social Science Perspectives on the Sustainability of Societies
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the perspectives of social science using examples from different countries to explore how social issues regarding sustainability are influenced by a society’s changing economic and political institutions, and how economic, political, and other social choices affect their sustainability.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS H30C. EARTHSS H30C with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Cities: Focal Point for Sustainability Problems and Solutions I
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the nature of cities, focusing on the challenges facing cities today, their possible solutions, and the technical and social constraints on those solutions.

allCourses.title: Cities: Focal Point for Sustainability Problems and Solutions II
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the nature of cities, focusing on the challenges facing cities today, their possible solutions, and the technical and social constraints on those solutions.

allCourses.title: Neurodivergent
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the evolution of the diagnosis of autism through history. Deep inquiry of the neuroscience, etiology, and genetics of neurodivergent individuals as well as a review of the validity of the varied treatments will inform critical thinking.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Urban Studies
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Cities
allCourses.description: Surveys the global and historical co-evolution of cities and social institutions, including religion, the economy, governance, the arts, technology, and family life.

allCourses.title: Urban Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines structural inequality and the influence that urbanization has in affecting race, ethnic, and class relations. Explores how race/ethnicity, class, urban space, housing, economic development, public education, and land policy intersect in cities, both historically and today.

allCourses.title: Comparative Approaches to Urban Regions
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only. Urban Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to comparative urbanization in developing countries. Introduces students to the geography, history, and theories of urbanization, and then reviews urban planning, public policy, and governance.

allCourses.title: Urban America
allCourses.description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

allCourses.title: Urban and Regional Planning
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Important substantive areas, concepts, tools in the field of urban and regional planning. Topics include: forces that have historically guided and are currently guiding U.S. urbanization; land use, economic development, housing and community development, environmental planning; legal, environmental, governmental contexts.

allCourses.title: Cities and Transportation
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The relationship between urban areas and transportation systems. Economic analysis of cities, transportation and urban form, highway congestion, environmental impacts of transportation, public transit, land use and transportation, and political influences on transportation planning.

allCourses.title: Housing and Urban Development Policy
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys public policy issues and develops analytic techniques in the areas of housing and urban development. Examines a range of policy topics including housing assistance to low- and moderate-income families, housing finance system, incentives for economic development, and neighborhood preservation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Previous course work in economics.

allCourses.title: Urban Economic Development Policy
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and practical perspectives on local economic development policy.  Integrates economic, planning, and political perspectives. Overview of economic role of cities and metropolitan areas. Specific development issues include: link between taxes, regulation, job growth; redevelopment planning; evaluation economic development policy.

allCourses.title: Climate Solutions
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to climate change science and impacts on the health of people and the planet with a focus on the multi-dimensional aspects of solutions to the climate crisis.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Community Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Poverty and Change in Developing Countries
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on poverty in developing countries.  Analyzes the magnitude and changing nature of poverty in the global south. Critically examines poverty conceptualized in terms of economic deprivation, well-being, and social exclusion.

allCourses.title: Advanced Research Methods
allCourses.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SE 10 and SE 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Global Poverty and Inequality in the 21st Century
allCourses.description: Explores a multidisciplinary understanding of poverty and inequality in the 21st century and assesses impact of education, health, technology, and other interventions. Course offered online only.

allCourses.title: Environmental Justice
allCourses.description: Engages students to critically analyze and evaluate environmental problems, environmental responses, and planning and policy debates regarding "environmental justice" - essentially the race, class, and equity implications of environmental problems and policies.

allCourses.title: Gentrification
allCourses.description: Gentrification is a complex process that changes the makeup of neighborhoods and fuels political and policy conflicts. Students are provided with tools to understand the process and conceive of policies to ensure more inclusive and equitable cities.

allCourses.title: Introduction to GIS for Planning and Policy
allCourses.description: Provides hands-on experience creating, visualizing, and interpreting spatial data, with a focus on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for urban planning and public policy.

allCourses.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides hands-on experience using geoprocessing to analyze spatial data and using maps to visualize and communicate findings, with a focus on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for urban planning and public policy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: UPPP 120. UPPP 120 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Spatial Analysis Project
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: As the capstone in the Geographic Information Systems (GIS) degree specialization, students are guided through the process of applying their GIS skills to designing and conducting an original spatial research project, focusing on research design and research methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: UPPP 125 and UPPP 120. UPPP 125 with a grade of C or better. UPPP 120 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.title: Cities and Food
allCourses.description: Explores the role of cities in transforming global diets: how urbanization has shaped what and how we eat, and what the co-evolution of diets and city life portend for the future.

allCourses.title: Environmental Sustainability I
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to sustainability from different points of view; historical, scientific, political, ethical, and economic.

allCourses.title: Environmental Sustainability II
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Investigates how sustainability can be implemented in a variety of contexts including water, energy, non-renewable resources, biodiversity, and urban policy, and also how it could be measured.

allCourses.title: Environmental Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors only. Urban Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Environmental law as a combination of traditional legal principles and newly created statutes, rules, and decisions applied to environmental protection. Investigates roles of courts, legislature, executive branch and administrative agencies, and private citizens attempting to regulate environmental quality.

allCourses.title: Water Resource Policy
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of contemporary water problems worldwide, with particular attention to the competing water demands in the western U.S., and water demand by the poor in developing countries. History and analysis of U.S. water policies at local, state, and federal levels.

allCourses.title: Environmental Hazards in an Urbanizing World
allCourses.description: Development patterns, including urbanization, can contribute to environmental hazard severity. Humans can plan, mitigate, and prepare to reduce costly hazard losses. Students learn about environmental hazards and human response to these threats.

allCourses.title: Environmental Governance
allCourses.description: How should the environment be managed and who should be responsible? What is effective environmental management, and for whom? These questions are answered by exploring traditional and emerging theoretical frameworks and applying them to real world environmental challenges.

allCourses.title: Principles of Economics for Planning and Policy
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction into economics for planning and policy students.

allCourses.title: Cultural Ecology and Environmental Design
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to cultural ecology and environmental and architectural design. Addresses the understanding of people’s relationships with their built environments, the basic elements of architecture, architectural analysis, and cultural analysis are covered. Examines values in design and design for multicultural societies.

allCourses.title: Elements of Environmental Design
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic elements of environmental design such as scale, proportion, rhythm, color, sound, lighting, surfaces, texture, architectural definition of spaces, volumes, massing volumetric analysis, solids and voids, and cultural aspects of design. Excitement and creativity in design, imageability.

allCourses.title: Urban Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of urban design and its applications.  Study of contemporary and traditional theories of urban design formulated to improve physical characteristics of built environment to facilitate an enhanced quality of life.  A variety of case studies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Urban Politics and Policy
allCourses.description: Examines why and how urban policies are enacted and carried out in contemporary U.S. cities and regions. Topics include evolution and organization of city governments and policymaking over the past century; who directs public policy and controls how cities develop.

allCourses.title: Public Policy and Governance
allCourses.restriction: Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Exposes students to best practices that assure effective planning and implementation of policies and programs in government, business, and nonprofit sectors. Includes guest lecturers who are proven leaders in four principal institutions of community: business, education, government, and non-profit.

allCourses.title: Health Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States.  What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care?  International comparisons will be made wherever possible.

allCourses.title: Latino Metropolis
allCourses.description: Explores the processes of Latino urbanization in the United States and the spatialization of Latino identities, particularly in the context of Southern California with selected comparisons drawing from other cities.

allCourses.title: Chicano Movement
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the history of Mexicans in the U.S. with particular attention paid to their integration into the U.S. capitalist economy.  Examines this economic history and the Chicano movement, "El Movimiento," within the wide context of socio-economic change.

allCourses.title: International Divided Cities
allCourses.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

allCourses.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.

allCourses.title: History of Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the historical roots and fundamental perspectives of urban and regional planning.  Exploration of the significant historical phases and personalities which have shaped the profession.  The roles and responsibilities, the limitations and potential, of urban planning.

allCourses.title: Theoretical Foundations of Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intellectual excursion into central themes in policy and planning, including philosophy of the market, institutionalization of space, hypostatizations of policy, constructions of communities, logics of spatial analysis. Objective is engagement of the professional in thoughtful reflections on practice and institutions.

allCourses.title: Plan Development and Communication
allCourses.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning Majors only.
allCourses.description: Graphic representation and communication of physical place characteristics, design and physical planning ideas, and concepts using a variety of graphic techniques of free hand drawing, sketching, orthographic representations, scale drawings, 3D representations, maps, photo-documentation, and various media.

allCourses.title: Environmental Economics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a broad introduction to environmental economics and to environmental policy.  Environmental problems facing the United States and Europe are analyzed, and whenever possible, the environmental problems facing developing countries.

allCourses.title: Microeconomic Analysis for Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a working knowledge of basic microeconomic concepts.  Emphasizes applications related to urban planning and policy analysis.  Topics covered include demand analysis, firm behavior, market structure, public goods, externalities, and the role of economics in land markets.

allCourses.title: Land-Use Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Investigates legal and institutional frameworks for development control. Review of constitutional issues implicated in land-use regulation. Traces development control historically and analyzes contemporary approaches to land-use control which reflect environmental and economic development concerns.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods: Overview
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of “qualitative” research and non-positivistic inquiry. Formulation of research questions, selection of method, data collection techniques, and analysis (briefly). Overview of selected methods from ethnography, naturalistic field research, phenomenology, ethnoarchaeology, critical approaches, and others.

allCourses.title: Practice Experience
allCourses.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides Master of Urban and Regional Planning students an opportunity to link classroom knowledge with real planning situations through a 10-week unpaid practice experience.

allCourses.title: Transportation Planning and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces current topics in transportation planning. Includes an analysis of the economic role of transportation in urban areas, land-use impacts of transportation projects, traffic congestion, air quality, alternatives to the automobile, and other transportation topics.

allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

allCourses.title: Quantitative Analysis for Planners
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the basic statistical concepts used to address issues of public concern.  Prepares students to perform, interpret, and evaluate quantitative data analyses commonly used in professional studies.

allCourses.title: Analytical Methods for Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the development of analytical techniques proven useful in the fields of management and administration.  Topics include multiple regression, cost-benefit analysis and discounting, decision trees, and other techniques useful for the purposes of community analysis and planning.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Methods for Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory course with focus on gaining a sound understanding of what constitutes credible evidence in support of policy arguments and management decisions.

allCourses.title: Information and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Evaluates strengths and weaknesses of qualitative and quantitative methods and the data used in making public policy claims. Looks at the bases of certain widely accepted measures of poverty, growth, environmental quality, and the like.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Methods: Fieldwork and Data Collection
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.

allCourses.title: Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst.  Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.

allCourses.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews and critiques literature on discussion topics including: the nature and effectiveness of environmental movements and policies; the role of science and technology; the use of economic incentives in policy; decentralization of decision making; and creating arenas for public involvement.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Methods for Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.

allCourses.title: Economics of Government
allCourses.description: Prepares students to analyze public policy questions with tools from economics. By the end, students should be able to identify important economic issues in public policy debates and consume and critique economic research on these topics.

allCourses.title: Demographics for Planning and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides planning and policy practitioners with a condensed, nonspecialist orientation to the sources, applications, and interpretation of population statistics, and conveys the steps used in constructing local-area population forecasts and projections.

allCourses.title: Transportation and Environmental Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critically evaluates how transportation can promote sustainable, healthy, and equitable cities. Examines the interaction of transportation systems with urban form, land use, community health, and environmental quality.

allCourses.title: Water Policy and Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines major issues in global water management including privatization, emerging water quality challenges, water system planning, affordability, conservation strategies, and flood resilience. Emphasizes integrated understanding of economics, governance, environmental health, technology, and development.

allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Problem Solving in Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the application of geographic information systems (GIS) in urban planning.  Steps through a GIS-based planning procedure that balances housing, jobs, tax base, utilities, transportation, and the natural environment.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
allCourses.description: Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to the field of urban and regional planning.  Emphasizes current issues that occur in actual implementation settings. Lecture/discussion followed by laboratory demonstrating the area of GIS discussed.  Offers "hands-on" student usage of GIS software.

allCourses.title: Urban Design Theories and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to contemporary and traditional theories of urban design and their applications.  Organized around one question:  How might planning and design of built environment contribute to making a good city?  National and international case studies are introduced.

allCourses.title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of microeconomics that are required for applied policy analysis. Provides students with an intuitive understanding of the microeconomic approach, and familiarizes them with concepts used in applied public policy analysis.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Public Health Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Master of Public Policy Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban and Regional Planning Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

allCourses.title: Land-Use Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examination of the role of public policy in guiding growth and development in urban and suburban environments.  Description of a wide-ranging set of growth policies, the rationales underlying their use, controversies and legal constraints, and evaluation of their effectiveness.

allCourses.title: Housing Policy
allCourses.description: Examines theories and practices of housing policy and the relationship of housing to larger neighborhood, community, and regional development issues. Considers the roles of private for-profit and not-for-profit developers, lenders, and all levels of government in the provision of housing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Familiarity with basic statistics is required.

allCourses.title: Poverty and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

allCourses.title: Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Treatment of legal and policy strategies for promoting environmental protection and deterring environmental degradation within the context of other societal objectives. Topical approach with a focus on problems of special interest to criminologists and to environmental policy specialists.

allCourses.title: Policy and Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines the challenge of identifying ethical principles that can guide us in formulating and assessing public policy, the public policy process from an ethical perspective, and the ethics of the individual engaged in the public policy arena.

allCourses.title: Economic Democracy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores a wide range of radical democratic and egalitarian visions (including but not limited to the Marxist tradition) for a more sane, just, and sustainable future.

allCourses.title: Public Finance for Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to public project financing, including overviews of major expenditure and revenue sources, budgeting processes, and the relationship between budgeting and planning. Practical skills covered include public financing methods, relevant mathematical analytic techniques, and grant writing.

allCourses.title: Site Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basics of site plan review (e.g., site/plot plans, floor plans, elevations) to ensure compliance with the zoning code, comparison of ministerial vs. discretionary review processes, Intersection of California Environmental Quality Act with review processes, understanding reporting requirements.

allCourses.title: Global Urbanization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the 20th century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds.

allCourses.title: MPP Capstone Research Project and Briefing
allCourses.restriction: Master of Public Policy Degree students only. Graduate students only. Must be taken at the end of the second year in the program.
allCourses.description: Focuses on an issue by emphasizing all aspects of the policy process, including problem definition, mobilizing support, design, implementation, management, and entrepreneurship. Two quarters in length. Students work in teams and present their product to faculty, students, and policymakers.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Special topics in urban and regional planning are offered from time to time, but not on a regular basis. Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Planning for Sustainable Cities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Measurement, implementation, and evaluation of urban sustainability practices.

allCourses.title: Site Planning and Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Enhance understanding of planning documents, including site plans, sections, design guidelines that are part of the everyday practice of most planners. Students gain opportunities to create a physical end product that can be added to a professional portfolio.

allCourses.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

allCourses.title: Transportation Practice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Broad survey of transportation policy issues that are confronting transportation planners, engineers, policymakers, and citizens.

allCourses.title: Advanced Theory
allCourses.description: Provides urban planning and public policy students with an introduction to advanced theory. Addresses broad theoretical approaches that cut across disciplinary and topical boundaries. Designed primarily for Ph.D. students.

allCourses.title: Urban Design Studio for Planners: An Introduction
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory urban design for planners.  Organized around a variety of assignments to encourage learning by design in a studio setting. Students work on design projects and drawing assignments to learn practical aspects of urban design.

allCourses.title: Collaborative Governance and Public Management
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to inclusive management. To make effective use of public resources, public managers are inventing ways of managing that alter relationships within organizations, between organizations, between sectors, and with the public. Requires rethinking fundamentals such as leadership and motivation.

allCourses.title: Professional Report
allCourses.description: Workshop designed to assist M.U.R.P. students in conducting their professional reports.  Students select topics, design projects, conduct professional investigations, and write up reports.

allCourses.title: Urban Planning Practicum I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.

allCourses.title: Urban Planning Practicum II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.

allCourses.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Urban Planning and Public Policy faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides training in research design and methods. Students learn how to evaluate the strength of research findings based on the methods used by a researcher and learn to use lessons from the course to develop a research proposal.

allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed studies in Urban Planning.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent Study in Urban Planning.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Urban Studies
allCourses.restriction: School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the substantive areas, concepts, and tools in the field of urban studies.  Acquaints students with physical, environmental, social, economic, and political dimensions of cities. Examines the challenges facing cities, including poverty, sustainability, development, globalization, and others.

allCourses.title: Urban Sociology
allCourses.description: Overview of theoretical, substantive, and policy issues in urban sociology.  History of urbanization, the school of human ecology, and recent trends regarding urbanism.  Time is devoted to understanding the causes and possible solutions to urban problems.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Urban Planning and Policy
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the basic issues in urban planning and public policy.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Analysis and Design
allCourses.description: Overview of general concepts, theoretical principles, and analytical techniques for investigating environmental systems. Integrates tools from natural and social sciences to analyze contemporary environmental challenges such as pollution, resource acquisition, facility and ecosystem design, impact assessments, formulation of environmental policy.

allCourses.title: Vietnamese Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
allCourses.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. VIETMSE 10A is for language mentors.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Vietnamese Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
allCourses.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. VIETMSE 10B is for language mentees.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
allCourses.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Vietnamese
allCourses.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Vietnamese. Natural approach with emphasis on four fundamental skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Conducted in Vietnamese.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: VIETMSE 1A. VIETMSE 1A with a grade of C or better. Placement into VIETMSE 1B is also accepted.

allCourses.description: Vietnamese culture and society in modern and historical contexts through the study of literary works, film, and other media. Philosophy and religious practices may also be examined. Course is taught in English.

allCourses.title: Art History:Theories and Methods
allCourses.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in Art History.

allCourses.title: Film & Media Studies: Theories and Methods
allCourses.description: Examines canonical texts and explores current directions in Film and Media Studies.

allCourses.description: Special graduate seminar offered at the Getty Research Institute in Los Angeles, involving faculty and graduate students from the five graduate programs in Art History or Visual Studies located in southern California (UCI, UCLA, UCR, UCSB, and USC).
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Graduate Seminar in Visual Studies
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Visual Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Directed Reading
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed reading on a specific topic agreed upon by student and instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Writing Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Offered winter quarter each year and taught in a workshop format. Assists students with the preparation and revision of the dissertation prospectus so that they may advance to candidacy.

allCourses.description: Readings in literature, with discussions and written rhetorical responses on their making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (WRITING 30 or WRITING 31) and (WRITING 90 or WRITING 91) and (WRITING 30 or WRITING 31 or WRITING 90 or WRITING 91 or ENGLISH 16 or ENGLISH 17). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Writing Internship
allCourses.description: Internships focused on writing. In consultation with a faculty advisor, students create a course from response essays, research essays, and assessment project data. Internships may include editing and publication projects, supervised teaching and tutoring assignments, community literacy projects.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement.
